```text
Data Object "Audience Segment and Suppression List" — read by User task
  "Load audience segments and suppression lists into Marketing Automation
  Platform".
Data Object "Launch Confirmation Record" — written by User task "Record
  launch confirmation and initial metrics".

V10.05 Launch Campaign activates the campaign across paid media and
automated digital channels by configuring the marketing automation
platform, uploading and submitting ad assets to the advertising platform,
triggering the first sends, and confirming delivery. It hands a live,
delivering campaign with initial engagement signals to V10.06 Capture
Response, which begins collecting and recording prospect interactions.
```


### V10.06 — Capture Response

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.06 Capture Response — the subprocess that collects and records
every inbound prospect response across channels, sitting between Launch
Campaign and Enrich & Score Response in the Market to Lead value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the organisation running the capture process,
with lanes for Marketing Operations.
Pool "Prospect" — the external individual or organisation responding to the
campaign.
Pool "Marketing Automation Platform" — the system that receives and logs
digital responses and engagement signals.
Pool "Web Analytics System" — the system that records web visits, page views,
and on-site behaviour.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospect" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Marketing Automation Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Web Analytics System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospect
2. Marketing Organisation
3. Marketing Automation Platform
4. Web Analytics System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Marketing Operations lane:

Message start event "Campaign launched — ready to receive responses from
Launch Campaign"

User task "Monitor active response channels"

Intermediate message catch event "Prospect response received"

Exclusive gateway "Response channel?"
- branch "Form submission or content download": Service task "Retrieve form
  submission data from Marketing Automation Platform"
  then Service task "Log form response record"
- branch "Email click or open": Service task "Retrieve email engagement
  event from Marketing Automation Platform"
  then Service task "Log email engagement record"
- branch "Web visit or page view": Service task "Retrieve web visit data
  from Web Analytics System"
  then Service task "Log web visit record"
- branch "Event registration": User task "Record event registration
  details"
  then Service task "Log event registration record"
Exclusive merge gateway "Response channel?"

User task "Check response for duplicate record"

Exclusive gateway "Duplicate exists?"
- branch "Yes — existing record found": User task "Merge response with
  existing contact record"
- branch "No — new contact": User task "Create new contact record"
Exclusive merge gateway "Duplicate exists?"

Service task "Apply consent and suppression check"

Exclusive gateway "Consent valid?"
- branch "No — suppressed or no consent": User task "Flag record as
  suppressed and close"
  then End event "Response suppressed — no further processing"
- branch "Yes — consent confirmed": Service task "Update consent status on
  contact record"
Exclusive merge gateway "Consent valid?"

User task "Confirm channel preferences and opt-in selections"

Service task "Write completed response record to Marketing Automation
Platform"

End event "Response record captured — ready for Enrich and Score Response"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Monitor active response channels"
labelled "Campaign response window closed" — leads to End event "Response
window expired — no responses captured".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Marketing Operations lane.
After the start event, the flow passes through channel monitoring, the
message catch event, and into the channel gateway. Each branch — form
submission, email engagement, web visit, and event registration — retrieves
and logs the relevant data before rejoining at the channel merge gateway.
The flow then proceeds through duplicate checking (merge or create branches
rejoining at their merge gateway), consent checking (suppressed branch ends
at its own end event; confirmed branch continues through the consent merge
gateway), preference confirmation, final write-back, and the end event.

Message flows:
Prospect → Marketing Organisation, Marketing Operations lane (response
signals: form submissions, downloads, email clicks and opens, event
registrations).
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Organisation, Marketing
Operations lane (digital response events and email engagement data
delivered to retrieve tasks).
Marketing Organisation, Marketing Operations lane → Marketing Automation
Platform (completed response record written back via "Write completed
response record to Marketing Automation Platform").
Web Analytics System → Marketing Organisation, Marketing Operations lane
(web visit and page-view data delivered to "Retrieve web visit data from
Web Analytics System").

7. Data objects

Data Object "Prospect Response Record" — written by "Log form response
record", "Log email engagement record", "Log web visit record", "Log event
registration record"; read by "Check response for duplicate record".

Data Object "Event Registration Details" — written by "Record event
registration details"; read by "Log event registration record".

Data Object "Contact Record" — written by "Create new contact record" and
"Merge response with existing contact record"; read by "Apply consent and
suppression check" and "Confirm channel preferences and opt-in selections".

Data Object "Consent and Suppression Status" — written by "Update consent
status on contact record"; read by "Write completed response record to
Marketing Automation Platform".

"Write completed response record to Marketing Automation Platform"; read by
"Retrieve form submission data from Marketing Automation Platform" and
"Retrieve email engagement event from Marketing Automation Platform".

System; read by "Retrieve web visit data from Web Analytics System".

Capture Response collects inbound prospect signals from all active campaign
channels — form submissions, email engagement, web visits, and event
registrations — and consolidates them into a single, consent-validated
contact record. It resolves duplicates, enforces suppression rules, and
records channel preferences before writing the completed record back to the
Marketing Automation Platform. The enriched and normalised response record
it produces is handed directly to Enrich and Score Response for further
qualification.
```


### V10.07 — Enrich & Score Response

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.07 Enrich & Score Response — third enrichment and scoring
subprocess in the Market to Lead value chain, taking raw captured
responses and producing scored, enriched records ready for lead
qualification.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the internal team running enrichment
and scoring.
  Lane "Marketing Operations" — marketing operations analyst who
  orchestrates enrichment requests and updates response records.
  Lane "Data & Analytics" — data analyst who reviews enrichment
  results and applies and validates lead scores.

Pool "Data Provider" — external supplier of firmographic,
demographic, and contact enrichment data.

Pool "Data Enrichment Service" — system that matches response records
against third-party data and returns enrichment results.

Pool "Customer Data Platform (CDP)" — system that holds the unified
customer and prospect profile and stores final scores.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Enrichment Service" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Customer Data Platform (CDP)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Provider
2. Marketing Organisation
3. Data Enrichment Service
4. Customer Data Platform (CDP)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Marketing Operations lane:
  Message start event "Captured response record received from
  Capture Response"
  Service task "Retrieve existing profile from CDP"
  User task "Review response record and flag missing fields"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient data to enrich?"
  - branch "No — data gaps identified":
      Send task "Request supplementary data from Data Provider"
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary data received
      from Data Provider"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient data to enrich?"
  - branch "Yes — data adequate":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient data to enrich?"
  Service task "Submit response record to Data Enrichment Service"
  Intermediate message catch event "Enrichment results received from
  Data Enrichment Service"
  User task "Review enrichment results and resolve conflicts"
  Exclusive gateway "Enrichment match acceptable?"
  - branch "No — match rejected or low confidence":
      User task "Mark record as unmatched and note reason"
      End event "Unmatched record flagged — passed to Qualify Lead
      for manual review"
  - branch "Yes — match accepted":
      User task "Merge enriched fields into response record"
      (passes to Data & Analytics lane)

Data & Analytics lane:
  User task "Apply lead scoring model to enriched record"
  Exclusive gateway "Score meets minimum threshold?"
  - branch "Below threshold":
      User task "Tag record as below threshold"
      Service task "Write below-threshold record to CDP"
      End event "Below-threshold record stored — passed to Nurture
      Unqualified Response"
  - branch "At or above threshold":
      User task "Validate score and confirm segment assignment"
      Service task "Write scored and enriched record to CDP"
      End event "Scored lead record stored — passed to Qualify Lead"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit response record to Data
Enrichment Service" — label "Enrichment response overdue (24 hours)"
— flow continues to User task "Mark record as unmatched and note
reason" in Marketing Operations lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in Marketing Operations, moves through
the data-gap gateway and optionally loops via the Data Provider
branch before merging and continuing to the enrichment submission
step; after enrichment results arrive, the acceptable-match gateway
branches to either the unmatched end event or the merge task, which
then crosses into the Data & Analytics lane for scoring; the scoring
gateway branches to the below-threshold end event or the validated,
scored end event.

Message flows:
Data Provider → Marketing Operations (supplementary firmographic and
contact data in response to request).
Marketing Operations → Data Provider (request for supplementary data
on identified gap fields).
Marketing Operations → Data Enrichment Service (response record
submitted for matching and enrichment).
Data Enrichment Service → Marketing Operations (enrichment results
and match confidence scores returned).
Marketing Operations → Customer Data Platform (CDP) (retrieve
existing prospect profile).
Customer Data Platform (CDP) → Marketing Operations (existing profile
record returned).
Data & Analytics → Customer Data Platform (CDP) (scored and enriched
record written, or below-threshold record written).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Captured Response Record" — read by "Review response
record and flag missing fields"; read by "Submit response record to
Data Enrichment Service".
Data Object "Enrichment Results" — written by Data Enrichment Service
(via message); read by "Review enrichment results and resolve
conflicts".
Data Object "Supplementary Data Package" — written by Data Provider
(via message); read by "Review response record and flag missing
fields".
"Retrieve existing profile from CDP"; written by "Write scored and
enriched record to CDP"; written by "Write below-threshold record
to CDP".
Data Object "Scored Lead Record" — written by "Write scored and
enriched record to CDP"; read by "Validate score and confirm segment
assignment".
Data Object "Unmatched Record Note" — written by "Mark record as
unmatched and note reason".

V10.07 Enrich & Score Response takes the raw captured response
records produced by V10.06, fills data gaps through the Data
Provider, matches and augments each record via the Data Enrichment
Service, and then applies the lead scoring model in Data & Analytics.
Records that meet the score threshold are written to the CDP as
qualified candidates and passed to V10.08 Qualify Lead; records that
fall below the threshold are stored separately and handed to V10.10
Nurture Unqualified Response for ongoing engagement.
```


### V10.08 — Qualify Lead

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.08 Qualify Lead — fifth subprocess in the Market to Lead value
chain, converting enriched and scored responses into qualified or
unqualified leads for downstream routing or nurturing.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the organisation running the qualification
process, containing the Sales Development lane.
Pool "Prospect" — the individual or organisation whose response is being
qualified.
Pool "CRM System" — system of record for lead and contact data used during
qualification.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospect" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospect
2. Marketing Organisation
3. CRM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Sales Development lane:
  Message start event "Enriched and scored response received from
    Enrich & Score Response"
  Service task "Retrieve lead record and score from CRM"
  Exclusive gateway "Lead score meets qualification threshold?"
    - branch "Score below threshold": End event "Response marked
        unqualified — passed to Nurture Unqualified Response"
    - branch "Score at or above threshold": User task "Review lead
        details and enrichment data"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Lead score meets qualification threshold?"
  User task "Conduct qualification outreach to prospect"
  Intermediate message catch event "Prospect responds"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Qualification Outcome Confirmed"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Record prospect
    response and update lead record in CRM", User task "Reassess lead
    against qualification criteria", Exclusive gateway "Outcome
    confirmed?",
      - branch "Not yet confirmed — more information needed": User task
          "Send follow-up request to prospect",
      - branch "Outcome confirmed": continue to loop exit
    Exclusive merge gateway "Outcome confirmed?"
  Exclusive gateway "Lead qualifies?"
    - branch "Does not qualify": End event "Lead marked unqualified —
        passed to Nurture Unqualified Response"
    - branch "Qualifies": User task "Mark lead as qualified in CRM"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Lead qualifies?"
  User task "Assign qualification notes and next-step recommendation"
  End event "Lead qualified — ready for Route Qualified Lead to Sales"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Conduct qualification outreach
to prospect", labelled "No response after outreach window", leading to
User task "Flag lead as non-responsive and mark unqualified in CRM",
then to End event "Lead marked unqualified — passed to Nurture
Unqualified Response".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The single Sales Development lane carries all flow.
From the start event the sequence passes through CRM retrieval, then
the score-threshold gateway splits into a below-threshold branch
(ending immediately as unqualified) and an above-threshold branch
(continuing to lead review), rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway.
Flow continues to outreach, the prospect-response catch event, and the
loop subprocess. On exit, the "Lead qualifies?" gateway splits into a
does-not-qualify branch (ending as unqualified) and a qualifies branch
(continuing to mark qualified and add notes), rejoining at its merge
gateway before the final end event.

Message flows:
Prospect → Marketing Organisation / Sales Development lane (prospect
  response to qualification outreach).
Marketing Organisation / Sales Development lane → Prospect (qualification
  outreach message and any follow-up requests).
Marketing Organisation / Sales Development lane → CRM System (lead record
  updates: qualification status, notes, response data).
CRM System → Marketing Organisation / Sales Development lane (existing
  lead record, enrichment data, and current score).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Enriched Lead Record" — read by "Retrieve lead record and
  score from CRM"; written by "Record prospect response and update lead
  record in CRM".
Data Object "Qualification Outreach Log" — written by "Conduct
  qualification outreach to prospect"; read by "Reassess lead against
  qualification criteria".
Data Object "Prospect Response" — written by "Record prospect response
  and update lead record in CRM"; read by "Reassess lead against
  qualification criteria".
Data Object "Qualification Notes" — written by "Assign qualification
  notes and next-step recommendation"; read by end event flow to Route
  Qualified Lead to Sales.

V10.08 Qualify Lead takes an enriched and scored response and applies
formal qualification criteria — lead score thresholds, outreach
confirmation, and reassessment — to determine whether the prospect is
sales-ready. Leads that meet the criteria are marked qualified in the
CRM, annotated with notes and a next-step recommendation, and passed
to V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales. Responses that fall below the
threshold or remain unresponsive are marked unqualified and handed to
V10.10 Nurture Unqualified Response.
```


### V10.09 — Route Qualified Lead to Sales

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales — the subprocess that assigns
a qualified lead to the appropriate sales owner and confirms acceptance,
handing an owned opportunity to Sales within the Market to Lead value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the internal team that routes and accepts
the qualified lead.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Sales Development (sales development representative)
  - Sales (account manager)

Pool "CRM System" — IT system that records lead assignment, ownership,
and acceptance.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Marketing Organisation (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. CRM System (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Sales Development lane:
  Message start event "Qualified lead received from Qualify Lead"
  User task "Review qualified lead record"
  User task "Determine routing rules and sales territory"
  Exclusive gateway "Existing account owner identified?"
  - branch "Yes — known account owner": Service task "Assign lead to
    existing account owner in CRM"
  - branch "No — no known owner": User task "Select account manager
    by territory or product line"
    Service task "Assign lead to selected account manager in CRM"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Existing account owner identified?"
  Send task "Notify account manager of lead assignment"
  Intermediate message catch event "Assignment acknowledgement received"
  User task "Confirm lead handover is complete"
  Service task "Update lead status to Handed Over in CRM"

Sales lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Lead assignment notification received"
  User task "Review lead details and context"
  Exclusive gateway "Lead accepted?"
  - branch "Yes — accepted": Service task "Convert lead to opportunity
    in CRM"
    User task "Confirm acceptance to Sales Development"
    Send task "Send acceptance confirmation"
    End event "Lead accepted and opportunity created — sales engagement
    begins"
  - branch "No — rejected or needs clarification": User task "Record
    reason for rejection or clarification request"
    Send task "Return rejection or query to Sales Development"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Lead accepted?"
    (rejoins Sales Development flow — see below)

  Returning from rejection or query in Sales Development lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Rejection or clarification received
  from Sales"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Lead Resolved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Review rejection reason or
    clarification query", User task "Amend lead record or gather
    additional information", Service task "Update lead record in CRM",
    Send task "Re-notify account manager of revised lead"
  Intermediate message catch event "Assignment acknowledgement received
  after revision"
  (flow rejoins at "Confirm lead handover is complete" above)

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Lead Resolved" — label "SLA deadline exceeded (lead follow-up SLA)" —
on trigger, flow continues to: User task "Escalate unresolved lead to
marketing manager", then End event "Lead escalated — resolution required
outside standard routing".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Sales Development lane at the message
start event and moves through lead review, territory determination, and
the routing gateway. The "Yes" branch assigns directly to an existing
owner; the "No" branch selects and then assigns. Both branches rejoin at
the exclusive merge gateway before the send task notifies the account
manager. Flow then pauses at the intermediate message catch event
awaiting acknowledgement, advances to confirm handover, and updates the
CRM. In the Sales lane, the notification catch event leads to lead
review and the acceptance gateway. The "Yes — accepted" branch converts
the lead, confirms acceptance, and ends. The "No — rejected" branch
records the reason and returns a message to Sales Development, where the
loop subprocess handles rework until resolved; after the revision
acknowledgement catch event the flow rejoins the handover confirmation
step. The timer boundary event on the loop subprocess exits to
escalation and a terminal end event.

Message flows:
Marketing Automation Platform (upstream) → Sales Development lane,
  message start event (qualified lead record)
Sales Development lane, Send task "Notify account manager of lead
  assignment" → Sales lane, intermediate message catch event
  (lead assignment notification)
Sales lane, Send task "Send acceptance confirmation" → Sales Development
  lane (acceptance confirmation)
Sales lane, Send task "Return rejection or query to Sales Development"
  → Sales Development lane, intermediate message catch event
  (rejection or clarification)
Sales Development lane, Send task "Re-notify account manager of revised
  lead" → Sales lane (revised lead notification)
Sales Development lane, Service task "Assign lead to existing account
  owner in CRM" → CRM System (lead assignment write)
Sales Development lane, Service task "Assign lead to selected account
  manager in CRM" → CRM System (lead assignment write)
Sales Development lane, Service task "Update lead status to Handed Over
  in CRM" → CRM System (status update)
Sales lane, Service task "Convert lead to opportunity in CRM"
  → CRM System (opportunity creation)
Sales lane, User task "Record reason for rejection or clarification
  request" → CRM System (rejection reason write)
Sales Development lane, Service task "Update lead record in CRM"
  (inside loop) → CRM System (amended lead record write)
CRM System → Sales Development lane, User task "Review qualified lead
  record" (existing lead and account context)
CRM System → Sales lane, User task "Review lead details and context"
  (full lead record and account history)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Qualified Lead Record" — read by "Review qualified lead
  record"; written by "Assign lead to existing account owner in CRM"
  and "Assign lead to selected account manager in CRM".
Data Object "Routing Decision" — written by "Determine routing rules
  and sales territory"; read by the exclusive gateway "Existing account
  owner identified?".
Data Object "Lead Assignment Notification" — written by "Notify account
  manager of lead assignment"; read by "Review lead details and context".
Data Object "Rejection or Clarification Note" — written by "Record
  reason for rejection or clarification request"; read by "Review
  rejection reason or clarification query".

V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales takes a scored and qualified lead
from Sales Development and ensures it reaches the correct account manager
with full context, a formal acceptance, and an open opportunity record in
the CRM. It enforces the Marketing-to-Sales SLA by looping through
rework when a lead is initially rejected or needs clarification, and
escalating if the SLA deadline is breached. On successful completion it
hands an accepted, CRM-recorded opportunity to Sales, from which active
sales engagement begins.
```

```text
BPMN: V10.10 Nurture Unqualified Response — keeps unqualified responses

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Prospect" — the individual or organisation receiving nurture

Pool "Marketing Automation Platform" — the system that executes automated

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospect" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Marketing Automation Platform" — black-box, System = true,

3. Layout

Top to bottom:

2. Marketing Organisation
3. Marketing Automation Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Marketing lane (campaign manager):

  Message start event "Unqualified response received from Qualify Lead"
  User task "Review unqualified response and select nurture track"
  User task "Configure nurture sequence for selected track"
  Service task "Enrol contact in nurture sequence"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Re-qualified or Withdrawn" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    Service task "Deliver nurture content asset to prospect",
    Intermediate message catch event "Engagement signal received",
    User task "Review engagement and re-score contact",
    Exclusive gateway "Re-qualification threshold met?"
    - branch "Yes — threshold met": proceed to merge
    - branch "No — continue nurturing": return to next loop iteration
    Exclusive merge gateway "Re-qualification threshold met"
  Exclusive gateway "Outcome of nurture?"
  - branch "Re-qualified": Send task "Notify Sales Development of
      re-qualified lead"
  - branch "Permanently unresponsive — withdraw": User task "Mark contact
      as inactive and suppress from active nurturing",
      End event "Contact suppressed — nurture closed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Outcome of nurture"
  End event "Re-qualified lead handed to Route Qualified Lead to Sales"

Marketing Operations lane (marketing operations analyst):

  User task "Confirm contact consent and suppression status"
  User task "Monitor nurture sequence delivery and engagement metrics"
  User task "Update response record with nurture outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Re-qualified or Withdrawn", label "Maximum nurture duration elapsed",
  leading to User task "Mark contact as inactive and suppress from active
  nurturing" in the Marketing lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Marketing lane with the message start
event, passes to "Review unqualified response and select nurture track",
then to "Configure nurture sequence for selected track". Before enrolment,
flow crosses to the Marketing Operations lane for "Confirm contact consent
and suppression status", then returns to the Marketing lane for "Enrol
contact in nurture sequence". The nurture loop subprocess follows; on
completion the "Outcome of nurture?" gateway splits into the re-qualified
branch, which passes through "Notify Sales Development of re-qualified lead"
and merges at "Outcome of nurture" before reaching the re-qualified end
event, and the withdraw branch, which passes through "Mark contact as
inactive and suppress from active nurturing" to its own end event and does
not rejoin. During the loop the Marketing Operations lane handles "Monitor
nurture sequence delivery and engagement metrics" in parallel, and "Update
response record with nurture outcome" fires after the merge gateway. The
timer boundary event on the subprocess routes directly to "Mark contact as
inactive and suppress from active nurturing".

Message flows:
Marketing Automation Platform → Prospect (nurture content assets and
  campaign messages delivered per sequence schedule).
Prospect → Marketing Automation Platform (engagement signals: opens, clicks,
  page visits, unsubscribe actions).
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Organisation (engagement metrics
  and delivery status returned to Marketing Operations lane).
Marketing Organisation → Marketing Automation Platform (nurture sequence
  configuration and contact enrolment instructions sent from Marketing lane).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Unqualified Response Record" — read by "Review unqualified
  response and select nurture track"; written by "Update response record
  with nurture outcome".
Data Object "Nurture Track Configuration" — written by "Configure nurture
  sequence for selected track"; read by "Enrol contact in nurture sequence".
Data Object "Consent and Suppression Record" — read by "Confirm contact
  consent and suppression status".
Data Object "Engagement Signal Log" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Engagement signal received"; read by "Review engagement and
  re-score contact".
Data Object "Re-qualification Notification" — written by "Notify Sales
  Development of re-qualified lead".

This subprocess keeps unqualified responses warm through structured,
consent-compliant nurture sequences, re-scoring contacts as engagement
signals arrive. Contacts that cross the re-qualification threshold are
handed to Route Qualified Lead to Sales; contacts that remain unresponsive
beyond the maximum nurture window are suppressed and the record closed.
```

## V11 — Sign to Onboard

**Teams and roles involved.**
Sign to Onboard usually involves Sales, Customer Success, Onboarding/Implementation, Service Delivery, Finance/Billing, IT or Provisioning, Legal or Contracts, and Support. Key roles include account manager, onboarding manager, implementation consultant, solution architect, data migration specialist, trainer, billing officer, provisioning engineer, and customer success manager.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the New Customer, represented by a sponsor, project contact and end users. The process is initiated when a contract is signed or an order for a new service is accepted. Other external parties include the customer's own IT provider, third-party implementation partners, integration vendors, and sometimes regulators where the service is licensed.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: accept signed contract, confirm scope and entitlements, assign the onboarding team, run kick-off, collect customer requirements and data, configure and provision the service, migrate data, test and validate with the customer, train users, obtain go-live acceptance, activate billing, and hand over to business as usual.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include CRM, contract lifecycle management, project or onboarding management tooling, provisioning and identity systems, the product or service platform itself, data migration tooling, billing and subscription management, knowledge base and learning management, and customer support/ticketing.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include contract acceptance and handover procedure, entitlement and scope-change rules, customer data handling and privacy policy, migration and cut-over procedure, acceptance and sign-off criteria, training standards, billing activation rules, and escalation paths where onboarding is delayed.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides contacts and authorised signatories, configuration requirements, existing data for migration, environment and access details, testing feedback, and formal acceptance. The process provides the customer with an onboarding plan and schedule, configuration and readiness updates, migration reports, training materials and sessions, go-live confirmation, and the first invoice and support arrangements.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates customer accounts, entitlements and licences, provisioned environments, user identities and roles, migrated records, onboarding tasks and milestones, and billing schedules. IT systems provide contract and order terms, provisioning status, migration validation results, usage and readiness telemetry, and support-case history.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Service Provider" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are
the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V11.01** Accept Signed Contract | New Customer | Sales (account manager), Legal / Contracts (contracts administrator) | Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) |
| **V11.02** Confirm Scope & Entitlements | New Customer | Onboarding (onboarding manager), Sales (account manager) | CRM System |
| **V11.03** Assign Onboarding Team | — | Onboarding (onboarding manager), Service Delivery (implementation consultant) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.04** Run Kick-off | New Customer | Onboarding (onboarding manager), Service Delivery (solution architect) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.05** Collect Requirements & Data | New Customer | Service Delivery (implementation consultant) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.06** Configure & Provision Service | — | Service Delivery (implementation consultant), IT / Provisioning (provisioning engineer) | Provisioning & Identity System, Product Platform |
| **V11.07** Migrate Data | New Customer, Implementation Partner | Service Delivery (data migration specialist) | Data Migration Tooling, Product Platform |
| **V11.08** Test & Validate with Customer | New Customer | Service Delivery (implementation consultant), Onboarding (onboarding manager) | Product Platform |
| **V11.09** Train Users | New Customer | Onboarding (trainer) | Learning Management System (LMS) |
| **V11.10** Obtain Go-Live Acceptance | New Customer | Onboarding (onboarding manager) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.11** Activate Billing | New Customer | Finance / Billing (billing officer) | Billing & Subscription System |
| **V11.12** Hand Over to Business as Usual | New Customer | Customer Success (customer success manager), Support (support lead) | CRM System, Support / Ticketing System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V11):

- **External actors:** New Customer (V11.01, V11.02, V11.04, V11.05, V11.07–V11.12); Implementation Partner (V11.07).
- **Teams:** Sales (V11.01, V11.02); Legal / Contracts (V11.01); Onboarding (V11.02–V11.05, V11.08–V11.10); Service Delivery (V11.03–V11.08); IT / Provisioning (V11.06); Finance / Billing (V11.11); Customer Success (V11.12); Support (V11.12).
- **IT systems:** Contract Lifecycle Management / CLM (V11.01); CRM System (V11.02, V11.12); Onboarding / Project Management System (V11.03–V11.05, V11.10); Provisioning & Identity System (V11.06); Product Platform (V11.06–V11.08); Data Migration Tooling (V11.07); Learning Management System / LMS (V11.09); Billing & Subscription System (V11.11); Support / Ticketing System (V11.12).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V11 — Sign to Onboard — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Sign to Onboard value chain, from contract acceptance through to handover
to business as usual. The diagram is arranged in three horizontal bands, read
top-to-bottom as service realisation: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) →
BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) → APPLICATIONS (bottom band). The demand-
side actor (New Customer) sits on the far left; delivery and settlement actors
(Implementation Partner) sit on the far right. Each band reads left to right
in the order the customer encounters the services.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- New Customer: demand-side actor, placed on the far left, present across
  contract acceptance, kick-off, requirements gathering, migration, testing,
  training, go-live, billing, and handover.
- Implementation Partner: delivery-side actor, placed on the far right,
  engaged during data migration.

2. Interfaces

- Contract Submission Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Contract
  Acceptance Service; serves V11.01.
- Scope Confirmation Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Scope and
  Entitlements Service; serves V11.02.
- Kick-off Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Onboarding
  Engagement Service; serves V11.04.
- Requirements Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Requirements
  Collection Service; serves V11.05.
- Migration Collaboration Interface: used by New Customer and Implementation
  Partner to ACCESS the Data Migration Service; serves V11.07.
- Testing Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Test and Validation
  Service; serves V11.08.
- Training Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the User Training
  Service; serves V11.09.
- Acceptance Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Go-Live Acceptance
  Service; serves V11.10.
- Billing Notification Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Billing
  Activation Service; serves V11.11.
- Handover Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Business-as-Usual
  Handover Service; serves V11.12.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Contract Acceptance Service: receives and validates the signed contract or
  accepted order from the customer.
- Scope and Entitlements Service: confirms agreed scope, licences, and
  entitlements with the customer.
- Onboarding Team Assignment Service: assigns the dedicated onboarding and
  implementation team.
- Onboarding Engagement Service: delivers the kick-off meeting and onboarding
  plan to the customer.
- Requirements Collection Service: gathers customer configuration requirements
  and existing data.
- Configuration and Provisioning Service: configures and provisions the
  product environment and user identities.
- Data Migration Service: migrates customer data into the provisioned
  environment.
- Test and Validation Service: supports joint testing and validation of the
  provisioned service.
- User Training Service: delivers training to customer end users.
- Go-Live Acceptance Service: obtains formal customer sign-off to proceed to
  live.
- Billing Activation Service: activates billing and issues the first invoice.
- Business-as-Usual Handover Service: transitions the customer to ongoing
  support and customer success.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V11.01 Accept Signed Contract: receives the executed contract, logs it, and
  triggers the onboarding workflow.
- V11.02 Confirm Scope & Entitlements: reconciles order terms, entitlements,
  and licences against the contract.
- V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team: selects and assigns onboarding manager,
  implementation consultant, and solution architect.
- V11.04 Run Kick-off: conducts the kick-off meeting, shares the onboarding
  plan, and aligns stakeholders.
- V11.05 Collect Requirements & Data: elicits configuration requirements,
  environment details, and data for migration.
- V11.06 Configure & Provision Service: provisions environments, configures
  the product platform, and creates user identities.
- V11.07 Migrate Data: extracts, transforms, loads, and validates customer
  data in the product platform.
- V11.08 Test & Validate with Customer: runs structured testing cycles with
  the customer and resolves issues.
- V11.09 Train Users: delivers product training to customer end users using
  learning materials.
- V11.10 Obtain Go-Live Acceptance: collects formal acceptance sign-off and
  records the go-live decision.
- V11.11 Activate Billing: sets up billing schedules and subscription records
  and issues the first invoice.
- V11.12 Hand Over to Business as Usual: completes onboarding, transfers the
  account to customer success, and opens support arrangements.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band, left to right

- Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM): manages contract storage, status, and
  handover; used in V11.01.
- CRM System: holds customer account, contact, and entitlement records; used
  in V11.02 and V11.12.
- Onboarding / Project Management System: tracks onboarding tasks, milestones,
  team assignments, and schedules; used in V11.03, V11.04, V11.05, V11.10.
- Provisioning & Identity System: provisions environments and manages user
  identities and roles; used in V11.06.
- Product Platform: the live service platform used across provisioning,
  migration, and testing; used in V11.06, V11.07, V11.08.
- Data Migration Tooling: extracts, transforms, and loads customer data into
  the product platform; used in V11.07.
- Learning Management System (LMS): hosts training content and delivers user
  training sessions; used in V11.09.
- Billing & Subscription System: manages billing schedules, subscription
  records, and invoice generation; used in V11.11.
- Support / Ticketing System: manages support cases and customer-facing support
  arrangements post-handover; used in V11.12.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process):
- Contract Lifecycle Management SERVES V11.01 Accept Signed Contract.
- CRM System SERVES V11.02 Confirm Scope & Entitlements.
- Onboarding / Project Management System SERVES V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team.
- Onboarding / Project Management System SERVES V11.04 Run Kick-off.
- Onboarding / Project Management System SERVES V11.05 Collect Requirements
  & Data.
- Provisioning & Identity System SERVES V11.06 Configure & Provision Service.
- Product Platform SERVES V11.06 Configure & Provision Service.
- Data Migration Tooling SERVES V11.07 Migrate Data.
- Product Platform SERVES V11.07 Migrate Data.
- Product Platform SERVES V11.08 Test & Validate with Customer.
- Learning Management System SERVES V11.09 Train Users.
- Onboarding / Project Management System SERVES V11.10 Obtain Go-Live
  Acceptance.
- Billing & Subscription System SERVES V11.11 Activate Billing.
- CRM System SERVES V11.12 Hand Over to Business as Usual.
- Support / Ticketing System SERVES V11.12 Hand Over to Business as Usual.

SERVING (business service SERVES business actor):
- Contract Acceptance Service SERVES New Customer.
- Scope and Entitlements Service SERVES New Customer.
- Onboarding Engagement Service SERVES New Customer.
- Requirements Collection Service SERVES New Customer.
- Data Migration Service SERVES New Customer.
- Data Migration Service SERVES Implementation Partner.
- Test and Validation Service SERVES New Customer.
- User Training Service SERVES New Customer.
- Go-Live Acceptance Service SERVES New Customer.
- Billing Activation Service SERVES New Customer.
- Business-as-Usual Handover Service SERVES New Customer.

REALISATION (business process REALISES business service):
- V11.01 Accept Signed Contract REALISES Contract Acceptance Service.
- V11.02 Confirm Scope & Entitlements REALISES Scope and Entitlements Service.
- V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team REALISES Onboarding Team Assignment Service.

- V11.10 Obtain Go-Live Acceptance REALISES Go-Live Acceptance Service.
- V11.11 Activate Billing REALISES Billing Activation Service.
- V11.12 Hand Over to Business as Usual REALISES Business-as-Usual Handover
  Service.

ACCESS (business actor ACCESSES interface):
- New Customer ACCESSES Contract Submission Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Scope Confirmation Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Kick-off Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Requirements Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Migration Collaboration Interface.
- Implementation Partner ACCESSES Migration Collaboration Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Testing Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Training Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Acceptance Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Billing Notification Interface.
- New Customer ACCESSES Handover Interface.

ASSIGNMENT (interface ASSIGNED TO business service):

- Scope Confirmation Interface ASSIGNED TO Scope and Entitlements Service.

- Billing Notification Interface ASSIGNED TO Billing Activation Service.
```

```text
chain, from initial contract acceptance through scoping, team assignment,
kick-off, requirements gathering, provisioning, data migration, testing,
training, and go-live acceptance, to billing activation and handover to
business as usual. It serves the New Customer and Implementation Partner
externally, and is operated by Sales, Legal / Contracts, Onboarding, Service
Delivery, IT / Provisioning, Finance / Billing, Customer Success, and Support
internally, with nine supporting IT systems spanning contract management,
CRM, project tracking, provisioning, the product platform, migration tooling,
learning management, billing, and support ticketing.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V11 - Sign to Onboard

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of twelve high-level process stages,
one chevron per stage, in the order listed below. Each chevron carries only
its stage code and name. No swimlanes, no system icons, no data flows — this
is the top-level chain overview only.

V11.01. Accept Signed Contract
V11.02. Confirm Scope & Entitlements
V11.03. Assign Onboarding Team
V11.04. Run Kick-off
V11.05. Collect Requirements & Data
V11.06. Configure & Provision Service

V11.09. Train Users
V11.10. Obtain Go-Live Acceptance
V11.11. Activate Billing
V11.12. Hand Over to Business as Usual

This chain carries a new customer from the moment a signed contract or accepted
order is received through every step needed to make the service live and fully
supported. The main external participant is the New Customer, whose act of
signing or placing an order triggers V11.01. The chain ends when the customer
has formally accepted go-live, billing has been activated, and ongoing
responsibility has been handed to Customer Success and Support under business
as usual.
```
