### V11.01 — Accept Signed Contract

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.01 Accept Signed Contract — first subprocess in the Sign to
Onboard value chain, triggered when a new customer delivers a signed
contract or accepted order to the service provider.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation receiving and processing the
signed contract, with lanes for Sales and Legal / Contracts.
Pool "New Customer" — the external party submitting the signed contract.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — the IT system in which the
contract is recorded and stored.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Sales lane:
  Message start event "Signed contract received from New Customer"
  User task "Log contract receipt and assign reference number"
  User task "Review contract for completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract complete?"
  - branch "Incomplete": Send task "Request missing information from
    customer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Missing information received from
    New Customer"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Contract complete?"
  - branch "Complete": continue to next task
  User task "Confirm customer identity and authorised signatories"
  Exclusive gateway "Signatories verified?"
  - branch "Not verified": Send task "Request signatory clarification
    from customer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Signatory clarification received
    from New Customer"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Signatories verified?"
  - branch "Verified": continue to next task
  User task "Hand over contract package to Legal / Contracts"

Legal / Contracts lane:
  User task "Conduct formal contract acceptance review"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract accepted?"
  - branch "Rejected": User task "Notify Sales of rejection and record
    reason"
    Send task "Notify New Customer of rejection"
    End event "Contract rejected — process ends"
  - branch "Accepted": continue to next task
  Service task "Record accepted contract in CLM"
  User task "Confirm entitlements, term dates and commercial terms"
  User task "Prepare contract acceptance confirmation document"
  Send task "Issue acceptance confirmation to New Customer"
  End event "Contract accepted — ready for Confirm Scope and Entitlements"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review contract for
completeness" — label "Review overdue (2 business days)" — triggers
escalation to onboarding manager to chase completion.
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Missing information received from New Customer" — label "No response
within 5 business days" — triggers Send task "Escalate missing
information to account manager" then End event "Contract stalled —
escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Sales lane, passes through the
completeness gateway (incomplete branch loops through the message catch
event and rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway before continuing;
complete branch proceeds directly to signatory verification, which
similarly loops through its own message catch event and merge gateway
before reaching handover), then crosses to the Legal / Contracts lane
for formal acceptance review; the rejected branch ends at its own end
event; the accepted branch continues through CLM recording and
confirmation steps to the process end event.

Message flows:
New Customer → Sales lane (signed contract document submitted to trigger
start event)
Sales lane → New Customer (request for missing information)
New Customer → Sales lane (missing information response)
Sales lane → New Customer (request for signatory clarification)
New Customer → Sales lane (signatory clarification response)
Legal / Contracts lane → Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) (accepted
contract record written via service task)
Legal / Contracts lane → New Customer (rejection notification)
Legal / Contracts lane → New Customer (acceptance confirmation document)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Signed Contract" — read by User task "Review contract for
completeness"; read by User task "Conduct formal contract acceptance
review".
Data Object "Missing Information Request" — written by Send task
"Request missing information from customer"; read by Intermediate message
catch event "Missing information received from New Customer".
Data Object "Signatory Clarification Request" — written by Send task
"Request signatory clarification from customer"; read by Intermediate
message catch event "Signatory clarification received from New Customer".
Data Object "Contract Acceptance Confirmation" — written by User task
"Prepare contract acceptance confirmation document"; read by Send task
"Issue acceptance confirmation to New Customer".
task "Record accepted contract in CLM".

This subprocess captures the signed contract from the new customer,
verifies its completeness and the authority of its signatories, performs
a formal legal acceptance review, and records the accepted contract in
the CLM system. It hands a confirmed, fully recorded contract with
verified commercial terms and entitlements to the next subprocess,
Confirm Scope and Entitlements.
```


### V11.02 — Confirm Scope & Entitlements

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.02 Confirm Scope & Entitlements — second subprocess in the Sign
to Onboard value chain, confirming the contracted scope and customer
entitlements before the onboarding team is assigned.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation delivering the onboarding process,
  containing all internal work lanes.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Onboarding (onboarding manager)
  - Sales (account manager)
Pool "New Customer" — the customer sponsor or project contact who reviews and
  confirms scope.
Pool "CRM System" — the customer relationship management platform that stores
  account and entitlement records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. CRM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane:
  Message start event "Accepted contract received from Accept Signed Contract"
  User task "Retrieve contract and order terms"
  Service task "Pull customer account record from CRM"
  User task "Review contracted scope and service entitlements"
  User task "Draft scope and entitlements summary"
  Send task "Send scope summary to customer for review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Scope confirmed by customer?"
  - branch "Yes — confirmed": Exclusive merge gateway
      "Scope confirmed by customer?"
  - branch "No — amendments requested":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Scope Agreed" (standard loop)
        containing, in order:
        User task "Log requested amendments",
        User task "Assess amendment against contract terms",
        Exclusive gateway "Amendment within contracted scope?"
        - branch "Within scope": User task "Update scope and entitlements
            summary", sequence continues to loop exit
        - branch "Out of scope": User task "Escalate to Sales for scope
            change decision", Intermediate message catch event
            "Sales decision received",
            User task "Update scope and entitlements summary",
            sequence continues to loop exit
        Exclusive merge gateway "Amendment within contracted scope?",
        Send task "Resend revised scope summary to customer",
        Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Scope confirmed by customer?"
  User task "Record confirmed entitlements in CRM"
  User task "Finalise and publish onboarding scope baseline"
  End event "Scope and entitlements confirmed — ready for Assign
      Onboarding Team"

Sales lane:
  User task "Provide contract clarification if requested"
  User task "Approve or reject out-of-scope amendment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Scope
  Agreed" — label "Scope alignment overdue (5 business days)" — triggers
  User task "Escalate unresolved scope dispute to senior onboarding
  management" in Onboarding lane, ending in an Error end event
  "Scope not confirmed — escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Onboarding lane at the message start event
and moves through retrieval, review, and drafting tasks before the send task
passes the summary to the customer. On a positive response the exclusive
gateway routes to record and finalise tasks and then to the end event. On a
negative response the flow enters the loop subprocess, where an inner gateway
routes within-scope amendments directly to update and loop exit, and
out-of-scope amendments to the Sales lane tasks before returning; the loop
exits when the customer confirms, merging back at the outer exclusive merge
gateway before the record and finalise tasks. The timer boundary event exits
the subprocess to the escalation task and error end event without rejoining
the main flow.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Send task "Send scope summary to customer for review")
    → New Customer (scope and entitlements summary for review)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer response received") (scope confirmation or amendment
    requests)
  Service Provider (Send task "Resend revised scope summary to customer")
    → New Customer (revised scope and entitlements summary)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer response received" inside loop) (revised confirmation or
    further amendments)
  Service Provider (Service task "Pull customer account record from CRM")
    → CRM System (account record request)
  CRM System → Service Provider (Service task "Pull customer account
    record from CRM") (customer account and order terms)
  Service Provider (User task "Record confirmed entitlements in CRM")
    → CRM System (confirmed entitlements and scope baseline)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Contract and Order Terms" — read by User task "Retrieve
  contract and order terms".
Data Object "Scope and Entitlements Summary" — written by User task "Draft
  scope and entitlements summary"; read by Send task "Send scope summary
  to customer for review"; written by User task "Update scope and
  entitlements summary"; read by Send task "Resend revised scope summary
  to customer".
Data Object "Customer Amendment Request" — written by User task "Log
  requested amendments"; read by User task "Assess amendment against
  contract terms".

This subprocess takes the accepted contract handed over from Accept Signed
Contract and reaches a customer-confirmed, CRM-recorded baseline of scope
and entitlements. It resolves any misalignment between what was sold and
what will be delivered — including escalating out-of-scope requests to
Sales — so that the Assign Onboarding Team subprocess receives a clean,
agreed scope baseline against which the team, plan, and resources can be
matched.
```


### V11.03 — Assign Onboarding Team

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team — internal resourcing subprocess that
allocates an onboarding team following scope confirmation in the Sign to
Onboard value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
  with lanes for Onboarding and Service Delivery.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — project and task management
  tooling used to record and publish the team assignment.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top: Service Provider (white-box, two lanes top to bottom: Onboarding,
  Service Delivery).
Bottom: Onboarding / Project Management System (black-box).

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane:
  Message start event "Confirmed scope and entitlements received from
    Confirm Scope & Entitlements"
  User task "Review confirmed scope and resource requirements"
  User task "Identify onboarding manager for engagement"
  User task "Check team availability and workload"
  Exclusive gateway "Suitable resources available?"
    - branch "Yes": proceed to Exclusive merge gateway
        "Suitable resources available"
    - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Resources Secured"
        (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Escalate resource
        gap to Onboarding lead", Intermediate message catch event
        "Capacity or resource decision received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Suitable resources available"
  User task "Formally assign onboarding manager to project"
  User task "Confirm team roster and notify assigned members"
  Send task "Publish team assignment to project record"

Service Delivery lane:
  User task "Nominate implementation consultant for engagement"
  User task "Confirm implementation consultant availability"
  User task "Record implementation consultant assignment"
  End event "Onboarding team assigned — ready for Run Kick-off"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Resources Secured", label "48-hour escalation deadline exceeded", leading
  to End event "Resource assignment failed — escalation required".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Onboarding lane with the message start
  event, passes through scope review, manager identification, and
  availability check, then through the exclusive gateway; the "No" branch
  enters the loop subprocess and rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway;
  both branches merge there and continue to formal assignment, roster
  confirmation, and the send task. Control then passes to the Service
  Delivery lane for consultant nomination, availability confirmation, and
  assignment recording, ending at the end event.

Message flows:
  Onboarding lane "Publish team assignment to project record" →
    Onboarding / Project Management System (team roster and role
    assignments).
  Onboarding / Project Management System → Onboarding lane "Review
    confirmed scope and resource requirements" (confirmed scope record and
    entitlements summary).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Confirmed Scope Record" — read by "Review confirmed scope and
  resource requirements".
Data Object "Resource Availability Report" — read by "Check team
  availability and workload"; written by "Confirm implementation consultant
  availability".
Data Object "Team Assignment Record" — written by "Formally assign
  onboarding manager to project"; written by "Record implementation
  consultant assignment"; read by "Publish team assignment to project
  record".

V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team takes the confirmed scope and entitlements
from V11.02 and uses them to identify, check availability of, and formally
allocate an onboarding manager and an implementation consultant to the
engagement. A loop with a 48-hour escalation boundary handles cases where
suitable resources are not immediately available. The subprocess closes by
publishing the completed team roster to the Onboarding / Project Management
System, handing a named, committed team to V11.04 Run Kick-off.
```


### V11.04 — Run Kick-off

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.04 Run Kick-off — fourth subprocess in the Sign to Onboard
value chain, where the assigned onboarding team formally opens the
engagement with the new customer, confirms the onboarding plan and
schedule, and sets expectations for all parties before requirements
collection begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation delivering the onboarding,
  containing the Onboarding and Service Delivery lanes.
Pool "New Customer" — the customer's sponsor, project contact and
  attendees participating in the kick-off.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — tooling used to
  record milestones, distribute the onboarding plan, and log kick-off
  outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box,
  System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Onboarding / Project Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane (onboarding manager):

  Message start event "Onboarding team assignment confirmed — ready
    from Assign Onboarding Team"
  User task "Prepare kick-off agenda and onboarding plan"
  Send task "Send kick-off invitation and agenda to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms kick-off
    attendance"
  User task "Facilitate kick-off meeting"
  User task "Present onboarding plan, schedule and milestones"
  User task "Agree communication cadence and escalation path"
  Exclusive gateway "All agenda items resolved?"
  - branch "Yes — all items resolved": continue to Service Delivery
    lane handoff
  - branch "No — open items remain": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
    Until All Items Resolved" (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Record open item", User task "Assign owner and target
    resolution date", User task "Circulate updated action log to
    customer"; Intermediate timer catch event "Resolution deadline
    reached"; Exclusive merge gateway "All agenda items resolved?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "All agenda items resolved?"
  User task "Confirm kick-off minutes and distribute to all parties"
  Service task "Record kick-off completion in project system"
  End event "Kick-off complete — ready for Collect Requirements
    & Data"

Service Delivery lane (solution architect):

  User task "Present solution architecture and technical scope"
  User task "Confirm integration and environment prerequisites"
  User task "Log technical prerequisites and assumptions"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until All Items Resolved" — label "Escalation deadline exceeded";
  triggers Send task "Escalate unresolved items to onboarding manager
  and customer sponsor", which ends in a local escalation End event
  (does not rejoin the main flow).

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Onboarding lane with the message
  start event and proceeds through agenda preparation, invitation
  dispatch, and the attendance confirmation catch event to the
  kick-off meeting. During the meeting the solution architect's tasks
  in the Service Delivery lane run in parallel via a parallel split,
  rejoining the Onboarding lane at "Agree communication cadence and
  escalation path". The exclusive gateway then either passes resolved
  items straight to the merge or routes through the standard-loop
  subprocess; both branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway
  before proceeding to minutes confirmation, system recording, and
  the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Send task "Send kick-off invitation and agenda
    to customer") → New Customer (kick-off invitation and agenda).
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer confirms kick-off attendance") (attendance
    confirmation).
  Service Provider (User task "Facilitate kick-off meeting") ↔
    New Customer (kick-off meeting dialogue).
  Service Provider (User task "Circulate updated action log to
    customer") → New Customer (action log update).
  Service Provider (User task "Confirm kick-off minutes and
    distribute to all parties") → New Customer (kick-off minutes).
  Service Provider (Service task "Record kick-off completion in
    project system") → Onboarding / Project Management System
    (kick-off completion record and milestone update).
  Onboarding / Project Management System → Service Provider
    (User task "Prepare kick-off agenda and onboarding plan")
    (onboarding plan template and existing milestone data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Kick-off Agenda" — written by User task "Prepare
  kick-off agenda and onboarding plan"; read by Send task "Send
  kick-off invitation and agenda to customer".
Data Object "Onboarding Plan and Schedule" — written by User task
  "Prepare kick-off agenda and onboarding plan"; read by User task
  "Present onboarding plan, schedule and milestones"; read by User
  task "Confirm kick-off minutes and distribute to all parties".
Data Object "Action Log" — written by User task "Record open item";
  written by User task "Assign owner and target resolution date";
  read by User task "Circulate updated action log to customer".
Data Object "Technical Prerequisites and Assumptions" — written by
  User task "Log technical prerequisites and assumptions"; read by
  User task "Confirm kick-off minutes and distribute to all parties".
Data Object "Kick-off Minutes" — written by User task "Confirm
  kick-off minutes and distribute to all parties"; read by Service
  task "Record kick-off completion in project system".

V11.04 Run Kick-off brings the onboarding team and the new customer
together for the first formal engagement, aligning both sides on the
onboarding plan, schedule, technical prerequisites, and communication
arrangements. Any items left unresolved during the meeting are tracked
and owned before the session is closed. The subprocess hands a
completed kick-off record, agreed plan, and confirmed prerequisites
to V11.05 Collect Requirements & Data, where the implementation
consultant begins gathering the detailed customer requirements and
data needed to configure the service.
```


### V11.05 — Collect Requirements & Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.05 Collect Requirements & Data — fifth subprocess in the
Sign to Onboard value chain, gathering detailed customer requirements and
data after the kick-off to prepare for configuration and provisioning.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
with lanes for the team involved.
  Lane "Service Delivery (Implementation Consultant)" — captures and
  validates all requirements and data supplied by the customer.
  Lane "Onboarding (Onboarding Manager)" — oversees completeness, chases
  outstanding items, and approves the finalised requirements package.

Pool "New Customer" — the customer organisation providing configuration
requirements, existing data, and environment and access details.

Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — tooling used to log
requirements, track outstanding items, and store the completed package.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Onboarding / Project Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Service Delivery (Implementation Consultant) lane:
  Message start event "Requirements and data request received from
  Run Kick-off"
  User task "Prepare requirements questionnaire and data templates"
  Send task "Issue questionnaire and templates to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer returns completed
  questionnaire and data"
  User task "Review submitted requirements and data for completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Submission complete?"
  - branch "Incomplete — items outstanding":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Submission Complete"
      (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Log outstanding
      items in project system", Send task "Request missing information
      from customer", Intermediate message catch event "Customer provides
      additional information", User task "Re-review submission for
      completeness"
  - branch "Complete — all items received":
      continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Submission complete"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Submission complete"
  User task "Validate data formats and environment access details"
  Exclusive gateway "Validation passed?"
  - branch "Validation issues found":
      Send task "Notify customer of data or access issues"
      Intermediate message catch event "Customer resolves issues and
      resubmits"
      continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed"
  - branch "Validation passed":
      continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed"
  Service task "Record validated requirements in project system"
  User task "Compile finalised requirements and data package"

Onboarding (Onboarding Manager) lane:
  User task "Review and approve finalised requirements package"
  Exclusive gateway "Package approved?"
  - branch "Approved":
      continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Package approved"
  - branch "Revisions required":
      User task "Return package to implementation consultant with notes"
      continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Package approved"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Package approved"
  End event "Requirements and data package approved — ready for
  Configure and Provision Service"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Submission Complete" — label "Submission overdue (defined chase limit
reached)" — triggers escalation task in Onboarding Manager lane:
User task "Escalate outstanding submission to customer sponsor", then
flows to an Error end event "Submission not received — onboarding
stalled".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Service Delivery lane at the message
start event, proceeds through questionnaire preparation and issuance,
then waits for the customer response. On return, the completeness gateway
branches to the loop subprocess for incomplete submissions or straight to
the merge for complete ones; both branches rejoin at the "Submission
complete" merge gateway. After data validation the validation gateway
branches to notify-and-wait for issues or passes through directly; both
rejoin at the "Validation passed" merge. Flow continues through recording
and compiling the package, then crosses into the Onboarding Manager lane
for approval. The approval gateway branches to direct approval or a
revision loop returning the package to the implementation consultant;
both branches rejoin at the "Package approved" merge gateway before
reaching the end event.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider / Service Delivery lane (completed
questionnaire and requirements data)
New Customer → Service Provider / Service Delivery lane (additional
information supplied during chase loop)
New Customer → Service Provider / Service Delivery lane (resubmitted
data after issue resolution)
Service Provider / Service Delivery lane → New Customer (requirements
questionnaire and data templates)
Service Provider / Service Delivery lane → New Customer (request for
missing information)
Service Provider / Service Delivery lane → New Customer (notification
of data or access issues)
Service Provider / Service Delivery lane → Onboarding / Project
Management System (validated requirements recorded)
Onboarding / Project Management System → Service Provider / Service
Delivery lane (confirmation of record saved and outstanding-item log)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Requirements Questionnaire and Data Templates" — written by
User task "Prepare requirements questionnaire and data templates"; read
by Send task "Issue questionnaire and templates to customer".

Data Object "Customer Submission" — written by Intermediate message catch
event "Customer returns completed questionnaire and data"; read by User
task "Review submitted requirements and data for completeness".

Data Object "Outstanding Items Log" — written by User task "Log
outstanding items in project system"; read by Send task "Request missing
information from customer".

Data Object "Validated Requirements and Data Package" — written by User
task "Compile finalised requirements and data package"; read by User task
"Review and approve finalised requirements package".

Service task "Record validated requirements in project system"; read by
User task "Review and approve finalised requirements package".

This subprocess gathers, chases, and validates all configuration
requirements, existing customer data, and environment access details
submitted by the customer following the kick-off. It applies a structured
loop to resolve incomplete or invalid submissions and concludes with
onboarding manager approval of a consolidated requirements and data
package. That approved package is handed to Configure and Provision
Service, where it drives the build-out of the customer's environment.
```


### V11.06 — Configure & Provision Service

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.06 Configure & Provision Service — the sixth subprocess in the
Sign to Onboard value chain, translating confirmed requirements into a fully
provisioned and configured service environment ready for data migration.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the configuration and
provisioning process, containing Service Delivery and IT / Provisioning lanes.
Pool "Provisioning & Identity System" — identity and environment provisioning
platform.
Pool "Product Platform" — the product or service platform being configured
and provisioned for the customer.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Provisioning & Identity System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Product Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Service Provider
2. Provisioning & Identity System
3. Product Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Service Delivery lane:
  Start event "Requirements and data collected — received from Collect
    Requirements and Data"
  User task "Review confirmed requirements and configuration specification"
  User task "Define environment and access design"
  Send task "Submit provisioning request to Provisioning and Identity System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Provisioning confirmation received"
  User task "Apply service configuration to Product Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Configuration acknowledgement received
    from Product Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Configuration accepted?"
  - branch "No — errors returned":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Configuration Accepted" (standard
        loop) containing, in order: User task "Review configuration errors",
        User task "Correct and resubmit configuration to Product Platform",
        Intermediate message catch event "Configuration re-check result
          received"
      Timer boundary event on subprocess "48-hour correction deadline"
        — interrupting — if deadline expires, flow continues to Error end
        event "Configuration deadline exceeded — escalate to IT / Provisioning"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Configuration accepted"
  - branch "Yes — accepted":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Configuration accepted"
  User task "Verify user identities and roles in Provisioning and Identity
    System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Identity verification result received"
  Exclusive gateway "Identities verified?"
  - branch "No — identity issues":
      User task "Resolve identity and access issues"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Identities verified"
  - branch "Yes — all verified":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Identities verified"
  User task "Conduct internal readiness check on configured environment"
  Exclusive gateway "Readiness check passed?"
  - branch "No — remediation needed":
      User task "Document and assign remediation actions"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Readiness check passed"
  - branch "Yes — passed":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Readiness check passed"
  User task "Compile configuration and provisioning report"
  Send task "Notify IT / Provisioning of provisioning completion"
  End event "Service configured and provisioned — ready for Migrate Data"

IT / Provisioning lane:
  User task "Receive and validate provisioning request"
  User task "Execute environment build and identity provisioning"
  User task "Confirm provisioning completion to Service Delivery"
  User task "Support identity and access resolution on request"
  User task "Acknowledge provisioning completion notification"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "48-hour correction deadline" — mounted on
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Configuration Accepted" — if the deadline
  expires before configuration is accepted, flow exits the subprocess and
  routes to Error end event "Configuration deadline exceeded — escalate to
  IT / Provisioning".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Service Delivery lane with the start event
and proceeds through requirements review, environment design, and provisioning
request submission; it then passes control actions to the IT / Provisioning
lane for validation and execution before returning to Service Delivery for
configuration application, the configuration-accepted gateway with its
correction loop, identity verification with its resolution branch, and the
readiness check with its remediation branch; all gateway branches rejoin at
their named merge gateways before the flow concludes with report compilation
and the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Delivery "Submit provisioning request" → Provisioning & Identity
    System (provisioning request including environment and access design)
  Provisioning & Identity System → Service Delivery "Provisioning
    confirmation received" (environment build and identity provisioning
    confirmation)
  Service Delivery "Apply service configuration" → Product Platform
    (configuration specification and settings)
  Product Platform → Service Delivery "Configuration acknowledgement received"
    (configuration acceptance or error detail)
  Service Delivery "Verify user identities and roles" → Provisioning &
    Identity System (identity and role verification request)
  Provisioning & Identity System → Service Delivery "Identity verification
    result received" (verification result including any issues)
  IT / Provisioning "Acknowledge provisioning completion notification" →
    Product Platform (readiness confirmation for customer environment)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Configuration Specification" — written by "Review confirmed
  requirements and configuration specification"; read by "Apply service
  configuration to Product Platform".
Data Object "Environment and Access Design" — written by "Define environment
  and access design"; read by "Submit provisioning request to Provisioning
  and Identity System".
Data Object "Provisioning Request" — written by "Submit provisioning request
  to Provisioning and Identity System"; read by "Receive and validate
  provisioning request".
Data Object "Configuration Error Log" — written by "Review configuration
  errors"; read by "Correct and resubmit configuration to Product Platform".
Data Object "Identity and Role Register" — written by "Execute environment
  build and identity provisioning"; read by "Verify user identities and roles
  in Provisioning and Identity System".
Data Object "Remediation Action List" — written by "Document and assign
  remediation actions"; read by "Conduct internal readiness check on
  configured environment".
Data Object "Configuration and Provisioning Report" — written by "Compile
  configuration and provisioning report"; read by "Notify IT / Provisioning
  of provisioning completion".

This subprocess takes the collected and confirmed customer requirements from
V11.05 and produces a fully built, configured, and internally validated service
environment, complete with provisioned user identities and roles. The
configuration and provisioning report compiled here is handed to V11.07
Migrate Data, giving the migration team a verified target environment into
which customer data can be safely loaded.
```


### V11.07 — Migrate Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.07 Migrate Data — the seventh subprocess in the Sign to Onboard
value chain, in which the data migration specialist, implementation partner,
and customer collaborate to extract, validate, transform, load, and confirm
migration of the customer's existing data into the product platform.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the migration, with lanes
for the team involved.
  Lane "Service Delivery (Data Migration Specialist)"
Pool "New Customer" — the customer providing source data and confirmations.
Pool "Implementation Partner" — third-party partner supporting data
extraction and transfer.
Pool "Data Migration Tooling" — IT system managing extraction, transformation,
and validation jobs.
Pool "Product Platform" — IT system receiving and hosting migrated data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Implementation Partner" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Migration Tooling" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Product Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Implementation Partner
3. Service Provider
4. Data Migration Tooling
5. Product Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Service Delivery (Data Migration Specialist) lane:
  Message start event "Migration plan and requirements received from
    Collect Requirements and Data"
  User task "Prepare migration plan and data mapping"
  Send task "Issue data extraction instructions to customer and partner"
  Intermediate message catch event "Source data and environment access
    received"
  User task "Assess and profile source data quality"
  Exclusive gateway "Data quality acceptable?"
    - branch "Issues found": Send task "Return data issues to customer for
      remediation"
      Intermediate message catch event "Remediated data received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Data quality acceptable?"
    - branch "Quality acceptable": Exclusive merge gateway "Data quality
      acceptable?"
  User task "Configure data transformation and load job"
  Service task "Execute extraction and transformation in Data Migration
    Tooling"
  Intermediate message catch event "Transformation results received from
    Data Migration Tooling"
  User task "Review transformation output and error report"
  Exclusive gateway "Transformation errors present?"
    - branch "Errors present": User task "Correct mapping rules and data
      exceptions"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Transformation errors present?"
    - branch "No errors": Exclusive merge gateway "Transformation errors
      present?"
  Service task "Submit transformed data load to Product Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Load completion status received from
    Product Platform"
  User task "Run post-load validation checks"
  Exclusive gateway "Validation passed?"
    - branch "Validation failed": User task "Investigate and remediate load
      failures"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed?"
    - branch "Passed": Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed?"
  User task "Compile migration report"
  Send task "Send migration report to customer for review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer migration confirmation
    received"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer accepts migration?"
    - branch "Not accepted": User task "Log customer objections and plan
      remedial migration"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Customer accepts migration?"
    - branch "Accepted": Exclusive merge gateway "Customer accepts
      migration?"
  End event "Data migration accepted — ready for Test and Validate with
    Customer"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on expanded subprocess scope — not
applicable as a formal looping subprocess here; instead, an interrupting
timer boundary event on User task "Run post-load validation checks",
labelled "Validation deadline exceeded (48 hours)", triggers Send task
"Raise migration delay escalation to onboarding manager", which flows to
an Error end event "Migration validation overdue — escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single lane flows top to bottom through the Data
Migration Specialist lane. After "Issue data extraction instructions", the
flow waits at an intermediate message catch event before proceeding. The
data quality gateway branches to the remediation send task, pauses at an
intermediate message catch, then rejoins the merge gateway before
continuing to configuration. The transformation error gateway branches to
the correction task and rejoins before the load step. The validation
gateway branches to investigation and rejoins before compiling the report.
The customer acceptance gateway branches to a remedial-planning task and
rejoins before the end event.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider, Service Delivery lane (source data files
  and environment access credentials)
Service Provider, Service Delivery lane → New Customer (data extraction
  instructions and data quality issue notifications)
New Customer → Service Provider, Service Delivery lane (remediated data and
  migration confirmation response)
Implementation Partner → Service Provider, Service Delivery lane (source
  data extract and environment access support)
Service Provider, Service Delivery lane → Implementation Partner (extraction
  instructions)
Service Provider, Service Delivery lane → Data Migration Tooling (extraction
  and transformation job configuration)
Data Migration Tooling → Service Provider, Service Delivery lane
  (transformation results and error report)
Service Provider, Service Delivery lane → Product Platform (transformed data
  load submission)
Product Platform → Service Provider, Service Delivery lane (load completion
  status)
Service Provider, Service Delivery lane → New Customer (migration report for
  review)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Data Mapping Document" — written by User task "Prepare
  migration plan and data mapping"; read by User task "Configure data
  transformation and load job".
Data Object "Source Data Extract" — read by User task "Assess and profile
  source data quality"; written by (received from) New Customer and
  Implementation Partner via message flow.
Data Object "Data Quality Report" — written by User task "Assess and
  profile source data quality"; read by Exclusive gateway "Data quality
  acceptable?".
Data Object "Transformation Error Report" — written by Service task
  "Execute extraction and transformation in Data Migration Tooling"; read
  by User task "Review transformation output and error report".
Data Object "Load Completion Status" — written by Product Platform via
  message; read by User task "Run post-load validation checks".
Data Object "Migration Report" — written by User task "Compile migration
  report"; read by Send task "Send migration report to customer for review".

Migrate Data takes the customer's source data through extraction, quality
profiling, transformation, loading into the product platform, and
post-load validation, resolving errors and remediation loops at each stage.
Once the customer formally confirms the migration report, the subprocess
closes with verified, platform-resident data and hands a migration-accepted
signal to Test and Validate with Customer, where the implementation
consultant and customer will exercise the loaded data in the live
environment.
```


### V11.08 — Test & Validate with Customer

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.08 Test & Validate with Customer — the subprocess in which the
Service Provider runs structured testing of the configured and migrated service
with the New Customer, resolves defects, and hands a validated service forward
to obtain go-live acceptance.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
containing all active lanes.
- Lane "Service Delivery (Implementation Consultant)" — leads testing
  activities, logs defects, and coordinates fixes.
- Lane "Onboarding (Onboarding Manager)" — tracks test progress, manages
  escalation, and confirms test completion with the customer.

Pool "New Customer" — external party that executes test cases, reports
findings, and provides sign-off on test results.

Pool "Product Platform" — the live product or service environment against
which testing is performed.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Product Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Product Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Service Delivery lane:
  Message start event "Configured and provisioned service received from
    Configure & Provision Service"
  User task "Prepare test plan and test cases"
  Send task "Share test plan with customer for review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer test plan approval received"
  Service task "Set up test environment on Product Platform"
  Send task "Issue test access credentials to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer ready to begin testing"
  User task "Execute internal smoke tests"
  Exclusive gateway "Smoke tests passed?"
  - branch "No — defects found": User task "Log defects and remediate issues"
    then Exclusive merge gateway "Smoke tests passed?"
  - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Smoke tests passed?"
  Send task "Notify customer to begin user acceptance testing"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer test results and defect report
    received"
  User task "Review and triage customer-reported defects"
  Exclusive gateway "Critical defects outstanding?"
  - branch "Yes — critical defects": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All
    Critical Defects Resolved" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
    "Assign defects to resolution owner", User task "Apply fix to Product
    Platform", Service task "Retest fixed items on Product Platform",
    Send task "Notify customer of fixes for re-test",
    Intermediate message catch event "Customer re-test results received",
    User task "Verify defect closure"
  - branch "No — no critical defects": continues to merge
  Exclusive merge gateway "Critical defects outstanding?"

Onboarding lane:
  User task "Compile test completion report"
  Send task "Send test completion report to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer test sign-off received"
  User task "Record test sign-off in Onboarding Project Management System"
  End event "Testing validated and signed off — ready for Obtain Go-Live
    Acceptance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All
  Critical Defects Resolved" — label "Defect resolution deadline exceeded" —
  triggers Onboarding lane escalation task "Escalate unresolved defects to
  onboarding manager", which leads to a terminating End event "Testing
  blocked — escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Service Delivery lane and progresses
through test preparation, environment setup, internal smoke testing, and the
smoke-test exclusive gateway whose "No" branch loops back through defect
remediation and whose "Yes" branch merges and continues. After the customer
UAT message is caught, the defect-triage exclusive gateway branches to the
critical-defect subprocess on the "Yes" path, rejoining the merge on
resolution; the "No" branch skips directly to the merge. Flow then crosses to
the Onboarding lane for report compilation, customer notification, sign-off
capture, and the end event.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider (test plan approval)
Service Provider → New Customer (test plan for review)
Service Provider → New Customer (test access credentials)
New Customer → Service Provider (confirmation of readiness to test)
New Customer → Service Provider (UAT test results and defect report)
Service Provider → New Customer (notification of fixes applied for re-test)
New Customer → Service Provider (re-test results during defect loop)
Service Provider → New Customer (test completion report)
New Customer → Service Provider (formal test sign-off)
Service Provider → Product Platform (smoke test execution request)
Product Platform → Service Provider (smoke test results)
Service Provider → Product Platform (fix deployment and retest request)
Product Platform → Service Provider (retest validation results)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Test Plan and Test Cases" — written by User task "Prepare test
  plan and test cases"; read by Send task "Share test plan with customer for
  review"; read by User task "Execute internal smoke tests".
Data Object "Defect Log" — written by User task "Log defects and remediate
  issues"; written by User task "Review and triage customer-reported defects";
  written by User task "Verify defect closure"; read by User task "Compile
  test completion report".
Data Object "Customer UAT Results" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Customer test results and defect report received"; read by User task
  "Review and triage customer-reported defects".
Data Object "Test Completion Report" — written by User task "Compile test
  completion report"; read by Send task "Send test completion report to
  customer".
Data Object "Test Sign-off Record" — written by User task "Record test
  sign-off in Onboarding Project Management System".

This subprocess takes the provisioned and migrated service from Configure &
Provision Service and subjects it to structured internal smoke testing and
customer user acceptance testing, resolving all critical defects before
closing. It produces a formally signed-off test completion report, which
confirms the service meets agreed acceptance criteria and hands the validated
service to Obtain Go-Live Acceptance as the basis for the customer's final
go-live decision.
```


### V11.09 — Train Users

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.09 Train Users — the subprocess in which the Onboarding team
delivers user training to the New Customer after testing and validation is
complete, within the Sign to Onboard value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
  with lanes for the teams involved in delivering training.
Pool "New Customer" — the customer's sponsor, project contact, and end
  users who receive and participate in training.
Pool "Learning Management System (LMS)" — the LMS platform used to host
  course materials, track completion, and record outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Learning Management System (LMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Learning Management System (LMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane:

  Message start event "Validated service received from Test & Validate
    with Customer"
  User task "Confirm training audience and schedule with customer"
  User task "Prepare training plan and materials"
  Service task "Upload training materials to LMS"
  Send task "Send training invitations and schedule to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms attendance and
    readiness"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Training Sessions Delivered"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Deliver training
    session", Service task "Record session attendance and outcomes in LMS",
    User task "Collect session feedback from participants"
  Service task "Retrieve training completion report from LMS"
  Exclusive gateway "All required users trained and competency met?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to User task "Compile training summary report"
    - branch "No — gaps identified": User task "Schedule remedial training
        sessions", then rejoin
  Exclusive merge gateway "All required users trained and competency met"
  User task "Compile training summary report"
  Send task "Send training summary report to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer acknowledges training
    completion"
  End event "Training complete — ready for Obtain Go-Live Acceptance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  All Training Sessions Delivered", labelled "Training window deadline
  reached", triggering an escalation task in the Onboarding lane: User task
  "Escalate training delay to onboarding manager and agree revised plan".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Onboarding lane at the message start
  event, progresses through confirmation, preparation, upload, and
  invitation tasks, pauses at the attendance confirmation catch event, then
  enters the standard-loop subprocess that cycles through session delivery,
  attendance recording, and feedback collection until all sessions are done.
  After the loop, the completion report is retrieved and the exclusive
  gateway branches to either remedial scheduling (which rejoins at the
  exclusive merge gateway) or directly to the merge gateway; flow then
  continues through the summary report task, the send task, the
  acknowledgement catch event, and ends at the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Send task "Send training invitations and schedule to
    customer") → New Customer (training invitations and schedule)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer confirms attendance and readiness") (attendance confirmation)
  Service Provider (Service task "Upload training materials to LMS") →
    Learning Management System (LMS) (training materials and course content)
  Service Provider (User task "Deliver training session") →
    New Customer (live training session content)
  New Customer → Service Provider (User task "Collect session feedback
    from participants") (participant feedback)
  Learning Management System (LMS) → Service Provider (Service task
    "Retrieve training completion report from LMS") (completion and
    competency report)
  Service Provider (Send task "Send training summary report to customer")
    → New Customer (training summary report)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer acknowledges training completion") (training acknowledgement)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Training Plan" — written by User task "Prepare training plan
  and materials"; read by User task "Deliver training session".
Data Object "Training Materials" — written by User task "Prepare training
  and materials"; read by Service task "Upload training materials to LMS".
Data Object "Training Schedule" — written by User task "Confirm training
  audience and schedule with customer"; read by Send task "Send training
  invitations and schedule to customer".
Data Object "Session Attendance Record" — written by Service task "Record
  session attendance and outcomes in LMS"; read by Service task "Retrieve
  training completion report from LMS".
Data Object "Participant Feedback" — written by User task "Collect session
  feedback from participants"; read by User task "Compile training summary
  report".
Data Object "Training Completion Report" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve training completion report from LMS"; read by Exclusive gateway
  "All required users trained and competency met?".
Data Object "Training Summary Report" — written by User task "Compile
  training summary report"; read by Send task "Send training summary report
  to customer".

This subprocess delivers all required training sessions to the customer's
users, records attendance and competency outcomes in the LMS, and resolves
any gaps through remedial sessions before producing a signed-off training
summary report. It hands a confirmed, acknowledged training completion
record to the next subprocess, Obtain Go-Live Acceptance, giving the
onboarding manager the evidence needed to seek formal customer sign-off
on readiness for go-live.
```


### V11.10 — Obtain Go-Live Acceptance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.10 Obtain Go-Live Acceptance — the subprocess in which the
onboarding team seeks and records the customer's formal acceptance that the
service is ready for go-live, within the Sign to Onboard value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
  with lanes for Onboarding and Service Delivery.
Pool "New Customer" — the external customer representative providing
  formal go-live acceptance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — the project and task
  management platform used to record acceptance and close onboarding
  milestones.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Onboarding / Project Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane:
  Message start event "Go-live readiness confirmed from Test & Validate
    with Customer"
  User task "Prepare go-live acceptance pack"
  Send task "Distribute acceptance pack to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer acceptance response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Acceptance granted?"
    - branch "Yes — accepted": User task "Record formal acceptance sign-off"
      then continue to exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance granted"
    - branch "No — issues raised": Service task "Log outstanding issues in
      Onboarding / Project Management System"
      then Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Acceptance Granted" (standard
        loop) containing, in order: User task "Coordinate issue resolution
        with Service Delivery", Send task "Notify customer of resolution
        and resubmit acceptance request", Intermediate message catch event
        "Customer re-review response received"
      then continue to exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance granted"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance granted"
  User task "Close onboarding milestones in Onboarding / Project Management
    System"
  User task "Notify internal stakeholders of go-live acceptance"
  End event "Go-live acceptance obtained — ready for Activate Billing"

Service Delivery lane:
  User task "Confirm readiness evidence is complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Acceptance Granted", labelled "Acceptance overdue — escalation deadline
  reached"; on trigger, flow continues to User task "Escalate unresolved
  acceptance to onboarding manager" in Onboarding lane, then to an Error
  end event "Acceptance escalated — onboarding blocked".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the process begins in the Onboarding lane with the message
start event, moves to preparation and distribution of the acceptance pack,
then waits for the customer response. The exclusive gateway "Acceptance
granted?" splits into the accepted branch, which proceeds directly to
recording sign-off, and the issues-raised branch, which logs issues and
enters the resolution loop; both branches rejoin at the exclusive merge
gateway "Acceptance granted". Before the acceptance pack is distributed,
a sequence flow crosses to the Service Delivery lane for confirmation of
readiness evidence, returning to the Onboarding lane before the send task
fires. After the merge gateway the flow closes milestones and notifies
stakeholders before reaching the end event.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider, Onboarding lane (signed or emailed
  acceptance response / issues list).
Service Provider, Onboarding lane → New Customer (acceptance pack
  containing go-live checklist, sign-off form, and readiness summary).
Service Provider, Onboarding lane → New Customer (resolution notification
  and resubmission request, inside loop).
Service Provider, Onboarding lane → Onboarding / Project Management System
  (issue log entries from "Log outstanding issues" service task).
Service Provider, Onboarding lane → Onboarding / Project Management System
  (acceptance sign-off record and milestone closure from "Close onboarding
  milestones" user task).
Onboarding / Project Management System → Service Provider, Onboarding lane
  (provisioning status and readiness telemetry read during "Prepare go-live
  acceptance pack").

7. Data objects

Data Object "Go-Live Acceptance Pack" — written by "Prepare go-live
  acceptance pack"; read by "Distribute acceptance pack to customer".
Data Object "Customer Acceptance Response" — read by "Record formal
  acceptance sign-off"; read by "Log outstanding issues in Onboarding /
  Project Management System".
Data Object "Outstanding Issues List" — written by "Log outstanding issues
  in Onboarding / Project Management System"; read by "Coordinate issue
  resolution with Service Delivery".

This subprocess confirms that the service meets the customer's agreed
acceptance criteria before billing and support handover begin. The onboarding
team assembles evidence of readiness, distributes a formal sign-off pack to
the customer, and works through any outstanding issues until acceptance is
granted. The recorded acceptance sign-off and closed project milestones are
then passed to Activate Billing to trigger the first invoice and subscription
schedule.
```

```text
        manager"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Billing terms clear?"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Billing terms clear?"
  Service task "Create billing schedule in Billing & Subscription System"
  Service task "Activate subscription and entitlements in Billing &
    Subscription System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Activation confirmation received from
    Billing & Subscription System"
  User task "Review activation record and confirm accuracy"
  Service task "Generate first invoice in Billing & Subscription System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Invoice document received from Billing &
    Subscription System"
  Send task "Issue first invoice to New Customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Invoice acknowledgement received from
    New Customer"
  Exclusive gateway "Invoice accepted without dispute?"
    - branch "No — customer disputes invoice": User task "Log dispute and
      initiate resolution"
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Invoice Dispute Resolved" (standard
        loop) containing, in order: User task "Review disputed line items with
        customer", User task "Correct invoice in Billing & Subscription
        System", Send task "Reissue corrected invoice to New Customer",
        Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Invoice accepted without dispute?"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Invoice accepted without
        dispute?"
  User task "Record billing activation and first invoice in billing ledger"
  End event "Billing activated — ready for Hand Over to Business as Usual"

Onboarding lane:
  User task "Confirm go-live date and billing trigger to Finance / Billing"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Invoice Dispute Resolved" — label "Dispute unresolved after 10 business
days" — triggers Escalation end event "Escalate unresolved billing dispute
to Onboarding manager and Finance lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Finance / Billing lane on receipt of
go-live acceptance; the Onboarding lane contributes go-live date
confirmation before billing terms are checked; the exclusive gateway
"Billing terms clear?" branches to a clarification loop that merges before
schedule creation; main flow continues through activation and invoice
generation; the "Invoice accepted without dispute?" gateway branches to a
dispute-resolution subprocess that merges on acceptance; flow ends in
Finance / Billing with the billing ledger update.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider / Finance / Billing (invoice
  acknowledgement or dispute notification)
Service Provider / Finance / Billing → New Customer (first invoice and any
  corrected invoice)
Service Provider / Finance / Billing → Billing & Subscription System
  (create billing schedule request)
Service Provider / Finance / Billing → Billing & Subscription System
  (activate subscription request)
Service Provider / Finance / Billing → Billing & Subscription System
  (generate invoice request)
Billing & Subscription System → Service Provider / Finance / Billing
  (activation confirmation)
Billing & Subscription System → Service Provider / Finance / Billing
  (invoice document)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Signed Contract and Entitlement Details" — read by "Retrieve
  confirmed contract and entitlement details".
Data Object "Billing Schedule" — written by "Create billing schedule in
  Billing & Subscription System"; read by "Review activation record and
  confirm accuracy".
Data Object "Activation Confirmation" — written by Billing & Subscription
  System; read by "Review activation record and confirm accuracy".
Data Object "First Invoice" — written by "Generate first invoice in Billing
  & Subscription System"; read by "Issue first invoice to New Customer".
Data Object "Invoice Dispute Record" — written by "Log dispute and initiate
  resolution"; read by "Review disputed line items with customer".

Activate Billing takes the go-live acceptance produced by Obtain Go-Live
Acceptance and converts it into an active billing relationship. Finance /
Billing retrieves contract terms, creates the billing schedule, activates
the subscription in the Billing & Subscription System, and issues the first
invoice to the customer. Any dispute is resolved through a bounded loop
before the record is committed to the billing ledger. The subprocess hands
an activated billing record and acknowledged first invoice to Hand Over to
Business as Usual.
```

```text
6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Customer Success lane with the message
start event, proceeds through profile review, handover pack preparation and
dispatch, then waits for customer acknowledgement before the handover
meeting and CRM updates. The exclusive gateway "Outstanding issues flagged?"
branches to a log task on "Yes" and directly to the merge on "No"; both
branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Outstanding issues
resolved". Flow continues through confirming support arrangements and
dispatching go-live confirmation, then crosses to the Support lane for
customer registration, support account creation, team briefing, and

Message flows:

New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event

This subprocess transfers the newly onboarded customer from the onboarding
team to the permanent customer success and support structure. The customer
success manager closes out the onboarding record in the CRM, delivers a
```

## V12 — Renew to Retain

**Teams and roles involved.**
Renew to Retain usually involves Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, Renewals, Finance/Billing, Support, and Product, with Legal or Contracts involved where terms change. Key roles include customer success manager, renewals manager, account manager, support lead, billing officer, contracts administrator, and product or adoption analyst.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Existing Customer, usually represented by a commercial owner and a service owner. The process is initiated by an approaching contract end date, a usage or health trigger, or a customer-initiated cancellation or change request. Other external parties include resellers and channel partners, procurement teams acting for the customer, and payment providers.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: monitor account health and usage, identify the renewal opportunity, review service performance with the customer, assess risk of churn, prepare the renewal proposal, negotiate terms, handle cancellation or downgrade requests, execute the renewal, update entitlements and billing, and run win-back for lapsed customers.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include CRM, customer success platform, subscription and billing management, contract lifecycle management, product usage analytics, support/ticketing, survey and feedback tools, and business intelligence reporting.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include renewal notice periods and auto-renewal terms, discounting and approval authority, price-increase policy, cancellation and refund terms, customer health scoring definitions, escalation procedure for at-risk accounts, and retention offer approval rules.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides renewal intent, feedback on service performance, changes to required volumes or scope, cancellation or non-renewal notice, and purchase orders or signatures. The process provides the customer with renewal notices, service and value reviews, proposals and pricing, negotiated terms, confirmation of renewal or cancellation, and revised billing schedules.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates renewal opportunities, health scores and risk flags, proposals and quotes, amended contracts, entitlement changes, and billing schedules. IT systems provide contract dates and terms, usage and adoption data, support-case volumes and satisfaction scores, invoice and payment history, and churn and renewal-rate reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Service Provider" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are
the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V12.01** Monitor Account Health & Usage | — | Customer Success (customer success manager) | Customer Success Platform, Product Usage Analytics |
| **V12.02** Identify Renewal Opportunity | — | Renewals (renewals manager), Customer Success (customer success manager) | CRM System |
| **V12.03** Review Service Performance with Customer | Existing Customer | Customer Success (customer success manager), Support (support lead) | Customer Success Platform, Support / Ticketing System |
| **V12.04** Assess Churn Risk | — | Customer Success (customer success manager), Product (adoption analyst) | Product Usage Analytics, Business Intelligence Platform |
| **V12.05** Prepare Renewal Proposal | — | Renewals (renewals manager), Account Management (account manager) | CRM System |
| **V12.06** Negotiate Terms | Existing Customer, Channel Partner | Renewals (renewals manager), Legal / Contracts (contracts administrator) | Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) |
| **V12.07** Handle Cancellation or Downgrade | Existing Customer | Customer Success (customer success manager), Renewals (renewals manager) | CRM System, Billing & Subscription System |
| **V12.08** Execute Renewal | Existing Customer | Renewals (renewals manager), Legal / Contracts (contracts administrator) | Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) |
| **V12.09** Update Entitlements & Billing | Payment Provider | Finance / Billing (billing officer) | Billing & Subscription System |
| **V12.10** Run Win-Back | Existing Customer | Account Management (account manager), Customer Success (customer success manager) | CRM System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V12):

- **External actors:** Existing Customer (V12.03, V12.06–V12.08, V12.10); Channel Partner (V12.06); Payment Provider (V12.09).
- **Teams:** Customer Success (V12.01–V12.04, V12.07, V12.10); Renewals (V12.02, V12.05–V12.08); Support (V12.03); Product (V12.04); Account Management (V12.05, V12.10); Legal / Contracts (V12.06, V12.08); Finance / Billing (V12.09).
- **IT systems:** Customer Success Platform (V12.01, V12.03); Product Usage Analytics (V12.01, V12.04); CRM System (V12.02, V12.05, V12.07, V12.10); Support / Ticketing System (V12.03); Business Intelligence Platform (V12.04); Contract Lifecycle Management / CLM (V12.06, V12.08); Billing & Subscription System (V12.07, V12.09).

```text
This chain manages the full lifecycle of a contract renewal, from continuous
health monitoring through to confirmed renewal or, where retention fails,
a structured win-back attempt. The main external participant is the Existing

is triggered by an approaching contract end date, a usage or health alert,

win-back campaign targeting customers who have lapsed or cancelled.
```

### V12.01 — Monitor Account Health & Usage

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.01 Monitor Account Health & Usage — first subprocess of the
Renew to Retain value chain, establishing the ongoing health and usage
baseline that triggers all downstream renewal activity.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the monitoring process,
  with lanes for Customer Success and (implicitly) the automated systems
  it orchestrates.
  Lanes top to bottom:
  - Customer Success (customer success manager)
Pool "Customer Success Platform" — SaaS platform aggregating customer
  health signals.
Pool "Product Usage Analytics" — analytics system supplying product
  adoption and usage data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer Success Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Product Usage Analytics" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer Success Platform
2. Service Provider
3. Product Usage Analytics

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Customer Success lane:
  Timer start event "Scheduled monitoring cycle triggered (recurring)"
  Service task "Pull usage and adoption data from Product Usage Analytics"
  Service task "Pull health signals from Customer Success Platform"
  Service task "Calculate health score for each account"
  Exclusive gateway "Health score within acceptable threshold?"
  - branch "Yes — healthy": Service task "Log health status and
    schedule next monitoring cycle"
    End event "Account confirmed healthy — monitoring cycle complete"
  - branch "No — at risk or declining": User task "Review flagged
    accounts and validate risk signals"
    Exclusive gateway "Risk signals confirmed?"
    - branch "No — false positive": Service task "Update health
      record and clear flag"
      End event "Account confirmed healthy — monitoring cycle complete"
    - branch "Yes — genuine risk": Service task "Raise health alert
      and set risk flag on account"
      End event "Health alert raised — ready for Identify Renewal
      Opportunity"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Risk signals confirmed?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Health score within acceptable threshold?"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Customer Success lane, flow runs from the
timer start event through the two data-pull service tasks, then health
score calculation, then the first exclusive gateway. The "Yes" branch
logs status and ends. The "No" branch moves to the review user task,
then the second exclusive gateway; the "No — false positive" branch
clears the flag and rejoins the "Yes" branch at the first merge gateway,
both converging on the healthy end event; the "Yes — genuine risk"
branch raises the alert and reaches the risk-flagged end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Service task "Pull usage and adoption data from
    Product Usage Analytics") → Product Usage Analytics
    (usage and adoption data request)
  Product Usage Analytics → Service Provider (Service task "Pull usage
    and adoption data from Product Usage Analytics")
    (usage metrics and adoption data)
  Service Provider (Service task "Pull health signals from Customer
    Success Platform") → Customer Success Platform
    (health signal data request)
  Customer Success Platform → Service Provider (Service task "Pull
    health signals from Customer Success Platform")
    (aggregated health signals and scores)
  Service Provider (Service task "Raise health alert and set risk flag
    on account") → Customer Success Platform
    (risk flag and health alert record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Usage and Adoption Data" — read by "Calculate health score
  for each account"; written by "Pull usage and adoption data from
  Product Usage Analytics".
Data Object "Health Signal Report" — read by "Calculate health score
  for each account"; written by "Pull health signals from Customer
  Success Platform".
Data Object "Health Alert" — written by "Raise health alert and set
  risk flag on account"; read by "Review flagged accounts and validate
  risk signals".

V12.01 runs on a recurring schedule to collect product usage metrics and
platform health signals, compute a health score for every account, and
identify those whose score falls below the acceptable threshold. Accounts
confirmed as healthy are logged and held for the next cycle. Accounts
where risk signals are validated have a health alert raised and a risk
flag set, making them immediately visible to the Identify Renewal
Opportunity subprocess that follows.
```

```text
2. Service Provider
```

```text
and recommended action".
```

```text
approved proposal in CRM".
```
