### V12.06 — Negotiate Terms

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.06 Negotiate Terms — sixth subprocess in the Renew to Retain
value chain, handling negotiation of renewal terms between the service
provider, the existing customer, and channel partners until agreed terms
are finalised or escalated.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the negotiation process,
with lanes for Renewals and Legal / Contracts.
Pool "Existing Customer" — external customer party reviewing and responding
to proposed terms.
Pool "Channel Partner" — external reseller or channel party where involved
in the deal.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — IT system used to draft,
version, and store contract documents during negotiation.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Existing Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Channel Partner" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Existing Customer
2. Channel Partner
3. Service Provider
4. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Renewals lane:
  Message start event "Renewal proposal received from Prepare Renewal
    Proposal"
  User task "Review proposal readiness and confirm negotiation scope"
  Exclusive gateway "Channel partner involved?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Notify channel partner of negotiation
      opening"
  - branch "No": (continues to merge)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Channel partner involvement confirmed"
  User task "Present proposal terms to customer"
  Send task "Send proposal and supporting documents to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer accepts terms as presented?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to merge below)
  - branch "No — changes requested": User task "Log requested changes
      and assess impact"
    Exclusive gateway "Changes within renewals authority?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Adjust terms within approved parameters"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Terms adjustment complete"
      (continues to merge below)
    - branch "No — requires legal or approval": (passes to Legal /
        Contracts lane via sequence flow)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Terms agreed or returned from Legal"

Legal / Contracts lane:
  User task "Review requested changes against contract policy"
  Exclusive gateway "Changes acceptable under policy?"
  - branch "Yes — draft amended terms": Service task "Instruct CLM to
      draft amended contract version"
    Intermediate message catch event "Amended draft received from CLM"
    User task "Review and approve amended draft"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Legal review outcome"
    (returns to Renewals lane merge above)
  - branch "No — escalate or reject": User task "Escalate to senior
      management and advise customer"
    Exclusive gateway "Escalation resolved?"
    - branch "Resolved — proceed": Exclusive merge gateway "Legal review
        outcome"
      (returns to Renewals lane merge above)
    - branch "Unresolved — terminate negotiation": End event "Negotiation
        failed — customer proceeds to Handle Cancellation or Downgrade"

Renewals lane (continuing from merge):
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Parties Confirm Acceptance"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: Send task "Issue revised terms
    to customer and channel partner", Intermediate message catch event
    "Confirmation response received", User task "Record confirmation
    status against each party"
  Service task "Instruct CLM to lock final agreed terms"
  Intermediate message catch event "Final contract version confirmed
    by CLM"
  User task "Obtain authorised signatures or electronic acceptances"
  Send task "Issue countersigned terms confirmation to customer"
  End event "Terms agreed and signed — ready for Execute Renewal"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Parties Confirm Acceptance", labelled "Negotiation deadline
exceeded", leading to User task "Escalate overdue negotiation to
senior management" in the Renewals lane, then to End event "Negotiation
timed out — customer proceeds to Handle Cancellation or Downgrade".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Renewals lane, branches at "Channel
partner involved?" with the Yes branch notifying the channel partner
before merging back. The main flow continues through proposal
presentation and the customer response catch event. At "Customer accepts
terms as presented?" the Yes branch merges immediately at "Terms agreed
or returned from Legal"; the No branch evaluates renewals authority,
with in-authority adjustments returning to the same merge, and
out-of-authority items crossing to the Legal / Contracts lane. Legal
outcomes (acceptable or escalation-resolved) return to the Renewals
merge; an unresolved escalation ends in its own terminating End event.
After the merge the standard-loop subprocess runs until all parties
confirm, followed by CLM locking, signature collection, and the
successful End event.

Message flows:
Service Provider (Renewals) → Existing Customer (proposal and
  supporting documents sent for review).
Existing Customer → Service Provider (Renewals) (customer response
  and change requests).
Service Provider (Renewals) → Channel Partner (negotiation opening
  notification and revised terms).
Channel Partner → Service Provider (Renewals) (channel partner
  confirmation response).
Service Provider (Legal / Contracts) → Contract Lifecycle Management
  (CLM) (instruction to draft amended contract version).
Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) → Service Provider (Legal /
  Contracts) (amended draft returned for review).
Service Provider (Renewals) → Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)
  (instruction to lock final agreed terms).
Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) → Service Provider (Renewals)
  (final contract version confirmed).
Service Provider (Renewals) → Existing Customer (countersigned terms
  confirmation issued).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Renewal Proposal" — read by User task "Review proposal
  readiness and confirm negotiation scope".
Data Object "Requested Changes Log" — written by User task "Log
  requested changes and assess impact"; read by User task "Review
  requested changes against contract policy".
Data Object "Amended Contract Draft" — written by Service task
  "Instruct CLM to draft amended contract version"; read by User task
  "Review and approve amended draft".
Data Object "Confirmation Status Record" — written by User task
  "Record confirmation status against each party".
Data Object "Signed Terms Confirmation" — written by User task "Obtain
  authorised signatures or electronic acceptances"; read by Send task
  "Issue countersigned terms confirmation to customer".

V12.06 Negotiate Terms takes the prepared renewal proposal and drives it
through structured negotiation with the customer and, where applicable,
the channel partner, escalating out-of-authority changes to Legal /
Contracts and using CLM to version and lock agreed language. The
subprocess ends when all parties have confirmed and signed the agreed
terms, handing a fully executed set of renewal terms to Execute Renewal
(V12.08), or, where negotiation fails or times out, routing the account
to Handle Cancellation or Downgrade (V12.07).
```


### V12.07 — Handle Cancellation or Downgrade

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.07 Handle Cancellation or Downgrade — manages customer-initiated
cancellation or downgrade requests within the Renew to Retain value chain,
sitting after Negotiate Terms and before Execute Renewal.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation handling the cancellation or
downgrade request, containing Customer Success and Renewals lanes.
Pool "Existing Customer" — the customer who has submitted a cancellation
or downgrade request.
Pool "CRM System" — system of record for customer accounts and
opportunities.
Pool "Billing & Subscription System" — system that manages subscription
entitlements and billing schedules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Existing Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Billing & Subscription System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Existing Customer
2. Service Provider
3. CRM System
4. Billing & Subscription System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Customer Success lane:
  Message start event "Cancellation or downgrade request received from
    Existing Customer"
  User task "Log and acknowledge request"
  Service task "Retrieve account health and usage data from CRM System"
  User task "Assess reason for cancellation or downgrade"
  Exclusive gateway "Request type?"
  - branch "Downgrade": User task "Identify revised scope and affected
      entitlements"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved"
  - branch "Cancellation": User task "Confirm cancellation intent and
      effective date"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved"
  User task "Present retention offer or escalation options"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer responds to retention offer"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer decision?"
  - branch "Accepts retention offer": User task "Record revised
      agreement in CRM System"
      End event "Retention agreed — ready for Execute Renewal"
  - branch "Proceeds with downgrade": User task "Confirm revised
      subscription terms with customer"
      Send task "Send downgrade confirmation to Existing Customer"
      (continues to Renewals lane hand-off)
  - branch "Proceeds with cancellation": User task "Initiate
      cancellation procedure"
      Send task "Send cancellation confirmation to Existing Customer"
      (continues to Renewals lane hand-off)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer decision resolved"

Renewals lane:
  User task "Review and approve retention offer or exit terms"
  Exclusive gateway "Approval required?"
  - branch "Yes — discount or exception applies": User task "Obtain
      discounting or retention approval"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Approval resolved"
  - branch "No — standard terms apply": Exclusive merge gateway
      "Approval resolved"
  Service task "Update opportunity status in CRM System"
  Service task "Trigger subscription change or cancellation in Billing
    and Subscription System"
  User task "Confirm effective date and notify Finance"
  End event "Cancellation or downgrade processed — ready for
    Execute Renewal or Update Entitlements and Billing"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Present retention offer or
escalation options" — label "Retention response deadline exceeded" —
flow continues to User task "Escalate unresponsive account to
renewals manager" then to Send task "Send cancellation confirmation
to Existing Customer" and merges into the cancellation branch flow.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Customer Success lane, progressing
through logging, retrieval, assessment, and the Request type gateway
whose downgrade and cancellation branches each rejoin at the Request
type resolved merge, then continues through the retention offer step
and the Customer decision gateway; the retention-accepted branch ends
in its own End event; the downgrade and cancellation branches each
merge at Customer decision resolved and pass to the Renewals lane,
where the Approval required gateway splits and rejoins at Approval
resolved before the CRM update, subscription system trigger, and
final End event.

Message flows:
Existing Customer → Service Provider Customer Success lane
  (cancellation or downgrade request)
Service Provider Customer Success lane → Existing Customer
  (request acknowledgement)
Service Provider Customer Success lane → Existing Customer
  (retention offer)
Existing Customer → Service Provider Customer Success lane
  (customer decision response)
Service Provider Customer Success lane → Existing Customer
  (downgrade confirmation or cancellation confirmation)
Service Provider Customer Success lane → CRM System
  (retrieve account health and usage data)
Service Provider Renewals lane → CRM System
  (update opportunity status)
CRM System → Service Provider Customer Success lane
  (account health, usage, and contract data)
Service Provider Renewals lane → Billing & Subscription System
  (subscription change or cancellation instruction)
Billing & Subscription System → Service Provider Renewals lane
  (change or cancellation confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Cancellation or Downgrade Request" — written by User task
  "Log and acknowledge request"; read by User task "Assess reason for
  cancellation or downgrade".
Data Object "Account Health and Usage Data" — read by Service task
  "Retrieve account health and usage data from CRM System"; read by
  User task "Assess reason for cancellation or downgrade".
Data Object "Retention Offer" — written by User task "Present retention
  offer or escalation options"; read by User task "Review and approve
  retention offer or exit terms".
Data Object "Revised Subscription Terms" — written by User task
  "Confirm revised subscription terms with customer"; read by Service
  task "Trigger subscription change or cancellation in Billing and
  Subscription System".

This subprocess captures and resolves a customer-initiated cancellation
or downgrade by logging the request, diagnosing the reason, presenting
a retention offer, and routing the customer decision through approval
where required. If retention succeeds, the subprocess hands a revised
agreement to Execute Renewal; if the customer proceeds with a downgrade
or cancellation, it delivers confirmed exit or reduced terms to Update
Entitlements and Billing.
```

### V12.08 — Execute Renewal

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.08 Execute Renewal — the subprocess in which the Renewals and
Legal / Contracts teams finalise and execute the renewed agreement with the
Existing Customer, forming the handoff from negotiated terms to billing and
entitlement updates.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation executing the renewal, with lanes
for Renewals and Legal / Contracts.
Pool "Existing Customer" — the customer who signs or approves the renewed
agreement.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — the CLM system that stores,

Pool "Existing Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

Top to bottom:
1. Existing Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

Renewals lane:

  - branch "No — corrections needed":

      containing: Send task "Return documents with correction notes to
      Existing Customer", Intermediate message catch event "Corrected
      documents received", User task "Re-review corrected documents"
      rejoining the exclusive merge gateway

Legal / Contracts lane:

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Documents Accepted", labelled "Signature deadline exceeded (14 days)";

escalated to account management".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Renewals lane, passing from confirmation
of terms through document generation and issuance to the wait for the
customer's signature. On receipt, the completeness gateway routes to either
the correction loop (which returns to the merge gateway when documents are
accepted) or directly to the merge gateway. From the merge gateway, flow

Existing Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event

Service Provider (Service task "Upload executed contract to CLM") →
Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) (executed contract document).
Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) → Service Provider (User task
"Record renewal effective date and contract reference") (contract
reference and effective date).
Service Provider (Send task "Send renewal confirmation to Existing
Customer") → Existing Customer (renewal confirmation).

terms and pricing".
Data Object "Renewal Contract Document" — written by Service task
"Generate renewal order in CLM"; read by Send task "Issue renewal documents
to Existing Customer for signature"; read by User task "Review signed
documents for completeness".

catch event "Signed renewal documents received"; read by User task "Review
signed documents for completeness"; read by User task "Countersign renewal
agreement".
executed contract to CLM"; read by User task "Record renewal effective date
and contract reference".
Data Object "Renewal Confirmation Notice" — written by Send task "Send
renewal confirmation to Existing Customer".

This subprocess takes the agreed terms from negotiation and drives them
through document generation, customer signature, compliance review, and
countersignature to produce a fully executed renewal agreement. The CLM
```

```text
Customer Success lane (customer success manager):

and churn reason from CRM".

offer".
Data Object "Account Health and Usage Summary" — written by "Compile
account health history and usage summary"; read by "Prepare
customer-specific value narrative for win-back review".
Data Object "Value Narrative" — written by "Prepare customer-specific
value narrative for win-back review"; read by "Conduct win-back review
and present revised offer".

written by "Record win-back success and close opportunity in CRM",
"Update CRM with closed-lost status and decline reason", and "Update
CRM with no-response closed-lost status".

V12.10 Run Win-Back begins when a cancellation or non-renewal is
confirmed, triggering a structured outreach campaign by Account
Management and Customer Success to re-engage the lapsed customer with a
tailored offer and a value-focused review. Where the customer accepts,
the account is handed to Renewals to execute a new contract and the win
is recorded in CRM. Where the customer declines or does not respond
within the campaign window, the account is closed-lost with the reason
captured. This subprocess concludes the Renew to Retain value chain,
feeding closed-won recoveries into the Execute Renewal flow and
closed-lost outcomes into CRM for long-term pipeline and retention
reporting.
```


## V13 — Return to Refund

**Teams and roles involved.**
Return to Refund usually involves Customer Service, Returns/Reverse Logistics, Warehouse, Quality, Repairs or Refurbishment, Finance/Accounts Receivable, and sometimes Supplier Management where the fault lies upstream. Key roles include customer service agent, returns coordinator, warehouse receiver, quality inspector, repair technician, disposition analyst, credit controller, and finance officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Customer returning goods. The process is initiated when the customer requests a return, reports a fault, exercises a right of withdrawal, or a recall is issued. Other external parties include freight carriers, third-party returns processors, suppliers and manufacturers, recyclers and disposal partners, and payment providers.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive return request, validate eligibility against policy, authorise the return and issue an RMA, arrange collection or return shipping, receive and inspect the goods, decide disposition (restock, repair, refurbish, scrap, return to supplier), process the refund or replacement, update inventory and financial records, recover cost from the supplier where applicable, and analyse return reasons.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include customer service/ticketing, order management, returns management, warehouse management, quality management, repair or field-service management, inventory and ERP, transport management, billing and accounts receivable, payment gateway, and reporting/analytics.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include returns and refunds policy, statutory withdrawal and consumer-guarantee rights, warranty terms, restocking and shipping-cost rules, inspection and disposition criteria, hazardous or regulated goods handling, recall procedure, supplier recovery and warranty-claim terms, and refund authorisation limits.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides the return request and reason, order and product identifiers, condition and fault description, evidence such as photographs, and return shipment details. The process provides the customer with eligibility decisions, return authorisation and labels, collection arrangements, receipt and inspection outcomes, refund or replacement confirmation, and credit notes.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates return authorisations, inbound shipments, inspection results, disposition decisions, inventory adjustments, credit notes, refunds, and supplier claims. IT systems provide original order and payment details, product and warranty data, stock locations, carrier tracking, refund status, and return-reason analytics.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Retail Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V13.01** Receive Return Request | Customer | Customer Service (customer service agent) | Customer Service / Ticketing System |
| **V13.02** Validate Eligibility | Customer | Customer Service (customer service agent), Returns (returns coordinator) | Order Management System (OMS), Returns Management System |
| **V13.03** Authorise Return & Issue RMA | Customer | Returns (returns coordinator) | Returns Management System |
| **V13.04** Arrange Collection | Customer, Freight Carrier | Returns (returns coordinator), Logistics (logistics coordinator) | Transport Management System (TMS) |
| **V13.05** Receive & Inspect Goods | Freight Carrier | Warehouse (warehouse receiver), Quality (quality inspector) | Warehouse Management System (WMS), Quality Management System |
| **V13.06** Decide Disposition | — | Quality (disposition analyst), Repairs (repair technician) | Returns Management System, Inventory / ERP System |
| **V13.07** Process Refund or Replacement | Customer, Payment Provider | Finance (finance officer), Customer Service (customer service agent) | Billing / ERP System, Payment Gateway |
| **V13.08** Update Inventory & Financials | — | Warehouse (inventory controller), Finance (finance officer) | Inventory / ERP System |
| **V13.09** Recover Cost from Supplier | Supplier | Supplier Management (supplier manager), Finance (credit controller) | Procurement / ERP System |
| **V13.10** Analyse Return Reasons | — | Quality (quality manager), Customer Service (service manager) | Business Intelligence Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V13):

- **External actors:** Customer (V13.01–V13.04, V13.07); Freight Carrier (V13.04, V13.05); Payment Provider (V13.07); Supplier (V13.09).
- **Teams:** Customer Service (V13.01, V13.02, V13.07, V13.10); Returns (V13.02–V13.04); Logistics (V13.04); Warehouse (V13.05, V13.08); Quality (V13.05, V13.06, V13.10); Repairs (V13.06); Finance (V13.07–V13.09); Supplier Management (V13.09).

**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V13 — Return to Refund — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Return to Refund value chain, from the moment a customer raises a
return request through to supplier cost recovery and return-reason analysis.
The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS
SERVICES (top), BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle), and APPLICATIONS (bottom).
The demand-side actor (Customer) sits on the far left; delivery and
settlement actors (Freight Carrier, Payment Provider, Supplier) sit on the
far right. The diagram is read top-to-bottom as service realisation:
business services are realised by business processes, which are supported
by application components below them.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Customer — far left; initiates the return and receives refund or
  replacement outcomes across V13.01 through V13.04 and V13.07.
- Freight Carrier — far right; participates in collection and inbound
  goods receipt in V13.04 and V13.05.
- Payment Provider — far right; processes refund disbursements in V13.07.
- Supplier — far right; receives cost-recovery claims and warranty
  submissions in V13.09.

2. Interfaces

- Customer Service Interface — accessed by Customer; serves the Return
  Request Handling service and the Refund or Replacement Confirmation
  service.
- Carrier Booking Interface — accessed by Freight Carrier; serves the
  Collection Arrangement service.
- Payment Gateway Interface — accessed by Payment Provider; serves the
  Refund Processing service.
- Supplier Claim Interface — accessed by Supplier; serves the Supplier
  Cost Recovery service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Return Request Handling — receives and acknowledges the customer's
  return request, reason, and supporting evidence.
- Eligibility Validation — assesses the request against returns policy,
  warranty terms, and statutory rights.
- Return Authorisation & RMA Issuance — grants authorisation and issues
  an RMA number and return label to the customer.
- Collection Arrangement — coordinates return shipping or carrier
  collection with the customer and freight carrier.
- Goods Receipt & Inspection — accepts inbound returned goods and
  records inspection and quality findings.
- Disposition Decision — determines the appropriate outcome for each
  returned item: restock, repair, refurbish, scrap, or return to
  supplier.
- Refund or Replacement Processing — executes the customer credit, refund
  payment, or replacement order.
- Inventory & Financial Update — adjusts stock records and posts
  financial entries for the completed return.
- Supplier Cost Recovery — raises and tracks warranty claims or cost
  recovery requests against the responsible supplier.
- Return Reason Analysis — aggregates and analyses return data to
  identify trends and drive improvement.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, chain order

- V13.01 Receive Return Request — captures the return request, reason,
  order identifiers, fault description, and any photographic evidence
  from the customer.
- V13.02 Validate Eligibility — checks the request against returns
  policy, withdrawal rights, and warranty terms using order and product
  data.
- V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA — approves the return, generates
  the RMA, and communicates authorisation and labels to the customer.
- V13.04 Arrange Collection — books freight carrier collection or
  generates a return-postage label and confirms arrangements with the
  customer.
- V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods — receives the inbound shipment,
  inspects condition, records quality findings, and confirms receipt.
- V13.06 Decide Disposition — evaluates inspection results and assigns
  each item a disposition: restock, repair, refurbish, scrap, or return
  to supplier.
- V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement — issues a credit note or refund
  via the payment provider, or initiates a replacement order.
- V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials — posts inventory adjustments,
  updates stock locations, and records financial entries in the ERP.
- V13.09 Recover Cost from Supplier — raises warranty or fault claims,
  manages supplier correspondence, and tracks recovery amounts.
- V13.10 Analyse Return Reasons — extracts and analyses return-reason
  data to produce insights, trend reports, and improvement
  recommendations.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Customer Service / Ticketing System — supports return request intake
  and customer communication in V13.01, V13.02, V13.07, and V13.10.
- Order Management System (OMS) — provides original order and payment
  reference data used in V13.02.
- Returns Management System — manages return authorisations, RMA
  records, and disposition decisions in V13.02, V13.03, and V13.06.
- Transport Management System (TMS) — books carriers and tracks
  collection and inbound shipments in V13.04.
- Warehouse Management System (WMS) — records goods receipt, stock
  movements, and location updates in V13.05 and V13.08.
- Quality Management System — captures inspection results and quality
  findings in V13.05.
- Inventory / ERP System — maintains stock levels and supports
  disposition and inventory adjustment in V13.06 and V13.08.
- Billing / ERP System — generates credit notes and manages accounts
  receivable entries in V13.07.
- Payment Gateway — processes refund disbursements to the customer in
  V13.07.
- Procurement / ERP System — manages supplier claims and cost-recovery
  records in V13.09.
- Business Intelligence Platform — aggregates return-reason data and
  produces analytics and trend reports in V13.10.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process):
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.01 Receive Return
  Request.
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.02 Validate Eligibility.
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.07 Process Refund or
  Replacement.
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.10 Analyse Return
  Reasons.
- Order Management System SERVES V13.02 Validate Eligibility.
- Returns Management System SERVES V13.02 Validate Eligibility.
- Returns Management System SERVES V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA.
- Returns Management System SERVES V13.06 Decide Disposition.
- Transport Management System SERVES V13.04 Arrange Collection.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V13.08 Update Inventory &
  Financials.
- Quality Management System SERVES V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods.
- Inventory / ERP System SERVES V13.06 Decide Disposition.
- Inventory / ERP System SERVES V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials.
- Billing / ERP System SERVES V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement.
- Billing / ERP System SERVES V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials.
- Payment Gateway SERVES V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V13.09 Recover Cost from Supplier.
- Business Intelligence Platform SERVES V13.10 Analyse Return Reasons.

SERVING (business service SERVES business actor):
- Return Request Handling SERVES Customer.
- Eligibility Validation SERVES Customer.
- Return Authorisation & RMA Issuance SERVES Customer.
- Collection Arrangement SERVES Customer.
- Collection Arrangement SERVES Freight Carrier.
- Goods Receipt & Inspection SERVES Freight Carrier.
- Refund or Replacement Processing SERVES Customer.
- Refund or Replacement Processing SERVES Payment Provider.
- Supplier Cost Recovery SERVES Supplier.

REALISATION (business process REALISES business service):

  RMA Issuance.

- V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials REALISES Inventory & Financial

- V13.10 Analyse Return Reasons REALISES Return Reason Analysis.

ACCESS (business actor ACCESSES interface):

- Supplier ACCESSES Supplier Claim Interface.

SERVING (interface SERVES business service):
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V13 - Return to Refund

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each represented as a chevron, in the order listed below. Each chevron
carries only the stage code and name. No swimlanes, no system icons, no
data flows — this is an overview diagram only.

V13.10. Analyse Return Reasons

This chain governs the end-to-end handling of a customer return, from the
moment the Customer submits a return request through eligibility checking,
physical collection, goods inspection, and disposition, to the settlement
of a refund or replacement, the correction of inventory and financial
records, the recovery of costs from a Supplier where fault lies upstream,
and the analysis of return reasons to drive continuous improvement. The
chain is triggered by the Customer requesting a return, reporting a fault,
exercising a statutory right of withdrawal, or by the issue of a product
recall.
```

### V13.01 — Receive Return Request

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.01 Receive Return Request — first subprocess of the Return to
Refund value chain, capturing the customer's return request and opening a
support ticket before eligibility is assessed.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the company receiving and logging the return
request, with lanes for Customer Service.
Pool "Customer" — the external party initiating the return.
Pool "Customer Service / Ticketing System" — the IT system that records
and tracks return requests.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer Service / Ticketing System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Customer Service / Ticketing System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Customer Service lane (customer service agent):
  Message start event "Return request received from Customer"
  User task "Review and acknowledge return request"
  User task "Capture return reason and product details"
  User task "Record order and product identifiers"
  User task "Request supporting evidence from customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer submits evidence"
  Exclusive gateway "Is sufficient information provided?"
  - branch "Yes — all details and evidence received":
      Service task "Log return request in ticketing system"
      End event "Return request logged — ready for Validate Eligibility"
  - branch "No — information incomplete":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Notify customer of missing information",
        Intermediate message catch event "Customer provides additional
        information",
        User task "Review updated information"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Is sufficient information provided?"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Details Complete" — label "72-hour response deadline exceeded" —
flow continues to: User task "Close request as abandoned and notify
customer", then a Terminate end event "Request abandoned — no
further action".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Customer Service lane when the message
start event fires, passes through acknowledgement and data-capture tasks,
then waits at the intermediate message catch event for evidence. The
exclusive gateway branches to the logging service task and end event when
complete, or to the repeat subprocess when incomplete; on exit the
subprocess rejoins the exclusive merge gateway and re-evaluates the
condition. The timer boundary event on the subprocess exits to the
abandoned-request task and terminate end event without rejoining the
main branch.

Message flows:
Customer → Retail Organisation / Customer Service lane (return request,
reason, order and product identifiers, fault description).
Customer → Retail Organisation / Customer Service lane (supporting
evidence such as photographs, submitted in response to request).
Retail Organisation / Customer Service lane → Customer (acknowledgement
of return request receipt).
Retail Organisation / Customer Service lane → Customer (notification of
missing information, sent from within the repeat subprocess).
Retail Organisation / Customer Service lane →
Customer Service / Ticketing System (return request record to be
logged).
Customer Service / Ticketing System → Retail Organisation /
Customer Service lane (confirmed ticket reference number and
logged request data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Return Request Form" — written by "Capture return reason
and product details"; read by "Log return request in ticketing system".
Data Object "Supporting Evidence" — written by "Request supporting
evidence from customer"; read by "Review updated information" and
"Log return request in ticketing system".
Data Object "Order and Product Identifiers" — written by "Record order
and product identifiers"; read by "Log return request in ticketing
system".
"Log return request in ticketing system".

This subprocess captures and structures the customer's return request in
full — reason, order references, product identifiers, and any supporting
evidence — and records it as a formal ticket in the Customer Service /
Ticketing System. It handles incomplete submissions through a timed
repeat loop and closes abandoned requests cleanly. On successful
completion it hands a fully populated return request record to Validate
Eligibility so that policy checks can begin immediately.
```

```text
This subprocess takes the logged return request from Receive Return
Request and determines whether the customer's claim is eligible under
```

```text
BPMN: V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA — third subprocess in the

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  'Customer acknowledgement received'" — label "Acknowledgement overdue
  (48 hours)" — if no acknowledgement is received within 48 hours, flow
  continues to User task "Chase customer for acknowledgement" then rejoins
  before End event "RMA issued and acknowledged — ready for Arrange
  Collection".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Returns lane at the message start event,
  passes through the review task to the exclusive gateway. The "Yes" branch
  runs through RMA creation, label generation and recording, issuance, and
  the acknowledgement catch event before reaching the positive end event.
  The "No" branch runs through the decline preparation and notification tasks
  before reaching the decline end event. The two branches do not rejoin; the
  "Exclusive merge gateway 'Return authorised?'" is not reached by the "No"
  branch, which terminates independently.

Message flows:
  Returns Management System → Returns lane (RMA record confirmation — after
    RMA creation service task)
  Returns lane → Returns Management System (RMA creation request — from
    "Create RMA record in Returns Management System")
  Returns lane → Returns Management System (return label recording — from
    "Record return label against RMA")
  Returns lane → Customer (RMA and return shipping label — from "Issue RMA
    and return label to customer")
  Returns lane → Customer (decline notification — from "Send decline
    notification to customer")
  Customer → Returns lane (acknowledgement of RMA receipt — received at
    "Customer acknowledgement received" catch event)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Return Decision" — read by "Review validated return
  decision".
Data Object "RMA Record" — written by "Create RMA record in Returns
  Management System"; read by "Generate return shipping label" and
  "Record return label against RMA".
Data Object "Return Shipping Label" — written by "Generate return shipping
  label"; read by "Record return label against RMA" and "Issue RMA and
  return label to customer".
Data Object "Decline Notification" — written by "Prepare decline
  notification"; read by "Send decline notification to customer".

This subprocess converts a validated eligibility decision into a formal
Return Merchandise Authorisation. The returns coordinator reviews the
decision, raises the RMA in the Returns Management System, attaches a
prepaid or carrier-specific return label, and sends both to the customer.
A 48-hour timer guards against silent non-response. On completion, an
acknowledged RMA is in place and the process hands off to Arrange
Collection so that the physical goods movement can begin.
```


### V13.04 — Arrange Collection

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.04 Arrange Collection — coordinates return shipment between
the authorised customer and a freight carrier, sitting between
Authorise Return & Issue RMA and Receive & Inspect Goods in the
Return to Refund value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the internal teams arranging collection
  Lane "Returns" — returns coordinator managing the return shipment
  Lane "Logistics" — logistics coordinator booking and confirming
    the carrier
Pool "Customer" — the customer returning goods
Pool "Freight Carrier" — the carrier collecting the goods
Pool "Transport Management System (TMS)" — IT system used to book
  and track shipments

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Freight Carrier" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Transport Management System (TMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Freight Carrier
4. Transport Management System (TMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Returns lane:
  Message start event "Return authorisation received from
    Authorise Return & Issue RMA"
  User task "Review RMA details and confirm collection requirements"
  User task "Select preferred collection method"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer drop-off or carrier collection?"
  - branch "Customer drop-off": Send task "Send drop-off
      instructions to customer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms drop-off
        completed"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Collection method resolved"
  - branch "Carrier collection": (continues in Logistics lane,
      rejoins at Exclusive merge gateway "Collection method resolved"
      after carrier confirmation is received)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Collection method resolved"
  User task "Record shipment details on return record"
  End event "Collection arranged — ready for Receive & Inspect Goods"

Logistics lane:
  User task "Raise shipment booking request in TMS"
  Service task "Retrieve carrier options and rates from TMS"
  User task "Confirm carrier booking and collection slot"
  Send task "Send collection booking confirmation to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Freight carrier confirms
    collection appointment"
  Send task "Provide collection details to freight carrier"
  (sequence flow returns to Exclusive merge gateway "Collection
    method resolved" in Returns lane)

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch
  event "Freight carrier confirms collection appointment" — label
  "Carrier response overdue (24 hours)" — if carrier does not
  confirm within 24 hours, flow moves to User task "Escalate
  carrier booking failure to returns coordinator" in Logistics lane,
  ending in a local End event "Carrier booking failed — escalated".

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch
  event "Customer confirms drop-off completed" — label "Drop-off
  not confirmed (5 business days)" — if customer does not confirm
  within 5 business days, flow moves to User task "Follow up with
  customer on drop-off status" in Returns lane, ending in a local
  End event "Drop-off unresolved — escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The Returns lane opens the process, reviews the
RMA, and routes on the exclusive gateway "Customer drop-off or
carrier collection?". The drop-off branch sends instructions to the
customer, waits for confirmation, and rejoins the merge gateway
"Collection method resolved" in the Returns lane. The carrier
collection branch passes to the Logistics lane, where the booking is
raised in TMS, the carrier is selected, confirmed and notified, the
customer is informed, the carrier's appointment confirmation is
awaited, and collection details are sent to the carrier before the
flow rejoins the merge gateway "Collection method resolved". After
the merge, the Returns lane records shipment details and closes with
the end event.

Message flows:
  Send task "Send drop-off instructions to customer" → Customer
    (drop-off instructions and return label)
  Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms
    drop-off completed" (drop-off confirmation)
  Retail Organisation (User task "Raise shipment booking request
    in TMS") → Transport Management System (TMS) (shipment booking
    request)
  Transport Management System (TMS) → Retail Organisation (Service
    task "Retrieve carrier options and rates from TMS") (carrier
    options and rates)
  Retail Organisation (User task "Confirm carrier booking and
    collection slot") → Transport Management System (TMS) (confirmed
    booking instruction)
  Send task "Send collection booking confirmation to customer" →
    Customer (booking confirmation and collection slot details)
  Freight Carrier → Intermediate message catch event "Freight carrier
    confirms collection appointment" (collection appointment
    confirmation)
  Send task "Provide collection details to freight carrier" →
    Freight Carrier (return address, package details, and RMA
    reference)

7. Data objects

Data Object "RMA Record" — read by User task "Review RMA details
  and confirm collection requirements"; written by User task "Record
  shipment details on return record".
Data Object "Shipment Booking Request" — written by User task
  "Raise shipment booking request in TMS"; read by Service task
  "Retrieve carrier options and rates from TMS".
Data Object "Carrier Booking Confirmation" — written by User task
  "Confirm carrier booking and collection slot"; read by Send task
  "Provide collection details to freight carrier".
Data Object "Collection Instructions" — written by Send task "Send
  drop-off instructions to customer" and Send task "Send collection
  booking confirmation to customer"; read by the Customer pool.

This subprocess takes a validated and authorised return and converts
it into a concrete collection or drop-off arrangement. It selects
the appropriate method, books and confirms a carrier where needed,
and notifies both the customer and the carrier. On completion it
hands a fully recorded shipment — with carrier, slot, and RMA
reference confirmed — to Receive & Inspect Goods so the warehouse
can expect and receipt the inbound return.
```


### V13.05 — Receive & Inspect Goods

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods — the fifth subprocess in the
Return to Refund value chain, covering physical receipt of returned goods
from the freight carrier and quality inspection leading to a recorded
inspection outcome ready for disposition.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the organisation receiving and inspecting
returned goods, with lanes for Warehouse and Quality.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — external party delivering the returned goods to
the warehouse.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — IT system recording inbound
shipments and updating stock receipt.
Pool "Quality Management System" — IT system recording inspection results
and condition assessments.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Quality Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Freight Carrier
2. Retail Organisation
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)
4. Quality Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Warehouse lane:
  Message start event "Return shipment arrived from Arrange Collection"
  User task "Verify delivery against RMA documentation"
  Exclusive gateway "Shipment details match RMA?"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found": User task "Log discrepancy and
    notify Returns coordinator"
    End event "Discrepancy escalated — returns coordinator to resolve"
  - branch "Yes — details match": continue to merge
  Exclusive merge gateway "Shipment details match RMA"
  User task "Book goods into inbound receipt"
  Service task "Record inbound shipment in WMS"
  User task "Move goods to inspection area"
  Send task "Notify Quality of goods ready for inspection"

Quality lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Goods ready for inspection"
  User task "Retrieve inspection checklist for product type"
  User task "Perform physical inspection of returned goods"
  Exclusive gateway "Goods condition assessable?"
  - branch "No — unidentifiable or hazardous": User task "Flag goods
    for specialist handling"
    End event "Specialist handling required — process paused for
    resolution"
  - branch "Yes — condition clear": continue to merge
  Exclusive merge gateway "Goods condition assessable"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Inspection Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Record condition findings",
    User task "Capture photographic or documentary evidence",
    User task "Verify completeness of inspection record"
  Service task "Submit inspection results to Quality Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Inspection outcome?"
  - branch "Pass — goods acceptable": User task "Mark goods as
    inspected and passed"
  - branch "Fail — goods damaged or non-conforming": User task "Mark
    goods as inspected and failed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome"
  End event "Inspection complete — ready for Decide Disposition"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Perform physical inspection of
returned goods" — label "Inspection deadline exceeded (24 hours)" —
triggers User task "Escalate overdue inspection to Quality manager",
then End event "Inspection escalated — awaiting Quality manager action".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow runs from the message start event in the Warehouse
lane through the RMA verification gateway; the discrepancy branch ends
in its own end event while the matching branch merges and continues
through goods booking, WMS recording, and movement to inspection area,
ending with the notification send task. The Quality lane begins at the
intermediate message catch event and proceeds through checklist
retrieval, physical inspection, the assessability gateway (the hazardous
branch ends in its own end event; the clear branch merges), the
inspection loop subprocess, QMS submission, the pass/fail outcome
gateway (both branches merge), and finally the end event.

Message flows:
Freight Carrier → Retail Organisation / Warehouse lane (return
shipment delivery and proof of delivery).
Retail Organisation / Warehouse lane → Warehouse Management System
(WMS) (inbound shipment record — written by "Record inbound shipment
in WMS").
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Retail Organisation / Warehouse
lane (confirmed receipt acknowledgement).
Retail Organisation / Quality lane → Quality Management System
(inspection results submission — written by "Submit inspection results
to Quality Management System").
Quality Management System → Retail Organisation / Quality lane
(inspection record confirmation and product/warranty reference data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "RMA Documentation" — read by "Verify delivery against RMA
documentation".
Data Object "Inbound Shipment Record" — written by "Book goods into
inbound receipt"; read by "Record inbound shipment in WMS".
Data Object "Inspection Checklist" — read by "Retrieve inspection
checklist for product type"; read by "Perform physical inspection of
returned goods".
Data Object "Inspection Report" — written by "Record condition
findings"; written by "Capture photographic or documentary evidence";
written by "Verify completeness of inspection record"; read by "Submit
inspection results to Quality Management System".
Data Object "Condition Assessment Record" — written by "Mark goods as
inspected and passed" and "Mark goods as inspected and failed"; read
by Quality Management System.
"Submit inspection results to Quality Management System".
shipment in WMS".

This subprocess physically receives the returned goods from the freight
carrier, reconciles them against the RMA, books them into the warehouse
system, and carries out a structured quality inspection that produces a
complete, evidenced inspection report stored in the Quality Management
System. The verified inspection outcome — pass or fail with full
condition detail — is handed to Decide Disposition, which uses it to
determine the correct onward path for each item.
```


### V13.06 — Decide Disposition

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.06 Decide Disposition — the Quality and Repairs teams evaluate
inspected returned goods and assign a disposition category, feeding the
decision into Process Refund or Replacement and Update Inventory & Financials.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out disposition
  analysis and repair assessment.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
    - Quality (disposition analyst)
    - Repairs (repair technician)
Pool "Returns Management System" — records disposition decisions against
  the return authorisation.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — receives disposition categories to drive
  downstream stock and financial updates.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Returns Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Retail Organisation" — centre (process owner).
Pool "Returns Management System" — below Retail Organisation.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — below Returns Management System.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Quality lane:
  Message start event "Inspection result received from Receive & Inspect Goods"
  Service task "Retrieve inspection record and disposition criteria"
  Exclusive gateway "Inspection outcome?"
    - branch "Pass — item in resaleable condition": User task
        "Record restock disposition"
    - branch "Repairable — item has correctable defect": User task
        "Refer item to Repairs for assessment"
    - branch "Scrap — item beyond economic repair": User task
        "Record scrap disposition"
    - branch "Return to supplier — item under supplier warranty": User task
        "Record return-to-supplier disposition"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome"
  (Note: the repairable branch diverges into the Repairs lane before
   rejoining; see below.)
  User task "Confirm final disposition decision"
  Service task "Write disposition decision to Returns Management System"
  Service task "Write disposition category to Inventory / ERP System"
  End event "Disposition decided — ready for Process Refund or Replacement
    and Update Inventory & Financials"

Repairs lane:
  (Receives work from "Refer item to Repairs for assessment" via sequence flow)
  User task "Assess repair feasibility and estimated cost"
  Exclusive gateway "Repair economically viable?"
    - branch "Yes — repair viable": User task
        "Log repair disposition and estimated cost"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Repair economically viable"
      (rejoins Quality lane at Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome")
    - branch "No — not viable": User task
        "Escalate to Quality: recommend scrap or return to supplier"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Repair economically viable"
      (rejoins Quality lane at Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome")

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Assess repair feasibility and estimated
  cost" — label "Repair assessment deadline exceeded (48 hours)" — on trigger,
  flow moves to User task "Escalate to Quality: recommend scrap or return to
  supplier" in the Repairs lane, then rejoins at Exclusive merge gateway
  "Inspection outcome" in the Quality lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Quality lane, flow runs from the start event
  through retrieval, the "Inspection outcome?" gateway and its branches;
  the restock, scrap, and return-to-supplier branches each complete their
  respective User tasks and converge at the Exclusive merge gateway
  "Inspection outcome"; the repairable branch passes to the Repairs lane
  for feasibility assessment, the "Repair economically viable?" gateway
  splits into viable and not-viable branches, both converge at the Exclusive
  merge gateway "Repair economically viable" before returning to the Quality
  lane at the Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome"; from there flow
  continues through confirmation and the two service tasks to the end event.

Message flows:
  Returns Management System → Quality lane: "Retrieve inspection record and
    disposition criteria" (inspection record and disposition criteria).
  Quality lane: "Write disposition decision to Returns Management System" →
    Returns Management System (disposition decision record).
  Quality lane: "Write disposition category to Inventory / ERP System" →
    Inventory / ERP System (disposition category and quantity).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inspection Record" — read by "Retrieve inspection record and
  disposition criteria".
Data Object "Disposition Criteria" — read by "Retrieve inspection record and
  disposition criteria".
Data Object "Repair Feasibility Report" — written by "Assess repair
  feasibility and estimated cost"; read by "Confirm final disposition
  decision".
Data Object "Disposition Decision" — written by "Confirm final disposition
  decision"; read by "Write disposition decision to Returns Management
  System" and "Write disposition category to Inventory / ERP System".

This subprocess takes inspected goods and assigns each item a formal
disposition — restock, repair, scrap, or return to supplier — using a
structured assessment involving Quality and, where needed, the Repairs team.
The confirmed disposition decision is persisted in the Returns Management
System and the Inventory / ERP System, giving Process Refund or Replacement
the commercial outcome it needs to trigger a refund or replacement, and
giving Update Inventory & Financials the category it needs to post the
correct stock and cost adjustments.
```


### V13.07 — Process Refund or Replacement

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement — the subprocess that executes
the financial settlement or goods replacement following an approved disposition
decision in the Return to Refund value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the company processing the refund or replacement,
  containing Finance and Customer Service teams.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Finance (finance officer)
  - Customer Service (customer service agent)
Pool "Customer" — the customer receiving the refund or replacement.
Pool "Payment Provider" — the external payment service that executes the
  monetary refund.
Pool "Billing / ERP System" — system of record for credit notes and billing
  transactions.
Pool "Payment Gateway" — system interface through which refund payments are
  submitted and confirmed.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Billing / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Payment Gateway" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Payment Provider
4. Billing / ERP System
5. Payment Gateway

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Finance lane:
  Message start event "Approved disposition decision received from Decide
    Disposition"
  User task "Review disposition outcome and determine settlement type"
  Exclusive gateway "Settlement type?"
  - branch "Refund":
      Service task "Retrieve original order and payment details from
        Billing / ERP System"
      User task "Raise credit note"
      Service task "Record credit note in Billing / ERP System"
      User task "Submit refund instruction to Payment Gateway"
      Intermediate message catch event "Refund confirmation received from
        Payment Gateway"
      User task "Confirm refund posted to customer account"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Settlement type"
  - branch "Replacement":
      Service task "Retrieve original order details from Billing / ERP System"
      User task "Raise replacement order"
      Service task "Record replacement order in Billing / ERP System"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Settlement type"
  User task "Verify refund authorisation limit compliance"
  Exclusive gateway "Within authorisation limit?"
  - branch "Yes":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Within authorisation limit"
  - branch "No — escalate":
      User task "Escalate to senior finance officer for approval"
      Intermediate message catch event "Escalation approval received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Within authorisation limit"
  End event "Settlement record finalised — ready for Update Inventory &
    Financials"

Customer Service lane:
  User task "Notify customer of refund or replacement decision"
  Send task "Send refund confirmation or replacement order confirmation
    to customer"
  User task "Issue credit note or dispatch confirmation to customer"

Note on flow: After "Exclusive merge gateway Within authorisation limit",
  flow passes to the Customer Service lane task "Notify customer of refund
  or replacement decision", then continues through the Customer Service lane
  tasks in order, ending at the End event in the Finance lane.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Escalate to senior finance officer for
  approval" — label "Escalation overdue (24 hours)" — triggers a Send task
  "Send escalation reminder" which rejoins the flow at "Intermediate message
  catch event Escalation approval received".
Interrupting error boundary event on "Submit refund instruction to Payment
  Gateway" — label "Payment Gateway error" — triggers User task "Log payment
  failure and retry or escalate" ending at an Error end event "Refund payment
  failed — escalate to Finance".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Finance lane at the message start event,
  proceeds to "Review disposition outcome and determine settlement type", then
  to the "Settlement type?" exclusive gateway. The Refund branch traverses
  retrieval, credit-note creation, recording, submission, confirmation catch
  event, and account confirmation before merging at "Exclusive merge gateway
  Settlement type". The Replacement branch traverses retrieval, replacement
  order creation, and recording before merging at the same gateway. Flow then
  moves to "Verify refund authorisation limit compliance" and the "Within
  authorisation limit?" gateway; the Yes branch merges immediately at
  "Exclusive merge gateway Within authorisation limit"; the No branch passes
  through escalation and approval catch event before merging. From the merge,
  flow crosses to the Customer Service lane for notification, confirmation
  dispatch, and credit note or dispatch confirmation tasks, then returns to the
  Finance lane end event.

Message flows:
  Billing / ERP System → Finance lane "Retrieve original order and payment
    details from Billing / ERP System" (original order and payment details).
  Finance lane "Record credit note in Billing / ERP System" → Billing / ERP
    System (credit note record).
  Finance lane "Record replacement order in Billing / ERP System" → Billing /
    ERP System (replacement order record).
  Finance lane "Submit refund instruction to Payment Gateway" → Payment
    Gateway (refund instruction).
  Payment Gateway → Finance lane "Refund confirmation received from Payment
    Gateway" (refund confirmation).
  Payment Gateway → Payment Provider (refund payment instruction).
  Payment Provider → Customer (refund payment).
  Customer Service lane "Send refund confirmation or replacement order
    confirmation to customer" → Customer (refund or replacement confirmation
    notification).
  Customer Service lane "Issue credit note or dispatch confirmation to
    customer" → Customer (credit note or dispatch confirmation document).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Disposition Decision" — read by "Review disposition outcome and
  determine settlement type".
Data Object "Credit Note" — written by "Raise credit note"; read by "Record
  credit note in Billing / ERP System"; read by "Issue credit note or dispatch
  confirmation to customer".
Data Object "Refund Instruction" — written by "Submit refund instruction to
  Payment Gateway"; read by Payment Gateway.
Data Object "Refund Confirmation" — written by "Confirm refund posted to
  customer account"; read by "Notify customer of refund or replacement
  decision".
Data Object "Replacement Order" — written by "Raise replacement order"; read
  by "Record replacement order in Billing / ERP System"; read by "Issue credit
  note or dispatch confirmation to customer".
Data Object "Original Order and Payment Record" — read by "Retrieve original
  order and payment details from Billing / ERP System"; read by "Retrieve
  original order details from Billing / ERP System".

This subprocess takes the approved disposition decision and converts it into a
concrete financial or logistical settlement: either a verified monetary refund
routed through the Payment Gateway and confirmed to the customer, or a
replacement order raised and confirmed in the Billing / ERP System. All credit
notes and replacement orders are recorded as the authoritative settlement
record. The completed and confirmed settlement, together with the credit note
or replacement order reference, is handed to Update Inventory & Financials so
that stock levels and the accounts receivable ledger can be adjusted
accordingly.
```


### V13.08 — Update Inventory & Financials

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials — the subprocess that posts
inventory adjustments and financial entries after disposition, handing a
complete ledger record to the next subprocess in the Return to Refund chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the company executing the return-to-refund
process, containing Warehouse and Finance lanes.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — the integrated inventory and enterprise
resource planning platform used for stock and financial records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Retail Organisation (white-box, process flow)
2. Inventory / ERP System (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Warehouse lane:
  Message start event "Disposition decision received from Decide Disposition"
  User task "Review disposition decision and stock adjustment requirements"
  Service task "Submit inventory adjustment to Inventory / ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Inventory adjustment confirmation received"
  User task "Confirm physical stock location or write-off in system"
  Exclusive gateway "Stock adjustment type?"
  - branch "Restock to available inventory": User task
    "Assign restocked units to bin location"
  - branch "Scrapped or written off": User task
    "Record write-off and remove units from stock register"
  - branch "Returned to supplier": User task
    "Mark units as pending supplier return and quarantine in system"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Stock adjustment type"
  User task "Verify inventory record accuracy against physical count"
  Send task "Send inventory update confirmation to Finance lane"

Finance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Inventory update confirmation received
  from Warehouse"
  User task "Retrieve refund or replacement cost data from completed
  transaction"
  Service task "Post credit note or cost entry to Billing / ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Financial posting confirmation received"
  User task "Reconcile refund amount against original order value"
  Exclusive gateway "Financial entries balanced?"
  - branch "Yes — balanced": User task "Mark financial record as
    reconciled"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found": Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Until
    Entries Balanced" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
    "Identify discrepancy source", User task "Correct entry in Billing /
    ERP System", Service task "Resubmit corrected posting"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Financial entries balanced"
  User task "File credit note and updated financial records"
  End event "Inventory and financials updated — ready for Recover Cost
  from Supplier"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Until
Entries Balanced", labelled "Reconciliation deadline exceeded (2 business
days)", triggering User task "Escalate unresolved discrepancy to Finance
Manager" followed by an End event "Escalated — process paused pending
Finance Manager resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Warehouse lane with the message start
event, progresses through inventory review, submission, and confirmation,
then through the stock adjustment type gateway whose three branches
(Restock, Scrapped or Written Off, Returned to Supplier) all rejoin at the
Exclusive merge gateway "Stock adjustment type", continuing to verification
and the send task. Flow crosses to the Finance lane at the intermediate
message catch event, proceeds through cost retrieval, posting, and
reconciliation, through the "Financial entries balanced?" gateway whose
Yes branch and the loop subprocess (with its timer boundary escalation
path) both rejoin at the Exclusive merge gateway "Financial entries
balanced", then on to filing and the end event.

Message flows:
Retail Organisation (Warehouse lane, "Submit inventory adjustment to
Inventory / ERP System") → Inventory / ERP System (inventory adjustment
request).
Inventory / ERP System → Retail Organisation (Warehouse lane, "Inventory
adjustment confirmation received") (stock adjustment confirmation).
Retail Organisation (Finance lane, "Post credit note or cost entry to
Billing / ERP System") → Inventory / ERP System (financial posting
request).
```

```text
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
```
