## V14 — Dock to Stock

**Teams and roles involved.**
Dock to Stock usually involves Inbound Logistics, Warehouse Operations, Goods Receipt, Quality Assurance, Inventory Control, Procurement, and Accounts Payable. Key roles include inbound coordinator, dock supervisor, goods-receipt clerk, quality inspector, putaway operator, inventory controller, buyer, and accounts payable officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Supplier, together with the Carrier delivering the goods. The process is initiated when a shipment arrives at the receiving dock against a purchase order or transfer order. Other external parties include customs brokers and freight forwarders for imported goods, third-party logistics providers, and testing or certification bodies.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: schedule the inbound delivery, receive the shipment at the dock, verify against the purchase order and delivery documents, unload and count, inspect quality and record any damage, record the goods receipt, put stock away to its location, handle discrepancies and rejections, release stock as available to promise, and match the receipt to the supplier invoice.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include warehouse management, ERP and inventory, purchase order and procurement systems, transport and yard management, barcode or RFID scanning, quality management, customs and trade compliance systems, and accounts payable/invoice matching.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include receiving and inspection procedure, tolerance rules for over- and under-delivery, quality acceptance criteria and sampling plans, damage and discrepancy reporting, segregation of duties between ordering and receiving, dangerous-goods and cold-chain handling, customs and import compliance, stock valuation rules, and three-way matching before payment.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The supplier and carrier provide advance shipping notices, delivery dockets and packing lists, certificates of analysis or conformance, customs documentation, and proof of delivery. The process provides the supplier and carrier with delivery booking slots, receipt confirmations, discrepancy and damage notifications, rejection notices, and returns instructions.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates inbound delivery records, goods receipts, inspection results, stock quantities and locations, quarantine and hold flags, discrepancy records, and accounts-payable matching entries. IT systems provide open purchase orders and expected quantities, item master and storage rules, available locations, quality specifications, and stock-availability and receipt-performance reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Receiving Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V14.01** Schedule Inbound Delivery | Supplier, Carrier | Inbound Logistics (inbound coordinator) | Transport & Yard Management System |
| **V14.02** Receive Shipment at Dock | Carrier | Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) | Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.03** Verify Against Purchase Order | Supplier | Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) | Procurement / ERP System |
| **V14.04** Unload & Count | Carrier | Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) | Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.05** Inspect Quality | — | Quality Assurance (quality inspector) | Quality Management System |
| **V14.06** Record Goods Receipt | — | Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) | Procurement / ERP System, Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.07** Put Stock Away | — | Warehouse Operations (putaway operator) | Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.08** Handle Discrepancies | Supplier, Customs Broker | Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk), Procurement (buyer) | Procurement / ERP System |
| **V14.09** Release Stock as Available | — | Inventory Control (inventory controller) | Inventory / ERP System |
| **V14.10** Match Receipt to Invoice | Supplier | Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) | Accounts Payable / ERP System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V14):

- **External actors:** Supplier (V14.01, V14.03, V14.08, V14.10); Carrier (V14.01, V14.02, V14.04); Customs Broker (V14.08).
- **Teams:** Inbound Logistics (V14.01); Warehouse Operations (V14.02, V14.04, V14.07); Goods Receipt (V14.03, V14.06, V14.08); Quality Assurance (V14.05); Procurement (V14.08); Inventory Control (V14.09); Accounts Payable (V14.10).
- **IT systems:** Transport & Yard Management System (V14.01); Warehouse Management System / WMS (V14.02, V14.04, V14.06, V14.07); Procurement / ERP System (V14.03, V14.06, V14.08); Quality Management System (V14.05); Inventory / ERP System (V14.09); Accounts Payable / ERP System (V14.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V14 — Dock to Stock — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Dock to Stock value chain, from the moment a supplier and carrier
initiate an inbound delivery to the point where a matched invoice is
ready for payment. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands
read top to bottom — BUSINESS SERVICES (top), BUSINESS PROCESSES
(middle), APPLICATIONS (bottom) — expressing ArchiMate service
realisation. Demand-side actors (Supplier, Carrier, Customs Broker)
sit on the far left; internal delivery teams occupy the centre; no
external settlement actor exists at the far right, so the rightmost
position is held by the Accounts Payable team completing invoice
matching.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Supplier: far left; initiates delivery booking, provides shipping
  documents and invoices, receives receipt confirmations and
  discrepancy notices.
- Carrier: far left, below Supplier; delivers goods to dock, provides
  proof of delivery, and participates in unloading.
- Customs Broker: far left, below Carrier; supports import compliance
  and discrepancy resolution for international shipments.
- Inbound Logistics team: centre-left; responsible for scheduling
  inbound deliveries (inbound coordinator).
- Warehouse Operations team: centre; responsible for dock receipt,
  unloading, counting, and putaway (dock supervisor, putaway operator).
- Goods Receipt team: centre; responsible for PO verification, goods
  receipt recording, and discrepancy handling (goods-receipt clerk).
- Quality Assurance team: centre; responsible for quality inspection
  (quality inspector).
- Procurement team: centre; supports discrepancy resolution and buyer
  decisions (buyer).
- Inventory Control team: centre-right; releases stock as available
  (inventory controller).
- Accounts Payable team: far right; performs invoice matching
  (accounts payable officer).

2. Interfaces

- Delivery Booking Interface: used by Supplier and Carrier to ACCESS
  the Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service; exposed by the Transport
  & Yard Management System.
- Shipping Document Interface: used by Supplier and Carrier to ACCESS
  the Shipment Receipt and PO Verification Services; carries advance
  shipping notices, packing lists, and delivery dockets.
- Discrepancy Notification Interface: used by Goods Receipt and
  Procurement teams to ACCESS the Discrepancy Handling Service and
  to inform the Supplier and Customs Broker of rejections or holds.
- Invoice Submission Interface: used by Supplier to ACCESS the Invoice
  Matching Service; carries supplier invoices for three-way matching.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service: provides delivery slot booking
  and advance shipment notice processing for inbound shipments.
- Shipment Receipt Service: provides dock-level acknowledgement of
  arriving carriers and goods.
- Purchase Order Verification Service: provides confirmation that
  arriving goods match an open purchase order and delivery documents.
- Unload & Count Service: provides supervised physical unloading and
  unit counting against expected quantities.
- Quality Inspection Service: provides inspection, sampling, and
  acceptance or rejection decisions against quality criteria.
- Goods Receipt Recording Service: provides formal recording of
  received quantities, storage locations, and valuation entries.
- Putaway Service: provides directed movement of stock to its
  designated warehouse location.
- Discrepancy Handling Service: provides investigation, reporting,
  and resolution of quantity, damage, or compliance discrepancies.
- Stock Release Service: provides updating of stock availability and
  release to available-to-promise for downstream demand.
- Invoice Matching Service: provides three-way matching of purchase
  order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice before payment approval.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band

- V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery: inbound coordinator books
  delivery slots and captures advance shipping notices.
- V14.02 Receive Shipment at Dock: dock supervisor acknowledges
  carrier arrival and registers inbound delivery in WMS.
- V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order: goods-receipt clerk checks
  delivery documents against open purchase order lines.
- V14.04 Unload & Count: dock supervisor oversees physical unloading
  and unit count, recording variances.
- V14.05 Inspect Quality: quality inspector performs sampling and
  inspection, logging results and raising holds if required.
- V14.06 Record Goods Receipt: goods-receipt clerk posts the goods
  receipt, updating stock quantities and triggering valuation.
- V14.07 Put Stock Away: putaway operator moves stock to directed
  locations and confirms putaway in WMS.
- V14.08 Handle Discrepancies: goods-receipt clerk and buyer manage
  short deliveries, damages, rejections, and customs issues.
- V14.09 Release Stock as Available: inventory controller removes
  quarantine flags and releases stock to available inventory.
- V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice: accounts payable officer performs
  three-way match and approves invoice for payment.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Transport & Yard Management System: manages delivery scheduling,
  slot booking, yard movements, and carrier communications.
- Warehouse Management System (WMS): manages dock registration,
  unloading, goods receipt posting, putaway direction, and
  stock-location records.
- Procurement / ERP System: manages open purchase orders, goods
  receipt documents, discrepancy records, and supplier master data.
- Quality Management System: manages inspection plans, sampling
  rules, quality results, certificates, and quarantine flags.
- Inventory / ERP System: manages stock quantities, availability
  flags, valuation, and available-to-promise updates.
- Accounts Payable / ERP System: manages invoice capture, three-way
  matching rules, payment approval, and supplier ledger entries.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- Transport & Yard Management System SERVES V14.01 Schedule
  Inbound Delivery.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.02 Receive Shipment
  at Dock.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V14.03 Verify Against
  Purchase Order.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.04 Unload & Count.
- Quality Management System SERVES V14.05 Inspect Quality.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V14.06 Record Goods Receipt.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.06 Record Goods Receipt.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.07 Put Stock Away.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.
- Inventory / ERP System SERVES V14.09 Release Stock as Available.
- Accounts Payable / ERP System SERVES V14.10 Match Receipt
  to Invoice.

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery REALISES Inbound Delivery
  Scheduling Service.
- V14.02 Receive Shipment at Dock REALISES Shipment Receipt Service.
- V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order REALISES Purchase Order
  Verification Service.
- V14.04 Unload & Count REALISES Unload & Count Service.
- V14.05 Inspect Quality REALISES Quality Inspection Service.
- V14.06 Record Goods Receipt REALISES Goods Receipt Recording
  Service.
- V14.07 Put Stock Away REALISES Putaway Service.
- V14.08 Handle Discrepancies REALISES Discrepancy Handling Service.
- V14.09 Release Stock as Available REALISES Stock Release Service.
- V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice REALISES Invoice Matching Service.

ASSIGNMENT (actor assigned to process):
- Inbound Logistics team ASSIGNED TO V14.01 Schedule Inbound
  Delivery.
- Warehouse Operations team ASSIGNED TO V14.02 Receive Shipment
  at Dock.
- Goods Receipt team ASSIGNED TO V14.03 Verify Against Purchase
  Order.
- Warehouse Operations team ASSIGNED TO V14.04 Unload & Count.
- Quality Assurance team ASSIGNED TO V14.05 Inspect Quality.
- Goods Receipt team ASSIGNED TO V14.06 Record Goods Receipt.
- Warehouse Operations team ASSIGNED TO V14.07 Put Stock Away.
- Goods Receipt team ASSIGNED TO V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.
- Procurement team ASSIGNED TO V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.
- Inventory Control team ASSIGNED TO V14.09 Release Stock as
  Available.
- Accounts Payable team ASSIGNED TO V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice.

ACCESS (external actor accesses service via interface):
- Supplier ACCESSES Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service via
  Delivery Booking Interface.
- Carrier ACCESSES Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service via
  Delivery Booking Interface.
- Carrier ACCESSES Shipment Receipt Service via Shipping Document
  Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Purchase Order Verification Service via
  Shipping Document Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Discrepancy Handling Service via Discrepancy
  Notification Interface.
- Customs Broker ACCESSES Discrepancy Handling Service via
  Discrepancy Notification Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Invoice Matching Service via Invoice Submission
  Interface.
```

```text
resolution workflows in V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.

Quality Management System holds quality specifications, sampling plans,
and acceptance criteria for V14.05 Inspect Quality.

Inventory / ERP System updates stock-availability flags and
available-to-promise quantities in V14.09 Release Stock as Available.

Accounts Payable / ERP System retrieves receipt records and supplier
invoice data to support three-way matching in
V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice.

The system boundary contains all ten subprocesses that move an inbound
shipment from dock arrival through to stock availability and invoice
matching. It serves three external actors — Supplier, Carrier, and
Customs Broker — who initiate or respond to the process, and seven
internal teams supported by six IT systems spanning yard management,
warehousing, procurement, quality, inventory, and accounts payable.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V14 - Dock to Stock

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron shape, one chevron per stage, in the order listed
below. The chevrons must flow continuously from left to right across the
diagram, each pointing into the next, with no branching or return paths.

V14.01. Schedule Inbound Delivery
V14.02. Receive Shipment at Dock
V14.03. Verify Against Purchase Order
V14.04. Unload & Count
V14.05. Inspect Quality
V14.06. Record Goods Receipt
V14.07. Put Stock Away
V14.08. Handle Discrepancies
V14.09. Release Stock as Available
V14.10. Match Receipt to Invoice

This chain governs the end-to-end movement of incoming goods from the moment
a shipment arrives at the receiving dock through to stock being available for
use and the supplier invoice being cleared for payment. It is triggered by a
Supplier and Carrier delivering goods against an open purchase order or
transfer order. The chain takes stock from physical arrival through
verification, counting, quality inspection, and putaway, resolving any
discrepancies along the way, before confirming inventory availability and
completing three-way invoice matching in Accounts Payable.
```
### V14.01 — Schedule Inbound Delivery

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery — opens the Dock to Stock value
chain by booking a delivery slot before any shipment arrives at the dock.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the company scheduling and coordinating
  inbound deliveries, containing all active process lanes.
  Lanes, top to bottom:
    - Inbound Logistics (inbound coordinator)

Pool "Supplier" — external party initiating contact and providing shipment
  information.
Pool "Carrier" — external party responsible for transporting and delivering
  the goods.
Pool "Transport & Yard Management System" — IT system managing yard slots,
  dock door assignments, and delivery booking records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Transport & Yard Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Carrier
4. Transport & Yard Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Inbound Logistics lane:
  Message start event "Advance shipping notice received from Supplier"
  User task "Review advance shipping notice and purchase order details"
  Exclusive gateway "Shipment details acceptable?"
  - branch "No — details incomplete or mismatched":
      Send task "Request corrected shipment information from Supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected shipment information
        received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Shipment details acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes — details confirmed":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Shipment details acceptable?"
      User task "Identify available dock door and yard slot"
      Service task "Check slot availability in Transport & Yard Management
        System"
      Exclusive gateway "Slot available at requested time?"
      - branch "No — no slot at requested time":
          User task "Propose alternative delivery window to Carrier"
          Intermediate message catch event "Carrier confirms alternative
            slot"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Slot available at requested time?"
      - branch "Yes — slot available":
          Exclusive merge gateway "Slot available at requested time?"
          Service task "Record delivery booking in Transport & Yard
            Management System"
          Send task "Send delivery booking confirmation to Carrier"
          Send task "Send booking acknowledgement to Supplier"
          User task "Prepare inbound delivery record and expected
            quantities"
          End event "Delivery slot confirmed — ready for Receive Shipment
            at Dock"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request corrected shipment
  information from Supplier" — label "Correction overdue (48 hours)" —
  leads to End event "Shipment scheduling failed — supplier notified,
  process abandoned".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Inbound Logistics lane carries the flow from
  the message start event through review, then into the "Shipment details
  acceptable?" gateway; the No branch sends a correction request and waits
  for a message catch event before rejoining the merge gateway; the Yes
  branch continues to slot identification and the "Slot available at
  requested time?" gateway; the No branch proposes an alternative window
  and waits for the carrier's confirmation message catch event before
  rejoining that merge gateway; the Yes branch proceeds through booking
  recording, confirmation sends, and inbound record preparation to the
  end event.

Message flows:
  Supplier → Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics (advance shipping
    notice with packing list and delivery docket)
  Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics → Supplier (request for
    corrected shipment information)
  Supplier → Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics (corrected
    shipment information)
  Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics → Carrier (proposed
    alternative delivery window)
  Carrier → Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics (confirmed delivery
    slot)
  Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics → Carrier (delivery booking
    confirmation with dock door and slot details)
  Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics → Supplier (booking
    acknowledgement)
  Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics →
    Transport & Yard Management System (slot availability query)
  Transport & Yard Management System → Receiving Organisation /
    Inbound Logistics (available slot data)
  Receiving Organisation / Inbound Logistics →
    Transport & Yard Management System (confirmed delivery booking record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Advance Shipping Notice" — read by "Review advance shipping
  notice and purchase order details"; written by Supplier (received at
  start event).
Data Object "Purchase Order Details" — read by "Review advance shipping
  notice and purchase order details".
Data Object "Corrected Shipment Information" — read by Exclusive merge
  gateway "Shipment details acceptable?"; written by "Request corrected
  shipment information from Supplier".
Data Object "Delivery Booking Confirmation" — written by "Send delivery
  booking confirmation to Carrier"; read by Carrier.
Data Object "Booking Acknowledgement" — written by "Send booking
  acknowledgement to Supplier"; read by Supplier.
Data Object "Inbound Delivery Record" — written by "Prepare inbound
  delivery record and expected quantities".

V14.01 coordinates everything that must happen before a truck arrives at
the dock: it validates the supplier's advance shipping notice against the
open purchase order, secures an available yard slot and dock door through
the Transport & Yard Management System, and issues confirmed booking
details to both the Carrier and the Supplier. The completed inbound
delivery record and confirmed slot are then handed to V14.02 Receive
Shipment at Dock, which takes over the moment the carrier presents at the
gate.
```


### V14.02 — Receive Shipment at Dock

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.02 Receive Shipment at Dock — second subprocess in the Dock to
Stock value chain, covering the physical arrival of the carrier at the
receiving dock, identity and documentation checks, and dock-door assignment
before verification against the purchase order begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the warehouse business receiving the
shipment, containing all active process lanes.
  Lane "Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor)" — manages dock arrival,
  checks credentials and documents, assigns a dock door, and confirms
  receipt of the shipment.
Pool "Carrier" — the external transport party delivering the goods.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — the IT system used to register
the inbound delivery, assign dock doors, and update shipment status.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Carrier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) lane:
  Message start event "Carrier arrives at dock from Schedule Inbound
  Delivery"
  User task "Check in carrier and verify driver identity"
  User task "Collect delivery documents from carrier"
  Exclusive gateway "Documents present and valid?"
  - branch "Documents missing or invalid": Send task "Request missing
    documents from carrier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Corrected documents received"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Documents present and valid?"
  - branch "Documents valid": Exclusive merge gateway "Documents present
    and valid?"
  User task "Match delivery to open inbound delivery record"
  Exclusive gateway "Delivery matches inbound record?"
  - branch "No match found": Send task "Notify carrier of mismatch and
    place on hold"
    End event "Shipment held — routed to Handle Discrepancies"
  - branch "Match confirmed": Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery matches
    inbound record?"
  Service task "Request dock-door assignment from WMS"
  Intermediate message catch event "Dock door assigned"
  User task "Direct carrier to assigned dock door"
  User task "Confirm shipment physically present at dock door"
  Service task "Update inbound delivery status to arrived in WMS"
  Send task "Issue dock receipt confirmation to carrier"
  End event "Shipment received at dock — ready for Verify Against
  Purchase Order"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request missing documents from
carrier" — label "Document wait timeout (30 minutes)" — if timer fires,
flow proceeds to Send task "Notify carrier of mismatch and place on hold"
then to End event "Shipment held — routed to Handle Discrepancies".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Warehouse Operations lane,
moving from the message start event through identity and document checks,
then through the "Documents present and valid?" exclusive gateway whose
invalid branch sends a document request and waits for a message catch
event before rejoining at the merge gateway; the valid branch rejoins
immediately. Flow continues to the inbound-record match gateway, whose
no-match branch ends at a hold event while the match-confirmed branch
rejoins and continues through dock-door request, intermediate catch,
physical confirmation, WMS status update, carrier confirmation, and the
end event.

Message flows:
Carrier → Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) (carrier arrival
notification and delivery documents)
Carrier → Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) (corrected documents, in
response to document request)
Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) → Carrier (request for missing
documents)
Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) → Carrier (dock receipt
confirmation)
Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) → Warehouse Management System
(WMS) (dock-door assignment request)
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Warehouse Operations (dock
supervisor) (dock door assigned)
Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) → Warehouse Management System
(WMS) (inbound delivery status update to arrived)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Delivery Documents (docket, packing list, ASN)" — read by
"Collect delivery documents from carrier"; read by "Match delivery to
open inbound delivery record".
Data Object "Driver Identity Record" — written by "Check in carrier and
verify driver identity".
Data Object "Inbound Delivery Record" — read by "Match delivery to open
inbound delivery record"; read by "Request dock-door assignment from WMS".
Data Object "Dock Receipt Confirmation" — written by "Issue dock receipt
confirmation to carrier".
assignment from WMS"; written by "Update inbound delivery status to
arrived in WMS".

V14.02 receives the carrier at the physical dock, validates driver
identity and delivery documents, matches the physical shipment to the
open inbound delivery record held in the WMS, and secures an assigned
dock door. The subprocess hands a dock-receipted, status-updated
inbound delivery record to V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order, where
the goods-receipt clerk will compare quantities and line items against
the purchase order in the Procurement / ERP System.
```


### V14.03 — Verify Against Purchase Order

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order — third subprocess in the
Dock to Stock value chain, following receipt of the shipment at the dock
and preceding unloading and counting.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation running the verification
process, containing the Goods Receipt team.
- Lane "Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk)"

Pool "Supplier" — external party that issued the purchase order documents
and delivery paperwork.

Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — IT system holding open purchase orders,
item master data, and tolerance rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Procurement / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) lane:
  Message start event "Shipment received at dock — handed over from
      Receive Shipment at Dock"
  User task "Collect delivery documents from carrier"
  Service task "Retrieve open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System"
  User task "Match delivery docket and packing list to purchase order"
  Exclusive gateway "Documents present and legible?"
    - branch "No — documents missing or illegible": User task "Request
          missing documents from supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected documents received
          from supplier"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Documents present and legible?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to next step
  Exclusive merge gateway "Documents present and legible?"
  User task "Verify item descriptions, quantities and units of measure
      against purchase order lines"
  Service task "Check quantities against tolerance rules in
      Procurement / ERP System"
  Exclusive gateway "Within tolerance and items match?"
    - branch "Yes — fully verified": continue to next step
    - branch "No — discrepancy or mismatch found": User task
          "Flag discrepancy and record variance against purchase order"
      Service task "Update discrepancy record in Procurement / ERP System"
      End event "Discrepancy flagged — routed to Handle Discrepancies"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Within tolerance and items match?"
  User task "Record verification result and sign off delivery documents"
  Service task "Post verification outcome to Procurement / ERP System"
  Send task "Send receipt confirmation to supplier"
  End event "Purchase order verified — ready for Unload & Count"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Request missing
documents from supplier" — label "48-hour document deadline exceeded" —
triggers Send task "Send escalation notice to buyer"; flow continues to
an escalation End event "Document escalation raised — buyer notified".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Goods Receipt lane.
After the start event the clerk collects documents, then retrieves the
purchase order, then matches documents. The exclusive gateway "Documents
present and legible?" splits to a document-request branch, which waits for
the corrected documents message and rejoins at the merge gateway, or passes
straight through the Yes branch to the same merge. Flow continues through
item and quantity verification to the tolerance gateway "Within tolerance
and items match?", whose No branch records the discrepancy and ends, while
the Yes branch continues through sign-off, posting, and confirmation before
reaching the final end event.

Message flows:
Procurement / ERP System → Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) (open
    purchase order, item master data, and tolerance rules retrieved by
    service task)
Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) → Procurement / ERP System
    (discrepancy record and verification outcome posted by service tasks)
Supplier → Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) (delivery docket, packing
    list, and certificates of analysis or conformance collected at start;
    corrected documents received at intermediate catch event)
Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) → Supplier (receipt confirmation
    sent by send task)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Delivery Docket" — read by "Match delivery docket and
    packing list to purchase order"; written by "Collect delivery documents
    from carrier".
Data Object "Packing List" — read by "Match delivery docket and packing
    list to purchase order"; written by "Collect delivery documents from
    carrier".
Data Object "Purchase Order" — read by "Match delivery docket and packing
    list to purchase order" and "Verify item descriptions, quantities and
    units of measure against purchase order lines"; written by "Retrieve
    open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System".
Data Object "Discrepancy Record" — written by "Flag discrepancy and record
    variance against purchase order"; read by "Update discrepancy record in
    Procurement / ERP System".
Data Object "Verification Outcome" — written by "Record verification result
    and sign off delivery documents"; read by "Post verification outcome to
    Procurement / ERP System".

This subprocess confirms that what has physically arrived at the dock
matches what was ordered: the goods-receipt clerk checks delivery documents
against the open purchase order, applies tolerance rules held in the
Procurement / ERP System, and either flags a discrepancy for handling later
or signs off the verification. A clean outcome passes a verified purchase
order record forward to Unload & Count, while any mismatch is streamed
directly to Handle Discrepancies.
```


### V14.04 — Unload & Count

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.04 Unload & Count — fourth subprocess in the Dock to Stock
value chain, following Verify Against Purchase Order and preceding Inspect
Quality.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the warehouse business running the unload
and count process, with lanes for Warehouse Operations.
Pool "Carrier" — the external transport party delivering the shipment at
the dock.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — the IT system recording
unload progress, item counts, and scan data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Carrier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Warehouse Operations lane (dock supervisor):
  Message start event "Shipment verified — received from Verify Against
    Purchase Order"
  User task "Brief unloading crew and assign dock positions"
  Service task "Retrieve unload instructions from WMS"
  User task "Unload goods from carrier vehicle"
  Intermediate message catch event "Carrier confirms unloading complete"
  User task "Stage goods in receiving area by purchase order line"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Lines Counted" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Scan or record item and quantity",
    Service task "Submit count against WMS expected quantity",
    User task "Resolve scan error or unreadable label"
  User task "Reconcile physical count totals with expected quantities"
  Exclusive gateway "Count within tolerance?"
    - branch "Yes — within tolerance": proceed to end event
    - branch "No — discrepancy found": User task "Flag discrepancy and
      annotate count record", then proceed to end event
  Exclusive merge gateway "Count within tolerance?"
  End event "Unload and count complete — ready for Inspect Quality"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Unload goods from carrier
vehicle", labelled "Unloading time limit exceeded", triggering User task
"Escalate delay to dock supervisor and notify carrier".

Non-interrupting escalation boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
Until All Lines Counted", labelled "Unreadable or missing label detected",
triggering User task "Request replacement label or documentation from
carrier".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Warehouse Operations lane with the
message start event and proceeds linearly through briefing, WMS retrieval,
unloading, the carrier confirmation catch event, staging, the counting
subprocess, reconciliation, and the tolerance gateway; the "Yes" branch and
the "No — discrepancy found" branch (after flagging) both converge at the
exclusive merge gateway before the end event.

Message flows:
Carrier → Receiving Organisation (advance unloading confirmation and
  proof of delivery handed to dock supervisor).
Receiving Organisation → Warehouse Management System (WMS) (unload
  instructions request; item scan and count submissions per line).
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Receiving Organisation (expected
  quantities, unload instructions, and real-time count acknowledgements
  returned to dock supervisor).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Packing List" — read by User task "Stage goods in receiving
  area by purchase order line".
Data Object "Unload Instructions" — read by User task "Brief unloading
  crew and assign dock positions"; written by Service task "Retrieve unload
  instructions from WMS".
Data Object "Physical Count Record" — written by Expanded Subprocess
  "Repeat Until All Lines Counted"; read by User task "Reconcile physical
  count totals with expected quantities".
Data Object "Discrepancy Annotation" — written by User task "Flag
  discrepancy and annotate count record".

V14.04 Unload & Count takes the verified shipment from the dock door and
produces a confirmed physical count against every purchase order line. The
warehouse crew unloads, stages, and scans each item, with the WMS tracking
expected versus actual quantities in real time. Any count outside tolerance
is flagged before the subprocess closes, giving the next stage, Inspect
Quality, a clean, annotated count record on which to base its sampling and
inspection decisions.
```


### V14.05 — Inspect Quality

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.05 Inspect Quality — fifth subprocess in the Dock to Stock
value chain, receiving unloaded and counted goods from Unload & Count
and passing accepted stock to Record Goods Receipt.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation conducting goods
inspection, with Quality Assurance as the single lane.
Pool "Quality Management System" — IT system supporting inspection
recording, results capture, and quarantine flagging.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Quality Management System": black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation (white-box, one lane)
2. Quality Management System (black-box)

No external parties participate in this subprocess.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Quality Assurance lane:
  Message start event "Unloaded and counted goods ready for inspection
    received from Unload & Count"
  User task "Retrieve quality specifications for items"
  Service task "Retrieve quality specifications from Quality Management
    System"
  User task "Select inspection sample per sampling plan"
  User task "Conduct physical and visual inspection"
  User task "Record inspection results and observations"
  Service task "Log inspection results in Quality Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Inspection outcome?"
    - branch "Accepted — all items meet quality criteria":
        User task "Apply accepted status and release to goods receipt"
        Service task "Update acceptance status in Quality Management System"
        End event "Goods accepted — ready for Record Goods Receipt"
    - branch "Conditional acceptance — minor non-conformances within
        tolerance":
        User task "Document non-conformance details and tolerance decision"
        Service task "Record conditional acceptance in Quality Management
          System"
        User task "Notify goods-receipt clerk of conditional acceptance
          with notes"
        End event "Goods conditionally accepted — ready for Record
          Goods Receipt with non-conformance notes"
    - branch "Rejected — items fail quality criteria":
        User task "Segregate and quarantine rejected goods"
        Service task "Raise quarantine and hold flag in Quality Management
          System"
        User task "Prepare rejection and damage report"
        Send task "Notify Handle Discrepancies of rejection"
        End event "Goods rejected — escalated to Handle Discrepancies"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The Quality Assurance lane runs in a single thread from
the message start event through specification retrieval, sample
selection, physical inspection, results recording, and the exclusive
gateway "Inspection outcome?". The accepted branch and the conditional
acceptance branch each complete with their own end events after updating
the Quality Management System; neither rejoins the rejected branch. The
rejected branch segregates goods, raises a quarantine flag, produces a
rejection report, and sends notification before its own end event. No
branches converge at the merge gateway because each terminates
independently; the merge gateway is present to formally close the
divergence for accepted and conditional paths should a modelling tool
require it.

Message flows:
  Quality Assurance lane → Quality Management System (quality
    specifications request)
  Quality Management System → Quality Assurance lane (quality
    specifications and sampling plan)
  Quality Assurance lane → Quality Management System (inspection
    results and observations)
  Quality Assurance lane → Quality Management System (acceptance,
    conditional acceptance, or quarantine and hold flag)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Quality Specifications" — read by "Retrieve quality
  specifications for items"; written by "Retrieve quality specifications
  from Quality Management System".
Data Object "Sampling Plan" — read by "Select inspection sample per
  sampling plan"; written by "Retrieve quality specifications from
  Quality Management System".
Data Object "Inspection Results Record" — written by "Record inspection
  results and observations"; read by "Log inspection results in Quality
  Management System".
Data Object "Non-Conformance Report" — written by "Document
  non-conformance details and tolerance decision"; read by "Record
  conditional acceptance in Quality Management System".
Data Object "Rejection and Damage Report" — written by "Prepare
  rejection and damage report"; read by "Send notification to Handle
  Discrepancies".

V14.05 Inspect Quality takes the unloaded and counted goods handed over
from Unload & Count and subjects them to structured sampling, physical
and visual examination, and results capture against defined quality
specifications. Accepted goods and conditionally accepted goods with
documented non-conformances are both forwarded to Record Goods Receipt,
carrying their inspection outcomes. Rejected goods are quarantined,
flagged in the Quality Management System, and escalated directly to
Handle Discrepancies so that returns and supplier notifications can
proceed without blocking the main receipt flow.
```

```text
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — the ERP and procurement system that

Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — the WMS that receives stock

2. Pool properties

Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — top.
Pool "Receiving Organisation" — middle (white-box, holds the flow).
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Goods Receipt lane (goods-receipt clerk):

Message start event "Inspection result received from Inspect Quality"
User task "Retrieve open purchase order and expected line items"
Service task "Pull goods-receipt data from Procurement / ERP System"
User task "Confirm received quantities and item details against PO lines"
Exclusive gateway "Quantities within tolerance?"
- branch "Yes — within tolerance": proceed to record goods receipt
- branch "No — outside tolerance": User task "Flag discrepancy and note
  variance on receipt record", then rejoin merge gateway
Exclusive merge gateway "Quantities within tolerance"
User task "Enter goods receipt details for each line"
Service task "Post goods receipt to Procurement / ERP System"
Intermediate message catch event "Goods receipt confirmation returned
from Procurement / ERP System"
User task "Assign stock to storage locations"
Service task "Update stock quantities and locations in WMS"
Intermediate message catch event "WMS location update confirmed"
User task "Apply quarantine or hold flags where required"
Exclusive gateway "Any lines under hold or quarantine?"
- branch "Yes — hold or quarantine required": Service task "Post
  quarantine flag to Procurement / ERP System", then rejoin merge gateway
- branch "No — all lines clear": proceed directly to merge gateway
Exclusive merge gateway "Any lines under hold or quarantine"
User task "Generate and issue goods receipt document"
End event "Goods receipt recorded — ready for Put Stock Away"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Enter goods receipt
details for each line" — label "Entry not completed within allotted
time" — triggers an escalation path to a supervisor review task, ending
in an escalation end event "Escalated to supervisor for resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work moves top to bottom through the Goods Receipt lane.
After "Quantities within tolerance?" the Yes branch continues to the merge
gateway and the No branch passes through the discrepancy flagging task
before rejoining the same merge gateway. After "Any lines under hold or
quarantine?" the Yes branch posts the quarantine flag and rejoins the merge
gateway; the No branch rejoins directly. The timer boundary event on
"Enter goods receipt details for each line" leaves the main flow and ends
at its own escalation end event without rejoining.

Message flows:
Service task "Pull goods-receipt data from Procurement / ERP System" →
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" (request for open PO and expected line
data).
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" → Service task "Pull goods-receipt data
from Procurement / ERP System" (open purchase order lines and expected
quantities).
Service task "Post goods receipt to Procurement / ERP System" → Pool
"Procurement / ERP System" (goods-receipt posting with quantities and
line details).
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" → Intermediate message catch event
"Goods receipt confirmation returned from Procurement / ERP System"
(confirmation of GR posting).
Service task "Post quarantine flag to Procurement / ERP System" → Pool
"Procurement / ERP System" (quarantine or hold flag per line).
Service task "Update stock quantities and locations in WMS" → Pool
"Warehouse Management System (WMS)" (stock quantity and location
update).
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" → Intermediate message catch
event "WMS location update confirmed" (confirmation of location record
update).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Goods Receipt Document" — written by User task "Generate
and issue goods receipt document"; read by User task "Enter goods receipt
details for each line".
Data Object "Inspection Result" — read by User task "Confirm received
quantities and item details against PO lines".
Data Object "Discrepancy Note" — written by User task "Flag discrepancy
and note variance on receipt record".
goods-receipt data from Procurement / ERP System"; updated by Service
task "Post goods receipt to Procurement / ERP System".
task "Update stock quantities and locations in WMS".
"Post quarantine flag to Procurement / ERP System".

V14.06 Record Goods Receipt takes the completed inspection outcome and
formally posts the goods receipt across both the ERP and the WMS,
reconciling received quantities against open purchase order lines,
flagging any out-of-tolerance variances, and setting quarantine holds
where required. It produces a confirmed goods receipt document and
updated stock records that serve as the foundation for the next
subprocess, Put Stock Away, which uses the assigned locations and
quantities to direct physical stock placement.
```


### V14.07 — Put Stock Away

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.07 Put Stock Away — the subprocess in which warehouse
operations moves received and inspected goods from the dock staging area
to their assigned storage locations, completing the physical inward flow
before stock is released as available.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the warehouse and operations teams
  executing the putaway process.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Warehouse Operations (putaway operator)
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — IT system directing
  putaway tasks and recording locations.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation (white-box, contains the process flow)
2. Warehouse Management System (WMS) (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Warehouse Operations lane:
  Message start event "Goods receipt confirmed — received from Record
    Goods Receipt"
  Service task "Retrieve putaway instructions from WMS"
  Exclusive gateway "Storage type required?"
  - branch "Ambient / standard storage": User task "Collect goods
      from staging area"
  - branch "Cold-chain or hazardous storage": User task "Apply
      special-handling controls and collect goods"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Storage type required?"
  Service task "Scan goods and confirm putaway task in WMS"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Location Confirmed" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Move goods to directed
    storage location", Service task "Scan location barcode or RFID
    tag", Exclusive gateway "Location scan accepted?",
    - branch "Accepted": continue,
    - branch "Rejected — location mismatch": User task "Correct
        location or reassign via WMS"
  Service task "Record stock location and quantity in WMS"
  Exclusive gateway "All putaway tasks complete?"
  - branch "No — further tasks remain": Intermediate message catch
      event "Next putaway task issued by WMS", then loop back to
      User task "Collect goods from staging area" via merge
  - branch "Yes — all tasks complete": continue
  Exclusive merge gateway "All putaway tasks complete?"
  User task "Confirm putaway completion and close inbound delivery"
  End event "Stock putaway complete — ready for Release Stock as
    Available"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Location Confirmed", labelled "Putaway time limit exceeded",
  leading to User task "Escalate putaway failure to dock supervisor"
  and then an End event "Putaway escalated — process terminated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Warehouse Operations
  lane. After the start event, putaway instructions are retrieved,
  then the storage-type gateway splits to the relevant collection
  task; both branches rejoin at the storage-type merge gateway before
  scanning. The loop subprocess handles repeated location attempts
  until confirmed. After WMS records the location, the completion
  gateway either issues a catch event for the next task (cycling back
  to collection) or, when all tasks are done, continues to final
  confirmation and the end event. The timer boundary on the loop
  subprocess exits to the escalation task and its own end event.

Message flows:
  Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Warehouse Operations lane
    (putaway instructions and directed location assignments)
  Warehouse Operations lane → Warehouse Management System (WMS)
    (location scan confirmations and stock-location updates)
  Warehouse Operations lane → Warehouse Management System (WMS)
    (putaway completion and inbound delivery closure)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Putaway Instructions" — read by "Retrieve putaway
  instructions from WMS"; read by "Scan goods and confirm putaway
  task in WMS".
Data Object "Inbound Delivery Record" — read by "Retrieve putaway
  instructions from WMS"; written by "Confirm putaway completion and
  close inbound delivery".
Data Object "Putaway Task List" — read by "Retrieve putaway
  instructions from WMS"; written by "Confirm putaway completion and
  close inbound delivery".

V14.07 Put Stock Away moves goods from the dock staging area to their
confirmed storage locations under direction from the WMS, scanning
each location to validate placement and recording the final quantity
and position against the inbound delivery. Special-handling rules are
applied for cold-chain or hazardous items. Once all putaway tasks are
closed and the inbound delivery is marked complete, the subprocess
hands a fully located and recorded stock position to V14.09 Release
Stock as Available.
```


### V14.08 — Handle Discrepancies

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.08 Handle Discrepancies — the subprocess that investigates,
communicates, and resolves quantity and quality discrepancies found during
receiving, sitting between Record Goods Receipt and Release Stock as Available
in the Dock to Stock value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the internal teams that investigate and
resolve discrepancies.
  Lane "Goods Receipt" — goods-receipt clerk who initiates and coordinates
  discrepancy handling.
  Lane "Procurement" — buyer who liaises with the supplier and decides
  resolution actions.
Pool "Supplier" — external party notified of discrepancies and from whom
responses and credits are sought.
Pool "Customs Broker" — external party consulted when discrepancies involve
import compliance or customs documentation.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — system that records discrepancy notices,
holds purchase order data, and tracks resolution outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Customs Broker" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Customs Broker
4. Procurement / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Goods Receipt lane:
  Message start event "Discrepancy identified — received from Record Goods
  Receipt"
  User task "Classify discrepancy type"
  Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy type?"
  - branch "Quantity discrepancy": User task "Prepare quantity discrepancy
    notice"
  - branch "Quality or damage discrepancy": User task "Prepare quality
    discrepancy notice"
  - branch "Documentation or customs discrepancy": Send task "Notify Customs
    Broker of documentation issue"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy type"
  Service task "Log discrepancy record in Procurement / ERP System"
  Send task "Send discrepancy notification to Supplier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
  User task "Review supplier response"
  Exclusive gateway "Response acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes — accept supplier resolution": User task "Update discrepancy
    record with agreed resolution"
  - branch "No — escalate to buyer": (continues in Procurement lane, see
    below)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Response acceptable"
  User task "Apply resolution to goods receipt record"
  Exclusive gateway "Goods to be returned?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Prepare return and rejection documentation"
    Send task "Send rejection notice and returns instructions to Supplier"
    End event "Goods returned — discrepancy closed"
  - branch "No — retain with adjustment": (flow continues to end below)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Goods to be returned"
  End event "Discrepancy resolved — ready for Release Stock as Available"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Assess escalated discrepancy"
  Exclusive gateway "Credit note or replacement required?"
  - branch "Credit note required": Send task "Request credit note from
    Supplier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Credit note received from Supplier"
    User task "Verify credit note against discrepancy"
  - branch "Replacement required": Send task "Request replacement delivery
    from Supplier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Replacement delivery confirmed by
    Supplier"
    User task "Arrange new inbound delivery booking"
  - branch "Write off — no supplier action": User task "Authorise inventory
    write-off"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Credit note or replacement required"
  (flow returns to Goods Receipt lane at exclusive merge gateway
  "Response acceptable")

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review supplier response" —
label "Supplier response overdue (5 business days)" — triggers Send task
"Send chaser to Supplier" which loops back into waiting for the supplier
response; modelled as Expanded Subprocess "Await Supplier Response" (standard
loop) containing: Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response
received", User task "Review supplier response", with interrupting timer
boundary event "Supplier response overdue (5 business days)" on the
subprocess — on expiry flow goes to User task "Escalate unresolved
discrepancy to buyer".

Interrupting error boundary event on Service task "Log discrepancy record in
Procurement / ERP System" — label "System error on discrepancy logging" —
triggers User task "Record discrepancy manually and alert IT support".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Goods Receipt lane, passes through
discrepancy classification and the three-branch exclusive gateway, rejoins at
the discrepancy type merge, then proceeds through system logging and supplier
notification. The process waits for a supplier response, reviews it, and at
the "Response acceptable" gateway either continues in Goods Receipt to apply
the resolution, or diverts to the Procurement lane for escalation. The
Procurement lane resolves through its own three-branch gateway (credit note,
replacement, or write-off) and rejoins at the Procurement merge before
returning the flow to the Goods Receipt merge gateway. From there the goods-
returned gateway splits: the return branch ends with rejection notices and its
own end event; the retain branch continues to the final end event.

Message flows:
Goods Receipt lane Send task "Send discrepancy notification to Supplier" →
Supplier (discrepancy notice with details of quantity, quality, or
documentation shortfall).
Supplier → Goods Receipt lane Intermediate message catch event "Supplier
response received" (supplier response, credit note offer, or replacement
proposal).
Procurement lane Send task "Request credit note from Supplier" → Supplier
(formal credit note request referencing purchase order and discrepancy
record).
Supplier → Procurement lane Intermediate message catch event "Credit note
received from Supplier" (credit note document).
Procurement lane Send task "Request replacement delivery from Supplier" →
Supplier (replacement delivery request).
Supplier → Procurement lane Intermediate message catch event "Replacement
delivery confirmed by Supplier" (replacement delivery confirmation).
Goods Receipt lane Send task "Send rejection notice and returns instructions
to Supplier" → Supplier (rejection notice and returns instructions).
Goods Receipt lane Send task "Notify Customs Broker of documentation issue"
→ Customs Broker (documentation discrepancy details requiring customs
advice).
Customs Broker → Goods Receipt lane (customs guidance or corrected
documentation — received as intermediate message catch event after
notification send task).
Service task "Log discrepancy record in Procurement / ERP System" →
Procurement / ERP System (discrepancy record, type, quantities, and status).
Procurement / ERP System → Goods Receipt lane User task "Classify
discrepancy type" (open purchase order data and expected quantities for
reference).
Goods Receipt lane User task "Update discrepancy record with agreed
resolution" → Procurement / ERP System (resolution outcome update).
Procurement lane User task "Verify credit note against discrepancy" →
Procurement / ERP System (matched credit note entry).
Procurement lane User task "Authorise inventory write-off" → Procurement /
ERP System (write-off authorisation record).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Discrepancy Notice" — written by User task "Prepare quantity
discrepancy notice" / User task "Prepare quality discrepancy notice" /
User task "Prepare return and rejection documentation"; read by Send task
"Send discrepancy notification to Supplier".
Data Object "Supplier Response" — written by (received via) Intermediate
message catch event "Supplier response received"; read by User task "Review
supplier response".
Data Object "Credit Note" — written by (received via) Intermediate message
catch event "Credit note received from Supplier"; read by User task "Verify
credit note against discrepancy".
Data Object "Rejection and Returns Documentation" — written by User task
"Prepare return and rejection documentation"; read by Send task "Send
rejection notice and returns instructions to Supplier".
task "Log discrepancy record in Procurement / ERP System" and User task
"Update discrepancy record with agreed resolution" and User task "Verify
credit note against discrepancy" and User task "Authorise inventory
write-off"; read by User task "Classify discrepancy type".

This subprocess takes ownership of every discrepancy surfaced during goods
receipt — quantity shortages or overages, quality failures, and documentation
or customs gaps — and drives each to a defined conclusion: an agreed
adjustment, a credit note, a replacement delivery, an inventory write-off, or
a physical return to the supplier. All outcomes are recorded in the
Procurement / ERP System so that the discrepancy register is current before
the next subprocess, Release Stock as Available, acts on the corrected stock
position.
```


### V14.09 — Release Stock as Available

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.09 Release Stock as Available — the subprocess in which
Inventory Control confirms inspection clearance and removes holds so that
stock becomes available to promise within the Dock to Stock value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out the
stock-release process.
  Lane "Inventory Control (inventory controller)" — reviews hold status,
  resolves quarantine conditions, updates availability flags, and confirms
  release.

Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — the system that holds stock quantities,
hold flags, and availability records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation
2. Inventory / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Inventory Control lane:
  Message start event "Goods receipt and inspection results received
    from Record Goods Receipt"
  Service task "Retrieve current hold and quarantine flags"
  Exclusive gateway "Stock on hold or in quarantine?"
  - branch "No holds — cleared for release":
      User task "Confirm stock quantity and location details"
      Service task "Update stock status to Available in Inventory / ERP
        System"
      Send task "Send stock-availability notification"
      End event "Stock released as available — ready for Match Receipt
        to Invoice"
  - branch "Hold or quarantine flag present":
      User task "Review reason for hold"
      Exclusive gateway "Hold can be resolved now?"
      - branch "Yes — resolve hold":
          User task "Clear hold condition and document resolution"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Hold resolution complete"
      - branch "No — escalate":
          Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Hold Resolved"
            (standard loop) containing, in order:
            User task "Liaise with Quality Assurance or Goods Receipt
              to resolve hold",
            Intermediate message catch event "Updated clearance
              decision received",
            User task "Re-assess hold status"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Hold resolution complete"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Hold resolution complete"
      Service task "Update stock status to Available in Inventory / ERP
        System"
      Send task "Send stock-availability notification"
      End event "Stock released as available — ready for Match Receipt
        to Invoice"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Stock on hold or in quarantine?"

Note: the merge gateway for the top-level "Stock on hold or in
quarantine?" gateway is placed after the Send task in each branch; each
branch terminates at its own End event so no rejoining merge is needed
at the outer level.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Hold Resolved" — label "Hold resolution deadline exceeded" — triggers an
escalation path ending in an error end event "Hold unresolved —
escalated to Procurement".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Inventory Control lane at the message
start event, proceeds to retrieve hold flags, then to the gateway "Stock
on hold or in quarantine?". The cleared branch runs through quantity
confirmation, status update, notification, and end event. The hold
branch runs through hold review, inner gateway "Hold can be resolved
now?", with the "Yes" path clearing the hold and the "No" path entering
the loop subprocess; both rejoin at the inner exclusive merge gateway
"Hold resolution complete" before continuing to the status update,
notification, and end event.

Message flows:
Inventory / ERP System → Inventory Control lane (current hold flags,
  quarantine status, stock quantities and locations)
Inventory Control lane → Inventory / ERP System (updated stock
  availability flag and hold clearance record)
Inventory Control lane → Inventory / ERP System (availability release
  confirmation written to stock record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Hold and Quarantine Flag Report" — read by "Review reason
  for hold"; written by "Retrieve current hold and quarantine flags".
Data Object "Hold Resolution Record" — written by "Clear hold condition
  and document resolution"; read by "Update stock status to Available in
  Inventory / ERP System".
Data Object "Stock Availability Notification" — written by "Send
  stock-availability notification".

This subprocess takes the confirmed goods receipt and inspection outcome
from Record Goods Receipt and systematically removes any hold or
quarantine flags that stand between physical stock and its commercial
availability. Where holds cannot be cleared immediately, a supervised
loop engages relevant teams until the condition is resolved or escalated.
Once cleared, the inventory record is updated and a stock-availability
notification is issued, handing a fully available stock position to the
final subprocess, Match Receipt to Invoice.
```


### V14.10 — Match Receipt to Invoice

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice — final subprocess of the Dock to
Stock value chain, closing the financial loop by matching the confirmed
goods receipt to the supplier invoice before approving payment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the company processing the invoice match.
  Lane "Accounts Payable" — accounts payable officer performing matching
  and payment approval steps.

Pool "Supplier" — external party that submits the invoice and receives
  payment confirmation or dispute notification.

Pool "Accounts Payable / ERP System" — IT system that holds invoice
  records, goods-receipt data, purchase order data, and processes the
  three-way match and payment entry.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Accounts Payable / ERP System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Accounts Payable / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Accounts Payable lane:
  Message start event "Goods receipt confirmed — received from Release
    Stock as Available"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier invoice received"
  Service task "Retrieve open purchase order and goods-receipt record"
  Service task "Run three-way match — purchase order, goods receipt,
    invoice"
  Exclusive gateway "Match result?"
    - branch "Matched within tolerance": User task "Review and approve
        matched invoice"
      Service task "Post payment entry in Accounts Payable / ERP System"
      Send task "Send payment confirmation to Supplier"
      End event "Invoice matched and payment posted — process complete"
    - branch "Discrepancy found": User task "Identify and classify
        discrepancy — price, quantity, or tax variance"
      Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy resolvable internally?"
        - branch "Yes — minor variance within policy": User task "Apply
            tolerance adjustment and approve invoice"
          Service task "Post adjusted payment entry in Accounts Payable /
            ERP System"
          Send task "Send payment confirmation to Supplier"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolvable internally"
          End event "Invoice matched and payment posted — process complete"
        - branch "No — requires supplier correction": Send task "Send
            dispute notification to Supplier"
          Intermediate message catch event "Corrected invoice received
            from Supplier"
          Service task "Re-run three-way match on corrected invoice"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolvable internally"
          End event "Invoice matched and payment posted — process complete"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Match result"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Identify and classify
  discrepancy — price, quantity, or tax variance" — label "Dispute
  resolution deadline exceeded" — triggers Send task "Escalate unresolved
  dispute to buyer and Accounts Payable manager" followed by End event
  "Invoice dispute escalated — process closed pending manual resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the flow begins in the Accounts Payable lane with the
  message start event, moves to the intermediate message catch event
  awaiting the supplier invoice, then to the two service tasks that
  retrieve and match records, then to the "Match result" exclusive
  gateway. The matched branch proceeds through approval, posting, and
  the send task to its end event, then merges at "Match result". The
  discrepancy branch proceeds to classification; from the inner
  "Discrepancy resolvable internally" gateway the yes-branch applies a
  tolerance adjustment, posts, and sends confirmation before rejoining
  the inner merge, while the no-branch sends a dispute notification,
  waits for a corrected invoice, re-runs the match, and rejoins the
  same inner merge, which then leads to its own end event.

Message flows:
  Supplier → Accounts Payable lane (supplier invoice submitted)
  Supplier → Accounts Payable lane (corrected invoice submitted)
  Accounts Payable lane → Supplier (dispute notification)
  Accounts Payable lane → Supplier (payment confirmation)
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (retrieve
    purchase order and goods-receipt record)
  Accounts Payable / ERP System → Accounts Payable lane (purchase order,
    goods-receipt, and invoice data returned)
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (three-way
    match execution request)
  Accounts Payable / ERP System → Accounts Payable lane (match result
    returned)
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (payment entry
    posted)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Supplier Invoice" — read by Service task "Run three-way
  match — purchase order, goods receipt, invoice"; written by
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier invoice received".
Data Object "Corrected Invoice" — read by Service task "Re-run
  three-way match on corrected invoice"; written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Corrected invoice received from Supplier".
Data Object "Discrepancy Record" — written by User task "Identify and
  classify discrepancy — price, quantity, or tax variance"; read by
  User task "Apply tolerance adjustment and approve invoice".

Match Receipt to Invoice closes the Dock to Stock value chain by
performing a three-way match across the purchase order, the confirmed
goods receipt, and the supplier invoice. Invoices that match within
tolerance are approved and posted for payment; discrepancies are either
resolved through a policy-permitted tolerance adjustment or returned to
the supplier for correction. Once payment is posted and the supplier
notified, the financial obligations arising from the inbound shipment
are fully settled and the chain is complete.
```


## V15 — Detect to Repair

**Teams and roles involved.**
Detect to Repair usually involves Maintenance, Reliability Engineering, Operations, Field Service, Planning and Scheduling, Spare Parts/Stores, Health and Safety, and Finance for cost capture. Key roles include maintenance planner, reliability engineer, condition-monitoring analyst, maintenance technician, field service engineer, scheduler, storeperson, safety officer, and asset manager.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are the Equipment Owner or Operator who reports the fault, and specialist Service Contractors or the Original Equipment Manufacturer where work is outsourced. The process is initiated by a fault report, an alarm or condition-monitoring exception, an inspection finding, or a preventive maintenance schedule falling due. Other external parties include parts suppliers, calibration and testing services, and regulators for safety-critical assets.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: detect the fault or condition exception, raise and triage the notification, assess criticality and safety impact, diagnose the fault, plan the work and required parts, schedule the work and secure permits, execute the repair, test and return the asset to service, close the work order and capture costs, and analyse failure causes to prevent recurrence.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include enterprise asset management or computerised maintenance management, condition-monitoring and IoT/SCADA platforms, work-order and field-service management, spare-parts inventory, permit-to-work and safety systems, document management for drawings and manuals, procurement for contracted services, and reliability analytics.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include asset criticality classification, maintenance strategy and preventive schedules, permit-to-work and isolation procedures, safety and lock-out/tag-out rules, spare-parts stocking policy, contractor approval and induction, warranty claim procedure, calibration and statutory inspection requirements, and cost capitalisation versus expense rules.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The operator or owner provides fault reports, symptoms and operating context, access windows, and confirmation that the asset can be taken offline. Contractors provide quotes, method statements, work completion reports and certificates. The process provides fault acknowledgements, expected downtime and schedules, work instructions and permits, completion and return-to-service notifications, and warranty or claim documentation.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates notifications, work orders, diagnoses, parts reservations and issues, labour and cost postings, permits, test results, and asset history. IT systems provide asset registers and hierarchies, condition and alarm data, maintenance history and failure codes, parts availability, technician skills and availability, and reliability and downtime reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Asset Owner Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT
systems are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V15.01** Detect Fault or Condition Exception | Equipment Operator | Reliability Engineering (condition-monitoring analyst) | Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform |

- **Teams:** Reliability Engineering (V15.01, V15.03, V15.04, V15.10); Maintenance (V15.02, V15.04, V15.05, V15.07–V15.09); Health & Safety (V15.03, V15.06); Spare Parts (V15.05); Planning & Scheduling (V15.06); Field Service (V15.07); Operations (V15.08); Finance (V15.09).
