**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V15 — Detect to Repair — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Detect to Repair value chain, from the moment a fault or condition
exception is detected through to failure-cause analysis and work-order
closure. The diagram is arranged in three horizontal bands, read top to
bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) → BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) →
APPLICATIONS (bottom band). The demand-side actor (Equipment Operator) sits
on the far left; delivery and settlement actors (Original Equipment
Manufacturer, Service Contractor) sit on the far right. Reading top-to-bottom
follows ArchiMate service realisation: each business service is realised by
one or more business processes, which are in turn supported by application
components below them.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Equipment Operator — far left; initiates fault reports, provides access
  windows, and confirms return to service.
- Original Equipment Manufacturer — far right; provides specialist
  diagnostic support for complex faults.
- Service Contractor — far right; executes outsourced repair work and
  supplies completion certificates.

2. Interfaces

- Fault Reporting Interface — used by Equipment Operator to ACCESS the
  Fault Detection & Notification Service; served by V15.01 and V15.02.
- Return-to-Service Confirmation Interface — used by Equipment Operator to
  ACCESS the Asset Return to Service; served by V15.08.
- Diagnostic Support Interface — used by Original Equipment Manufacturer
  to ACCESS the Fault Diagnosis Service; served by V15.04.
- Contractor Work Interface — used by Service Contractor to ACCESS the
  Work Execution & Permitting Service; served by V15.06 and V15.07.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Fault Detection & Notification Service — provides timely identification
  and acknowledgement of equipment faults and condition exceptions.
- Criticality & Safety Assessment Service — provides structured evaluation
  of asset criticality and safety impact before work begins.
- Fault Diagnosis Service — provides root-cause identification and
  technical advice to support repair planning.
- Work Planning & Parts Provision Service — provides complete work scope,
  bill of materials, and parts reservation for the repair.
- Work Scheduling & Permitting Service — provides confirmed work schedule,
  contractor co-ordination, and valid permits to work.
- Repair Execution Service — provides safe, controlled execution of the
  repair by qualified technicians or contractors.
- Asset Return to Service — provides tested confirmation that the asset
  meets required performance standards and is safe to operate.
- Work Order Closure & Cost Capture Service — provides accurate financial
  posting, work-order closure, and warranty documentation.
- Failure Analysis & Reliability Improvement Service — provides
  structured failure-cause analysis and improvement recommendations.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V15.01 Detect Fault or Condition Exception — monitors asset condition
  data and raises an initial alert or alarm.
- V15.02 Raise & Triage Notification — creates a formal notification,
  classifies the fault type, and assigns initial priority.
- V15.03 Assess Criticality & Safety Impact — evaluates asset criticality
  classification and any safety implications before progressing.
- V15.04 Diagnose Fault — investigates symptoms, reviews history, and
  establishes root cause with specialist support where needed.
- V15.05 Plan Work & Parts — defines work scope, identifies required
  parts, and reserves or procures materials.
- V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure Permits — confirms resource and time
  schedule, engages contractors, and issues permits to work.
- V15.07 Execute Repair — carries out the physical repair in line with
  work instructions, permits, and safety rules.
- V15.08 Test & Return to Service — tests repaired asset against
  acceptance criteria and obtains operational sign-off.
- V15.09 Close Work Order & Capture Costs — posts labour, parts and
  contractor costs, closes the work order, and records asset history.
- V15.10 Analyse Failure Causes — performs reliability analysis on failure
  data and recommends preventive or design improvements.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform — collects and streams real-time
  asset condition, alarm, and sensor data.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) — manages asset register, work
  orders, maintenance history, failure codes, and cost postings.
- Document Management System — stores and serves engineering drawings,
  maintenance manuals, and technical specifications.
- Spare Parts Inventory System — manages parts catalogue, stock levels,
  reservations, and issues.
- Permit-to-Work System — issues, controls, and closes permits to work
  and isolation certificates.
- Work Order Management System — manages field work-order assignment,
  progress tracking, and completion recording.
- Finance / ERP System — receives cost postings from EAM, manages
  capitalisation versus expense rules, and supports financial reporting.
- Reliability Analytics Platform — aggregates failure data, supports
  root-cause analysis, and produces reliability and downtime reports.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process):
- Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform SERVES V15.01 Detect Fault or
  Condition Exception.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.02 Raise & Triage
  Notification.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.03 Assess Criticality &
  Safety Impact.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.04 Diagnose Fault.
- Document Management System SERVES V15.04 Diagnose Fault.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.05 Plan Work & Parts.
- Spare Parts Inventory System SERVES V15.05 Plan Work & Parts.
- Permit-to-Work System SERVES V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure Permits.
- Work Order Management System SERVES V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure
  Permits.
- Work Order Management System SERVES V15.07 Execute Repair.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.08 Test & Return to
  Service.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.09 Close Work Order &
  Capture Costs.
- Finance / ERP System SERVES V15.09 Close Work Order & Capture Costs.
- Reliability Analytics Platform SERVES V15.10 Analyse Failure Causes.

REALISATION (business process REALISES business service):
- V15.01 and V15.02 REALISE Fault Detection & Notification Service.
- V15.03 REALISES Criticality & Safety Assessment Service.
- V15.04 REALISES Fault Diagnosis Service.
- V15.05 REALISES Work Planning & Parts Provision Service.
- V15.06 REALISES Work Scheduling & Permitting Service.
- V15.07 REALISES Repair Execution Service.
- V15.08 REALISES Asset Return to Service.
- V15.09 REALISES Work Order Closure & Cost Capture Service.
- V15.10 REALISES Failure Analysis & Reliability Improvement Service.

ASSIGNMENT (business actor ASSIGNED TO interface):
- Equipment Operator ASSIGNED TO Fault Reporting Interface.
- Equipment Operator ASSIGNED TO Return-to-Service Confirmation
  Interface.
- Original Equipment Manufacturer ASSIGNED TO Diagnostic Support
  Interface.
- Service Contractor ASSIGNED TO Contractor Work Interface.

ACCESS (interface ACCESSES business service):
- Fault Reporting Interface ACCESSES Fault Detection & Notification
  Service.
- Return-to-Service Confirmation Interface ACCESSES Asset Return to
  Service.
- Diagnostic Support Interface ACCESSES Fault Diagnosis Service.
- Contractor Work Interface ACCESSES Work Scheduling & Permitting Service.
- Contractor Work Interface ACCESSES Repair Execution Service.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V15 - Detect to Repair

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right, in the order listed below. One
chevron per stage; no substeps inside the chevrons on this diagram.

V15.01. Detect Fault or Condition Exception
V15.02. Raise & Triage Notification
V15.03. Assess Criticality & Safety Impact
V15.04. Diagnose Fault
V15.05. Plan Work & Parts
V15.06. Schedule Work & Secure Permits
V15.07. Execute Repair
V15.08. Test & Return to Service
V15.09. Close Work Order & Capture Costs
V15.10. Analyse Failure Causes

This chain covers the end-to-end maintenance response from the moment a
fault or condition exception is detected through to structured failure
analysis and prevention of recurrence. It is triggered by the Equipment
Operator reporting a fault, an alarm or condition-monitoring exception
from the Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform, an inspection finding,
or a preventive maintenance schedule falling due. The chain delivers a
repaired, tested, and returned-to-service asset together with closed
work orders, captured costs, and reliability insights that feed back into
maintenance strategy.
```

### V15.01 — Detect Fault or Condition Exception

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.01 Detect Fault or Condition Exception — first subprocess in the
Detect to Repair value chain, capturing how faults and condition exceptions
are first identified and passed to notification raising.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation running the detection
process, containing Reliability Engineering.
  Lane "Reliability Engineering (condition-monitoring analyst)" — receives
  signals, reviews exceptions, confirms and escalates detected faults.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — external party who reports observed faults or
abnormal symptoms from the field.
Pool "Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform" — the IT system supplying
continuous sensor, alarm and condition data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Equipment Operator": black-box, single instance.
Pool "Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform": black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Equipment Operator
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Reliability Engineering (condition-monitoring analyst) lane:
  Message start event "Fault report or condition exception received from
    Equipment Operator or Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform"
  User task "Review incoming signal or fault report"
  Exclusive gateway "Signal source type?"
    - branch "Operator-reported fault": User task "Capture reported symptoms
      and operating context"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Signal source type"
    - branch "Condition monitoring or SCADA alarm": Service task "Retrieve
      alarm and sensor data from Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Signal source type"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Signal source type"
  User task "Assess signal validity and rule out false positive"
  Exclusive gateway "Valid exception confirmed?"
    - branch "No — false positive": End event "False positive logged — no
      further action"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Record confirmed fault or condition exception"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Valid exception confirmed?"
  User task "Classify initial fault type and affected asset"
  User task "Send fault acknowledgement to Equipment Operator"
  End event "Confirmed fault or condition exception ready for Raise and
    Triage Notification"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins at the message start event in the Reliability
Engineering lane and proceeds through the signal-review task to the
exclusive gateway "Signal source type?", whose "Operator-reported fault"
branch runs through symptom capture and whose "Condition monitoring or SCADA
alarm" branch runs through data retrieval; both branches rejoin at the
exclusive merge gateway "Signal source type" before continuing through
validity assessment to the exclusive gateway "Valid exception confirmed?";
the "No" branch ends at its own end event and does not rejoin; the "Yes"
branch passes through the merge gateway before continuing through fault
recording, asset classification, and acknowledgement to the final end event.

Message flows:
Equipment Operator → Asset Owner Organisation / Reliability Engineering
  (fault report with symptoms and operating context)
Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform → Asset Owner Organisation /
  Reliability Engineering (alarm event and sensor data stream)
Asset Owner Organisation / Reliability Engineering → Equipment Operator
  (fault acknowledgement)
Asset Owner Organisation / Reliability Engineering →
  Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform (query for alarm and sensor data)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Fault Report" — written by "Capture reported symptoms and
  operating context"; read by "Assess signal validity and rule out false
  positive".
Data Object "Alarm and Sensor Data" — written by "Retrieve alarm and sensor
  data from Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform"; read by "Assess signal
  validity and rule out false positive".
Data Object "Confirmed Fault or Condition Exception Record" — written by
  "Record confirmed fault or condition exception"; read by "Classify initial
  fault type and affected asset".

This subprocess establishes that a genuine fault or condition exception
exists, distinguishing confirmed detections from false positives and
capturing the initial symptoms, signal data, and affected asset. It hands
a classified, confirmed fault record to Raise and Triage Notification,
where a formal work notification will be created and prioritised.
```


### V15.02 — Raise & Triage Notification

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.02 Raise & Triage Notification — second subprocess in the
Detect to Repair value chain, receiving a detected fault or condition
exception and producing a triaged notification ready for criticality
assessment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the maintenance and planning teams
that raise, validate and triage the notification.
  Lane "Maintenance" — maintenance planner who receives the alert,
  raises the work notification and triages it.
Lane "Equipment Operator" — external party who reported the fault and
confirms or supplements symptom details.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — the CMMS/EAM system used
to create and record the notification and work order.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Equipment Operator
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Fault or condition exception received from
  Detect Fault or Condition Exception"
  User task "Review incoming alert and confirm receipt"
  User task "Raise notification in EAM"
  Service task "Retrieve asset register details from EAM"
  User task "Record fault symptoms and operating context"
  Intermediate message catch event "Operator provides additional
  symptom details"
  User task "Validate and enrich notification with operator input"
  Exclusive gateway "Notification information sufficient?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to triage
    - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Notification
      Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
      "Request missing information from operator", Intermediate
      message catch event "Operator responds with information", User
      task "Update notification record in EAM"
      Timer boundary event on subprocess labelled "24-hour follow-up
      limit" — interrupting; on expiry: User task "Escalate
      incomplete notification to supervisor", then rejoin at
      Exclusive merge gateway "Notification information sufficient"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Notification information sufficient"
  User task "Classify notification type and work category"
  User task "Assign initial priority based on asset criticality
  and reported symptoms"
  Exclusive gateway "Valid maintenance notification?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to triage review
    - branch "No — duplicate or non-maintenance": User task
      "Close or redirect notification", then End event
      "Notification closed or redirected — no further action"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Valid maintenance notification"
  User task "Assign notification to responsible maintenance planner"
  User task "Confirm notification triage complete and update status
  in EAM"
  End event "Triaged notification confirmed — ready for Assess
  Criticality and Safety Impact"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "24-hour follow-up limit" mounted
on the Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Notification Complete";
on expiry the flow leaves the loop and enters User task "Escalate
incomplete notification to supervisor", then rejoins the main flow
at the Exclusive merge gateway "Notification information sufficient".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: All flow runs within the Maintenance lane from the
message start event forward through the review, raise, retrieve,
record and validate tasks, pausing at the intermediate message catch
event for operator input, then through the loop gateway and its
merge, into classification, priority assignment, the validity
gateway and its merge, and finally through the assignment and
status-update tasks to the end event. The "No" branch of the
validity gateway leads to the close/redirect task and terminates at
its own end event without rejoining.

Message flows:
Equipment Operator → Asset Owner Organisation / Maintenance
(initial fault report triggering the start event)
Equipment Operator → Asset Owner Organisation / Maintenance
(additional symptom details caught by the intermediate message
catch event and by responses within the loop)
Asset Owner Organisation / Maintenance → Equipment Operator
(request for missing information sent during the loop)
Asset Owner Organisation / Maintenance →
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (notification creation and
record update via "Raise notification in EAM" and "Update
notification record in EAM")
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Asset Owner Organisation /
Maintenance (asset register and criticality data returned to
"Retrieve asset register details from EAM")
Asset Owner Organisation / Maintenance →
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (final status update via
"Confirm notification triage complete and update status in EAM")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Fault Alert / Condition Exception Report" — read by
"Review incoming alert and confirm receipt"; written by the upstream
Detect Fault or Condition Exception subprocess.
Data Object "Maintenance Notification" — written by "Raise
notification in EAM"; read by "Record fault symptoms and operating
context", "Validate and enrich notification with operator input",
"Update notification record in EAM", and "Classify notification
type and work category".
details from EAM".
Data Object "Operator Symptom Statement" — written by "Validate
and enrich notification with operator input"; read by "Assign
initial priority based on asset criticality and reported symptoms".
Data Object "Triaged Notification Record" — written by "Confirm
notification triage complete and update status in EAM"; read by the
downstream Assess Criticality and Safety Impact subprocess.

This subprocess converts a raw fault alert or condition exception
into a validated, enriched and prioritised maintenance notification
held in the EAM. It draws on the Equipment Operator to fill any
gaps in symptom detail and screens out duplicates or non-maintenance
items. The completed, triaged notification record is handed to
Assess Criticality and Safety Impact, which will determine the
urgency, risk and safety implications before diagnosis is authorised.
```


### V15.03 — Assess Criticality & Safety Impact

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.03 Assess Criticality & Safety Impact — third subprocess in the
Detect to Repair value chain, receiving a triaged notification from Raise &
Triage Notification and handing a criticality-assessed work order to Diagnose
Fault.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the internal organisation running the
assessment process, containing Reliability Engineering and Health & Safety
lanes.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — the EAM system used to retrieve
asset data and record assessment outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Owner Organisation (white-box, spans full width)
2. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Reliability Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Triaged notification received from Raise and Triage
    Notification"
  Service task "Retrieve asset register and criticality classification"
  User task "Review asset criticality and production impact"
  User task "Document consequence of failure and downtime exposure"
  Exclusive gateway "Criticality level determined?"
  - branch "Further information needed":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Criticality Confirmed" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Request additional asset or operating
        context", Intermediate message catch event "Additional information
        received", User task "Re-evaluate criticality classification"
  - branch "Criticality confirmed":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Criticality level determined"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Criticality level determined"
  User task "Assign criticality rating and record in EAM"
  Exclusive gateway "Safety-critical asset?"
  - branch "Yes — safety implications identified":
      (continues in Health & Safety lane — see below)
  - branch "No — no safety implications":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Safety review complete"

Health & Safety lane:
  (receives flow from "Yes — safety implications identified" branch)
  User task "Conduct safety impact assessment"
  User task "Identify applicable permit-to-work and isolation requirements"
  User task "Determine whether regulatory notification is required"
  Exclusive gateway "Regulatory notification required?"
  - branch "Yes":
      User task "Raise regulatory notification record"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory notification required"
  - branch "No":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory notification required"
  User task "Record safety requirements and constraints on work order"
  (flow returns to Reliability Engineering lane)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Safety review complete"
  (back in Reliability Engineering lane)
  User task "Confirm assessment outcome and update work order priority"
  End event "Criticality and safety assessment complete — ready for
    Diagnose Fault"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Criticality Confirmed" — label "Assessment deadline exceeded (24 h)" —
on trigger, flow continues to User task "Escalate to asset manager for
decision" followed by a Termination end event "Escalated — assessment
closed without full classification".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow starts in the Reliability Engineering lane at the
message start event, proceeds through asset retrieval and review tasks,
then through the "Criticality level determined?" gateway whose "Further
information needed" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and whose
"Criticality confirmed" branch bypasses it; both rejoin at the exclusive
merge gateway "Criticality level determined". Flow continues to the
criticality rating task, then to the "Safety-critical asset?" gateway
whose "Yes" branch crosses into the Health & Safety lane and whose "No"
branch skips directly to the merge. In the Health & Safety lane the
assessment, permit identification and regulatory-notification tasks
proceed, with the "Regulatory notification required?" gateway branching
to the notification task or bypassing it, both rejoining at the merge
"Regulatory notification required". The safety requirements task then
returns flow to the Reliability Engineering lane at the merge gateway
"Safety review complete". The final confirmation task leads to the end
event.

Message flows:
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Reliability Engineering lane,
  Service task "Retrieve asset register and criticality classification"
  (asset register, criticality classification, maintenance history).
Reliability Engineering lane, User task "Assign criticality rating and
  record in EAM" → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (criticality
  rating update).
Health & Safety lane, User task "Record safety requirements and
  constraints on work order" → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
  (safety requirements, permit and isolation constraints).
Reliability Engineering lane, User task "Confirm assessment outcome and
  update work order priority" → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
  (updated work order priority and assessment outcome).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Triaged Notification" — read by User task "Review asset
  criticality and production impact".
Data Object "Asset Criticality Classification" — read by Service task
  "Retrieve asset register and criticality classification"; written by
  User task "Assign criticality rating and record in EAM".
Data Object "Consequence of Failure Record" — written by User task
  "Document consequence of failure and downtime exposure".
Data Object "Safety Impact Assessment" — written by User task "Conduct
  safety impact assessment".
Data Object "Permit and Isolation Requirements" — written by User task
  "Identify applicable permit-to-work and isolation requirements".
Data Object "Regulatory Notification Record" — written by User task
  "Raise regulatory notification record".

This subprocess takes the triaged notification produced by Raise & Triage
Notification and produces a fully rated work order carrying a criticality
level, a consequence-of-failure record, and any safety or regulatory
constraints that must govern the repair. Where the asset is safety-critical,
Health & Safety confirms isolation and permit requirements and flags any
regulator involvement before the rating is finalised. The enriched, prioritised
work order is then handed to Diagnose Fault so that investigation effort is
proportionate to risk.
```


### V15.04 — Diagnose Fault

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.04 Diagnose Fault — fourth subprocess in the Detect to Repair
value chain, receiving a triaged and criticality-assessed work order and
producing a confirmed diagnosis ready for work planning.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the maintenance and reliability teams
  carrying out fault diagnosis.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Maintenance (maintenance technician)
  - Reliability Engineering (reliability engineer)

Pool "Original Equipment Manufacturer" — external specialist consulted when
  in-house diagnosis is insufficient.

Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — system used to record diagnoses,
  update the work order, and retrieve asset and maintenance history.

Pool "Document Management System" — system used to retrieve technical
  drawings, manuals, and maintenance procedures.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Original Equipment Manufacturer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Original Equipment Manufacturer
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Criticality-assessed work order received from
    Assess Criticality & Safety Impact"
  Service task "Retrieve asset history and maintenance records from EAM"
  Service task "Retrieve technical drawings and manuals from Document
    Management System"
  User task "Review symptoms, operating context, and fault description"
  User task "Perform initial physical inspection and measurements"
  Exclusive gateway "Initial inspection sufficient to confirm fault?"
  - branch "Yes — fault identified": continue to "Record preliminary
      diagnosis and fault code in EAM" (Maintenance lane), then pass
      control to Reliability Engineering lane
  - branch "No — further analysis needed": pass control to Reliability
      Engineering lane for detailed analysis
  Exclusive merge gateway "Initial inspection sufficient to confirm fault?"
  User task "Record preliminary diagnosis and fault code in EAM"
  Exclusive gateway "Specialist OEM input required?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Request technical support from OEM"
      Intermediate message catch event "OEM technical guidance received"
      continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Specialist OEM input required?"
  - branch "No": continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Specialist OEM
      input required?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Specialist OEM input required?"
  User task "Confirm final diagnosis and select failure code in EAM"
  End event "Diagnosis confirmed — ready for Plan Work & Parts"

Reliability Engineering lane:
  User task "Conduct root-cause and failure-mode analysis"
  User task "Review condition-monitoring data and trends"
  Exclusive gateway "Diagnosis confirmed by reliability review?"
  - branch "Yes": return flow to Exclusive merge gateway "Initial
      inspection sufficient to confirm fault?" in Maintenance lane
  - branch "No — escalate": User task "Escalate and document
      unresolved diagnostic uncertainty"
      End event "Diagnostic escalation raised — return to Assess
        Criticality & Safety Impact for reassessment"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Diagnosis confirmed by reliability review?"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Conduct root-cause and
  failure-mode analysis" — label "Analysis taking too long (24 h)" —
  triggers User task "Notify maintenance planner of diagnosis delay"
  in Reliability Engineering lane; flow continues from that task to
  join the normal sequence at the merge gateway.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Maintenance lane with retrieval of
asset history and documents, then moves through initial inspection to
the "Initial inspection sufficient?" gateway; the "No" branch passes to
the Reliability Engineering lane for root-cause analysis and
condition-data review, which feeds the "Diagnosis confirmed?" gateway;
the "Yes" branch of that gateway merges back into the Maintenance lane
at the merge gateway; the "No — escalate" branch ends in its own End
event. From the merge gateway, Maintenance proceeds through the OEM
gateway: the "Yes" branch sends a request to the OEM, waits for the
message reply, then rejoins at the OEM merge gateway; the "No" branch
joins directly. From the OEM merge gateway, Maintenance records the
final diagnosis and ends.

Message flows:
  Maintenance lane "Request technical support from OEM" →
    Original Equipment Manufacturer (technical support request)
  Original Equipment Manufacturer → Intermediate message catch event
    "OEM technical guidance received" in Maintenance lane
    (technical guidance and method statement)
  Service task "Retrieve asset history and maintenance records from EAM"
    → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (asset history query)
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Service task "Retrieve asset
    history and maintenance records from EAM" (asset register, history,
    and failure codes)
  Service task "Retrieve technical drawings and manuals from Document
    Management System" → Document Management System (document request)
  Document Management System → Service task "Retrieve technical drawings
    and manuals from Document Management System" (drawings, manuals, and
    maintenance procedures)
  User task "Record preliminary diagnosis and fault code in EAM" →
    Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (preliminary diagnosis and fault
    code update)
  User task "Confirm final diagnosis and select failure code in EAM" →
    Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (confirmed diagnosis, failure
    code, and updated work order)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Criticality-Assessed Work Order" — read by "Review
  symptoms, operating context, and fault description".
Data Object "Inspection Findings and Measurements" — written by
  "Perform initial physical inspection and measurements"; read by
  "Conduct root-cause and failure-mode analysis".
Data Object "Condition-Monitoring Data" — read by "Review
  condition-monitoring data and trends".
Data Object "OEM Technical Guidance" — read by "Confirm final
  diagnosis and select failure code in EAM".
Data Object "Confirmed Diagnosis Record" — written by "Confirm final
  diagnosis and select failure code in EAM".

This subprocess takes the triaged, criticality-assessed work order and
drives it to a confirmed, coded diagnosis. Maintenance technicians
gather asset history and documentation, carry out physical inspection,
and — where initial findings are inconclusive — engage Reliability
Engineering for root-cause and condition-data analysis. OEM support is
sought when specialist knowledge is needed. The confirmed diagnosis and
failure code are recorded in EAM and handed to Plan Work & Parts, which
uses them to specify the exact scope, materials, and method for the
repair.
```


### V15.05 — Plan Work & Parts

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.05 Plan Work & Parts — fifth subprocess of the Detect to
Repair value chain, receiving a diagnosed fault and producing a fully
planned work order with parts reserved, ready for scheduling and
permitting.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the maintenance organisation planning
the repair and securing required parts.
  Lane "Maintenance" — maintenance planner who authors the work order,
  defines scope, and coordinates parts.
  Lane "Spare Parts" — storeperson who checks stock, reserves or orders
  parts, and confirms availability.

Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — system that holds the asset
register, maintenance history, work orders, and parts reservations.
Pool "Spare Parts Inventory System" — system that manages stock levels,
reservations, and purchase requisitions for spare parts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Spare Parts Inventory System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Owner Organisation
2. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
3. Spare Parts Inventory System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Diagnosed fault and work order received from
  Diagnose Fault"
  Service task "Retrieve asset history and maintenance records from EAM"
  User task "Define work scope, tasks, and labour requirements"
  User task "Identify required parts, materials, and special tools"
  Send task "Send parts requirement list to Spare Parts"
  Intermediate message catch event "Parts availability confirmation
  received"
  Exclusive gateway "All required parts available or committed?"
  - branch "Yes — all parts available or on order":
      User task "Finalise work order with parts, labour, and cost
      estimates"
      Service task "Update work order and cost estimate in EAM"
      End event "Work order planned and parts committed — ready for
      Schedule Work and Secure Permits"
  - branch "No — critical parts unavailable":
      User task "Assess alternatives — substitute parts, expedite
      order, or adjust scope"
      Exclusive merge gateway "All required parts available or committed?"
      (rejoins the Yes branch before "Finalise work order with parts,
      labour, and cost estimates")

Spare Parts lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Parts requirement list received from
  Maintenance"
  Service task "Check stock availability in Spare Parts Inventory System"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient stock on hand?"
  - branch "Yes — stock sufficient":
      Service task "Reserve parts against work order in Spare Parts
      Inventory System"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient stock on hand?"
  - branch "No — stock insufficient":
      User task "Raise purchase requisition for missing parts"
      Service task "Submit purchase requisition to Spare Parts Inventory
      System"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient stock on hand?"
  Send task "Send parts availability confirmation to Maintenance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Finalise work order with parts,
labour, and cost estimates", labelled "Planning duration limit exceeded",
leading to an escalation task "Escalate delayed work order to maintenance
planner manager"; flow then rejoins the main sequence before the
subsequent service task.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Maintenance lane with the message start
event, proceeds through asset history retrieval, scope definition, and
parts identification, then crosses to the Spare Parts lane via a message
flow carrying the parts requirement list. The Spare Parts lane checks
stock, branches on availability — the sufficient-stock branch reserves
parts directly while the insufficient-stock branch raises and submits a
purchase requisition — both branches merge before the send task that
returns the confirmation. Back in the Maintenance lane the message catch
event receives the confirmation, the exclusive gateway branches on full
availability; the unavailable branch runs through the alternatives
assessment task then merges back before the finalise task; the available
branch continues to finalise the work order, update EAM, and reach the
end event.

Message flows:
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Maintenance lane "Retrieve asset
history and maintenance records from EAM" (asset register, maintenance
history, failure codes).
Maintenance lane "Update work order and cost estimate in EAM" →
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (finalised work order with scope,
labour plan, and cost estimate).
Maintenance lane "Send parts requirement list to Spare Parts" → Spare
Parts lane "Parts requirement list received from Maintenance" (parts,
materials, and special tools list).
Spare Parts lane "Check stock availability in Spare Parts Inventory
System" → Spare Parts Inventory System (stock enquiry).
Spare Parts Inventory System → Spare Parts lane "Check stock
availability in Spare Parts Inventory System" (stock levels and
availability data).
Spare Parts lane "Reserve parts against work order in Spare Parts
Inventory System" → Spare Parts Inventory System (reservation
instruction).
Spare Parts lane "Submit purchase requisition to Spare Parts Inventory
System" → Spare Parts Inventory System (purchase requisition).
Spare Parts lane "Send parts availability confirmation to Maintenance"
→ Maintenance lane "Parts availability confirmation received"
(availability confirmation and reservation or order reference).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Parts Requirement List" — written by "Identify required
parts, materials, and special tools"; read by "Check stock availability
in Spare Parts Inventory System".
Data Object "Parts Availability Confirmation" — written by "Send parts
availability confirmation to Maintenance"; read by Maintenance lane
"Parts availability confirmation received".
Data Object "Purchase Requisition" — written by "Raise purchase
requisition for missing parts"; read by "Submit purchase requisition to
Spare Parts Inventory System".
history and maintenance records from EAM"; written by "Update work order
and cost estimate in EAM".
availability in Spare Parts Inventory System"; written by "Reserve parts
against work order in Spare Parts Inventory System" and "Submit purchase
requisition to Spare Parts Inventory System".
Data Object "Work Order" — written by "Define work scope, tasks, and
labour requirements" and "Finalise work order with parts, labour, and
cost estimates"; read by "Update work order and cost estimate in EAM".

This subprocess takes the diagnosed fault from V15.04 and converts it
into an actionable, costed work order by defining the repair scope,
identifying all labour and material needs, and confirming that parts are
either in stock and reserved or formally on order. It hands to V15.06
Schedule Work and Secure Permits a fully specified work order with parts
committed, enabling the scheduler and safety officer to fix a date,
assign resources, and raise the necessary permits.
```

```text
This subprocess takes a fully planned work order and transforms it into a
confirmed, resourced schedule agreed with the service contractor and backed

and timing commitments while Health & Safety validates isolation and access
controls before issuing the permit. The output — a scheduled job with an
```

```text
personnel on site, and drives execution of all repair tasks against the
approved work order and method statement, with quality checks and rework
loops ensuring the repair meets acceptance criteria before sign-off. It
hands a fully completed and documented repair, including the contractor
certificate and an updated work order, to Test & Return to Service, where
the asset will be re-energised, functionally tested, and released back
into operation.
```


### V15.08 — Test & Return to Service

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.08 Test & Return to Service — subprocess within the Detect to
Repair value chain, following Execute Repair and preceding Close Work Order
& Capture Costs.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the maintenance and operations teams
carrying out testing and return-to-service activities.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Maintenance (maintenance technician)
  - Operations (operations supervisor)

Pool "Equipment Operator" — external party who confirms the asset can be
returned to normal service and resumes operation.

Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — IT system that records test
results, updates asset status, and closes out the repair work order stage.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Equipment Operator
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Repair completion confirmed — ready from Execute
    Repair"
  User task "Review repair completion report and sign-off"
  User task "Prepare test plan and acceptance criteria"
  Service task "Record pre-test asset status in EAM"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Tests Pass" (standard loop) containing,
    in order: User task "Conduct functional and safety tests", User task
    "Record test results and observations", Exclusive gateway "All tests
    passed?"
    - branch "yes": exit subprocess
    - branch "no": User task "Identify and rectify test failure", then
      loop continues
  User task "Compile test completion report"
  Send task "Send return-to-service notification to Equipment Operator"
  Intermediate message catch event "Equipment Operator acceptance received"
  Service task "Update asset status to operational in EAM"
  Send task "Confirm asset return to service in EAM"

Operations lane:
  User task "Review test results and accept return to service"
  User task "Authorise removal of operational restrictions"
  End event "Asset returned to service — ready for Close Work Order &
    Capture Costs"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Tests Pass", labelled "Maximum test window elapsed", leading to an
interrupting End event "Test window exceeded — escalate to Reliability
Engineering".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Maintenance lane with the message start
event and proceeds through review, preparation, pre-test recording, and the
looping test subprocess. On exit from the subprocess the Maintenance lane
compiles the report and sends the return-to-service notification, then
waits at the intermediate message catch event for Equipment Operator
acceptance. Once received, Maintenance updates asset status and sends
confirmation to EAM. Control then passes to the Operations lane, where the
operations supervisor reviews results, accepts the return to service, and
authorises removal of restrictions, reaching the end event.

Message flows:
Equipment Operator → Maintenance lane (equipment access confirmation and
  acceptance of return to service).
Maintenance lane (Send task "Send return-to-service notification to
  Equipment Operator") → Equipment Operator (return-to-service
  notification and test completion report).
Maintenance lane (Service task "Record pre-test asset status in EAM") →
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (pre-test asset status record).
Maintenance lane (User task "Record test results and observations") →
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (test results and observations).
Maintenance lane (Service task "Update asset status to operational in
  EAM") → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (updated asset operational
  status).
Maintenance lane (Send task "Confirm asset return to service in EAM") →
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (return-to-service confirmation).
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Maintenance lane (current asset
  history, maintenance records, and prior test data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Repair Completion Report" — read by User task "Review repair
  completion report and sign-off".
Data Object "Test Plan and Acceptance Criteria" — written by User task
  "Prepare test plan and acceptance criteria"; read by User task "Conduct
  functional and safety tests".
Data Object "Test Results Record" — written by User task "Record test
  results and observations"; read by User task "Compile test completion
  report".
Data Object "Test Completion Report" — written by User task "Compile test
  completion report"; read by User task "Review test results and accept
  return to service".

This subprocess takes the repaired asset from a completion handoff and
subjects it to structured functional and safety testing against defined
acceptance criteria, cycling through rectification if any test fails. Once
all tests pass and the Equipment Operator formally accepts the result,
Operations authorises full reinstatement and the asset status is updated to
operational in EAM. The subprocess hands a confirmed return-to-service
record and closed test report to Close Work Order & Capture Costs.
```

## V16 — Detect to Respond

**Teams and roles involved.**
Detect to Respond usually involves Security Operations, Incident Response, IT Operations, Privacy/Data Protection, Legal, Risk and Compliance, Communications, and Executive Management, with Engineering teams drawn in for remediation. Key roles include security analyst, incident manager, threat hunter, forensic investigator, privacy officer, legal counsel, communications lead, service owner, and the executive incident sponsor.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are the Regulator and the Affected Individuals or Customers who must be notified where a breach is confirmed. The process is initiated by an alert from monitoring tooling, a report from staff or a customer, a third-party or law-enforcement notification, or a threat-intelligence advisory. Other external parties include managed security providers, forensic specialists, cyber insurers, law enforcement, and affected suppliers or partners.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: detect the event, triage and validate it, declare and classify the incident, contain the threat, investigate and preserve evidence, assess data and privacy impact, notify regulators and affected parties, eradicate and recover, confirm service restoration, and conduct a post-incident review with remediation actions.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include SIEM and log aggregation, endpoint and network detection and response, vulnerability management, identity and access management, case and incident management, forensic tooling, threat intelligence platforms, IT service management, secure communications and war-room tooling, and GRC/risk registers.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the incident response plan and severity matrix, breach notification obligations and statutory timeframes, evidence handling and chain-of-custody procedure, containment authority and emergency change rules, privacy impact assessment procedure, communications and disclosure policy, third-party notification obligations, insurance notification terms, and post-incident review requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Regulators receive breach notifications, impact assessments and remediation plans, and provide directions or findings. Affected individuals receive notification of what happened, what data was involved, and what they should do. Third parties provide threat intelligence, forensic findings, and their own breach notifications. The process provides status updates to executives, customers and partners throughout.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates incident records, timelines, evidence artefacts, containment and remediation actions, impact assessments, notifications, and risk-register entries. IT systems provide alerts and correlated events, log and telemetry evidence, asset and data classification, identity and access history, vulnerability and patch state, and incident metrics for reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V16.01** Detect Event | Managed Security Provider | Security Operations (security analyst) | SIEM Platform, Endpoint Detection & Response |
| **V16.02** Triage & Validate | — | Security Operations (security analyst) | SIEM Platform, Case Management System |
| **V16.03** Declare & Classify Incident | — | Incident Response (incident manager), Executive Management (executive sponsor) | Case Management System |
| **V16.04** Contain Threat | — | Incident Response (incident manager), IT Operations (service owner) | Endpoint Detection & Response, Identity & Access Management |
| **V16.05** Investigate & Preserve Evidence | Forensic Specialist | Incident Response (forensic investigator) | Forensic Tooling, SIEM Platform |
| **V16.06** Assess Data & Privacy Impact | — | Privacy (privacy officer), Legal (legal counsel) | Case Management System, GRC Platform |
| **V16.07** Notify Regulators & Affected Parties | Regulator, Affected Individual | Legal (legal counsel), Communications (communications lead) | Case Management System |
| **V16.08** Eradicate & Recover | — | IT Operations (service owner), Incident Response (incident manager) | IT Service Management, Endpoint Detection & Response |
| **V16.09** Confirm Service Restoration | — | IT Operations (service owner), Security Operations (security analyst) | IT Service Management |
| **V16.10** Conduct Post-Incident Review | Cyber Insurer | Risk & Compliance (risk manager), Incident Response (incident manager) | GRC Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V16):

- **External actors:** Managed Security Provider (V16.01); Forensic Specialist (V16.05); Regulator (V16.07); Affected Individual (V16.07); Cyber Insurer (V16.10).
- **Teams:** Security Operations (V16.01, V16.02, V16.09); Incident Response (V16.03–V16.05, V16.08, V16.10); Executive Management (V16.03); IT Operations (V16.04, V16.08, V16.09); Privacy (V16.06); Legal (V16.06, V16.07); Communications (V16.07); Risk & Compliance (V16.10).
- **IT systems:** SIEM Platform (V16.01, V16.02, V16.05); Endpoint Detection & Response (V16.01, V16.04, V16.08); Case Management System (V16.02, V16.03, V16.06, V16.07); Identity & Access Management (V16.04); Forensic Tooling (V16.05); GRC Platform (V16.06, V16.10); IT Service Management (V16.08, V16.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V16 — Detect to Respond — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Detect to Respond value chain, from initial event detection through
to post-incident review. The diagram is arranged in three horizontal bands,
top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES → BUSINESS PROCESSES → APPLICATIONS. The
demand-side actor (Managed Security Provider, plus staff and customer
report sources) sits on the far left; delivery and settlement actors
(Regulator, Affected Individual, Cyber Insurer, Forensic Specialist) sit
on the far right. The view is read top-to-bottom as service → process →
application, following ArchiMate service realisation conventions.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Managed Security Provider — far left; initiates detection by supplying
  alerts and threat intelligence into V16.01.
- Forensic Specialist — far right; engaged externally during V16.05 to
  supply forensic findings.
- Regulator — far right; receives breach notifications and issues
  directions in V16.07.
- Affected Individual — far right; receives breach notifications and
  guidance in V16.07.
- Cyber Insurer — far right; receives post-incident reporting and review
  outputs in V16.10.

2. Interfaces

- Security Alert Interface — ACCESSED by Managed Security Provider;
  SERVES the Event Detection Service and V16.01 Detect Event.
- Forensic Findings Interface — ACCESSED by Forensic Specialist; SERVES
  the Investigation & Evidence Service and V16.05.
- Breach Notification Interface — ACCESSED by Regulator and Affected
  Individual; SERVES the Notification Service and V16.07.
- Insurer Reporting Interface — ACCESSED by Cyber Insurer; SERVES the
  Post-Incident Review Service and V16.10.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Event Detection Service — provides continuous monitoring and alert
  ingestion, delivering confirmed candidate security events for triage.
- Triage & Validation Service — provides rapid assessment of candidate
  events to confirm or dismiss them as genuine incidents.
- Incident Declaration Service — provides formal classification and
  severity assignment, mobilising the incident response structure.
- Threat Containment Service — provides authorised containment actions
  to limit the spread and impact of a confirmed threat.
- Investigation & Evidence Service — provides forensic investigation,
  log analysis, and chain-of-custody evidence preservation.
- Data & Privacy Impact Service — provides structured assessment of data
  exposure and privacy-breach obligations.
- Regulatory & Party Notification Service — provides timely, compliant
  notification to regulators and affected individuals.
- Eradication & Recovery Service — provides removal of threat artefacts
  and restoration of affected systems and services.
- Service Restoration Confirmation Service — provides formal verification
  that systems are clean and operating normally before stand-down.
- Post-Incident Review Service — provides structured lessons-learned,
  remediation planning, and risk-register updates.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V16.01 Detect Event — security analyst ingests and correlates alerts
  from monitoring tooling, the managed security provider, staff reports,
  and threat-intelligence advisories.
- V16.02 Triage & Validate — security analyst validates the alert,
  enriches it with context, and determines whether a genuine incident
  exists.
- V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident — incident manager formally declares
  the incident, assigns severity, and notifies the executive sponsor.
- V16.04 Contain Threat — incident manager and service owner execute
  containment actions including isolation, access revocation, and
  emergency changes.
- V16.05 Investigate & Preserve Evidence — forensic investigator and
  external forensic specialist collect logs, artefacts, and timeline
  evidence under chain-of-custody controls.
- V16.06 Assess Data & Privacy Impact — privacy officer and legal counsel
  assess what data was involved, classify the breach, and determine
  notification obligations.
- V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties — legal counsel and
  communications lead draft and dispatch notifications to the regulator
  and affected individuals within statutory timeframes.
- V16.08 Eradicate & Recover — service owner and incident manager remove
  malicious artefacts, patch vulnerabilities, rebuild systems, and restore
  services.
- V16.09 Confirm Service Restoration — service owner and security analyst
  verify system integrity, close containment measures, and formally
  confirm restoration.
- V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review — risk manager and incident manager
  lead the post-incident review, document lessons learned, update the risk
  register, and report to the cyber insurer.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- SIEM Platform — provides log aggregation, event correlation, and alert
  generation; used in V16.01, V16.02, V16.05.
- Endpoint Detection & Response — provides endpoint and network threat
  detection, isolation capability, and telemetry; used in V16.01,
  V16.04, V16.08.
- Case Management System — provides incident record creation, workflow,
  timeline tracking, and notification drafting; used in V16.02, V16.03,
  V16.06, V16.07.
- Identity & Access Management — provides access history, account
  suspension, and credential revocation; used in V16.04.
- Forensic Tooling — provides forensic image acquisition, artefact
  analysis, and evidence preservation; used in V16.05.
- GRC Platform — provides risk-register entries, privacy impact
  assessment records, and post-incident findings; used in V16.06,
  V16.10.
- IT Service Management — provides change records, service restoration
  tracking, and incident closure; used in V16.08, V16.09.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process or business
service):
- SIEM Platform SERVES Event Detection Service.
- SIEM Platform SERVES Triage & Validation Service.
```

```text
Incident Response — V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident: leads incident
declaration and applies the severity classification matrix.

Incident Response — V16.04 Contain Threat: directs and executes containment
actions to limit the spread of the threat.

Incident Response — V16.05 Investigate & Preserve Evidence: conducts
forensic investigation and maintains chain-of-custody records.

Incident Response — V16.08 Eradicate & Recover: oversees eradication of the
threat and coordinates the recovery sequence.

Incident Response — V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review: participates in the
post-incident review and tracks remediation actions.

Executive Management — V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident: provides
executive sponsorship and authority to declare a major incident.

IT Operations — V16.04 Contain Threat: implements technical containment
measures across infrastructure and services.

IT Operations — V16.08 Eradicate & Recover: executes system eradication,
patching, and service recovery steps.

IT Operations — V16.09 Confirm Service Restoration: confirms that services
have been fully restored and are stable.

Forensic Specialist — V16.05 Investigate & Preserve Evidence: provides
specialist forensic analysis and delivers findings to the investigation.

Privacy — V16.06 Assess Data & Privacy Impact: leads the privacy impact
assessment and determines whether a notifiable breach has occurred.

Legal — V16.06 Assess Data & Privacy Impact: advises on legal obligations
and reviews the scope of data exposure.

Legal — V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties: prepares and approves
notification content in line with statutory timeframes.

Communications — V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties: manages
disclosure messaging and coordinates external communications.

Regulator — V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties: receives breach
notifications, impact assessments, and remediation plans; issues directions
or findings in return.

Affected Individual — V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties: receives
notification of the breach, data involved, and recommended protective
actions.

Risk & Compliance — V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review: leads the
post-incident review, updates the risk register, and tracks compliance with
remediation commitments.

Cyber Insurer — V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review: receives incident
summary and supporting evidence; provides findings or settlement guidance in
return.

The boundary contains all ten subprocesses of the Detect to Respond value
chain, from initial event detection through triage, declaration, containment,
investigation, privacy assessment, regulatory notification, eradication,
service restoration, and post-incident review. It serves internal teams
spanning Security Operations, Incident Response, IT Operations, Privacy,
Legal, Communications, Executive Management, and Risk & Compliance, as well
as external actors including the Managed Security Provider, Forensic
Specialist, Regulator, Affected Individual, and Cyber Insurer.
```
