**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V16 - Detect to Respond

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right, one chevron per stage, in the
order listed below. The chevrons should flow continuously from left to
right across the diagram with no gaps between them.

V16.01. Detect Event
V16.02. Triage & Validate
V16.03. Declare & Classify Incident
V16.04. Contain Threat
V16.05. Investigate & Preserve Evidence
V16.06. Assess Data & Privacy Impact
V16.07. Notify Regulators & Affected Parties
V16.08. Eradicate & Recover
V16.09. Confirm Service Restoration
V16.10. Conduct Post-Incident Review

This chain covers the end-to-end organisational response to a security
event, from the moment an alert or report is first detected through
containment, investigation, mandatory notification, recovery, and
structured review. The chain is triggered by an inbound signal — from
monitoring tooling, a staff or customer report, a third-party advisory,
or a law-enforcement notification. The primary external participants are
the Regulator and Affected Individuals, who must be formally notified
where a breach is confirmed, and whose directions and responses shape
the later stages of the chain.
```
### V16.01 — Detect Event

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.01 Detect Event — first subprocess in the Detect to Respond
value chain, capturing all inbound security signals and routing them for
triage.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams performing event detection.
  Lane "Security Operations (security analyst)" — receives and logs all
  incoming signals.
Pool "Managed Security Provider" — external party that forwards alerts to
  the organisation.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — correlates and aggregates log and alert data.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — supplies endpoint and network
  detection alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Managed Security Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Managed Security Provider
2. Organisation
3. SIEM Platform
4. Endpoint Detection & Response

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security Operations (security analyst) lane:

  Multiple start event "Security signal received — from monitoring
    tooling, staff report, customer report, third-party notification,
    or threat-intelligence advisory"
  Exclusive gateway "Signal source type?"
    - branch "Automated SIEM alert": Service task "Retrieve correlated
      alert from SIEM Platform"
    - branch "EDR alert": Service task "Retrieve endpoint or network
      detection alert from Endpoint Detection & Response"
    - branch "Manual report (staff, customer, or third party)": User
      task "Log manually reported event details"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Signal source type"
  User task "Review and enrich signal with asset and context data"
  Exclusive gateway "Signal warrants further attention?"
    - branch "No — noise or false positive": User task
      "Document signal as noise and close"
      End event "Signal dismissed — no further action"
    - branch "Yes — potential security event": Service task
      "Create initial event record in Case Management System"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Signal warrants further attention"
  User task "Assign severity indicator using incident response
    severity matrix"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Record Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Verify mandatory event fields",
    User task "Correct or supplement missing information"
  Send task "Forward validated event record for triage"
  End event "Event record complete — ready for Triage and Validate"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Record Complete" — label "Initial logging deadline exceeded (per
  incident response plan)" — flow continues to User task "Escalate
  incomplete record to senior analyst" then rejoins before Send task
  "Forward validated event record for triage".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins at the multiple start event, passes
  through the signal-source exclusive gateway whose three branches
  (automated SIEM alert, EDR alert, manual report) each complete their
  respective retrieve or log task before rejoining at the exclusive
  merge gateway "Signal source type"; flow continues through enrichment
  and the attention gateway, whose "No" branch ends in its own end
  event and whose "Yes" branch creates the case record and rejoins at
  the exclusive merge gateway "Signal warrants further attention";
  flow then proceeds through severity assignment, the record-complete
  subprocess, and the send task to the end event.

Message flows:
  Managed Security Provider → Security Operations (security analyst)
    (inbound threat alert or advisory)
  SIEM Platform → Service task "Retrieve correlated alert from SIEM
    Platform" (correlated event and log data)
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Service task "Retrieve endpoint or
    network detection alert from Endpoint Detection & Response"
    (endpoint and network detection alert)
  Service task "Create initial event record in Case Management System"
    → SIEM Platform (event record creation confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inbound Security Signal" — written by Multiple start
  event "Security signal received", read by Exclusive gateway
  "Signal source type?".
Data Object "Enriched Alert Record" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve correlated alert from SIEM Platform" and Service task
  "Retrieve endpoint or network detection alert from Endpoint
  Detection & Response" and User task "Log manually reported event
  details", read by User task "Review and enrich signal with asset
  and context data".
Data Object "Incident Response Severity Matrix" — read by User task
  "Assign severity indicator using incident response severity matrix".
Data Object "Validated Event Record" — written by Expanded Subprocess
  "Repeat Until Record Complete", read by Send task "Forward validated
  event record for triage".

This subprocess captures every inbound security signal regardless of its
origin, enriches it with asset and context data, applies a severity
indicator from the incident response severity matrix, and ensures the
event record meets mandatory logging standards. A complete, classified
event record is handed to Triage and Validate, where analysts will
determine whether a genuine threat exists and what priority to assign it.
```


### V16.02 — Triage & Validate

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.02 Triage & Validate — the second subprocess in the Detect to
Respond value chain, receiving a candidate event from Detect Event and
handing a validated or dismissed finding to Declare & Classify Incident.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams performing triage and validation.
  Lane "Security Operations (security analyst)" — analysts who examine,
    enrich, and validate the candidate event.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — the SIEM and log aggregation system that provides
  correlated events, log evidence, and telemetry.
Pool "Case Management System" — the platform used to create and update
  the incident record throughout this subprocess.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "SIEM Platform" — top.
Pool "Organisation" — middle (white-box).
Pool "Case Management System" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security Operations (security analyst) lane:
  Message start event "Candidate event received from Detect Event"
  User task "Review candidate event details"
  Service task "Retrieve correlated logs and telemetry from SIEM Platform"
  User task "Enrich event with threat intelligence and asset context"
  User task "Assess indicators of compromise"
  Exclusive gateway "Event credible?"
  - branch "No — false positive or benign":
      User task "Document dismissal rationale"
      Service task "Update case record as dismissed in Case Management
        System"
      End event "Event dismissed — no further action"
  - branch "Yes — credible threat signal":
      Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to validate?"
      - branch "No — additional evidence needed":
          Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Sufficient"
            (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Identify
            evidence gaps", Service task "Request additional logs from
            SIEM Platform", Intermediate message catch event "Log data
            received", User task "Re-assess indicators of compromise"
      - branch "Yes — evidence sufficient":
          Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to validate"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to validate"
      User task "Confirm event validated as genuine security incident"
      Service task "Create validated incident record in Case Management
        System"
      User task "Assign initial severity rating"
      Service task "Record severity and validation findings in Case
        Management System"
      End event "Validated incident record ready — ready for Declare and
        Classify Incident"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Event credible"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Evidence Sufficient", labelled "Evidence collection limit reached
  (defined by incident response plan)"; on trigger, flow continues to
  User task "Confirm event validated as genuine security incident" with
  the evidence gathered so far, and an annotation is added to the case
  record.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Security Operations lane runs from the message
  start event through review, log retrieval, enrichment, and indicator
  assessment to the "Event credible?" gateway. The false-positive branch
  leads through dismissal documentation and a case update to its own end
  event. The credible branch enters the "Sufficient information to
  validate?" gateway; the insufficient branch enters the standard-loop
  subprocess (with the timer boundary), and on completion merges at the
  "Sufficient information to validate" merge gateway; the sufficient
  branch joins the same merge. From there the flow continues through
  validation confirmation, record creation, severity assignment, and
  severity recording to the final end event. The "Event credible" merge
  gateway is not used; only the false-positive branch ends separately
  and does not rejoin.

Message flows:
  SIEM Platform → Security Operations "Correlated logs and telemetry
    retrieved" (triggered by "Retrieve correlated logs and telemetry
    from SIEM Platform").
  SIEM Platform → Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Sufficient"
    "Additional log data" (in response to evidence-gap requests).
  Security Operations → Case Management System "Dismissal record"
    (from "Update case record as dismissed in Case Management System").
  Security Operations → Case Management System "New validated incident
    record" (from "Create validated incident record in Case Management
    System").
  Security Operations → Case Management System "Severity and validation
    findings" (from "Record severity and validation findings in Case
    Management System").

7. Data objects

Data Object "Candidate Event Details" — read by "Review candidate event
  details"; written by the upstream Detect Event subprocess on handoff.
Data Object "Correlated Log and Telemetry Evidence" — written by
  "Retrieve correlated logs and telemetry from SIEM Platform"; read by
  "Assess indicators of compromise" and the loop subprocess tasks.
Data Object "Enrichment and Threat Intelligence Record" — written by
  "Enrich event with threat intelligence and asset context"; read by
  "Assess indicators of compromise".
Data Object "Dismissal Record" — written by "Document dismissal
  rationale"; read by "Update case record as dismissed in Case
  Management System".

Triage & Validate takes the raw candidate event surfaced by Detect Event,
enriches it with log evidence and threat-intelligence context, and tests
whether the indicators of compromise are credible and sufficiently evidenced.
Events that do not meet the threshold are dismissed and documented; those that
do are assigned an initial severity rating and captured as a validated incident
record in the Case Management System, which becomes the input for Declare &
Classify Incident.
```


### V16.03 — Declare & Classify Incident

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident — third subprocess in the
Detect to Respond value chain, receiving a validated event from Triage &
Validate and handing a classified incident record to Contain Threat.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that declare and classify the
incident, spanning Incident Response and Executive Management.
  Lane "Incident Response (incident manager)"
  Lane "Executive Management (executive sponsor)"
Pool "Case Management System" — records and tracks the declared incident.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, two lanes top to bottom: Incident Response,
   Executive Management)
2. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response (incident manager) lane:
  Message start event "Validated event received from Triage & Validate"
  User task "Review validated event details"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to declare?"
  - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Information Sufficient"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Request additional
    information from analyst", Intermediate message catch event "Additional
    information received"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Repeat Until Information Sufficient"
  - branch "Yes": continue to next task
  User task "Formally declare incident"
  User task "Apply severity classification using incident response matrix"
  Exclusive gateway "Severity requires executive notification?"
  - branch "No": continue to record task
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Notify executive sponsor of declared incident"

Executive Management (executive sponsor) lane:
  User task "Acknowledge incident declaration and confirm sponsorship"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Severity requires executive notification?"

Incident Response (incident manager) lane (continuing):
  Service task "Create incident record in Case Management System"
  User task "Assign incident manager and response team"
  User task "Open incident timeline and communication log"
  End event "Incident declared and classified — ready for Contain Threat"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Information Sufficient", labelled "24-hour wait limit exceeded", leading to
an Escalation end event "Escalate — information not received in time".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Incident Response lane with the message
start event and proceeds through review and the information-sufficiency
gateway. The "No" branch enters the loop subprocess; on exit the exclusive
merge gateway rejoins the "Yes" branch and continues to formal declaration,
severity classification, and the executive-notification gateway. The "Yes"
branch sends notification to the Executive Management lane, where the
sponsor acknowledges; the "No" branch bypasses that lane. Both branches
rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway in the Incident Response lane before
the service task creates the incident record; the lane then continues to
team assignment, timeline opening, and the end event.

Message flows:
Organisation (Service task "Create incident record in Case Management
System") → Case Management System (incident record created).
Case Management System → Organisation (Incident Response lane, task "Review
validated event details") (validated event details retrieved).
Organisation (Service task "Create incident record in Case Management
System") → Case Management System (incident timeline and communication log
opened).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Event Report" — read by "Review validated event
details".
Data Object "Incident Declaration Record" — written by "Formally declare
incident"; read by "Apply severity classification using incident response
matrix".
Data Object "Severity Classification" — written by "Apply severity
classification using incident response matrix"; read by "Create incident
record in Case Management System".
"Create incident record in Case Management System"; written by "Open
incident timeline and communication log".
Data Object "Response Team Assignment" — written by "Assign incident
manager and response team"; read by "Open incident timeline and
communication log".

This subprocess converts a validated security event into a formally declared
and severity-classified incident. The incident manager confirms sufficient
information, applies the incident response severity matrix, engages the
executive sponsor for high-severity events, and creates a structured incident
record with an open timeline in the Case Management System. The classified
incident record and assigned response team are handed to Contain Threat to
begin active response.
```


### V16.04 — Contain Threat

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.04 Contain Threat — the fourth subprocess of the Detect to
Respond value chain, receiving a declared and classified incident from
Declare & Classify Incident and passing a contained threat state to
Investigate & Preserve Evidence.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing threat containment.
  Lane "Incident Response" — incident manager directing containment actions.
  Lane "IT Operations" — service owner executing technical containment.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — EDR platform used to isolate
  endpoints and push containment actions.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — IAM platform used to revoke or
  suspend credentials and enforce access controls.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Organisation" — top (white-box process pool).
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — below Organisation.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response lane:
  Message start event "Classified incident received from Declare &
    Classify Incident"
  User task "Review incident classification and containment authority"
  User task "Define containment strategy and scope"
  Send task "Issue containment instructions to IT Operations"
  Intermediate message catch event "Containment actions confirmed by
    IT Operations"
  Exclusive gateway "Containment effective?"
  - branch "Yes — threat contained": proceed to
      Exclusive merge gateway "Containment effective"
  - branch "No — containment failed or incomplete":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Containment Effective"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Reassess containment approach",
        User task "Issue revised containment instructions to IT
          Operations",
        Intermediate message catch event "Revised actions confirmed
          by IT Operations"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Containment effective"
  User task "Confirm and document containment outcome"
  End event "Threat contained — ready for Investigate & Preserve
    Evidence"

IT Operations lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Containment instructions received
    from Incident Response"
  User task "Execute network segmentation and traffic blocking"
  Service task "Trigger endpoint isolation via Endpoint Detection &
    Response"
  Intermediate message catch event "Endpoint isolation confirmed by
    Endpoint Detection & Response"
  Service task "Suspend or revoke compromised credentials via
    Identity & Access Management"
  Intermediate message catch event "Credential actions confirmed by
    Identity & Access Management"
  User task "Apply emergency change and document actions taken"
  Send task "Report containment status to Incident Response"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Containment Effective" — label "Escalation deadline reached
  (containment authority timeout)" — triggers an escalation end event
  directing the incident manager to invoke emergency authority and
  halt the loop.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Incident Response lane the flow runs from
the start event through strategy tasks to the gateway; the "No"
branch enters the standard-loop subprocess, which rejoins at the
merge gateway, then continues to documentation and the end event.
Within the IT Operations lane the flow runs from the incoming message
catch event through network segmentation, endpoint isolation,
credential suspension, emergency-change documentation, and then the
send task back to Incident Response.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Incident Response, Send task "Issue containment
    instructions to IT Operations") → Organisation (IT Operations,
    Intermediate message catch event "Containment instructions
    received") (containment instruction message — internal cross-lane
    message flow shown for clarity).
  Organisation (IT Operations, Service task "Trigger endpoint
    isolation via Endpoint Detection & Response") →
    Endpoint Detection & Response (isolation command).
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Organisation (IT Operations,
    Intermediate message catch event "Endpoint isolation confirmed")
    (isolation confirmation).
  Organisation (IT Operations, Service task "Suspend or revoke
    compromised credentials via Identity & Access Management") →
    Identity & Access Management (credential suspension request).
  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (IT Operations,
    Intermediate message catch event "Credential actions confirmed")
    (credential action confirmation).
  Organisation (IT Operations, Send task "Report containment status
    to Incident Response") → Organisation (Incident Response,
    Intermediate message catch event "Containment actions confirmed")
    (containment status report).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incident Record" — read by "Review incident
  classification and containment authority"; written by "Confirm and
  document containment outcome".
Data Object "Containment Strategy" — written by "Define containment
  strategy and scope"; read by "Issue containment instructions to IT
  Operations".
Data Object "Emergency Change Record" — written by "Apply emergency
  change and document actions taken"; read by "Confirm and document
  containment outcome".
Data Object "Containment Status Report" — written by "Report
  containment status to Incident Response"; read by "Confirm and
  document containment outcome".

Contain Threat isolates the threat from spreading further by combining
coordinated endpoint isolation through the EDR platform with credential
revocation through IAM, all governed by the incident manager's
containment authority and emergency change rules. Where initial
containment falls short the subprocess loops until the threat is
demonstrably bounded, with a timer boundary escalation if the
deadline expires. A confirmed containment record is handed to
Investigate & Preserve Evidence so that forensic work begins on a
stable, scoped environment.
```


### V16.05 — Investigate & Preserve Evidence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.05 Investigate & Preserve Evidence — the fifth subprocess in the
Detect to Respond value chain, receiving a contained incident from Contain
Threat and handing forensic findings to Assess Data & Privacy Impact.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams conducting the investigation and
evidence preservation.
  Lane "Incident Response (forensic investigator)" — leads the forensic
  investigation, collects and preserves evidence, and manages chain of custody.
Pool "Forensic Specialist" — external forensic specialist engaged to support
or conduct specialist analysis.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — log aggregation and correlated event retrieval.
Pool "Forensic Tooling" — specialist forensic tooling used to acquire and
analyse evidence artefacts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Forensic Specialist" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Forensic Tooling" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Forensic Specialist
2. Organisation
3. SIEM Platform
4. Forensic Tooling

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response (forensic investigator) lane:
  Message start event "Contained incident received from Contain Threat"
  User task "Review incident record and scope investigation"
  User task "Identify evidence sources and collection priorities"
  Exclusive gateway "External forensic specialist required?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Engage external forensic specialist"
    Intermediate message catch event "Forensic specialist engagement confirmed"
  - branch "No": (continues directly to merge)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Forensic specialist required"
  Service task "Retrieve correlated events and logs from SIEM Platform"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Collection Complete" (standard
  loop) containing, in order: User task "Acquire evidence artefact",
  Service task "Submit artefact to Forensic Tooling for analysis",
  Intermediate message catch event "Analysis result received",
  User task "Record artefact in chain-of-custody log"
  User task "Validate chain-of-custody completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Chain of custody complete and defensible?"
  - branch "No": User task "Remediate chain-of-custody gaps"
    Sequence flow back to exclusive gateway — modelled by looping this
    correction step as:
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Chain of Custody Accepted" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Remediate chain-of-custody gaps",
    User task "Validate chain-of-custody completeness"
  - branch "Yes": (continues)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Chain of custody accepted"
  User task "Compile timeline of attacker activity"
  User task "Draft forensic investigation report"
  Exclusive gateway "External specialist contributed findings?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Request specialist forensic findings"
    Intermediate message catch event "Specialist forensic findings received"
    User task "Incorporate specialist findings into report"
  - branch "No": (continues directly to merge)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Specialist findings incorporated"
  User task "Finalise and approve forensic investigation report"
  User task "Secure and archive evidence artefacts"
  End event "Forensic investigation complete — ready for Assess Data and
  Privacy Impact"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Evidence Collection Complete" — label "Evidence collection deadline exceeded"
— triggers User task "Escalate incomplete evidence collection to incident
manager" which leads to an End event "Escalated — evidence collection
incomplete".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The single lane flows from the message start event through
scoping and source identification, then through the specialist-required
gateway (both branches rejoining at the merge), then to SIEM log retrieval,
then into the evidence collection loop subprocess, then to chain-of-custody
validation, through the chain-of-custody correction loop if needed, then to
timeline compilation, report drafting, through the specialist-findings
gateway (both branches rejoining at the merge), then to report finalisation
and evidence archiving, ending at the end event.

Message flows:

  (evidence analysis results)

  (evidence artefacts submitted for analysis)

forensic investigation report".
evidence artefacts".

This subprocess receives a contained incident from Contain Threat and
```

### V16.07 — Notify Regulators & Affected Parties

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties — the subprocess in the
Detect to Respond chain that fulfils statutory and organisational disclosure
obligations once a breach has been confirmed and assessed.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the teams preparing and issuing all notifications.
  Lane "Legal (legal counsel)" — manages regulatory notification drafting,
    reviews all disclosures, tracks statutory deadlines, and coordinates with
    the regulator.
  Lane "Communications (communications lead)" — drafts and issues notifications
    to affected individuals and manages public-facing messaging.

Pool "Regulator" — the external authority receiving breach notification and
  providing directions or findings in response.
Pool "Affected Individual" — external recipients of personal breach
  notification, who acknowledge or respond.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system holding the incident record,
  notification log, and supporting documentation.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Affected Individual" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Regulator
2. Affected Individual
3. Organisation
4. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Privacy and data impact assessment received from
    Assess Data and Privacy Impact"
  User task "Confirm notification obligations and statutory deadlines"
  Exclusive gateway "Regulatory notification required?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Draft regulatory breach notification"
      Send task "Submit breach notification to regulator"
      Intermediate message catch event "Regulator direction or
        acknowledgement received"
      User task "Log regulator response and update notification record"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory notification required"
  - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory notification required"
  User task "Review and approve individual notification content"
  Exclusive gateway "Third-party notification obligations apply?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Identify and notify affected third parties
      and partners"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Third-party notification obligations apply"
  - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Third-party notification
      obligations apply"
  User task "Record all notification outcomes in incident record"
  End event "Notifications complete — ready for Eradicate and Recover"

Communications lane:
  User task "Identify scope and contact details of affected individuals"
  User task "Draft individual breach notification"
  Send task "Issue notification to affected individuals"
  Intermediate message catch event "Individual acknowledgement or response
    received"
  User task "Log individual responses and escalate concerns"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Confirm notification
  obligations and statutory deadlines" — label "Statutory deadline
  threshold reached" — triggers an escalation sequence flow to User task
  "Escalate overdue notification to legal counsel and incident manager"
  ending in an Escalation end event "Deadline breach escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane at the message start event,
  proceeds through obligation confirmation, then the "Regulatory notification
  required?" gateway splits into a Yes branch covering draft, submit, wait
  for regulator response and log, and a No branch, both rejoining at the
  exclusive merge gateway. Flow continues to the approval task, then to the
  "Third-party notification obligations apply?" gateway splitting into a Yes
  branch covering third-party notification and a No branch, both rejoining at
  their exclusive merge gateway. Flow continues to recording outcomes and the
  end event. In the Communications lane, work starts in parallel after the
  start event: identify scope, draft, issue to individuals, wait for
  acknowledgement, and log responses; the Communications lane work rejoins
  the Legal lane before the "Review and approve individual notification
  content" task via a parallel merge.

Message flows:
  Legal lane "Submit breach notification to regulator" → Regulator (breach
    notification document).
  Regulator → Legal lane "Regulator direction or acknowledgement received"
    (direction or acknowledgement).
  Communications lane "Issue notification to affected individuals" →
    Affected Individual (personal breach notification).
  Affected Individual → Communications lane "Individual acknowledgement or
    response received" (acknowledgement or query).
  Case Management System → Legal lane "Confirm notification obligations and
    statutory deadlines" (incident record, impact assessment, data
    classification).
  Legal lane "Record all notification outcomes in incident record" →
    Case Management System (notification log, regulator correspondence,
    response records).

7. Data objects

  regulatory breach notification"; read by Send task "Submit breach
  notification to regulator".
Data Object "Individual Breach Notification" — written by User task "Draft
  individual breach notification"; read by Send task "Issue notification to

This subprocess fulfils the organisation's legal and regulatory disclosure
obligations following a confirmed breach. Legal confirms which statutory
deadlines apply, drafts and submits regulatory notifications, tracks the
regulator's response, and ensures third-party obligations are met.
Communications drafts and issues notifications to affected individuals and
captures their responses. All outcomes are recorded in the Case Management
System before the subprocess hands a complete notification record to
```

### V16.08 — Eradicate & Recover

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.08 Eradicate & Recover — the subprocess that removes confirmed
threats and restores affected systems, handing a clean and operational
environment to service restoration confirmation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing eradication and recovery.
  Lane "Incident Response" — incident manager coordinating eradication
    activities.
  Lane "IT Operations" — service owner executing technical remediation and
    system recovery.
Pool "IT Service Management" — ITSM platform recording changes and tracking
  recovery tasks.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — EDR platform enforcing eradication
  actions and verifying endpoint cleanliness.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation
2. IT Service Management
3. Endpoint Detection & Response

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response lane:
  Message start event "Contained incident received from Contain Threat"
  User task "Review containment summary and confirm eradication scope"
  User task "Authorise emergency change for eradication actions"
  Send task "Issue eradication work order to IT Operations"
  Intermediate message catch event "Eradication completion confirmed by
    IT Operations"
  User task "Verify eradication against incident indicators of compromise"
  Service task "Request endpoint clean confirmation from Endpoint Detection
    & Response"
  Intermediate message catch event "Endpoint clean status received"
  Exclusive gateway "All endpoints confirmed clean?"
    - branch "No — residual threat detected": User task "Escalate
      residual threat and revise eradication scope"
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised eradication work order
        acknowledged by IT Operations"
      Exclusive merge gateway "All endpoints confirmed clean?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to exclusive merge gateway
  Exclusive merge gateway "All endpoints confirmed clean?"
  User task "Update incident record with eradication outcome"
  Intermediate message catch event "Recovery completion confirmed by
    IT Operations"
  User task "Review recovery outcome and validate service readiness"
  End event "Eradication and recovery complete — ready for Confirm
    Service Restoration"

IT Operations lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Eradication work order received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Eradication Actions Complete"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Identify and remove
    malicious artefacts, accounts, and persistence mechanisms",
    Service task "Apply patches and harden affected systems via Endpoint
    Detection & Response", User task "Log remediation step in IT Service
    Management"
  Send task "Confirm eradication completion to Incident Response"
  User task "Raise recovery change request in IT Service Management"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Systems Restored" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Restore systems and data from
    clean backups", Service task "Record restoration step in IT Service
    Management", User task "Run post-restore health checks"
  Send task "Confirm recovery completion to Incident Response"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Eradication Actions Complete", label "Eradication deadline exceeded",
  triggers User task "Escalate eradication delay to incident manager".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Systems Restored", label "Recovery deadline exceeded", triggers User
  task "Escalate recovery delay to incident manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Incident Response lane with the message
start event, passes through scope review and change authorisation before
issuing a work order to IT Operations. IT Operations executes eradication
in a loop and sends confirmation back; Incident Response verifies endpoints
via the EDR pool, then the exclusive gateway branches on clean status —
the "No" branch escalates and awaits a revised work order before rejoining
the merge gateway, and the "Yes" branch rejoins directly. After the merge,
the incident record is updated, recovery confirmation is awaited from IT
Operations, and the subprocess ends with service readiness validated.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Incident Response) → IT Service Management (eradication
    work order and change authorisation details)
  IT Service Management → Organisation (IT Operations) (change request
    approval and task assignments)
  Organisation (IT Operations) → IT Service Management (remediation step
    logs and restoration records)
  Organisation (Incident Response) → Endpoint Detection & Response
    (request for endpoint clean confirmation)
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Organisation (Incident Response)
    (endpoint clean status)
  Organisation (IT Operations) → Endpoint Detection & Response (eradication
    and patch actions)
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Organisation (IT Operations) (patch and
    hardening results)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Containment Summary" — read by User task "Review containment
  summary and confirm eradication scope".
Data Object "Emergency Change Record" — written by User task "Authorise
  emergency change for eradication actions"; read by User task "Raise
  recovery change request in IT Service Management".
Data Object "Eradication Work Order" — written by Send task "Issue
  eradication work order to IT Operations"; read by IT Operations lane on
  receipt.
Data Object "Indicators of Compromise List" — read by User task "Verify
  eradication against incident indicators of compromise"; read by User task
  "Identify and remove malicious artefacts, accounts, and persistence
  mechanisms".
Data Object "Endpoint Clean Status Report" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Endpoint clean status received"; read by Exclusive
  gateway "All endpoints confirmed clean?".
Data Object "Recovery Completion Report" — written by Send task "Confirm
  recovery completion to Incident Response"; read by User task "Review
  recovery outcome and validate service readiness".

V16.08 Eradicate & Recover takes a fully contained incident and drives the
complete removal of malicious artefacts, persistence mechanisms, and
compromised accounts, then rebuilds or restores affected systems to a
verified clean state using authorised emergency changes tracked in IT
Service Management and endpoint cleanliness confirmed through EDR. Each
eradication and recovery cycle is logged to the incident record, and the
subprocess closes only once the incident manager has validated service
readiness, handing a confirmed-clean environment to V16.09 Confirm Service
Restoration.
```

```text
identify root causes, and produce an approved post-incident report.
Remediation actions are logged with owners in the GRC Platform, the risk
register and lessons-learned log are updated, and the finalised report is
delivered to the Cyber Insurer, bringing the entire chain to a governed
and auditable close.
```


## V17 — Audit to Action

**Teams and roles involved.**
Audit to Action usually involves Internal Audit, Risk and Compliance, the audited Business Units, Finance, IT, and the Audit and Risk Committee. Key roles include chief audit executive, audit manager, auditor, control owner, process owner, remediation owner, risk manager, and committee chair.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are External Auditors and Regulators, and in some sectors certification bodies. The process is initiated by the annual audit plan, a regulatory examination, a certification cycle, or a triggering event such as an incident or whistleblower report. Other external parties include co-sourced audit providers and specialist assessors.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: plan the audit and set scope, notify the auditee and agree logistics, gather evidence and test controls, evaluate findings and rate them, draft the audit report, agree management responses and owners, issue the final report, track remediation to completion, verify and close findings, and report status to the committee.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include audit management, GRC and risk registers, control libraries and testing workpapers, document and evidence repositories, issue and action tracking, data analytics tooling for full-population testing, and board reporting packs.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the internal audit charter and independence requirements, risk-based audit planning methodology, evidence sufficiency and workpaper standards, finding rating criteria, management response and escalation timeframes, overdue-action escalation, retest and closure evidence requirements, and committee reporting obligations.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
External auditors and regulators provide scope requests, information requests, findings and directions; the process provides evidence, management representations, remediation plans and progress reports. Auditees provide process documentation, system access, data extracts and explanations, and receive draft findings, agreed actions and closure confirmations.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates audit plans, engagements, test procedures and results, findings and ratings, management actions, and closure evidence. IT systems provide the control library and risk register, prior findings and their status, transaction and configuration data for testing, action due dates and overdue alerts, and assurance-coverage reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V17.01** Plan Audit & Set Scope | — | Internal Audit (chief audit executive), Risk & Compliance (risk manager) | Audit Management System, GRC Platform |
| **V17.02** Notify Auditee & Agree Logistics | — | Internal Audit (audit manager), Business Unit (process owner) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.03** Gather Evidence & Test Controls | External Auditor | Internal Audit (auditor), Business Unit (control owner) | Audit Management System, Evidence Repository |
| **V17.04** Evaluate & Rate Findings | — | Internal Audit (audit manager) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.05** Draft Audit Report | — | Internal Audit (audit manager) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.06** Agree Management Responses | — | Business Unit (process owner), Internal Audit (audit manager) | Issue & Action Tracking System |
| **V17.07** Issue Final Report | Regulator | Internal Audit (chief audit executive) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.08** Track Remediation | — | Risk & Compliance (risk manager), Business Unit (remediation owner) | Issue & Action Tracking System |
| **V17.09** Verify & Close Findings | — | Internal Audit (auditor) | Audit Management System, Evidence Repository |
| **V17.10** Report to Committee | Audit & Risk Committee | Internal Audit (chief audit executive) | Board Reporting System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V17):

- **External actors:** External Auditor (V17.03); Regulator (V17.07); Audit & Risk Committee (V17.10).
- **Teams:** Internal Audit (V17.01–V17.05, V17.07, V17.09, V17.10); Risk & Compliance (V17.01, V17.08); Business Unit (V17.02, V17.03, V17.06, V17.08).
- **IT systems:** Audit Management System (V17.01–V17.05, V17.07, V17.09); GRC Platform (V17.01); Evidence Repository (V17.03, V17.09); Issue & Action Tracking System (V17.06, V17.08); Board Reporting System (V17.10).

```text
ArchiMate: V17 — Audit to Action — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

diagram is read top-to-bottom as service → process → application,
expressing ArchiMate service realisation.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Business Unit — demand-side actor, far left; initiates audit engagement

  remediation tracking.
- External Auditor — far right; participates in evidence gathering and
  provides scope requests and findings.
- Regulator — far right; receives the final report and may issue directions
  or examination scope.
- Audit & Risk Committee — far right; receives assurance reporting and
  committee packs.

2. Interfaces

- Audit Engagement Interface — accessed by Business Unit (auditee); serves
  the Audit Planning & Scoping Service and the Notification & Logistics
  Service.
- Evidence Submission Interface — accessed by Business Unit (control owner)
  and External Auditor; serves the Evidence & Testing Service.
- Management Response Interface — accessed by Business Unit (process owner);
  serves the Management Response & Action Service.
- Regulatory Reporting Interface — accessed by Regulator; serves the Final
  Report Issuance Service.
- Committee Reporting Interface — accessed by Audit & Risk Committee; serves
  the Committee Assurance Reporting Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Audit Planning & Scoping Service — provides a risk-based annual audit plan
  with defined scope, objectives, and resourcing for each engagement.
- Notification & Logistics Service — provides formal notice of audit, agreed
  timelines, and access arrangements to the auditee.
- Evidence & Testing Service — provides structured collection, validation,
  and testing of controls across the audit population.
- Finding Evaluation & Rating Service — provides assessed and rated findings
  against defined criteria for significance and risk impact.
- Audit Report Drafting Service — provides a structured draft audit report
  for internal review and auditee comment.
- Management Response & Action Service — provides agreed management
  responses, remediation owners, and due dates for each finding.
- Final Report Issuance Service — provides the authorised final audit report
  distributed to relevant stakeholders including the Regulator.
- Remediation Tracking Service — provides ongoing monitoring of action
  completion against agreed due dates with overdue escalation.
- Finding Verification & Closure Service — provides evidence-based
  confirmation that remediation is complete and findings are closed.
- Committee Assurance Reporting Service — provides consolidated assurance
  status and outstanding actions to the Audit & Risk Committee.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V17.01 Plan Audit & Set Scope — risk-based planning and scope definition
  led by Internal Audit with input from Risk & Compliance.
- V17.02 Notify Auditee & Agree Logistics — formal notification and
  scheduling led by Internal Audit with Business Unit coordination.

- V17.07 Issue Final Report — chief audit executive authorises and issues

- V17.08 Track Remediation — Risk & Compliance and Business Unit

- V17.09 Verify & Close Findings — Internal Audit auditor retests and
  confirms closure with supporting evidence.
- V17.10 Report to Committee — chief audit executive presents assurance
  status and outstanding actions to the Audit & Risk Committee.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Audit Management System — core system supporting engagement planning,

- GRC Platform — risk register and control library providing risk-based
  inputs to audit planning.
- Evidence Repository — document and evidence store for workpapers, data

- Issue & Action Tracking System — records management responses, action
  owners, due dates, and overdue escalation alerts.
```

```text
This chain converts an audit trigger — whether an annual audit plan, a

Auditors and Regulators are the primary external participants, supplying
scope requests and information requests and receiving evidence, management
representations, and remediation progress in return. The chain ends when
the Audit and Risk Committee receives a consolidated status report
confirming remediation outcomes and residual risk positions.
```

### V17.01 — Plan Audit & Set Scope

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.01 Plan Audit & Set Scope — first subprocess of the Audit to
Action value chain, establishing the risk-based audit plan and engagement
scope before any auditee contact begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — Internal Audit and Risk & Compliance carrying out
  audit planning and scope-setting activities.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - "Internal Audit (Chief Audit Executive)"
  - "Risk & Compliance (Risk Manager)"
Pool "Audit Management System" — system that records the audit plan,
  engagements, and scope decisions.
Pool "GRC Platform" — system that supplies the risk register and prior
  findings to inform planning.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, two lanes)
2. Audit Management System
3. GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Internal Audit (Chief Audit Executive) lane:
  Start event "Annual audit plan cycle, regulatory examination, or
    triggering event initiates planning"
  User task "Identify audit universe and candidate engagements"
  Service task "Retrieve risk register and prior findings from GRC Platform"
  User task "Apply risk-based prioritisation methodology to rank
    engagements"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient risk information available?"
  - branch "Yes": continue to next task
  - branch "No": Intermediate message catch event "Additional risk input
      received from Risk & Compliance"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient risk information available"
  User task "Draft proposed audit plan and engagement list"
  User task "Define scope, objectives, and criteria for each engagement"
  Exclusive gateway "Internal Audit Charter independence check passed?"
  - branch "Yes": continue to next task
  - branch "No": User task "Resolve independence conflict or reassign
      engagement", then rejoin merge
  Exclusive merge gateway "Independence check passed"
  Service task "Record approved audit plan and scope in Audit Management
    System"
  User task "Obtain chief audit executive sign-off on audit plan"
  End event "Approved audit plan and scope confirmed — ready for Notify
    Auditee & Agree Logistics"

Risk & Compliance (Risk Manager) lane:
  User task "Provide risk register inputs, emerging risks, and prior
    findings summary"
  User task "Review and validate risk ratings applied to candidate
    engagements"
  User task "Confirm regulatory examination requirements and deadlines"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Draft proposed audit plan and
  engagement list" — label "Plan deadline approaching" — triggers a
  non-interrupting Send task "Escalate plan delay to chief audit executive".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Internal Audit lane at the start event,
moves through engagement identification, then crosses to the Risk &
Compliance lane for risk input and validation before returning to Internal
Audit for prioritisation and plan drafting. The "Sufficient risk
information available?" gateway branches: the "No" branch waits at an
intermediate message catch event until Risk & Compliance input arrives,
then rejoins at the merge gateway; the "Yes" branch proceeds directly to
the merge. After drafting, the independence gateway branches: the "No"
branch routes to the conflict-resolution task then rejoins the merge; the
"Yes" branch proceeds directly. Flow ends at the chief audit executive
sign-off task and then the end event.

Message flows:
  GRC Platform → Internal Audit (Chief Audit Executive) lane (risk
    register data, prior findings, and assurance-coverage report)
  Internal Audit (Chief Audit Executive) lane → Audit Management System
    (approved audit plan, engagement list, and scope records)
  Audit Management System → Internal Audit (Chief Audit Executive) lane
    (confirmation of plan recorded and engagement numbers assigned)
  Risk & Compliance (Risk Manager) lane → Internal Audit (Chief Audit
    Executive) lane (risk rating inputs, regulatory deadlines — carried
    as an internal message flow between lanes, represented as data hand-off)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Audit Universe" — written by "Identify audit universe and
  candidate engagements"; read by "Apply risk-based prioritisation
  methodology to rank engagements".
Data Object "Risk Register Extract" — read by "Apply risk-based
  prioritisation methodology to rank engagements"; written by "Provide
  risk register inputs, emerging risks, and prior findings summary".
Data Object "Prior Findings Summary" — read by "Apply risk-based
  prioritisation methodology to rank engagements"; written by "Provide
  risk register inputs, emerging risks, and prior findings summary".
Data Object "Proposed Audit Plan" — written by "Draft proposed audit plan
  and engagement list"; read by "Obtain chief audit executive sign-off on
  audit plan".
Data Object "Engagement Scope Definition" — written by "Define scope,
  objectives, and criteria for each engagement"; read by "Record approved
  audit plan and scope in Audit Management System".

V17.01 takes the organisation from a planning trigger — whether an annual
cycle, a regulatory examination, or an incident — through risk-based
prioritisation and independence checking to a fully signed-off audit plan
and engagement scope. The approved plan, with its scope definitions and
engagement list recorded in the Audit Management System, is the authorising
document handed forward so that V17.02 can begin notifying each auditee
and agreeing the practical logistics of the work.
```

```text
Data Object "Schedule Response" — written by "Review proposed schedule and
  raise any conflicts"; read by exclusive gateway "Schedule agreed?".
Data Object "Confirmed Logistics Record" — written by "Confirm logistics
  and access arrangements"; read by "Record confirmed logistics in Audit
  Management System".

This subprocess takes the approved audit plan from V17.01 and produces a
formally notified, logistically confirmed engagement: the audited Business
Unit has acknowledged the audit, agreed a schedule, and received details of
access arrangements. The confirmed logistics record in the Audit Management
System is the handoff that enables V17.03 Gather Evidence & Test Controls
to begin on a defined date with the right people and access in place.
```


### V17.03 — Gather Evidence & Test Controls

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.03 Gather Evidence & Test Controls — the evidence-gathering and
control-testing subprocess within the Audit to Action value chain, sitting
between Notify Auditee & Agree Logistics and Evaluate & Rate Findings.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams conducting evidence gathering and

  files and supporting documentation.

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Auditor" — black-box, single instance.

Pool "Evidence Repository" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

Top to bottom:
1. External Auditor
2. Organisation
3. Audit Management System
4. Evidence Repository

Internal Audit (Auditor) lane:

  User task "Prepare evidence request list and test procedures"
  Service task "Log evidence requests in Audit Management System"
  Send task "Issue evidence requests to Business Unit"
  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence package received from Business
    Unit"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient to proceed?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to Execute Test Procedures subprocess
    - branch "No": Send task "Request additional or clarified evidence from
        Business Unit"
        Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary evidence received"
        continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient to proceed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient to proceed"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Controls Tested" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Execute test procedure for control",

    Service task "Store evidence in Evidence Repository",
    Service task "Record test result in Audit Management System",
    Exclusive gateway "Control test passed?",

    - branch "Fail": User task "Raise preliminary finding and document
        exception"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Control test outcome recorded"
  Intermediate message catch event "Specialist input received from External
    Auditor"
  User task "Incorporate External Auditor results into workpapers"
  Service task "Update consolidated test results in Audit Management System"
  User task "Review completeness of all test procedures and workpapers"
  Exclusive gateway "All procedures complete and workpapers signed off?"
    - branch "Yes": continue to End event
    - branch "No": User task "Identify and assign outstanding procedures"
        continue to Exclusive merge gateway "All procedures complete"
  Exclusive merge gateway "All procedures complete"
  End event "Evidence and test results complete — ready for Evaluate & Rate
    Findings"

Business Unit (Control Owner) lane:

  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence requests received from Internal
    Audit"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Package Assembled" (standard
    loop) containing, in order:

    User task "Grant system access where required",
    User task "Provide explanations for control operation"
  Send task "Deliver evidence package to Internal Audit"

  User task "Gather supplementary or clarified evidence"
  Send task "Deliver supplementary evidence to Internal Audit"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All

  "Escalate incomplete testing to audit manager" in Internal Audit (Auditor)
  lane, leading to a separate End event "Testing deadline escalated".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Evidence Package Assembled", labelled "Evidence provision deadline
  exceeded", triggers Send task "Alert Internal Audit of evidence delay" in
  Business Unit (Control Owner) lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Internal Audit (Auditor) lane the flow runs from
  the message start event through retrieval and preparation tasks, through
  the evidence-sufficiency gateway and its merge, into the loop subprocess,
  then through external-auditor incorporation, consolidated update, the
  completeness review gateway and its merge, and finally to the end event.
  In the Business Unit (Control Owner) lane the flow runs from the catch
  event through the evidence-assembly loop to the delivery send task, then

  Internal Audit (Auditor) "Service task Record test result in Audit

  Internal Audit (Auditor) "Update consolidated test results in Audit

Data Object "Supplementary Evidence Package" — written by "Gather

This subprocess gathers all evidence needed to assess the in-scope controls,
executes and documents test procedures for each control, incorporates
specialist input from External Auditors, and stores the completed workpapers
in the Evidence Repository and Audit Management System. It hands a full set
of test results and preliminary findings — including any noted control
failures — to Evaluate & Rate Findings, where each finding will be assessed
and assigned a risk rating.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.04 Evaluate & Rate Findings — sits within the Audit to Action

and handing rated findings to Draft Audit Report.

  audit findings, structured into the lanes below.

  ratings, and supporting workpapers.

Pool "Audit Management System": black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Internal Audit Organisation (white-box)
2. Audit Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Internal Audit Organisation)

Internal Audit (audit manager) lane:
  Message start event "Tested evidence and control results received from
    Gather Evidence & Test Controls"
  User task "Review evidence packages and control test results"
  User task "Identify and articulate individual findings"
  Exclusive gateway "Are further tests or clarifications needed?"
  - branch "Yes — additional testing needed":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Is Sufficient"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Request additional evidence or re-test",
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional evidence received",
        User task "Assess sufficiency of additional evidence"
  - branch "No — evidence sufficient":
      continue to exclusive merge gateway
  Exclusive merge gateway "Are further tests or clarifications needed?"
  User task "Apply finding rating criteria to each finding"
  Exclusive gateway "Rating agreed internally?"
  - branch "No — rating disputed":
      User task "Escalate rating disagreement to chief audit executive"
      Intermediate message catch event "Rating adjudication received"
      continue to exclusive merge gateway
  - branch "Yes — rating confirmed":
      continue to exclusive merge gateway
  Exclusive merge gateway "Rating agreed internally?"
  User task "Document rated findings and root-cause analysis in workpapers"
  Service task "Record findings and ratings in Audit Management System"
  User task "Perform quality review of rated findings"
  Exclusive gateway "Quality review passed?"
  - branch "No — rework required":
      User task "Revise findings and ratings"
      continue to exclusive merge gateway
  - branch "Yes — findings approved":
      continue to exclusive merge gateway
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quality review passed?"
  End event "Rated findings approved — ready for Draft Audit Report"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Evidence Is Sufficient", labelled "Sufficiency deadline exceeded",
  leading to User task "Escalate evidence gap to audit manager and
  document limitation".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all flow within the Internal Audit (audit manager) lane
  from the message start event through evidence review, finding
  identification, the sufficiency loop gateway (loop subprocess on the
  "Yes" branch, merging back before rating), rating application, the
  rating-dispute gateway (escalation tasks on the "No" branch, merging
  back after adjudication), workpaper documentation, system recording,
  quality review, and the rework gateway (revision on the "No" branch,
  merging back before the end event), concluding at the end event.

Message flows:
  Internal Audit Organisation → Audit Management System (rated findings
    and root-cause workpapers recorded per service task "Record findings
    and ratings in Audit Management System")
  Audit Management System → Internal Audit Organisation (prior findings,

Data Object "Evidence Package" — read by "Review evidence packages and

Data Object "Audit Finding Record" — written by "Identify and articulate

  in workpapers"; written by "Revise findings and ratings".
Data Object "Finding Rating" — written by "Apply finding rating criteria
  to each finding"; read by "Perform quality review of rated findings".
Data Object "Root-Cause Analysis" — written by "Document rated findings
  and root-cause analysis in workpapers"; read by "Perform quality review

This subprocess takes the raw test results and evidence packages produced
in Gather Evidence & Test Controls, applies the organisation's finding
rating criteria, resolves any internal rating disputes, and completes a
quality review. It delivers a set of formally rated, workpaper-supported
findings — approved by the audit manager — that the next subprocess,
Draft Audit Report, will use to structure the report narrative and
summarise assurance conclusions.
```
