```text
      — ready for Verify & Close Findings"
  - branch "Escalation required": User task "Raise escalation report
      to chief audit executive"
    End event "Escalation reported — ready for Verify & Close
      Findings"

Business Unit lane:
  User task "Confirm remediation activities and provide progress update"
  Service task "Submit evidence of completion for closed actions"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Actions Closed or Escalated", labelled "Maximum tracking period
elapsed", leading to User task "Raise escalation report to chief audit
executive" in the Risk & Compliance lane, then to End event "Escalation
reported — ready for Verify & Close Findings".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Risk & Compliance lane at the
message start event, proceeds through loading actions, setting up the
schedule, and entering the tracking loop. Inside the loop the
"Action status?" gateway branches to an on-track timer wait, an
overdue escalation path through the escalation and recording tasks,
or a closed path through the acceptance task; all branches rejoin at
the exclusive merge gateway "Action status" before the loop repeats.
On loop exit, the risk manager compiles the status summary, then the
"All actions closed or further escalation needed?" gateway branches
to the all-closed end event or the escalation report task followed by
the escalation end event. The Business Unit lane tasks "Confirm
remediation activities and provide progress update" and "Submit
evidence of completion for closed actions" are triggered by sequence
flows from the "Review action progress against due dates" task and
the "Action status?" closed branch respectively, and their outputs
return to the merge gateway.

Message flows:
Issue & Action Tracking System → Risk & Compliance lane, "Load agreed
  actions and due dates from system" (action register with due dates
  and overdue alerts).
Risk & Compliance lane, "Record escalation in system" → Issue & Action
  Tracking System (escalation record update).
Risk & Compliance lane, "Accept closure submission and record status"
  → Issue & Action Tracking System (closure status update).
Issue & Action Tracking System → Risk & Compliance lane, "Retrieve
  action status and overdue alerts" (current action status and alert
  data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Remediation Progress Update" — written by "Confirm
  remediation activities and provide progress update"; read by
  "Review action progress against due dates".
Data Object "Closure Evidence Package" — written by "Submit evidence
  of completion for closed actions"; read by "Accept closure
  submission and record status".
Data Object "Remediation Status Summary" — written by "Compile
  remediation status summary"; read by "All actions closed or further
  escalation needed?" gateway.
Data Object "Escalation Report" — written by "Raise escalation report
  to chief audit executive".

Track Remediation monitors every agreed management action from the
point the final report is issued, cycling through status reviews,
capturing progress updates and closure evidence from Business Unit
remediation owners, and escalating overdue or stalled actions to the
risk manager and, where necessary, the chief audit executive. Once all
actions are either closed or formally escalated, the subprocess hands
a complete remediation status record to Verify & Close Findings, where
Internal Audit independently retests and confirms that each action has
been effectively implemented.
```


### V17.09 — Verify & Close Findings

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.09 Verify & Close Findings — subprocess in the Audit to Action
value chain where Internal Audit retests remediated controls, confirms
closure evidence is sufficient, and formally closes or escalates findings
before the results are reported to the committee.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the verification and closure
  process, with Internal Audit as the acting team.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Internal Audit (auditor)
Pool "Audit Management System" — system that holds findings, closure evidence,
  and engagement status.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — system that stores and retrieves closure evidence
  documents.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation
2. Audit Management System
3. Evidence Repository

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Internal Audit (auditor) lane:
  Message start event "Remediation due date reached — ready for Verify and
    Close Findings"
  Service task "Retrieve open findings and remediation evidence from Audit
    Management System"
  Service task "Pull closure evidence documents from Evidence Repository"
  User task "Review closure evidence against finding and retest criteria"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient and control retested?"
  - branch "Yes — evidence accepted":
      User task "Record finding as closed in Audit Management System"
      Service task "Update finding status to Closed in Evidence Repository"
      End event "Finding closed — ready for Report to Committee"
  - branch "No — evidence insufficient or retest failed":
      Exclusive gateway "Maximum retest attempts reached?"
      - branch "No — further retest possible":
          Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Accepted" (standard loop)
            containing, in order: User task "Request additional remediation
            evidence from remediation owner", Intermediate message catch event
            "Revised evidence received", User task "Review revised closure
            evidence and retest control"
      - branch "Yes — maximum attempts reached":
          User task "Escalate finding as unresolved to audit manager"
          User task "Record finding as escalated in Audit Management System"
          End event "Finding escalated — unresolved finding raised for Report
            to Committee"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient and control retested?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Maximum retest attempts reached?"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Evidence Accepted", labelled "Retest response deadline exceeded", leading
  to User task "Escalate finding as unresolved to audit manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Internal Audit (auditor) lane with the
message start event, proceeding through evidence retrieval and review to the
"Evidence sufficient and control retested?" gateway. The "Yes" branch records
closure and reaches the closed end event. The "No" branch tests maximum
attempts; if not reached, the loop subprocess repeats requesting and reviewing
revised evidence, returning to the "Evidence sufficient and control retested?"
merge gateway on acceptance; if maximum attempts are reached, the escalation
path records an unresolved finding and reaches the escalated end event. The
timer boundary event on the loop subprocess interrupts to the escalation
tasks when the deadline is exceeded.

Message flows:
Audit Management System → Organisation (open findings list and remediation
  status retrieved at process start and updated on closure or escalation).
Evidence Repository → Organisation (closure evidence documents pulled for
  review).
Organisation → Evidence Repository (closed finding status written back after
  closure confirmed).
Organisation → Audit Management System (finding status updated to Closed or
  Escalated).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Closure Evidence Package" — read by "Review closure evidence
  against finding and retest criteria"; written by "Pull closure evidence
  documents from Evidence Repository".
Data Object "Revised Closure Evidence" — read by "Review revised closure
  evidence and retest control"; written by "Request additional remediation
  evidence from remediation owner".
Data Object "Finding Closure Record" — written by "Record finding as closed
  in Audit Management System"; read by "Update finding status to Closed in
  Evidence Repository".

V17.09 Verify & Close Findings is the quality gate that confirms remediation
has genuinely resolved each audit finding. The auditor retrieves open
findings, pulls closure evidence, and retests the control; sufficient evidence
closes the finding, while insufficient evidence triggers a structured loop
requesting further remediation support, escalating to the audit manager if
the deadline or attempt limit is exceeded. The subprocess hands a fully
reconciled set of closed and escalated findings to V17.10 Report to
Committee, giving the chief audit executive an accurate picture of outstanding
risk to present to the Audit and Risk Committee.
```


### V17.10 — Report to Committee

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.10 Report to Committee — final subprocess of Audit to Action,
presenting remediation status and assurance findings to the Audit and Risk
Committee.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — Internal Audit team executing the reporting subprocess,
with lanes for Internal Audit and Risk & Compliance.
Pool "Audit & Risk Committee" — external governing body receiving the report
and providing direction.
Pool "Board Reporting System" — IT system used to publish and distribute the
board reporting pack.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit & Risk Committee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Board Reporting System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Audit & Risk Committee
2. Organisation
3. Board Reporting System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Internal Audit lane:
  Message start event "Verified and closed findings received from Verify and
    Close Findings"
  User task "Compile assurance coverage and remediation status summary"
  User task "Draft committee reporting pack"
  Service task "Publish draft pack to Board Reporting System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Draft pack available in Board Reporting
    System"
  User task "Review and approve pack for committee submission"
  Exclusive gateway "Pack approved?"
    - branch "Revisions required": Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until Pack
        Approved" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Incorporate
        review comments", Service task "Republish revised pack to Board
        Reporting System"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Revise Until Pack Approved"
    - branch "Approved": continue to Send task
  Send task "Submit final pack to Audit and Risk Committee"
  Intermediate message catch event "Committee questions received"
  User task "Prepare responses to committee questions"
  Send task "Send responses to Audit and Risk Committee"
  Intermediate message catch event "Committee resolution and directions received"
  User task "Record committee resolutions and any new directions"
  Service task "Update action register with new committee-directed actions"
  User task "Distribute signed committee minutes and final reporting pack
    to stakeholders"
  End event "Committee report issued and new actions recorded — audit cycle
    complete"

Risk & Compliance lane:
  User task "Contribute risk register status and open-issue metrics"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until Pack
Approved" — label "Revision deadline exceeded" — triggers an escalation end
event notifying the chief audit executive that the pack could not be finalised
in time.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Internal Audit lane at the message start
event and moves forward through compilation, drafting, and publication tasks
before pausing at the intermediate message catch event confirming the draft is
available. The approval gateway branches to the revision subprocess when changes
are needed, rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway before continuing to the
send task. After submission the flow pauses twice more — first for committee
questions and then for committee resolutions — before closing in the Internal
Audit lane. The Risk & Compliance lane contributes its metrics task early in
the flow, feeding the compilation step, with a sequence flow joining into
"Compile assurance coverage and remediation status summary".

Message flows:
Organisation (Send task "Submit final pack to Audit and Risk Committee") →
  Audit & Risk Committee (final reporting pack)
Audit & Risk Committee → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Committee questions received") (committee questions)
Organisation (Send task "Send responses to Audit and Risk Committee") →
  Audit & Risk Committee (responses to questions)
Audit & Risk Committee → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Committee resolution and directions received") (committee resolutions
  and directions)
Organisation (Service task "Publish draft pack to Board Reporting System") →
  Board Reporting System (draft reporting pack)
Board Reporting System → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Draft pack available in Board Reporting System") (publication confirmation)
Organisation (Service task "Update action register with new committee-directed
  actions") → Board Reporting System (updated action register)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Assurance Coverage and Remediation Status Summary" — written by
  "Compile assurance coverage and remediation status summary"; read by "Draft
  committee reporting pack".
Data Object "Risk Register Status and Open-Issue Metrics" — written by
  "Contribute risk register status and open-issue metrics"; read by "Compile
  assurance coverage and remediation status summary".
Data Object "Committee Reporting Pack" — written by "Draft committee reporting
  pack"; read by "Review and approve pack for committee submission" and "Submit
  final pack to Audit and Risk Committee".
Data Object "Committee Questions" — written by intermediate message catch event
  "Committee questions received"; read by "Prepare responses to committee
  questions".
Data Object "Committee Resolutions and Directions" — written by intermediate
  message catch event "Committee resolution and directions received"; read by
  "Record committee resolutions and any new directions".

V17.10 brings the Audit to Action cycle to its governance conclusion. The chief
audit executive presents the consolidated assurance picture — remediation
progress, open findings, and risk coverage — to the Audit and Risk Committee,
fields questions, and records the Committee's resolutions. Any new directions
become tracked actions in the register, and the signed minutes and final pack
are distributed, formally closing the audit cycle until the next planning
horizon triggers V17.01 again.
```


## V18 — Draft to Publish

**Teams and roles involved.**
Draft to Publish usually involves Policy Owners, Risk and Compliance, Legal, Subject-Matter Experts, Document Control, Communications, Learning and Development, and the approving Executive or Board Committee. Key roles include policy author, policy owner, compliance manager, legal reviewer, document controller, communications lead, training coordinator, and approving executive.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Regulators, whose requirements drive much of the content, and where relevant Industry Bodies and external counsel. The process is initiated by a new or changed regulatory obligation, a scheduled policy review date, an audit or incident finding, or an organisational change. Other external parties include external legal advisers, standards bodies, and consultation participants.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: identify the need or trigger, assign an owner and scope the change, draft or revise the document, consult stakeholders and subject-matter experts, obtain legal and compliance review, obtain formal approval, publish and version the document, communicate the change, deliver training and capture attestations, and schedule the next review.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include document management with version control, policy and GRC platforms, workflow and approval tooling, intranet or knowledge portal, learning management system for training and attestation, obligations registers, and reporting on currency and attestation coverage.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the policy framework and document hierarchy, mandatory review cycles, approval authority matrix, version control and change history requirements, consultation requirements, mandatory training and attestation rules, retention of superseded versions, and communication standards for material changes.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Regulators and industry bodies provide obligations, guidance, consultation papers and deadlines; the process provides submissions, attestations and evidence of compliance where required. Consultation participants provide comments and objections and receive dispositions and the final published document.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates drafts, review comments and dispositions, approval records, published versions and effective dates, superseded versions, communication records, and training and attestation records. IT systems provide the obligations register, current document inventory and review dates, approval routing and audit trails, distribution lists, and attestation completion reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V18.01** Identify Need or Trigger | Regulator | Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) | Obligations Register |
| **V18.02** Assign Owner & Scope Change | — | Risk & Compliance (compliance manager), Policy Owner (policy owner) | Policy / GRC Platform |
| **V18.03** Draft or Revise Document | — | Policy Owner (policy author), Subject-Matter Experts (subject-matter expert) | Document Management System |
| **V18.04** Consult Stakeholders | Industry Body | Policy Owner (policy author), Business Unit (stakeholder representative) | Document Management System |
| **V18.05** Obtain Legal & Compliance Review | External Counsel | Legal (legal reviewer), Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) | Policy / GRC Platform |
| **V18.06** Obtain Formal Approval | Board Committee | Executive Management (approving executive) | Workflow & Approval System |
| **V18.07** Publish & Version | — | Document Control (document controller) | Document Management System, Intranet / Knowledge Portal |
| **V18.08** Communicate Change | — | Communications (communications lead) | Intranet / Knowledge Portal |
| **V18.09** Deliver Training & Capture Attestations | — | Learning & Development (training coordinator) | Learning Management System (LMS) |
| **V18.10** Schedule Next Review | — | Document Control (document controller), Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) | Policy / GRC Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V18):

- **External actors:** Regulator (V18.01); Industry Body (V18.04); External Counsel (V18.05); Board Committee (V18.06).
- **Teams:** Risk & Compliance (V18.01, V18.02, V18.05, V18.10); Policy Owner (V18.02–V18.04); Subject-Matter Experts (V18.03); Business Unit (V18.04); Legal (V18.05); Executive Management (V18.06); Document Control (V18.07, V18.10); Communications (V18.08); Learning & Development (V18.09).
- **IT systems:** Obligations Register (V18.01); Policy / GRC Platform (V18.02, V18.05, V18.10); Document Management System (V18.03, V18.04, V18.07); Workflow & Approval System (V18.06); Intranet / Knowledge Portal (V18.07, V18.08); Learning Management System / LMS (V18.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V18 — Draft to Publish — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Draft to Publish value chain, covering everything from initial
regulatory trigger through to scheduled review. The canvas is arranged in
three horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top), BUSINESS
PROCESSES (middle), and APPLICATIONS (bottom). The demand-side actors
(Regulator, Industry Body, External Counsel, Board Committee) sit on the
far left; internal delivery teams occupy the centre; Document Control and
Risk & Compliance as scheduling actors sit on the far right. The view is
read top-to-bottom as service → process → application, expressing
ArchiMate service realisation.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Regulator: demand-side external actor, far left; triggers obligations
  and receives attestation evidence.
- Industry Body: demand-side external actor, far left; provides guidance
  and consultation papers during stakeholder consultation.
- External Counsel: demand-side external actor, far left; provides legal
  advice during legal and compliance review.
- Board Committee: demand-side external actor, far left; acts as formal
  approval authority.
- Document Control: internal delivery actor, far right; owns publishing
  and review scheduling.
- Risk & Compliance: internal delivery actor, far right; owns compliance
  review and next-review scheduling.

2. Interfaces

- Regulatory Intake Interface: accessed by Regulator; serves the
  Identify Need or Trigger business service.
- Industry Consultation Interface: accessed by Industry Body; serves the
  Consult Stakeholders business service.
- External Legal Advisory Interface: accessed by External Counsel; serves
  the Legal & Compliance Review business service.
- Board Approval Interface: accessed by Board Committee; serves the
  Formal Approval business service.
- Document Publication Interface: used by Document Control; serves the
  Publish & Version business service and connects to the Document
  Management System.
- Attestation Reporting Interface: used by Risk & Compliance; serves the
  Schedule Next Review business service and connects to the Policy / GRC
  Platform.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Regulatory Trigger & Obligation Identification Service: provides
  identification of new or changed regulatory obligations, audit findings,
  or scheduled review dates that initiate the chain.
- Owner Assignment & Scoping Service: provides formal assignment of a
  policy owner and scoping of the required change.
- Document Drafting & Revision Service: provides authoring and revision
  of policy documents with subject-matter expert input.
- Stakeholder Consultation Service: provides structured consultation with
  internal stakeholders and external industry participants.
- Legal & Compliance Review Service: provides independent legal and
  compliance assessment of draft documents.
- Formal Approval Service: provides routing and capture of executive or
  board-level approval decisions.
- Publish & Version Control Service: provides controlled publication,
  version numbering, and archiving of superseded documents.
- Change Communication Service: provides notification and distribution
  of published policy changes to affected audiences.
- Training & Attestation Service: provides delivery of training on the
  new or revised policy and capture of staff attestations.
- Review Scheduling Service: provides scheduling and registration of the
  next mandatory policy review date.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger: recognises the regulatory, audit,
  incident, or calendar trigger that initiates the policy lifecycle.
- V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change: formalises ownership and defines
  the scope of the required policy change or new document.
- V18.03 Draft or Revise Document: authors or revises the policy document
  with input from subject-matter experts.
- V18.04 Consult Stakeholders: circulates the draft for comment to
  internal stakeholders, business units, and external industry bodies.
- V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review: routes the draft to Legal and
  Risk & Compliance, incorporating external counsel where required.
- V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval: routes the reviewed document through
  the approval authority matrix to the approving executive or board
  committee.
- V18.07 Publish & Version: document controller publishes the approved
  document, assigns the version number, and archives the superseded
  version.
- V18.08 Communicate Change: communications lead distributes notification
  of the policy change to all affected audiences.
- V18.09 Deliver Training & Capture Attestations: learning and
  development delivers training and records staff attestations of
  understanding.
- V18.10 Schedule Next Review: document controller and compliance manager
  register the next mandatory review date in the GRC platform.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Obligations Register: records and tracks regulatory obligations and
  triggers that initiate the chain.
- Policy / GRC Platform: supports owner assignment, scoping, compliance
  review, and review scheduling; maintains the obligations register
  linkage and attestation reporting.
- Document Management System: stores and versions all draft and
  published documents; supports drafting, consultation, and publication
  workflows.
- Workflow & Approval System: manages approval routing, authority matrix
  enforcement, and audit trail for formal approval decisions.
- Intranet / Knowledge Portal: hosts the published policy library and
  distributes change communications to staff.
- Learning Management System (LMS): delivers training courses linked to
  new or revised policies and records staff attestation completion.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- Obligations Register SERVES V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger.
- Policy / GRC Platform SERVES V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change.
- Policy / GRC Platform SERVES V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review.
- Policy / GRC Platform SERVES V18.10 Schedule Next Review.
- Document Management System SERVES V18.03 Draft or Revise Document.
- Document Management System SERVES V18.04 Consult Stakeholders.
- Document Management System SERVES V18.07 Publish & Version.
- Workflow & Approval System SERVES V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval.
- Intranet / Knowledge Portal SERVES V18.07 Publish & Version.
- Intranet / Knowledge Portal SERVES V18.08 Communicate Change.
- Learning Management System SERVES V18.09 Deliver Training &
  Capture Attestations.

SERVING (business service serves business actor):

- Legal & Compliance Review Service SERVES External Counsel.
- Formal Approval Service SERVES Board Committee.

REALISATION (business process realises business service):

ASSIGNMENT (interface assigned to actor):

ACCESS (process or actor accesses application component):
```

```text
the scheduled next review date against the approved document record.

Communications connects to V18.08 Communicate Change, providing
communications materials and distributing change notices to staff
and relevant stakeholders.

Learning & Development connects to V18.09 Deliver Training & Capture
Attestations, providing training delivery, capturing staff attestations,
and reporting attestation completion coverage.

The system boundary contains all subprocesses from initial trigger
identification through drafting, consultation, legal and compliance
review, formal approval, publishing, communication, training, and
scheduling the next review. It serves internal teams responsible
for policy lifecycle management, external regulators whose obligations
drive content, industry bodies and external counsel who contribute
to review and consultation, and the board committee that provides
final approval authority.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V18 - Draft to Publish

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right, one chevron per stage, in the
order listed below. No chevron may be omitted or reordered.

V18.01. Identify Need or Trigger
V18.02. Assign Owner & Scope Change
V18.03. Draft or Revise Document
V18.04. Consult Stakeholders
V18.05. Obtain Legal & Compliance Review
V18.06. Obtain Formal Approval
V18.07. Publish & Version
V18.08. Communicate Change
V18.09. Deliver Training & Capture Attestations
V18.10. Schedule Next Review

This chain governs the end-to-end lifecycle of an organisational policy or
controlled document, from the moment a need is recognised through to the
scheduling of its next mandatory review. It is triggered externally by
Regulators — through a new or changed obligation, a consultation paper, or
a compliance deadline — or internally by a scheduled review date, an audit
finding, an incident, or an organisational change. The chain ensures that
every document is correctly scoped, drafted with subject-matter input,
reviewed by Legal and Compliance, formally approved at the right authority
level, versioned and published, communicated to affected staff, supported
by training and attestation evidence, and registered for future review.
```
### V18.01 — Identify Need or Trigger

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger — opening subprocess of the Draft to
Publish value chain, receiving regulatory and internal triggers and logging
confirmed obligations for owner assignment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the identify-need process,
  containing the Risk & Compliance team.
Pool "Regulator" — external regulatory body that issues obligations,
  guidance, and consultation papers.
Pool "Obligations Register" — IT system holding the obligations register
  and current document inventory.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Obligations Register" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Regulator
2. Organisation
3. Obligations Register

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Message start event "Regulatory obligation, guidance, or review trigger
    received"
  User task "Log and categorise trigger"
  Exclusive gateway "Trigger type?"
  - branch "External regulatory or industry obligation": User task
      "Retrieve current obligation details from register"
    Intermediate message catch event "Obligation detail confirmed"
  - branch "Scheduled review date": User task "Retrieve document and
      review date from register"
    Intermediate message catch event "Document record retrieved"
  - branch "Audit or incident finding": User task "Record audit or
      incident reference"
  - branch "Organisational change": User task "Record organisational
      change details"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Trigger type"
  User task "Assess materiality and urgency"
  Exclusive gateway "Proceed with policy change?"
  - branch "Yes — material or mandatory": User task "Confirm need and
      document trigger rationale"
    Service task "Record confirmed trigger in Obligations Register"
    End event "Trigger confirmed — ready for Assign Owner and Scope
      Change"
  - branch "No — not material": User task "Record decision not to
      proceed"
    End event "No action required — trigger closed"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins at the message start event in the Risk &
Compliance lane, passes through "Log and categorise trigger" to the
"Trigger type?" exclusive gateway. Each branch handles its specific
trigger category and rejoins at the "Trigger type" exclusive merge
gateway. Flow continues to "Assess materiality and urgency" and then to
the "Proceed with policy change?" exclusive gateway, whose "Yes" branch
ends at the confirmed trigger end event and whose "No" branch ends at the
closed end event.

Message flows:
Regulator → Risk & Compliance lane (regulatory obligation, guidance,
  consultation paper, or deadline notification).
Risk & Compliance lane → Obligations Register (query for current
  obligation details and document review dates).
Obligations Register → Risk & Compliance lane (obligation details and
  document record returned).
Risk & Compliance lane → Obligations Register (confirmed trigger record
  written).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Trigger Log" — written by "Log and categorise trigger";
  read by "Assess materiality and urgency".
Data Object "Trigger Rationale" — written by "Confirm need and document
  trigger rationale".

This subprocess captures every inbound signal — regulatory obligation,
scheduled review, audit finding, or organisational change — assesses
whether it warrants a policy change, and records a confirmed trigger with
its rationale in the Obligations Register. A confirmed trigger is handed
to the next subprocess, Assign Owner and Scope Change, which will
allocate a policy owner and define the scope of the required change. A
decision not to proceed closes the trigger without further action.
```


### V18.02 — Assign Owner & Scope Change

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change — second subprocess in the
Draft to Publish value chain, receiving a confirmed trigger from Identify
Need or Trigger and handing a scoped, owned change to Draft or Revise
Document.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the policy lifecycle process,
containing Risk & Compliance and Policy Owner lanes.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — workflow and registry system supporting
assignment, scoping, and record-keeping.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Organisation" — top (white-box process pool).
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — bottom (IT system pool).

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Message start event "Confirmed trigger received from Identify Need or
    Trigger"
  User task "Review trigger record and classify change type"
  User task "Identify candidate policy owner"
  Send task "Issue assignment notification to policy owner"
  Intermediate message catch event "Policy owner acceptance received"
  Exclusive gateway "Owner accepted assignment?"
  - branch "Yes": continue to Exclusive merge gateway
      "Owner accepted assignment"
  - branch "No": User task "Identify alternative policy owner", then Send
      task "Issue revised assignment notification", then Intermediate
      message catch event "Revised acceptance received", then Exclusive
      merge gateway "Owner accepted assignment"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Owner accepted assignment"
  Service task "Record assignment in Policy / GRC Platform"
  User task "Review and confirm scope definition from policy owner"
  Exclusive gateway "Scope agreed?"
  - branch "Yes": continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Scope agreed"
  - branch "No": User task "Log scope objection and facilitate resolution",
      then Exclusive merge gateway "Scope agreed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Scope agreed"
  Service task "Record final scope in Policy / GRC Platform"
  End event "Owner assigned and scope confirmed — ready for Draft or
    Revise Document"

Policy Owner lane:
  User task "Assess assignment and confirm or decline"
  User task "Define change scope and affected documents"
  User task "Submit scope definition for Risk & Compliance confirmation"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Policy owner acceptance received" — label "Assignment overdue (3 business
days)" — if no acceptance is received within three business days, flow
moves to User task "Escalate unacknowledged assignment to compliance
manager" in the Risk & Compliance lane, ending at a separate End event
"Assignment escalated — awaiting owner confirmation".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Risk & Compliance lane the flow runs from the
start event through classification, candidate identification, and the
assignment notification send task, then pauses at the intermediate message
catch event awaiting the Policy Owner lane response; the gateway branches
handle decline and re-assignment before merging; after the merge, recording
and scope confirmation continue, with the scope-agreement gateway branching
to resolution before merging and concluding at the end event. Message flows
connect the Policy Owner lane tasks back into the Risk & Compliance lane at
the catch events.

Message flows:
Policy / GRC Platform → Risk & Compliance lane, Service task "Record
  assignment in Policy / GRC Platform" (assignment record confirmation).
Policy / GRC Platform → Risk & Compliance lane, Service task "Record final
  scope in Policy / GRC Platform" (scope record confirmation).
Risk & Compliance lane, Send task "Issue assignment notification to policy
  owner" → Policy Owner lane, User task "Assess assignment and confirm or
  decline" (assignment notification).
Policy Owner lane, User task "Assess assignment and confirm or decline" →
  Risk & Compliance lane, Intermediate message catch event "Policy owner
  acceptance received" (acceptance or decline response).
Risk & Compliance lane, Send task "Issue revised assignment notification" →
  Policy Owner lane, User task "Assess assignment and confirm or decline"
  (revised assignment notification).
Policy Owner lane, User task "Submit scope definition for Risk & Compliance
  confirmation" → Risk & Compliance lane, User task "Review and confirm
  scope definition from policy owner" (scope definition document).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Trigger Record" — read by Risk & Compliance lane, User task
  "Review trigger record and classify change type".
Data Object "Assignment Notification" — written by Risk & Compliance lane,
  Send task "Issue assignment notification to policy owner"; read by Policy
  Owner lane, User task "Assess assignment and confirm or decline".
Data Object "Scope Definition" — written by Policy Owner lane, User task
  "Define change scope and affected documents"; read by Risk & Compliance
  lane, User task "Review and confirm scope definition from policy owner".

This subprocess takes the confirmed trigger produced by Identify Need or
Trigger and establishes clear accountability and boundaries for the change.
Risk & Compliance classifies the trigger, nominates and confirms a policy
owner, and jointly agrees the scope of affected documents with that owner.
The resulting assignment record and scoped change brief, registered in the
Policy / GRC Platform, are handed to Draft or Revise Document so that
authoring work can begin with an unambiguous remit.
```


### V18.03 — Draft or Revise Document

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.03 Draft or Revise Document — the authoring subprocess within
the Draft to Publish value chain, sitting between Assign Owner & Scope
Change and Consult Stakeholders.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the team performing drafting and revision work,
  with lanes for Policy Owner and Subject-Matter Experts.
Pool "Document Management System" — the version-controlled repository
  used to store and retrieve drafts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. Document Management System (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Policy Owner lane:
  Message start event "Scoped change brief received from Assign
    Owner & Scope Change"
  User task "Retrieve current document version and scope brief"
  Exclusive gateway "New document or revision?"
  - branch "New document": User task "Create document shell from
      approved template"
  - branch "Revision": Service task "Check out existing document
      from Document Management System"
  Exclusive merge gateway "New document or revision?"
  User task "Prepare initial draft or revised sections"
  Send task "Send draft sections to Subject-Matter Experts for
    input"
  Intermediate message catch event "Subject-matter expert input
    received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Draft Accepted by Policy
    Author" (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review SME input and annotate draft",
    User task "Incorporate accepted changes into draft",
    User task "Assess draft completeness against scope brief",
    Exclusive gateway "Further SME input needed?",
    - branch "Yes": Send task "Request additional SME input",
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional SME input
        received"
    - branch "No": (exit loop)
    Exclusive merge gateway "Further SME input needed?"
  User task "Conduct internal quality and consistency check"
  Exclusive gateway "Draft meets quality standard?"
  - branch "No": User task "Record quality issues and revise
      draft" then rejoin
  - branch "Yes": continue
  Exclusive merge gateway "Draft meets quality standard?"
  Service task "Save approved draft version in Document
    Management System"
  End event "Draft complete — ready for Consult Stakeholders"

Subject-Matter Experts lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Draft sections received from
    Policy Author"
  User task "Review assigned draft sections"
  User task "Provide written input, corrections and commentary"
  Send task "Return input to Policy Owner"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event, interrupting, attached to Expanded
  Subprocess "Repeat Until Draft Accepted by Policy Author",
  label "Drafting deadline exceeded", leading to End event
  "Draft escalated — deadline breached".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Policy Owner lane with the
  message start event, passes through the gateway branching on
  new versus revision, merges, then proceeds through initial
  drafting and the send task to Subject-Matter Experts; the
  Subject-Matter Experts lane runs in parallel through review
  and return of input; the Policy Owner lane resumes after the
  intermediate message catch event, entering the standard-loop
  subprocess; on exit the flow continues through the quality
  gateway, branching to revision on failure and merging on
  success, then to the service task saving the draft and the
  end event.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Policy Owner lane) → Document Management System
    (check-out / check-in of document version).
  Document Management System → Organisation (Policy Owner lane)
    (current document version and template retrieved).
  Organisation (Subject-Matter Experts lane) → Organisation
    (Policy Owner lane) (SME written input and commentary —
    internal message flow across lanes).
  Organisation (Policy Owner lane) → Document Management System
    (approved draft saved with new version record).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Scoped Change Brief" — read by "Retrieve current
  document version and scope brief".
Data Object "Approved Document Template" — read by "Create
  document shell from approved template".
Data Object "Working Draft" — written by "Prepare initial draft
  or revised sections"; read by "Review SME input and annotate
  draft"; written by "Incorporate accepted changes into draft".
Data Object "SME Input Record" — written by "Provide written
  input, corrections and commentary"; read by "Review SME input
  and annotate draft".
Data Object "Quality Check Record" — written by "Conduct
  internal quality and consistency check"; read by "Record
  quality issues and revise draft".

V18.03 takes the scoped change brief produced in V18.02 and
produces a quality-checked, version-controlled working draft
that fully reflects the approved scope. Policy Owner and
Subject-Matter Experts collaborate in an iterative loop until
the draft is internally accepted and saved to the Document
Management System. The completed draft is then handed to
V18.04 Consult Stakeholders for broader review and comment.
```


### V18.04 — Consult Stakeholders

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.04 Consult Stakeholders — the fourth subprocess in the
Draft to Publish value chain, where the policy author circulates a draft
document to internal business units and, where relevant, external industry
bodies, collects and dispositions comments, and hands a consultation-closed
draft to Legal and Compliance for review.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the consultation process,
  containing the Policy Owner and Business Unit teams.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Policy Owner lane (key role: policy author)
  - Business Unit lane (key role: stakeholder representative)
Pool "Industry Body" — external industry body that receives the draft and
  returns comments or guidance.
Pool "Document Management System" — platform used to circulate, store, and
  track drafts, comments, and disposition records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Industry Body" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Industry Body
2. Organisation (Policy Owner lane above Business Unit lane)
3. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Policy Owner lane:
  Message start event "Draft document received from Draft or Revise Document"
  User task "Identify consultation scope and stakeholder list"
  User task "Prepare consultation package"
  Service task "Upload draft and consultation package to Document
    Management System"
  Send task "Distribute consultation package to Business Unit
    stakeholders"
  Exclusive gateway "External consultation required?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Send draft to Industry Body for comment"
      Intermediate message catch event "Industry Body response received"
      User task "Log external comments in Document Management System"
  - branch "No": continue to exclusive merge gateway
  Exclusive merge gateway "External consultation required"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Internal consultation period elapsed"
  User task "Collate all stakeholder comments"
  Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Until All Comments Dispositioned"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review comment and determine disposition",
    User task "Record disposition in Document Management System",
    User task "Notify stakeholder of disposition"
  User task "Prepare consultation summary report"
  Service task "Store consultation summary in Document Management System"
  End event "Consultation closed — ready for Obtain Legal and
    Compliance Review"

Business Unit lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Consultation package received"
  User task "Review draft document"
  User task "Submit comments and objections"
  Intermediate message catch event "Disposition notification received"
  User task "Acknowledge disposition"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Until
  All Comments Dispositioned", labelled "Consultation deadline exceeded",
  leading to User task "Escalate unresolved comments to policy author for
  executive decision" in the Policy Owner lane, then rejoining before
  "Prepare consultation summary report".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Within the Policy Owner lane, flow runs from the message
start event through scope identification, package preparation, system
upload, and distribution, then to the exclusive gateway "External
consultation required?". The "Yes" branch sends the draft to the Industry
Body, waits for the response, and logs external comments before merging
at the exclusive merge gateway "External consultation required". The "No"
branch proceeds directly to that merge gateway. After the merge, the timer
catch event fires when the internal consultation period elapses, leading
to comment collation, the resolution subprocess, summary preparation,
system storage, and the end event. In the Business Unit lane, flow runs
from receipt of the package through review and comment submission, then
waits for the disposition notification and ends with acknowledgement.

Message flows:
Send task "Distribute consultation package to Business Unit stakeholders"
  → Business Unit lane Intermediate message catch event "Consultation
  package received" (consultation package including draft document).
Business Unit lane User task "Submit comments and objections" →
  Policy Owner lane User task "Collate all stakeholder comments"
  (stakeholder comments and objections).
Policy Owner lane User task "Notify stakeholder of disposition" →
  Business Unit lane Intermediate message catch event "Disposition
  notification received" (comment disposition and rationale).
Send task "Send draft to Industry Body for comment" → Industry Body
  (draft document for external comment).
Industry Body → Intermediate message catch event "Industry Body response
  received" (external comments and guidance).
Service task "Upload draft and consultation package to Document
  Management System" → Document Management System (draft document and
  consultation package).
Service task "Store consultation summary in Document Management System"
  → Document Management System (consultation summary report and
  disposition records).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Consultation Package" — written by User task "Prepare
  consultation package"; read by Send task "Distribute consultation
  package to Business Unit stakeholders" and Send task "Send draft to
  Industry Body for comment".
Data Object "Stakeholder Comment Register" — written by Business Unit
  lane User task "Submit comments and objections" and User task "Log
  external comments in Document Management System"; read by User task
  "Collate all stakeholder comments".
Data Object "Comment Disposition Record" — written by User task "Record
  disposition in Document Management System"; read by User task "Notify
  stakeholder of disposition".
Data Object "Consultation Summary Report" — written by User task "Prepare
  consultation summary report"; read by Service task "Store consultation
  summary in Document Management System".

V18.04 Consult Stakeholders opens when the drafted or revised document
arrives from the preceding subprocess and closes when every comment has
been dispositioned and a consultation summary has been stored in the
Document Management System. It ensures that Business Unit representatives
and, where required, the Industry Body have had a structured opportunity
to review and comment on the draft, and that all feedback is formally
recorded and resolved. The closed, annotated draft and the consultation
summary report are then handed to Legal and Risk and Compliance for the
legal and compliance review in V18.05.
```


### V18.05 — Obtain Legal & Compliance Review

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review — sits within the Draft to
Publish value chain, receiving a consulted draft and returning a reviewed,
legally cleared document ready for formal approval.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the teams that run the legal and compliance review.
  Lane "Legal" — legal reviewer conducts legal review and engages external
    counsel.
  Lane "Risk & Compliance" — compliance manager conducts compliance review
    and consolidates outcomes.
Pool "External Counsel" — external legal advisers who provide specialist
  legal opinion.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — workflow and records system supporting
  review routing, comment capture, and disposition logging.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Counsel" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. External Counsel
2. Organisation (Legal lane above Risk & Compliance lane)
3. Policy / GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Consulted draft received from Consult Stakeholders"
  Service task "Retrieve current draft and consultation record from Policy /
    GRC Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "External counsel required?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Engage external counsel and transmit draft"
      Intermediate message catch event "External counsel opinion received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "External counsel required?"
  - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "External counsel required?"
  User task "Conduct legal review and annotate draft"
  User task "Record legal review comments in Policy / GRC Platform"
  Send task "Transmit legal review outcome to Risk & Compliance"

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Legal review outcome received"
  User task "Conduct compliance review against obligations register"
  User task "Record compliance review comments in Policy / GRC Platform"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Issues Resolved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Identify outstanding legal or compliance
    issues", User task "Request clarification or revision from Legal",
    Intermediate message catch event "Clarification or revised input
    received", User task "Assess whether issues are resolved"
  User task "Consolidate legal and compliance review findings"
  Exclusive gateway "Review outcome?"
  - branch "Cleared": User task "Record clearance and close review in Policy
      / GRC Platform"
      End event "Legal and compliance clearance confirmed — ready for
        Obtain Formal Approval"
  - branch "Rejected — material issues unresolved": Send task "Return draft
      to Policy Owner with issues noted"
      End event "Draft returned to Draft or Revise Document for rework"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  All Issues Resolved", labelled "Review deadline exceeded", triggering an
  Escalation send task "Escalate unresolved review to compliance manager
  and legal reviewer" — flow continues on subprocess completion.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane with the message start event,
proceeds to draft retrieval, then to the external counsel gateway; the "Yes"
branch sends the draft to External Counsel, waits for the opinion, and
rejoins at the merge gateway; the "No" branch goes directly to the merge
gateway; both branches continue to the legal review and comment tasks, then
the send task passes control to the Risk & Compliance lane; in that lane
flow proceeds through the compliance review, the loop subprocess, and the
consolidation task to the review outcome gateway; the "Cleared" branch
ends with approval confirmed; the "Rejected" branch ends with the draft
returned.

Message flows:
External Counsel → Legal lane (external counsel legal opinion)
Legal lane → External Counsel (draft document and review instructions)
Legal lane → Policy / GRC Platform (legal review comments logged)
Risk & Compliance lane → Policy / GRC Platform (compliance review comments
  and clearance record logged)
Policy / GRC Platform → Legal lane (current draft and consultation record
  retrieved)
Risk & Compliance lane → Policy Owner (draft returned with issues noted,
  on rejection branch)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Consulted Draft" — read by User task "Conduct legal review
  and annotate draft"; read by User task "Conduct compliance review against
  obligations register".
Data Object "External Counsel Opinion" — read by User task "Conduct legal
  review and annotate draft".
Data Object "Legal Review Comments" — written by User task "Record legal
  review comments in Policy / GRC Platform".
Data Object "Compliance Review Comments" — written by User task "Record
  compliance review comments in Policy / GRC Platform".
Data Object "Consolidated Review Findings" — written by User task
  "Consolidate legal and compliance review findings"; read by Exclusive
  gateway "Review outcome?".

V18.05 brings the consulted draft through structured legal and compliance
scrutiny, engaging external counsel where specialist opinion is needed and
cycling through issue resolution until all material concerns are addressed
or the draft is returned for rework. On clearance, the subprocess passes a
legally and compliance-approved document, with a full audit trail in the
Policy / GRC Platform, to V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval.
```

```text
Pool "Board Committee" — external governing body that issues final

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Board Committee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Workflow & Approval System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Board Committee" — top.
Pool "Organisation" — middle (white-box process pool).
Pool "Workflow & Approval System" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Executive Management lane:
  Message start event "Compliance-reviewed document received from
    Obtain Legal & Compliance Review"
  User task "Prepare approval submission package"
  Service task "Submit package to Workflow & Approval System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received from
    Board Committee"
  Exclusive gateway "Decision?"
  - branch "Approved": User task "Confirm approval and record outcome"
    then continue to End event
  - branch "Rejected with conditions": Send task "Return document with
    rejection reasons to Risk & Compliance"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision?"
  End event "Approval confirmed — ready for Publish & Version"

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Message catch event "Rejection and reasons received"
  User task "Log rejection and initiate rework instruction"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Rework Accepted" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Coordinate document rework with
    Policy Owner", User task "Re-submit revised document for legal
    and compliance check", Intermediate message catch event "Re-review
    outcome received", User task "Assess re-review outcome and confirm
    readiness"
  User task "Repackage revised document for re-submission"
  Send task "Forward repackaged document to Executive Management"
    (sequence returns to Executive Management User task "Prepare
    approval submission package" via message flow)

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Rework Accepted", label "Rework deadline exceeded", triggers: Error
  end event "Rework escalation — process cannot continue".
Non-interrupting escalation boundary event on User task "Prepare
  approval submission package", label "Submission overdue", triggers:
  User task "Escalate delay to compliance manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Executive Management lane, flow runs from
  the message start event through preparation and submission, then waits
  for the Board Committee decision, enters the Decision gateway, the
  approved branch proceeds to confirm and record then merges at the
  Exclusive merge gateway and reaches the end event; the rejected branch
  sends the rejection to Risk & Compliance and does not rejoin the merge.
  Within the Risk & Compliance lane, flow runs from the message catch
  event through logging, into the rework subprocess, then repackaging
  and forward to Executive Management for re-submission. Gateway
  branches rejoin at the named Exclusive merge gateway "Decision?" in
  the approved path only; the rejected branch terminates that execution
  path in Risk & Compliance and re-enters Executive Management as a
  message flow.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Executive Management) → Workflow & Approval System
    (approval package submitted for routing).
  Workflow & Approval System → Board Committee (routed approval
    package and supporting materials).
  Board Committee → Organisation (Executive Management) (formal
    approval decision or rejection with reasons).
  Organisation (Executive Management) → Organisation (Risk &
    Compliance) (rejection notification and reasons — internal message
    flow between lanes).
  Organisation (Risk & Compliance) → Organisation (Executive
    Management) (repackaged revised document ready for re-submission —
    internal message flow between lanes).
  Workflow & Approval System → Organisation (Executive Management)
    (workflow status updates and audit trail confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approval Submission Package" — written by User task
  "Prepare approval submission package"; read by Service task "Submit
  package to Workflow & Approval System".
Data Object "Formal Approval Decision" — read by User task "Confirm
  approval and record outcome"; read by User task "Log rejection and
  initiate rework instruction".
Data Object "Rejection Reasons" — read by User task "Log rejection and
  initiate rework instruction"; read by User task "Coordinate document
  rework with Policy Owner".
Data Object "Rework Instruction" — written by User task "Log rejection
  and initiate rework instruction"; read by User task "Coordinate
  document rework with Policy Owner".

This subprocess receives the compliance-reviewed document from Obtain
Legal & Compliance Review and manages all steps needed to secure a
formal approval decision from the Board Committee via the Workflow &
Approval System. Where the document is rejected, Risk & Compliance
coordinates rework and re-submission until the document is accepted or
a deadline escalation terminates the loop. On approval, the confirmed
outcome and audit record are handed forward to Publish & Version.
```


### V18.07 — Publish & Version

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
Pool "Document Management System" — below Organisation.

    Approval"

  User task "Assign version number and set effective date"
  Service task "Upload versioned document to Document Management System"

    Management System"

  Intermediate message catch event "Publication confirmed by Intranet /
    Knowledge Portal"
  User task "Record published version, effective date and change summary"
  Exclusive gateway "Is the change material?"
    - branch "Yes — material change": continue to next task
    - branch "No — minor or administrative change": skip to end event
  Exclusive merge gateway "Is the change material?"
  User task "Flag record for mandatory communication and training"
  End event "Document published and versioned — ready for Communicate
    Change"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Upload versioned document
  to Document Management System", labelled "Upload timeout — 24 hours";
  flows to End event "Upload failure — escalate to Document Control

Interrupting timer boundary event on Service task "Publish document to
  Intranet / Knowledge Portal", labelled "Portal publish timeout —
  4 hours"; flows to End event "Portal publication failure — escalate

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Document Control lane with the message

Message flows:

  Document Management System → Organisation (Intermediate message catch

Data Object "Approval Record" — read by User task "Retrieve approved

V18.07 Publish & Version takes the formally approved document from

stores it in the Document Management System, archives the superseded
version, and publishes the live document to the Intranet / Knowledge
```

## V19 — Request to Access

**Teams and roles involved.**
Request to Access usually involves IT Service Desk, Identity and Access Management, Application and System Owners, Line Managers, Security, HR, and Internal Audit for periodic review. Key roles include requester, approving line manager, application owner, access administrator, identity engineer, security officer, and access-review certifier.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Contractors, Partners and Vendors who need access to organisational systems, and the Auditor who tests the controls. The process is initiated by a joiner, mover or leaver event, a project or engagement starting, a privileged-access request, or a scheduled access recertification. Other external parties include managed service providers and identity federation partners.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: raise the access request, validate identity and employment or engagement status, determine the entitlements required, check for segregation-of-duties conflicts, obtain approvals, provision the access, notify and confirm with the requester, review access periodically, revoke on change or exit, and evidence the whole cycle for audit.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include identity and access management, single sign-on and directory services, privileged access management, IT service management for requests, HR systems as the source of truth for people, application-level entitlement stores, access-review/certification tooling, and logging for audit evidence.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the access control policy, least-privilege and need-to-know principles, role definitions and entitlement catalogues, segregation-of-duties matrix, approval authority, privileged access rules and time limits, joiner/mover/leaver procedure, periodic recertification frequency, and revocation timeframes on termination.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Contractors and partners provide identity evidence, engagement details and acceptance of acceptable-use terms, and receive credentials, access confirmations and revocation notices. Auditors receive access registers, approval evidence, recertification results and exception reports.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates access requests, approvals, entitlement grants and revocations, segregation-of-duties exceptions, recertification decisions, and audit evidence. IT systems provide employment and engagement status, the entitlement catalogue and role definitions, current access holdings, conflict detection results, provisioning status, and orphaned or dormant account reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V19.01** Raise Access Request | Contractor | IT Service Desk (service desk agent) | IT Service Management |
| **V19.02** Validate Identity & Status | Contractor | IT Service Desk (service desk agent), Human Resources (HR officer) | HR System, Identity & Access Management |
| **V19.03** Determine Entitlements Required | — | Identity & Access Management (identity engineer), Application Owner (application owner) | Identity & Access Management |
| **V19.04** Check Segregation of Duties | — | Security (security officer) | Identity & Access Management, GRC Platform |
| **V19.05** Obtain Approvals | — | Line Management (approving line manager), Application Owner (application owner) | IT Service Management |
| **V19.06** Provision Access | — | Identity & Access Management (access administrator) | Identity & Access Management, Directory Services |
| **V19.07** Notify & Confirm with Requester | Contractor | IT Service Desk (service desk agent) | IT Service Management |
| **V19.08** Review Access Periodically | — | Application Owner (access-review certifier), Security (security officer) | Access Certification Platform |
| **V19.09** Revoke on Change or Exit | — | Human Resources (HR officer), Identity & Access Management (access administrator) | HR System, Identity & Access Management |
| **V19.10** Evidence for Audit | Auditor | Security (security officer), Internal Audit (auditor) | Access Certification Platform, GRC Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V19):

- **External actors:** Contractor (V19.01, V19.02, V19.07); Auditor (V19.10).
- **Teams:** IT Service Desk (V19.01, V19.02, V19.07); Human Resources (V19.02, V19.09); Identity & Access Management (V19.03, V19.06, V19.09); Application Owner (V19.03, V19.05, V19.08); Security (V19.04, V19.08, V19.10); Line Management (V19.05); Internal Audit (V19.10).
- **IT systems:** IT Service Management (V19.01, V19.05, V19.07); HR System (V19.02, V19.09); Identity & Access Management (V19.02–V19.04, V19.06, V19.09); GRC Platform (V19.04, V19.10); Directory Services (V19.06); Access Certification Platform (V19.08, V19.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V19 — Request to Access — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Request to Access value chain, covering the full lifecycle from initial
access request through periodic review, revocation, and audit evidence. The
diagram is organised in three horizontal bands read top-to-bottom as service
realisation: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) expresses what the organisation
delivers to requesters and auditors; BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) shows
the ten subprocesses that realise those services; APPLICATIONS (bottom band)
shows the IT systems that support those processes. The Contractor sits on the
far left as the primary demand-side actor initiating access requests and
receiving confirmations; the Auditor sits on the far right as the external
assurance actor receiving audit evidence.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Contractor: demand-side actor, far left; initiates access requests, provides
  identity evidence, receives credentials and revocation notices.
- Auditor: assurance actor, far right; receives access registers, approval
  evidence, recertification results and exception reports.
- IT Service Desk: internal team, left of centre; handles request intake,
  identity validation and requester notification.
- Human Resources: internal team, left of centre; provides employment and
  engagement status; drives joiner/mover/leaver events.
- Identity & Access Management: internal team, centre; determines entitlements,
  provisions access, and executes revocations.
- Application Owner: internal team, centre; confirms entitlements required and
  certifies periodic access reviews.
- Security: internal team, centre-right; checks segregation of duties and
  participates in periodic review and audit evidence.
- Line Management: internal team, centre; provides approval authority for
  access grants.
- Internal Audit: internal team, far right; reviews audit evidence alongside the
  external Auditor.

2. Interfaces

- Access Request Interface: used by Contractor (ACCESSES) to submit access
  requests; serves the Access Request Handling service.
- Approval Interface: used by Line Management and Application Owner (ACCESSES)
  to submit and record approvals; serves the Access Approval service.
- Notification Interface: used by IT Service Desk (ACCESSES) to send
  credentials and confirmations to Contractor; serves the Requester
  Notification service.
- Audit Evidence Interface: used by Auditor and Internal Audit (ACCESSES) to
  retrieve access registers and recertification reports; serves the Audit
  Evidence service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Access Request Handling: provides a structured channel for requesters to
  raise and track access requests.
- Identity Validation: provides verification of requester identity, employment
  or engagement status against authoritative sources.
- Entitlement Determination: provides mapping of business role to the
  entitlements and permissions required.
- Segregation of Duties Checking: provides conflict detection against the
  segregation-of-duties matrix before access is granted.
- Access Approval: provides a governed approval workflow capturing line-manager
  and application-owner sign-off.
- Access Provisioning: provides automated or administered provisioning of
  approved entitlements to target systems and directories.
- Requester Notification: provides timely confirmation of access grant or
  rejection, including credential delivery.
- Access Recertification: provides periodic certification campaigns to confirm
  or revoke continuing access entitlements.
- Access Revocation: provides timely revocation of access on change-of-role or
  exit events.
- Audit Evidence: provides compiled access registers, approval logs,
  recertification results and exception reports for audit consumption.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V19.01 Raise Access Request: requester or IT Service Desk logs the access
  request in the service management tool.
- V19.02 Validate Identity & Status: IT Service Desk and HR verify identity
  evidence and confirm employment or engagement status.
- V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required: Identity & Access Management and
  Application Owner identify the specific entitlements needed.
- V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties: Security evaluates the request against
  the segregation-of-duties matrix and flags conflicts.
- V19.05 Obtain Approvals: Line Management and Application Owner formally
  approve or reject the access request.
- V19.06 Provision Access: Identity & Access Management administrator
  provisions approved entitlements to directory and target systems.
- V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester: IT Service Desk sends access
  confirmation, credentials or rejection notice to the requester.
- V19.08 Review Access Periodically: Application Owner and Security certify
  current access holdings and revoke where no longer justified.
- V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit: HR triggers and Identity & Access Management
  executes timely revocation of access on role change or termination.
- V19.10 Evidence for Audit: Security and Internal Audit compile and present
  access logs, approvals and recertification records to the Auditor.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band, left to right

- IT Service Management: records and tracks access requests, approvals and
  notifications throughout the request lifecycle.
- HR System: authoritative source of employment and engagement status; triggers
  joiner, mover and leaver events.
- Identity & Access Management: manages entitlement catalogue, role
  definitions, access grants, conflict detection and revocations.
- GRC Platform: hosts the segregation-of-duties matrix and stores audit
  evidence and exception records.
- Directory Services: stores and enforces provisioned entitlements and account
  credentials in target directories.
- Access Certification Platform: runs periodic recertification campaigns and
  records certifier decisions for audit.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application components serve business processes):
- IT Service Management SERVES V19.01 Raise Access Request
- IT Service Management SERVES V19.05 Obtain Approvals
- IT Service Management SERVES V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester
- HR System SERVES V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- HR System SERVES V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.06 Provision Access
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- GRC Platform SERVES V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
- GRC Platform SERVES V19.10 Evidence for Audit
- Directory Services SERVES V19.06 Provision Access
- Access Certification Platform SERVES V19.08 Review Access Periodically
- Access Certification Platform SERVES V19.10 Evidence for Audit

REALISATION (business processes realise business services):
- V19.01 Raise Access Request REALISES Access Request Handling
- V19.02 Validate Identity & Status REALISES Identity Validation
- V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required REALISES Entitlement Determination
- V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties REALISES Segregation of Duties Checking
- V19.05 Obtain Approvals REALISES Access Approval
- V19.06 Provision Access REALISES Access Provisioning
- V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester REALISES Requester Notification
- V19.08 Review Access Periodically REALISES Access Recertification
- V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit REALISES Access Revocation
- V19.10 Evidence for Audit REALISES Audit Evidence

ASSIGNMENT (actors assigned to processes):
- IT Service Desk ASSIGNED TO V19.01 Raise Access Request
- IT Service Desk ASSIGNED TO V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- IT Service Desk ASSIGNED TO V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester
- Human Resources ASSIGNED TO V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- Human Resources ASSIGNED TO V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- Identity & Access Management ASSIGNED TO V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required
- Identity & Access Management ASSIGNED TO V19.06 Provision Access
- Identity & Access Management ASSIGNED TO V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- Application Owner ASSIGNED TO V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required
- Application Owner ASSIGNED TO V19.05 Obtain Approvals
- Application Owner ASSIGNED TO V19.08 Review Access Periodically
- Security ASSIGNED TO V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
- Security ASSIGNED TO V19.08 Review Access Periodically
- Security ASSIGNED TO V19.10 Evidence for Audit
- Line Management ASSIGNED TO V19.05 Obtain Approvals
- Internal Audit ASSIGNED TO V19.10 Evidence for Audit

ACCESS (external actors access interfaces and services):
- Contractor ACCESSES Access Request Interface
- Contractor ACCESSES Notification Interface
- Access Request Interface SERVES Access Request Handling
- Notification Interface SERVES Requester Notification
- Auditor ACCESSES Audit Evidence Interface
- Internal Audit ACCESSES Audit Evidence Interface
- Audit Evidence Interface SERVES Audit Evidence
- Line Management ACCESSES Approval Interface
- Application Owner ACCESSES Approval Interface
- Approval Interface SERVES Access Approval
```

```text
lifecycle of granting and maintaining access, from initial request
through identity validation, entitlement determination, segregation-of-

serves contractors, partners and vendors who require access to
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V19 - Request to Access

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages as
chevrons, one chevron per stage, in the order given below. Each stage name
must appear exactly as written. No stages may be added, removed, or reordered.

V19.07. Notify & Confirm with Requester
V19.08. Review Access Periodically
V19.09. Revoke on Change or Exit
V19.10. Evidence for Audit

This chain governs the end-to-end lifecycle of access rights, from the
moment a joiner, mover, leaver, or engagement-start event triggers an
access request through to provisioning, periodic recertification, revocation,
and the production of audit evidence. The main external participants are
Contractors and Partners who initiate requests and receive credentials, and
the Auditor who tests controls against the evidence produced. The chain
closes when all access activity for a given identity has been evidenced and
confirmed fit for audit.
```
