### V19.01 — Raise Access Request

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.01 Raise Access Request — first subprocess in the Request to
Access value chain, where a Contractor submits an access request that is
captured and logged by the IT Service Desk before passing to identity
validation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that receive, assess and record the
access request.
  Lane "IT Service Desk" — service desk agent who receives the request,
  captures details, and logs it in the ITSM tool.
Pool "Contractor" — external individual (contractor, partner or vendor)
who initiates the access request by submitting identity evidence and
engagement details.
Pool "IT Service Management" — ITSM platform that records and tracks the
access request ticket.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Organisation
3. IT Service Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Service Desk lane:
  Message start event "Access request received from Contractor"
  User task "Review submitted request and identity evidence"
  Exclusive gateway "Request information sufficient?"
  - branch "No — information missing":
      Send task "Request additional information from Contractor"
      Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received
      from Contractor"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Request information sufficient?"
  - branch "Yes — information complete":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Request information sufficient?"
  User task "Capture access request details"
  Service task "Log access request ticket in IT Service Management"
  User task "Confirm ticket reference with Contractor"
  Send task "Send ticket reference and acknowledgement to Contractor"
  End event "Access request logged — ready for Validate Identity and Status"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request additional information from
Contractor" — label "No response after 5 business days" — triggers an
escalation end event "Request abandoned — no response from Contractor".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the IT Service Desk lane flows start-to-end in a single
lane. After "Review submitted request and identity evidence" the exclusive
gateway "Request information sufficient?" branches: the "No" branch sends
a request for more information, waits at the intermediate message catch
event for the Contractor's reply, then rejoins at the exclusive merge
gateway "Request information sufficient?" before continuing; the "Yes"
branch goes directly to the merge. From the merge the flow continues to
"Capture access request details", then "Log access request ticket in IT
Service Management", then "Confirm ticket reference with Contractor", then
"Send ticket reference and acknowledgement to Contractor", then to the
end event.

Message flows:
Contractor → Organisation IT Service Desk lane (initial access request,
identity evidence and engagement details) — triggers message start event.
Organisation IT Service Desk lane → Contractor (request for additional
information) — from Send task "Request additional information from
Contractor".
Contractor → Organisation IT Service Desk lane (additional information
supplied) — received at intermediate message catch event.
Organisation IT Service Desk lane → IT Service Management (new access
request ticket creation) — from Service task "Log access request ticket
in IT Service Management".
IT Service Management → Organisation IT Service Desk lane (ticket
reference confirmed) — received at User task "Confirm ticket reference
with Contractor".
Organisation IT Service Desk lane → Contractor (ticket reference and
acknowledgement) — from Send task "Send ticket reference and
acknowledgement to Contractor".

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request Form" — written by "Capture access request
details"; read by "Log access request ticket in IT Service Management".
Data Object "Identity Evidence Package" — written by User task "Review
submitted request and identity evidence"; read by "Capture access request
details".
Data Object "ITSM Ticket" — written by "Log access request ticket in IT
Service Management"; read by "Confirm ticket reference with Contractor".

This subprocess receives the incoming access request from a Contractor,
Partner or Vendor, ensures all required identity evidence and engagement
details are present, and creates a tracked ITSM ticket that gives the
request a unique reference. It hands that logged, complete request to
Validate Identity and Status, where the Contractor's identity and
employment or engagement status are verified before entitlement
determination begins.
```


### V19.02 — Validate Identity & Status

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.02 Validate Identity & Status — second subprocess in the
Request to Access value chain, receiving a raised access request from
Raise Access Request and handing a validated identity record to
Determine Entitlements Required.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that validate identity and
employment or engagement status.
  Lane "IT Service Desk" — service desk agent who receives the request
  and coordinates validation.
  Lane "Human Resources" — HR officer who confirms employment or
  engagement status.
Pool "Contractor" — external contractor or partner supplying identity
evidence and acceptable-use acceptance.
Pool "HR System" — system of record for employment and engagement data.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — IAM platform used to check or
create the digital identity record.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "HR System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Organisation (white-box)
3. HR System
4. Identity & Access Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Service Desk lane:
  Message start event "Access request received from Raise Access
  Request"
  User task "Review access request and request identity evidence"
  Send task "Request identity evidence and acceptable-use acceptance
  from contractor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Identity evidence received from
  contractor"
  User task "Log identity evidence against request record"
  Send task "Forward identity evidence to HR for status check"

Human Resources lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Identity evidence received from
  IT Service Desk"
  Service task "Retrieve employment or engagement record from HR
  System"
  Exclusive gateway "Status confirmed?"
  - branch "Yes — active employment or engagement confirmed":
      User task "Record status confirmation"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Status confirmed"
  - branch "No — status unclear or not found":
      User task "Request clarification or additional evidence"
      Intermediate message catch event "Clarification received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Status confirmed"
  Service task "Check or create digital identity record in Identity
  and Access Management"
  Exclusive gateway "Digital identity exists and is current?"
  - branch "Yes — identity record valid":
      Exclusive merge gateway "Identity record resolved"
  - branch "No — identity record missing or stale":
      User task "Raise identity record creation or update request"
      Service task "Trigger identity record update in Identity and
      Access Management"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Identity record resolved"
  User task "Mark identity and status as validated on request record"
  Send task "Return validated identity record to IT Service Desk"

IT Service Desk lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Validated identity record received
  from HR"
  User task "Update request ticket with validation outcome"
  End event "Identity and status validated — ready for Determine
  Entitlements Required"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request identity evidence and
acceptable-use acceptance from contractor" — label "48-hour response
deadline" — triggers a Send task "Send reminder to contractor" which
rejoins the flow before the message catch event "Identity evidence
received from contractor".
Interrupting error boundary event on "Trigger identity record update
in Identity and Access Management" — label "Identity system error" —
triggers a User task "Escalate identity record failure to identity
engineer" ending in an Error end event "Identity provisioning failure".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs top to bottom through IT Service Desk then
crosses to Human Resources after evidence is forwarded; the "Status
confirmed?" gateway branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway
before the digital-identity check; the "Digital identity exists and
is current?" gateway branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway
"Identity record resolved" before the validation mark-up task; flow
returns to IT Service Desk for ticket update and the end event.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Send task "Request identity evidence and
  acceptable-use acceptance from contractor") → Contractor (identity
  evidence request)
  Contractor → Organisation (IT Service Desk, intermediate message

  Organisation (HR lane, Service task "Retrieve employment or

  HR System → Organisation (HR lane, Service task "Retrieve

  Organisation (HR lane, Service task "Check or create digital

  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (HR lane, Service task

  Organisation (HR lane, Service task "Trigger identity record update
  in Identity and Access Management") → Identity & Access Management
  (identity record creation or update instruction)
  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (HR lane, Service task
  "Trigger identity record update in Identity and Access Management")
  (updated identity record confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request" — read by "Review access request and
request identity evidence"; written by "Update request ticket with
validation outcome".
Data Object "Identity Evidence Package" — written by "Log identity
evidence against request record"; read by "Retrieve employment or
engagement record from HR System".
Data Object "Acceptable-Use Acceptance" — written by "Log identity
evidence against request record"; read by "Record status
confirmation".
engagement record from HR System"; written by HR System.
Data Object "Status Confirmation" — written by "Record status
confirmation"; read by "Mark identity and status as validated on
request record".
Data Object "Validated Identity Record" — written by "Mark identity
and status as validated on request record"; read by "Update request
ticket with validation outcome".

V19.02 Validate Identity & Status confirms that the person or
organisation behind an access request is who they claim to be and
that they hold a current employment or engagement relationship with
the organisation. The IT Service Desk collects identity evidence from
the contractor, Human Resources verifies status against the HR System,
and the IAM platform is checked or updated to ensure a digital
identity record exists. The subprocess hands a validated identity
record and confirmed status to Determine Entitlements Required so
```

### V19.03 — Determine Entitlements Required

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required — the subprocess within the
Request to Access value chain in which the identity engineer and application
owner translate an approved access request into a precise set of entitlements
drawn from the role catalogue.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that determine which entitlements
  are required.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Identity & Access Management (identity engineer)
  - Application Owner (application owner)
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — IAM platform that holds the
  entitlement catalogue, role definitions and current access holdings.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, with its two lanes)
2. Identity & Access Management System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Identity & Access Management lane:
  Message start event "Validated identity and status received from
    Validate Identity & Status"
  User task "Review access request details"
  Service task "Retrieve entitlement catalogue and role definitions from
    IAM system"
  Intermediate message catch event "Entitlement catalogue returned"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from IAM system"
  Intermediate message catch event "Current access holdings returned"
  User task "Identify candidate roles and entitlements"
  Send task "Send candidate entitlement list to Application Owner"

Application Owner lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Candidate entitlement list received"
  User task "Review candidate entitlements against application
    requirements"
  Exclusive gateway "Entitlements appropriate?"
  - branch "Yes — entitlements confirmed": User task "Confirm and
      record required entitlements"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Entitlements appropriate"
  - branch "No — adjustments needed":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Entitlements Agreed" (standard
      loop) containing, in order: User task "Return list with
      amendment notes to identity engineer", Intermediate message
      catch event "Revised entitlement list received", User task
      "Review and revise candidate entitlements", Send task "Send
      revised entitlement list to Application Owner", Intermediate
      message catch event "Application Owner response received",
      User task "Evaluate Application Owner feedback"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Entitlements appropriate"
  User task "Sign off finalised entitlement set"

Identity & Access Management lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Signed-off entitlement set received
    from Application Owner"
  User task "Record finalised entitlement set in IAM system"
  Service task "Write entitlement record to IAM system"
  End event "Entitlement set determined — ready for Check Segregation
    of Duties"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Entitlements Agreed", label "Review cycle exceeds 3 business
  days", triggers escalation task "Escalate entitlement disagreement
  to Security officer" in Identity & Access Management lane; flow
  continues to end of subprocess.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Identity & Access Management lane,
  passes to the Application Owner lane at the send task, cycles within
  the expanded subprocess until entitlements are agreed, then
  re-enters the Identity & Access Management lane for recording and
  writing to the IAM system before reaching the end event.
  The exclusive gateway "Entitlements appropriate?" branches to
  "Confirm and record required entitlements" on the Yes branch and
  to the expanded subprocess on the No branch; both branches rejoin
  at the merge gateway "Entitlements appropriate" before "Sign off
  finalised entitlement set".

Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Retrieve entitlement catalogue and role
    definitions from IAM system") → Identity & Access Management
    System (request for catalogue and role definitions)
  Identity & Access Management System → Organisation (Intermediate

    and role definitions payload)
  Organisation (Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from
    IAM system") → Identity & Access Management System (request for
    current access holdings)
  Identity & Access Management System → Organisation (Intermediate
    message catch event "Current access holdings returned") (current

  Organisation (Service task "Write entitlement record to IAM system")

    record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request" — read by "Review access request details".
Data Object "Entitlement Catalogue" — read by "Identify candidate roles
  and entitlements"; written by "Retrieve entitlement catalogue and
  role definitions from IAM system".
Data Object "Current Access Holdings" — read by "Identify candidate
  roles and entitlements"; written by "Retrieve current access
  holdings from IAM system".
Data Object "Candidate Entitlement List" — written by "Identify
  candidate roles and entitlements"; read by "Review candidate
  entitlements against application requirements".
Data Object "Amendment Notes" — written by "Return list with amendment
  notes to identity engineer"; read by "Review and revise candidate
  entitlements".

V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required takes the validated identity and
status confirmed by V19.02 and translates it into a precise, agreed and
recorded set of roles and entitlements. The identity engineer draws on the
IAM platform for the role catalogue and existing holdings, works iteratively
with the Application Owner until the entitlement set is mutually agreed and
signed off, then writes the finalised record to the IAM system. The
completed entitlement record is handed to V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
so that conflict detection can run against the confirmed set.
```


### V19.04 — Check Segregation of Duties

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties — subprocess in the Request to
Access value chain that detects and resolves segregation-of-duties conflicts
before access approvals are sought.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out the SoD check.
  Lane "Security" — security officer who runs the SoD check and resolves
    conflicts.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — IAM platform that holds entitlement
  and access data and runs conflict detection.
Pool "GRC Platform" — governance, risk and compliance platform that records
  SoD exceptions and decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Identity & Access Management (IT system — supplies current access data
   to trigger the check)
2. Organisation (white-box — process flow runs here)
3. GRC Platform (IT system — receives exception records)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security lane:
  Message start event "Entitlement proposal received from Determine
    Entitlements Required"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from IAM"
  Service task "Run SoD conflict detection"
  Intermediate message catch event "Conflict detection results returned"
  Exclusive gateway "Conflicts detected?"
    - branch "No conflicts": User task "Record clean SoD result in GRC
        Platform"
      End event "SoD check passed — ready for Obtain Approvals"
    - branch "Yes — conflicts found": User task "Review conflict details"
      Exclusive gateway "Conflict severity?"
        - branch "Acceptable with exception": Expanded Subprocess "Obtain
            SoD Exception Approval" (standard loop) containing, in order:
            User task "Prepare exception justification",
            Send task "Submit exception request to GRC Platform",
            Intermediate message catch event "Exception decision received"
          Exclusive gateway "Exception approved?"
            - branch "Approved": User task "Record approved exception in
                GRC Platform"
              End event "SoD exception approved — ready for Obtain
                Approvals"
            - branch "Rejected": User task "Record rejection and notify
                entitlement team"
              End event "SoD conflict unresolved — return to Determine
                Entitlements Required"
        - branch "Unacceptable — cannot grant": User task "Document
            blocking conflict in GRC Platform"
          End event "Access blocked — return to Determine Entitlements
            Required"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Conflict severity"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Exception approved"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Obtain SoD
  Exception Approval" — label "Exception review deadline exceeded" —
  flow continues to User task "Record rejection and notify entitlement
  team", then to End event "SoD conflict unresolved — return to Determine
  Entitlements Required".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the Security lane flows from the message start event
through retrieval and conflict detection, pausing at the intermediate
catch event, then through the "Conflicts detected?" gateway; the No-
conflicts branch leads directly to the clean-result task and its end
event; the Yes branch enters the "Conflict severity?" gateway; the
Acceptable branch enters the exception-approval subprocess, exits to the
"Exception approved?" gateway, which splits to the approved-exception end
event or the rejection end event; the Unacceptable branch leads to the
blocking-conflict task and its end event; the "Conflict severity" merge
gateway and "Exception approved" merge gateway close their respective
splits where branches rejoin.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from IAM")
    → Identity & Access Management (current access holdings and
    entitlement data requested)
  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (Service task "Run SoD
    conflict detection") (entitlement and current access data returned)
  Organisation (Service task "Run SoD conflict detection") → Identity &
    Access Management (conflict detection job submitted)
  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (Intermediate message catch
    event "Conflict detection results returned") (conflict detection
    results)
  Organisation (Send task "Submit exception request to GRC Platform") →
    GRC Platform (SoD exception request submitted)
  GRC Platform → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
    "Exception decision received") (exception approval or rejection
    decision)
  Organisation (User task "Record clean SoD result in GRC Platform") →
    GRC Platform (clean SoD result written)
  Organisation (User task "Record approved exception in GRC Platform") →
    GRC Platform (approved exception record written)
  Organisation (User task "Document blocking conflict in GRC Platform") →
    GRC Platform (blocking conflict record written)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Entitlement Proposal" — read by User task "Retrieve current
  access holdings from IAM".
Data Object "Current Access Holdings" — read by Service task "Run SoD
  conflict detection".
Data Object "Conflict Detection Results" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Conflict detection results returned"; read by User task
  "Review conflict details".
Data Object "Exception Justification" — written by User task "Prepare
  exception justification"; read by Send task "Submit exception request
  to GRC Platform".

This subprocess takes the proposed entitlement set from Determine
Entitlements Required, uses the IAM platform to detect conflicts against
current access holdings, and resolves them either by confirming a clean
result, securing a recorded exception, or blocking the request. Its
outcome — a GRC-logged clean or exception-approved status, or a blocking
notification — is handed to Obtain Approvals to continue the request, or
fed back to Determine Entitlements Required where the conflict cannot be
resolved.
```


### V19.05 — Obtain Approvals

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.05 Obtain Approvals — the fifth subprocess in the Request to
Access value chain, receiving a validated, entitlement-mapped,
segregation-of-duties-checked access request and obtaining the
required approvals before provisioning is triggered.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that route, review and
approve the access request.
  Lane "Line Management" — approving line manager who reviews and
  approves or rejects the business justification.
  Lane "Application Owner" — application owner who reviews and
  approves or rejects the entitlement-level detail.

Pool "IT Service Management" — the ITSM platform that carries the
request record, routes approval tasks and records decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box; Lane "Line Management" above Lane
   "Application Owner")
2. IT Service Management (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Line Management lane:
  Message start event "SoD-checked access request received from
  Check Segregation of Duties"
  Service task "Retrieve access request from IT Service Management"
  User task "Review business justification and access request"
  Exclusive gateway "Line manager decision?"
    - branch "Approved": Send task "Record line manager approval in
      IT Service Management"
      Intermediate message catch event "Application owner decision
      received"
      Exclusive gateway "Application owner approved?"
        - branch "Approved": End event "All approvals obtained —
          ready for Provision Access"
        - branch "Rejected": Send task "Record final rejection in
          IT Service Management"
          End event "Request rejected — no further action"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Application owner approved?"
    - branch "Rejected": Send task "Record line manager rejection in
      IT Service Management"
      End event "Request rejected at line manager stage — no
      further action"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Line manager decision?"

Application Owner lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Line manager approval
  notification received"
  User task "Review entitlement detail and access justification"
  Exclusive gateway "Application owner decision?"
    - branch "Approved": Send task "Send approval decision to Line
      Management"
    - branch "Rejected": Send task "Send rejection decision to Line
      Management"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Application owner decision?"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review business
justification and access request" — label "Approval overdue
(SLA breached)" — triggers a Send task "Escalate overdue approval
to line manager's manager" in the Line Management lane, then
rejoins the sequence flow at Exclusive gateway "Line manager
decision?".

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review entitlement
detail and access justification" — label "Approval overdue
(SLA breached)" — triggers a Send task "Escalate overdue approval
to application owner's delegate" in the Application Owner lane,
then rejoins the sequence flow at Exclusive gateway "Application
owner decision?".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Line Management lane with the
message start event, moves to the service task that retrieves the
request, then to the user task for review, and into the line
manager decision gateway. The approved branch records the approval
and then waits for the application owner decision via an
intermediate catch event before the application-owner-approved
gateway splits to either the all-approvals end event or the
rejection end event. The rejected branch from the line manager
gateway records the rejection and reaches its own end event.
In the Application Owner lane, the intermediate catch event fires
when line manager approval is recorded; work flows into the review
task, then the application owner decision gateway, whose approved
and rejected branches both lead to send tasks that message back to
the Line Management lane and then merge.

Message flows:
IT Service Management → Service task "Retrieve access request from
IT Service Management" (access request record with entitlement
mapping and SoD-check result).
Send task "Record line manager approval in IT Service Management"
→ IT Service Management (line manager approval decision).
Send task "Record line manager rejection in IT Service Management"
→ IT Service Management (line manager rejection decision).
Send task "Record final rejection in IT Service Management" →
IT Service Management (application owner rejection decision).
Send task "Record final rejection in IT Service Management" is also
the close-out record for application-owner rejections.
Send task "Send approval decision to Line Management" →
Intermediate message catch event "Application owner decision
received" (application owner approval notification).
Send task "Send rejection decision to Line Management" →
Intermediate message catch event "Application owner decision
received" (application owner rejection notification).
IT Service Management → Intermediate message catch event "Line
manager approval notification received" in Application Owner lane
(routed approval task notification).
Send task "Escalate overdue approval to line manager's manager" →
IT Service Management (escalation notification).
Send task "Escalate overdue approval to application owner's
delegate" → IT Service Management (escalation notification).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request Record" — read by Service task
"Retrieve access request from IT Service Management"; read by
User task "Review business justification and access request"; read
by User task "Review entitlement detail and access justification".
Data Object "Line Manager Approval Decision" — written by Send task
"Record line manager approval in IT Service Management"; written by
Send task "Record line manager rejection in IT Service Management".
Data Object "Application Owner Approval Decision" — written by
Send task "Record final rejection in IT Service Management"; read
by Exclusive gateway "Application owner approved?".
Data Object "Escalation Record" — written by Send task "Escalate
overdue approval to line manager's manager"; written by Send task
"Escalate overdue approval to application owner's delegate".

This subprocess collects the two mandatory approvals — from the
line manager on business justification and from the application
owner on entitlement detail — enforcing SLA timers and escalating
when either party is overdue. Rejection at either stage terminates
the request with a recorded decision. When both approvals are
confirmed, the fully authorised access request record is handed to
Provision Access for technical fulfilment.
```


### V19.06 — Provision Access

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.06 Provision Access — the subprocess in which the Identity &
Access Management team configures and activates the approved entitlements
in the directory and application systems, completing the fulfilment leg
of the Request to Access value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing the provisioning
  work, with two lanes: Identity & Access Management and (implicitly)
  the process boundary lanes needed to model the flow.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — the IAM platform that
  receives provisioning commands and returns status.
Pool "Directory Services" — the directory (e.g. Active Directory or
  LDAP) in which accounts and group memberships are created or updated.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Directory Services" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, one lane: Identity & Access Management)
2. Identity & Access Management System
3. Directory Services

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Identity & Access Management lane:
  Message start event "Approved access request received from
    Obtain Approvals"
  Service task "Retrieve approved entitlement specification from IAM
    System"
  Service task "Validate account existence in Directory Services"
  Exclusive gateway "Account exists?"
  - branch "No — new account needed": Service task "Create user account
      in Directory Services"
  - branch "Yes — account present": (continue to merge)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Account exists?"
  Service task "Assign roles and group memberships in Directory
    Services"
  Service task "Apply application-level entitlements in IAM System"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Provisioning Confirmed" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: Service task "Poll provisioning status
    from IAM System", Exclusive gateway "Provisioning complete?",
    branch "No — pending": continue loop,
    branch "Yes — confirmed": exit loop
  Exclusive gateway "Provisioning successful?"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Record provisioning outcome in IAM
      System"
  - branch "No — error": Service task "Log provisioning failure and
      raise incident"
      End event "Provisioning failed — escalated to service desk"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Provisioning successful?"
  Service task "Update access register in IAM System"
  End event "Access provisioned — ready for Notify & Confirm with
    Requester"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Provisioning Confirmed", labelled "Provisioning timeout — 2 hours";
  flow exits to: Service task "Log provisioning failure and raise
  incident", then End event "Provisioning failed — escalated to service
  desk".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all sequence flows run within the Identity & Access
Management lane. After the start event the flow passes through
entitlement retrieval and account validation, then branches at
"Account exists?" — the No branch creates the account and rejoins the
Yes branch at the merge gateway — before assigning roles in Directory
Services, applying application entitlements in the IAM System, and
entering the polling loop. On exit from the loop the "Provisioning
successful?" gateway branches: the No branch ends in the failure end
event; the Yes branch continues through outcome recording, access
register update, and the successful end event.

Message flows:
Identity & Access Management lane → Identity & Access Management
  System (entitlement specification retrieval request)
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management
  lane (approved entitlement specification)
Identity & Access Management lane → Directory Services (create account
  instruction)
Directory Services → Identity & Access Management lane (account
  creation confirmation)
Identity & Access Management lane → Directory Services (role and group
  membership assignment)
Directory Services → Identity & Access Management lane (membership
  assignment confirmation)
Identity & Access Management lane → Identity & Access Management
  System (application-level entitlement grant)
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management
  lane (provisioning status response)
Identity & Access Management lane → Identity & Access Management
  System (provisioning outcome and access register update)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Entitlement Specification" — read by "Retrieve
  approved entitlement specification from IAM System"; written by
  (upstream Obtain Approvals subprocess).
Data Object "Provisioning Status Report" — written by "Poll
  provisioning status from IAM System"; read by the gateway
  "Provisioning successful?".
Data Object "Provisioning Failure Incident" — written by "Log
  provisioning failure and raise incident".

This subprocess takes the approved entitlement specification from
Obtain Approvals and translates it into concrete technical actions:
creating or validating the user account in Directory Services, assigning
the approved roles and group memberships, and applying application-level
entitlements through the IAM System. It confirms successful completion
by updating the access register and then hands a provisioned-access
record to Notify & Confirm with Requester so that the requester and
contractor can be informed and credentials delivered.
```


### V19.07 — Notify & Confirm with Requester

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester — the subprocess that
closes the provisioning loop by informing the requester that access has
been granted and confirming receipt, sitting between Provision Access and
Review Access Periodically in the Request to Access value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that notify and confirm access
  with the requester.
  Lane "IT Service Desk" — service desk agent who sends notification,
    logs confirmation, and closes the service request.
Pool "Contractor" — the external contractor who receives the access
  notification and confirms receipt.
Pool "IT Service Management" — the ITSM platform used to update and
  close the access request ticket.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Organisation (white-box, one lane: IT Service Desk)
3. IT Service Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Service Desk lane:
  Message start event "Provisioned access record received from
    Provision Access"
  User task "Prepare access notification"
  Send task "Send access notification and credential details to
    requester"
  Service task "Log notification sent in IT Service Management"
  Intermediate message catch event "Contractor acknowledgement
    received"
  Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement received within deadline?"
  - branch "Yes — acknowledgement received":
      User task "Record confirmation of receipt"
      Service task "Update request ticket with confirmation in
        IT Service Management"
      Service task "Close access request ticket in IT Service
        Management"
      End event "Access confirmed and request closed — ready for
        Review Access Periodically"
  - branch "No — deadline elapsed":
      User task "Escalate non-response and re-send notification"
      Service task "Log escalation in IT Service Management"
      Intermediate message catch event "Contractor acknowledgement
        received after escalation"
      User task "Record confirmation of receipt after escalation"
      Service task "Update request ticket with confirmation in
        IT Service Management"
      Service task "Close access request ticket in IT Service
        Management"
      End event "Access confirmed after escalation — ready for
        Review Access Periodically"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Prepare access notification"
  labelled "Preparation overdue (4 hours)" — flows to a User task
  "Alert service desk supervisor" then rejoins before Send task.
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  "Contractor acknowledgement received" labelled "Acknowledgement
  deadline elapsed (48 hours)" — triggers the "No" branch of the
  Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement received within deadline?".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The single IT Service Desk lane flows from the message
start event through preparation, send, and logging, then waits at the
intermediate catch event before the exclusive gateway. The "Yes" branch
continues through record, update, and close tasks to the first end
event. The "No" branch proceeds through escalation, re-send, logging,
a second intermediate catch, record, update, and close tasks to the
second end event. Both branches are independent end paths and do not
rejoin.

Message flows:
IT Service Desk "Send access notification and credential details to
  requester" → Contractor (access notification and credential details).
Contractor → IT Service Desk "Contractor acknowledgement received"
  (acknowledgement of access notification).
Contractor → IT Service Desk "Contractor acknowledgement received after
  escalation" (acknowledgement following escalation re-send).
IT Service Desk "Log notification sent in IT Service Management" →
  IT Service Management (notification log entry).
IT Service Desk "Update request ticket with confirmation in IT Service
  Management" → IT Service Management (confirmation update).
IT Service Desk "Close access request ticket in IT Service Management"
  → IT Service Management (ticket closure instruction).
IT Service Desk "Log escalation in IT Service Management" →
  IT Service Management (escalation log entry).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Notification" — written by "Prepare access
  notification"; read by "Send access notification and credential
  details to requester".
Data Object "Contractor Acknowledgement" — written by "Record
  confirmation of receipt"; read by "Update request ticket with
  confirmation in IT Service Management".
Data Object "Escalation Record" — written by "Escalate non-response
  and re-send notification"; read by "Log escalation in IT Service
  Management".

V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester takes the provisioned access
record from V19.06 and ensures the contractor is formally informed of
their credentials and access details, with acknowledgement sought and
logged and the ITSM ticket closed on confirmation. If acknowledgement
is not returned within the deadline, the service desk escalates and
re-sends before closing. The closed, confirmed ticket and its audit
trail are available to V19.08 Review Access Periodically and ultimately
to V19.10 Evidence for Audit.
```


### V19.08 — Review Access Periodically

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.08 Review Access Periodically — the scheduled recertification
subprocess within the Request to Access value chain, where current access
holdings are reviewed, certified or revoked, and the outcome is recorded
for audit.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams running the periodic access review.
  Lane "Application Owner" — access-review certifier who certifies or
    revokes individual entitlements.
  Lane "Security" — security officer who oversees the review, manages
    exceptions, and closes the cycle.
Pool "Access Certification Platform" — tooling that drives the
  recertification campaign, holds current access holdings, and records
  certifier decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Access Certification Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
  1. Organisation (white-box; lanes: Application Owner, Security)
  2. Access Certification Platform (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Application Owner lane:
  Timer start event "Scheduled recertification cycle triggered"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from Access
    Certification Platform"
  Expanded Subprocess "Review Until All Entitlements Certified or
    Revoked" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Review
    individual entitlement", Exclusive gateway "Certify or revoke?",
    - branch "Certify": User task "Approve and certify entitlement"
    - branch "Revoke": User task "Flag entitlement for revocation"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Certify or revoke?"
  Service task "Submit certification decisions to Access Certification
    Platform"
  Send task "Forward revocation instructions to Security"

Security lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Revocation instructions received"
  User task "Review flagged entitlements and exceptions"
  Exclusive gateway "Exceptions acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes — no conflict": User task "Approve exception and
      document rationale"
  - branch "No — conflict confirmed": User task "Escalate to security
      officer for enforcement action"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Exceptions acceptable?"
  Service task "Record review outcome and exceptions in Access
    Certification Platform"
  User task "Close recertification cycle and confirm completion"
  End event "Recertification cycle complete — outcome ready for
    Evidence for Audit"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Review Until
  All Entitlements Certified or Revoked", labelled "Recertification
  deadline exceeded", triggers escalation to Security lane via an
  intermediate escalation throw.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Application Owner lane with the timer
start event and moves through retrieval and the certification loop before
the certifier submits decisions and forwards revocation instructions to
Security; the Security lane picks up from the message catch event,
passes through the exception gateway — the "no conflict" branch and the
"conflict confirmed" branch both rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway —
before recording the outcome and closing the cycle at the end event.

Message flows:
  Access Certification Platform → "Retrieve current access holdings
    from Access Certification Platform" (current access holdings and
    entitlement list)
  "Submit certification decisions to Access Certification Platform" →
    Access Certification Platform (certify/revoke decisions)
  "Record review outcome and exceptions in Access Certification
    Platform" → Access Certification Platform (review outcome and
    exception records)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Certification Decision Record" — written by "Approve and
  certify entitlement"; written by "Flag entitlement for revocation";
  read by "Submit certification decisions to Access Certification
  Platform".
Data Object "Revocation Instruction" — written by "Forward revocation
  instructions to Security"; read by "Review flagged entitlements and
  exceptions".
Data Object "Exception Rationale" — written by "Approve exception and
  document rationale"; read by "Record review outcome and exceptions in
  Access Certification Platform".

This subprocess runs the scheduled access recertification cycle, ensuring
every entitlement held by users and contractors is individually certified
as still required or flagged for removal. Exceptions are reviewed and
documented by the security officer before the cycle is formally closed.
The recorded outcome and exception evidence are then handed to Evidence
for Audit (V19.10) for compliance reporting and external audit use.
```


### V19.09 — Revoke on Change or Exit

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit — the subprocess that removes or
adjusts access entitlements when an employee or contractor moves role,
leaves the organisation, or ends an engagement, sitting between
Review Access Periodically and Evidence for Audit in the Request to
Access value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that action revocation.
  Lane "Human Resources" — HR officer who detects the change or exit
    event and initiates the revocation trigger.
  Lane "Identity & Access Management" — access administrator who
    executes the revocation and disables accounts.

Pool "HR System" — system of record for employment and engagement
  status.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — IAM platform used to
  revoke entitlements and disable or remove accounts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "HR System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. HR System
2. Organisation (Human Resources lane above Identity & Access
   Management lane)
3. Identity & Access Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Human Resources lane:
  Message start event "Change or exit event received from HR System"
  User task "Confirm nature of change or exit"
  Exclusive gateway "Type of event?"
    - branch "Mover (role change)": User task "Identify entitlements
      to remove or adjust"
    - branch "Leaver (exit or termination)": User task "Flag all
      accounts and entitlements for full revocation"
    - branch "Contractor or engagement end": User task "Flag
      contractor accounts for immediate revocation"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Type of event?"
  User task "Raise revocation request in IAM"
  Send task "Submit revocation instruction to Identity and Access
    Management"

Identity & Access Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Revocation instruction received"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from IAM system"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Entitlements Revoked"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    Service task "Revoke entitlement in IAM system",
    Service task "Disable or delete account in Directory Services via
      IAM system",
    User task "Verify revocation status for entitlement"
  Exclusive gateway "Any privileged access held?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Revoke privileged access via PAM
      controls"
    - branch "No": continue to merge
  Exclusive merge gateway "Any privileged access held?"
  Service task "Record revocation completion in IAM system"
  User task "Perform final reconciliation of access holdings"
  Exclusive gateway "All access successfully revoked?"
    - branch "Yes": Send task "Confirm revocation to Human Resources"
    - branch "No": User task "Escalate unresolved entitlements to
      security officer", then Send task "Confirm revocation to Human
        Resources"
  Exclusive merge gateway "All access successfully revoked?"
  End event "Access revoked — ready for Evidence for Audit"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  All Entitlements Revoked" — label "Revocation time limit exceeded" —
  flows to User task "Escalate unresolved entitlements to security
  officer" in Identity & Access Management lane.

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Raise revocation
  request in IAM" in Human Resources lane — label "Revocation SLA
  deadline" — flows to User task "Escalate overdue revocation to HR
  manager" then rejoins at Send task "Submit revocation instruction to
  Identity and Access Management".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Human Resources lane, passes
through the change-type gateway and its three branches — mover,
leaver, and contractor end — which converge at the exclusive merge
gateway before the revocation request is raised and submitted.
Control passes to the Identity & Access Management lane on receipt of
the instruction; the loop subprocess iterates over every entitlement
until all are revoked; the privileged-access gateway branches to a
PAM revocation task for "Yes" and skips for "No", both rejoining at
the merge gateway; the final reconciliation gateway branches to direct
confirmation for a clean result or escalation followed by
confirmation; both branches rejoin before the end event.

Message flows:
  HR System → Human Resources lane (change or exit event trigger,
    employment and engagement status data).
  Human Resources lane → Identity & Access Management System
    (revocation instruction and list of accounts to revoke).
  Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management
    lane (current access holdings, entitlement revocation
    confirmation, account disable or delete status).
  Identity & Access Management lane → HR System (revocation
    completion confirmation for personnel record update).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Change or Exit Notification" — written by User task
  "Confirm nature of change or exit"; read by User task "Identify
  entitlements to remove or adjust", User task "Flag all accounts and
  entitlements for full revocation", and User task "Flag contractor
  accounts for immediate revocation".
Data Object "Revocation Request" — written by User task "Raise
  revocation request in IAM"; read by Service task "Retrieve current
  access holdings from IAM system".
Data Object "Entitlement Revocation Record" — written by Service task
  "Revoke entitlement in IAM system"; read by User task "Verify
  revocation status for entitlement".

V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit removes all access entitlements held
by an individual whose employment or engagement status has changed,
ensuring that movers lose entitlements no longer appropriate to their
new role, leavers and contractors have all accounts disabled or
deleted within the required timeframe, and any privileged access is
subject to additional PAM controls. The completed revocation record,
reconciliation outcome, and any escalation evidence are handed to
Evidence for Audit so that the full lifecycle from grant to removal
can be demonstrated to reviewers and auditors.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.10 Evidence for Audit — closes the Request to Access value
chain by compiling, reviewing and delivering audit evidence to the Auditor.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that compile and present audit
evidence.
  Lane "Security" — security officer who assembles the evidence package.
  Lane "Internal Audit" — internal auditor who reviews evidence and liaises
  with the external Auditor.
Pool "Auditor" — external auditor who requests and tests access controls.
Pool "Access Certification Platform" — tooling that holds recertification
results and exception reports.
Pool "GRC Platform" — governance, risk and compliance system that stores
policy exceptions and audit trails.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Auditor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Access Certification Platform" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Auditor
2. Organisation (Security lane above Internal Audit lane)
3. Access Certification Platform
4. GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security lane:
  Message start event "Audit evidence request received from Notify &
  Confirm with Requester"
  Service task "Retrieve access register from Identity & Access
  Management"
  Service task "Pull recertification results from Access Certification
  Platform"
  Service task "Pull exception reports and SoD conflict records from GRC
  Platform"
  User task "Assemble evidence package"
  User task "Validate completeness of evidence package"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence package complete?"
  - branch "incomplete": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence
    Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Identify
    gaps in evidence", User task "Obtain missing records"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Repeat Until Evidence Complete"
  - branch "complete": continue to Send task below
  Send task "Submit evidence package to Internal Audit"

Internal Audit lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence package received from
  Security"
  User task "Review evidence package for accuracy and sufficiency"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient?"
  - branch "insufficient": Send task "Return evidence package to Security
    with review notes"
    Intermediate message catch event "Revised evidence package received"
    (rejoins review user task via Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence
    sufficient")
  - branch "sufficient": continue below
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient"
  User task "Prepare audit response report"
  Send task "Transmit audit evidence and report to Auditor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Auditor acknowledgement received"
  Exclusive gateway "Auditor queries raised?"
  - branch "yes": User task "Coordinate response to auditor queries"
    Send task "Send query responses to Auditor"
    Intermediate message catch event "Auditor satisfied"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Auditor queries raised"
  - branch "no": Exclusive merge gateway "Auditor queries raised"
  User task "Archive evidence package and close audit activity"
  End event "Audit evidence accepted and cycle evidenced — end of Request
  to Access chain"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Assemble evidence
package", label "Evidence assembly deadline exceeded", triggers Send task
"Notify Internal Audit of delay" which flows to an End event "Evidence
assembly overdue — escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Security lane the flow runs from the start
event through retrieval and assembly tasks, through the "Evidence package
complete?" gateway — the incomplete branch enters and exits the loop
subprocess before rejoining via the exclusive merge gateway, the complete
branch proceeds — then to the submit send task. Control passes to the
Internal Audit lane at the message catch event. Review flows through the
"Evidence sufficient?" gateway — the insufficient branch sends the package
back to Security, a message catch event receives the revision, and the
flow rejoins the merge gateway before continuing — the sufficient branch
proceeds directly to the merge gateway. From there the flow continues
through report preparation, transmission, the acknowledgement catch event,
the "Auditor queries raised?" gateway — the yes branch handles queries
and waits for satisfaction before rejoining the merge gateway, the no
branch joins immediately — and on through archiving to the end event.

Message flows:
  Auditor → Security lane (audit evidence request)
  Security lane → Access Certification Platform (request for
    recertification results)
  Access Certification Platform → Security lane (recertification results
    and exception reports)
  Security lane → GRC Platform (request for SoD conflict records and
    audit trail)
  GRC Platform → Security lane (SoD exception records and audit trail
    data)
  Internal Audit lane → Auditor (audit evidence package and report)
  Auditor → Internal Audit lane (acknowledgement and any audit queries)
  Internal Audit lane → Auditor (query responses)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Register" — read by "Retrieve access register from
Identity & Access Management"; written by "Assemble evidence package".
Data Object "Recertification Results" — read by "Pull recertification
results from Access Certification Platform"; written by "Assemble evidence
package".
Data Object "SoD Exception Reports" — read by "Pull exception reports and
SoD conflict records from GRC Platform"; written by "Assemble evidence
package".
Data Object "Evidence Package" — written by "Assemble evidence package";
read by "Validate completeness of evidence package", "Review evidence
package for accuracy and sufficiency", "Prepare audit response report".
Data Object "Audit Response Report" — written by "Prepare audit response
report"; read by "Transmit audit evidence and report to Auditor".
Data Object "Auditor Query Response" — written by "Coordinate response to
auditor queries"; read by "Send query responses to Auditor".
close audit activity".

V19.10 Evidence for Audit gathers access registers, recertification
results, SoD exception records and approval trails from the Access
Certification Platform and GRC Platform, assembles and internally reviews
them, then delivers a complete audit evidence package to the external
Auditor. Any auditor queries are resolved before the evidence is formally
accepted. This subprocess closes the Request to Access value chain,
leaving a durable archive of the full access-management cycle that
satisfies audit and regulatory obligations.
```


## V20 — Matter to Resolution

**Teams and roles involved.**
Matter to Resolution usually involves Legal, Compliance, Risk, Company Secretariat, the affected Business Unit, Finance for provisioning, and Executive Management. Key roles include general counsel, legal counsel, paralegal, compliance manager, matter owner, external counsel liaison, finance business partner, and company secretary.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are the Counterparty — a claimant, litigant, complainant or regulator — and External Counsel engaged to act. The process is initiated by a claim, dispute, complaint escalation, regulatory notice, subpoena or litigation filing. Other external parties include courts and tribunals, mediators and arbitrators, insurers, expert witnesses, and opposing counsel.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive and register the matter, assess merits and exposure, assign internal and external counsel, issue legal hold and preserve evidence, develop the strategy, manage discovery and disclosure, negotiate or mediate, litigate or defend where required, settle or obtain judgment, and close the matter with lessons learned.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include matter management, e-discovery and legal hold tooling, document management, contract repositories, spend and e-billing management for external counsel, risk registers and provisioning in finance systems, and board and committee reporting.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include legal engagement and outside-counsel guidelines, delegation of authority for settlement, legal hold and document retention obligations, privilege protection procedures, conflict-of-interest checks, disclosure obligations to regulators and insurers, provisioning and materiality thresholds for financial reporting, and reporting obligations to the board.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The counterparty and courts provide claims, pleadings, notices, discovery requests and judgments; the process provides responses, disclosures, submissions and settlement offers. External counsel receive instructions, evidence and authority limits, and provide advice, drafts, appearances and invoices.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates matter records, exposure assessments, legal holds, evidence collections, strategy and privilege logs, external counsel budgets and invoices, settlement records, and provisions. IT systems provide contract and transaction evidence, custodian and data-source mapping for holds, spend against budget, provision and accrual postings, and matter status and exposure reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V20.01** Receive & Register Matter | Counterparty | Legal (paralegal) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.02** Assess Merits & Exposure | — | Legal (legal counsel), Risk (risk manager) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.03** Assign Internal & External Counsel | External Counsel | Legal (general counsel) | Matter Management System, Legal Spend Management |
| **V20.04** Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence | — | Legal (paralegal), Business Unit (matter owner) | Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform |
| **V20.05** Develop Strategy | External Counsel | Legal (legal counsel) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.06** Manage Discovery & Disclosure | Counterparty, Court | Legal (paralegal), Business Unit (matter owner) | Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform, Document Management System |
| **V20.07** Negotiate or Mediate | Counterparty, Mediator | Legal (legal counsel), Executive Management (delegated approver) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.08** Litigate or Defend | Court, External Counsel | Legal (legal counsel) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.09** Settle or Obtain Judgment | Counterparty, Insurer | Legal (general counsel), Finance (finance business partner) | Matter Management System, Finance / ERP System |
| **V20.10** Close Matter & Capture Lessons | — | Legal (legal counsel), Company Secretariat (company secretary) | Matter Management System, Board Reporting System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V20):

- **External actors:** Counterparty (V20.01, V20.06, V20.07, V20.09); External Counsel (V20.03, V20.05, V20.08); Court (V20.06, V20.08); Mediator (V20.07); Insurer (V20.09).
- **Teams:** Legal (V20.01–V20.10); Risk (V20.02); Business Unit (V20.04, V20.06); Executive Management (V20.07); Finance (V20.09); Company Secretariat (V20.10).
- **IT systems:** Matter Management System (V20.01–V20.03, V20.05, V20.07–V20.10); Legal Spend Management (V20.03); Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform (V20.04, V20.06); Document Management System (V20.06); Finance / ERP System (V20.09); Board Reporting System (V20.10).

```text
from first notification through to final closure. It is triggered when a

claim, dispute, complaint, subpoena or regulatory notice against the
```

```text
  User task "Log initial matter details"
  User task "Check for conflict of interest"
  Exclusive gateway "Conflict identified?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Escalate conflict to General Counsel"
      End event "Matter on hold — conflict escalation in progress"
    - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Conflict identified?"
  User task "Classify matter type and assign preliminary priority"
  User task "Gather supporting documentation and file reference material"
  Service task "Create matter record in Matter Management System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Matter record confirmation received"
  User task "Assign matter owner and notify relevant business unit"
  Send task "Send acknowledgement of receipt to Counterparty"
  End event "Matter registered — ready for Assess Merits & Exposure"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Legal (Paralegal) lane from
the message start event through logging, conflict check, classification,
documentation gathering, system registration, owner assignment and
acknowledgement to the end event. The "Conflict identified?" gateway
splits to an escalation end event on the Yes branch and merges back to
the main flow on the No branch; all subsequent tasks follow the merge
gateway in order.

Message flows:
  Counterparty → Legal (Paralegal) lane (claim, dispute, notice,
    subpoena or litigation filing — triggers the start event)
  Legal (Paralegal) lane → Matter Management System (new matter record
    creation request)
  Matter Management System → Legal (Paralegal) lane (matter record
    confirmation — triggers intermediate catch event)
  Legal (Paralegal) lane → Counterparty (acknowledgement of receipt of
    matter)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incoming Matter Document" — read by "Log initial matter
  details".
Data Object "Conflict-of-Interest Check Record" — written by "Check for
  conflict of interest"; read by gateway "Conflict identified?".
Data Object "Supporting Documentation Package" — written by "Gather
  supporting documentation and file reference material"; read by "Create
  matter record in Matter Management System".

This subprocess captures every inbound claim, dispute, complaint,
regulatory notice, subpoena or litigation filing, runs a conflict-of-
interest check, classifies and prioritises the matter, and creates a
formal matter record in the Matter Management System. A registered matter
record, complete with assigned owner and supporting documentation, is
handed to the Assess Merits & Exposure subprocess for substantive
evaluation.
```


### V20.02 — Assess Merits & Exposure

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
to Resolution value chain, receiving a registered matter from Receive &

Pool "Organisation" — the legal function and risk team conducting the
assessment.
  Lane "Legal" — legal counsel performing merits review and privilege
  assessment.
  Lane "Risk" — risk manager conducting exposure quantification and
  provisioning recommendation.
Pool "Matter Management System" — system of record for matter and
exposure data.

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box; Legal lane above Risk lane)
2. Matter Management System

  Register Matter"

  User task "Review facts and identify applicable law"
  User task "Assess legal merits and likelihood of success"
  User task "Identify privilege and confidentiality considerations"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to assess?"
    - branch "No — information gaps": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      Information Sufficient" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify missing facts or documents",
      Send task "Request supplementary information from matter owner",
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary information
      received"
    - branch "Yes — proceed": continue to next task
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to assess"
  User task "Document merits assessment and legal opinion"
  Send task "Send merits assessment to Risk for exposure quantification"

Risk lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Merits assessment received from
  Legal"
  User task "Quantify financial exposure and worst-case liability"
  User task "Review applicable insurance coverage"
  User task "Determine provisioning and materiality classification"
  User task "Prepare exposure and provisioning recommendation"
  Send task "Return exposure assessment to Legal"

Legal lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Exposure assessment received from
  Risk"
  User task "Consolidate merits opinion and exposure assessment"
  Service task "Record consolidated assessment in Matter Management
  System"
  User task "Classify matter priority and escalation level"
  Exclusive gateway "Escalation required?"
    - branch "Yes — escalate": User task "Notify general counsel and
      executive management", then End event "Assessment escalated —
      ready for Assign Internal & External Counsel"
    - branch "No — standard": End event "Assessment complete — ready
      for Assign Internal & External Counsel"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Information Sufficient" — label "Assessment deadline reached" — triggers
User task "Flag matter as information-blocked and escalate to general
counsel", leading to End event "Escalated due to information gap —
ready for Assign Internal & External Counsel".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Legal lane with retrieval and review
tasks, passes through the sufficiency gateway (looping via the expanded
subprocess until resolved, then merging), continues to documentation
and hand-off to the Risk lane, then returns to Legal for consolidation,
system recording, and priority classification, concluding at one of two
end events depending on the escalation gateway branch.

Message flows:
Matter Management System → Legal lane "Retrieve matter record and
intake documents" (registered matter record and intake documents).
Legal lane "Service task — Record consolidated assessment in Matter
Management System" → Matter Management System (consolidated merits and
exposure assessment).
Legal lane "Send merits assessment to Risk for exposure quantification"
→ Risk lane "Intermediate message catch event — Merits assessment

Risk lane "Send task — Return exposure assessment to Legal" → Legal

7. Data objects

Data Object "Registered Matter Record" — read by "Retrieve matter
record and intake documents".
Data Object "Merits Assessment and Legal Opinion" — written by
"Document merits assessment and legal opinion"; read by "Consolidate
merits opinion and exposure assessment".
Data Object "Supplementary Information Request" — written by "Request

Data Object "Exposure and Provisioning Recommendation" — written by

"Consolidate merits opinion and exposure assessment".
consolidated assessment in Matter Management System".

This subprocess takes the registered matter and produces a consolidated
legal-merits opinion paired with a quantified exposure and provisioning
recommendation. Legal counsel reviews facts, applicable law, and
privilege considerations, looping to gather missing information where
needed, then passes a formal opinion to Risk for financial exposure
quantification and insurance review. The resulting consolidated record,
classified by priority and escalation level, is stored in the Matter
Management System and handed to Assign Internal & External Counsel so
that resourcing decisions are grounded in a clear view of merit and
financial risk.
```

```text
External counsel required" before "Confirm full counsel team and roles to
```

### V20.04 — Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.04 Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence — sits within the
Matter to Resolution value chain, triggered once internal and external
counsel have been assigned and activated.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal team, paralegal, and business unit matter
owner who issue the hold and collect evidence.
  Lane "Legal (Paralegal)" — drafts and issues the legal hold notice,
  tracks custodian acknowledgements, and manages hold records.
  Lane "Business Unit (Matter Owner)" — receives the hold notice,
  identifies and preserves relevant evidence within the business unit.

Pool "Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform" — the IT platform that
automates custodian notification, tracks acknowledgements, and collects
preserved data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top: Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Legal (Paralegal) above,
Business Unit (Matter Owner) below).
Bottom: Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform (black-box IT system pool).

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal (Paralegal) lane:
  Message start event "Counsel assignment confirmed — received from
  Assign Internal & External Counsel"
  User task "Identify custodians and data sources"
  Service task "Create legal hold notice in platform"
  Send task "Issue legal hold notice to custodians"
  Intermediate message catch event "Custodian acknowledgements received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Custodians Acknowledge"
  (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Chase non-responding
  custodians", Send task "Re-issue hold notice to non-respondents",
  Intermediate message catch event "Further acknowledgements received"
  Exclusive gateway "All custodians acknowledged?"
  - branch "Yes": proceed to User task "Confirm hold coverage complete"
  - branch "No, deadline elapsed": escalate via timer boundary
  Exclusive merge gateway "All custodians acknowledged?"
  User task "Confirm hold coverage complete"
  User task "Log hold record and custodian list"
  Service task "Record hold status in platform"

Business Unit (Matter Owner) lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Legal hold notice received"
  User task "Identify and quarantine relevant documents and data"
  User task "Suspend routine data-deletion schedules"
  User task "Compile evidence inventory"
  Send task "Submit evidence inventory to Legal"
  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence collection confirmed by
  Legal"
  End event "Hold issued and evidence preserved — ready for Develop
  Strategy"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Custodians Acknowledge", labelled "Acknowledgement deadline elapsed
(5 business days)" — triggers User task "Escalate non-compliance to
General Counsel" in the Legal (Paralegal) lane, then joins the flow at
Exclusive merge gateway "All custodians acknowledged?".
Interrupting error boundary event on Service task "Create legal hold
notice in platform", labelled "Platform error" — triggers User task
"Raise platform incident and retry manually" in the Legal (Paralegal)
lane, then returns to Service task "Create legal hold notice in
platform".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Legal (Paralegal) lane the flow runs from
the message start event through custodian identification, hold creation,
and hold issuance, then waits at the intermediate catch event before
entering the acknowledgement loop; the loop exits to the exclusive
gateway whose "Yes" branch leads to confirmation and logging tasks and
whose deadline-elapsed path joins at the merge gateway via the
escalation task; both branches rejoin at Exclusive merge gateway "All
custodians acknowledged?" and continue to confirm and log tasks and the
record service task. Within the Business Unit lane the flow runs from
receipt of the hold notice through quarantine, deletion-schedule
suspension, inventory compilation, and submission, then waits at the
confirmation catch event and ends. Sequence flows cross lanes where
Legal's send task triggers the Business Unit catch event and where the
Business Unit's send task returns to Legal's confirmation step.

Message flows:
Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform → Legal (Paralegal): Service task
"Create legal hold notice in platform" (hold notice created and stored
in platform).
Legal (Paralegal) → Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform: Service task
"Record hold status in platform" (custodian list and hold confirmation
written to platform).
Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform → Legal (Paralegal): Intermediate
message catch event "Custodian acknowledgements received"
(acknowledgement data returned from platform).
Business Unit (Matter Owner) → Legal (Paralegal): Send task "Submit
evidence inventory to Legal" (evidence inventory document).
Legal (Paralegal) → Business Unit (Matter Owner): send of evidence
collection confirmation (confirmation that inventory is accepted).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Legal Hold Notice" — written by User task "Create legal
hold notice in platform"; read by Send task "Issue legal hold notice to
custodians"; read by Business Unit User task "Identify and quarantine
relevant documents and data".
Data Object "Custodian List" — written by User task "Identify
custodians and data sources"; read by Service task "Record hold status
in platform".
Data Object "Custodian Acknowledgement Log" — written by Intermediate
message catch event "Custodian acknowledgements received"; read by
User task "Confirm hold coverage complete".
Data Object "Evidence Inventory" — written by User task "Compile
evidence inventory"; read by User task "Log hold record and custodian
list".
Service task "Record hold status in platform"; read by User task
"Confirm hold coverage complete".

V20.04 issues a formal legal hold to all relevant custodians, tracks
acknowledgement through the Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform, and
coordinates the business unit's quarantine of documents and suspension
of deletion schedules. It produces a confirmed custodian list, a
platform-recorded hold status, and an evidence inventory, all of which
are handed to V20.05 Develop Strategy so that counsel can work from a
complete and privilege-protected evidentiary foundation.
```

```text
  process, with lanes for Legal and External Counsel liaison work.
Pool "External Counsel" — external law firm or barrister engaged to act
  on the matter.
Pool "Matter Management System" — system of record for matter details,
  strategy documents and privilege logs.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Counsel" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
```
