```text
Top to bottom:
1. External Counsel
2. Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom: Legal)
3. Matter Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Counsel assignment confirmed — received from
    Assign Internal & External Counsel"
  Service task "Retrieve matter record and exposure assessment"
  User task "Define scope and objectives of strategy"
  User task "Draft initial strategy options"
  Send task "Issue strategy brief and instructions to External Counsel"
  Intermediate message catch event "External Counsel advice received"
  User task "Review and reconcile External Counsel advice with internal
    position"
  Exclusive gateway "Strategy options agreed?"
    - branch "Not agreed": Send task "Request further External Counsel
        input on disputed options"
      Intermediate message catch event "Further advice received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Strategy options agreed"
    - branch "Agreed": Exclusive merge gateway "Strategy options agreed"
  User task "Finalise and document approved strategy"
  User task "Record privilege log entry for strategy document"
  Service task "Store strategy and privilege log in Matter Management
    System"

      Exclusive merge gateway "Board reporting check"
    - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Board reporting check"
  End event "Strategy approved and recorded — ready for Manage Discovery
    & Disclosure"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on expanded subprocess — not
  applicable; no looping subprocess is used here.
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request further External Counsel
  input on disputed options" — label "Counsel response overdue (5
  business days)"; triggers Send task "Escalate delay to General
  Counsel"; flow rejoins at Exclusive merge gateway "Strategy options
  agreed".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Legal lane from the
  message start event through retrieval, drafting and briefing tasks,
  then waits at the intermediate catch event for External Counsel advice,
  proceeds to review, through the "Strategy options agreed?" exclusive
  gateway whose "Not agreed" branch fires a further send task and a
  second intermediate catch event before both branches rejoin at the

  logging tasks, then through the "Board or executive reporting

  summary task before both branches rejoin at its merge gateway and
  terminate at the end event.

Message flows:
  Legal lane "Issue strategy brief and instructions to External Counsel"
    → External Counsel (strategy brief, instructions and authority
    limits)
  External Counsel → Legal lane "Intermediate message catch event
    External Counsel advice received" (legal advice and draft strategy
    input)
  Legal lane "Request further External Counsel input on disputed options"
    → External Counsel (request for further advice on disputed options)
  External Counsel → Legal lane "Intermediate message catch event
    Further advice received" (supplementary advice)
  Legal lane "Store strategy and privilege log in Matter Management
    System" → Matter Management System (strategy document and privilege
    log entry)
  Matter Management System → Legal lane "Retrieve matter record and
    exposure assessment" (matter record and prior exposure assessment)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Strategy Brief" — written by "Draft initial strategy
  options"; read by "Issue strategy brief and instructions to External
  Counsel".
Data Object "External Counsel Advice" — written by External Counsel;
  read by "Review and reconcile External Counsel advice with internal
  position".
Data Object "Approved Strategy Document" — written by "Finalise and
  document approved strategy"; read by "Store strategy and privilege log
  in Matter Management System".
Data Object "Executive Strategy Summary" — written by "Prepare strategy
  summary for executive reporting"; read by the end event flow for
  onward reporting.

V20.05 Develop Strategy takes the confirmed counsel assignment from
V20.04 and produces an approved, privilege-protected strategy document
stored in the Matter Management System, incorporating External Counsel
advice and reconciled with the organisation's internal position. Where
required, an executive summary is prepared for board or management
reporting. The subprocess hands an agreed strategy, privilege log entry
and any executive summary to V20.06 Manage Discovery & Disclosure, which
will execute the strategy through the discovery and disclosure phases of
the matter.
```

```text
matter record with disclosure status".

Paralegal lane tasks retrieving stored documents.

V20.06 Manage Discovery & Disclosure receives a confirmed strategy from
V20.05 and takes responsibility for identifying custodian data sources,
collecting and reviewing documents, applying privilege protection, and
transmitting compliant disclosures to the counterparty and court. The
subprocess loops to handle supplemental requests until all discovery
obligations are satisfied. On completion it hands a fully documented
disclosure record and updated matter status to V20.07 Negotiate or
Mediate.
```


### V20.07 — Negotiate or Mediate

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate — subprocess within Matter to
Resolution in which Legal and Executive Management pursue negotiated
settlement or formal mediation with the Counterparty, assisted by a
Mediator where appointed, before the matter proceeds to litigation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal team and executive management conducting
negotiation and mediation.
  Lane "Legal (legal counsel)" — leads negotiation, instructs mediator,
  prepares offers and submissions.
  Lane "Executive Management (delegated approver)" — reviews and authorises
  settlement positions within delegation of authority.
Pool "Counterparty" — claimant, litigant, complainant or opposing party
participating in negotiation or mediation.
Pool "Mediator" — independent third-party mediator or arbitrator appointed
to facilitate settlement.
Pool "Matter Management System" — records negotiation positions, settlement
offers, and matter status.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Counterparty" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Mediator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Counterparty
2. Organisation
3. Mediator
4. Matter Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal (legal counsel) lane:
  Message start event "Strategy confirmed — received from Develop Strategy"
  Service task "Retrieve matter record and exposure assessment"
  User task "Prepare opening negotiation position and authority limits"
  Send task "Send negotiation opening position to Counterparty"
  Intermediate message catch event "Counterparty response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Response acceptable or counter-offer?"
    - branch "Settlement range acceptable": proceed to Exclusive merge
      gateway "Response acceptable or counter-offer?"
    - branch "Counter-offer received": proceed to Exclusive merge
      gateway "Response acceptable or counter-offer?"
    - branch "Negotiation stalled or breakdown": User task
      "Assess whether to appoint mediator"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Response acceptable or counter-offer?"
  Exclusive gateway "Appoint mediator?"
    - branch "Yes — appoint mediator": Send task
      "Send mediation appointment request to Mediator"
      Intermediate message catch event "Mediator acceptance and
      session date confirmed"
      User task "Prepare mediation brief and supporting materials"
      Send task "Submit mediation brief to Mediator"
      Intermediate message catch event "Mediation session outcome received"
    - branch "No — continue bilateral negotiation": proceed to
      Exclusive merge gateway "Appoint mediator?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Appoint mediator?"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Settlement Position Agreed"
  (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review latest position or mediation recommendation",
    User task "Revise settlement offer within authority limits",
    Send task "Send revised offer to Counterparty",
    Intermediate message catch event "Counterparty reply received"
  Service task "Record final negotiated position in matter record"
  Exclusive gateway "Settlement reached?"
    - branch "Yes — settlement agreed": User task
      "Draft settlement agreement terms"
      End event "Settlement agreed — ready for Settle or Obtain Judgment"
    - branch "No — negotiation and mediation exhausted": Send task
      "Notify Counterparty of breakdown"
      Service task "Update matter record with breakdown status"
      End event "Negotiation exhausted — ready for Litigate or Defend"

Executive Management (delegated approver) lane:
  User task "Review proposed settlement position against authority limits"
  Exclusive gateway "Within delegation of authority?"
    - branch "Approved within authority": proceed to Exclusive merge
      gateway "Within delegation of authority?"
    - branch "Requires escalation": User task
      "Escalate to higher authority for approval"
      Intermediate message catch event "Escalation decision received"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Within delegation of authority?"
  User task "Confirm authorised settlement mandate in writing"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Settlement Position Agreed" — label "Negotiation deadline elapsed" —
on expiry flow exits the subprocess and continues to Exclusive gateway
"Settlement reached?" with the "No — negotiation and mediation exhausted"
branch.
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Escalate to higher
authority for approval" — label "Escalation response overdue (48 hours)"
— on expiry, sequence flow proceeds to Exclusive merge gateway
"Within delegation of authority?" carrying a default approval denial.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane with the start event and
moves through position preparation, the counterparty response gateway
(three branches: acceptable, counter-offer, stalled, all rejoining at
the response merge gateway), then the mediator appointment gateway
(two branches: appoint mediator with its intermediate events and submit
brief sequence, or continue bilateral, both rejoining at the appoint
mediator merge gateway), then the settlement loop subprocess, then the
settlement-reached gateway (two branches: settlement agreed leading to
the first end event; negotiation exhausted leading to the second end
event, neither rejoining). The Executive Management lane is triggered by
sequence flow from the Legal lane after the revised offer is prepared
inside the loop, passes through the delegation gateway (two branches:
approved within authority, or escalate with its intermediate catch event,
rejoining at the delegation merge gateway), then returns confirmed mandate
by sequence flow back to the Legal lane.

Message flows:
Counterparty → Legal (legal counsel) (counterparty response and
counter-offers).
Legal (legal counsel) → Counterparty (negotiation opening position and
revised settlement offers).
Legal (legal counsel) → Mediator (mediation appointment request and
mediation brief).
Mediator → Legal (legal counsel) (mediator acceptance, session date
confirmation, and mediation session outcome).
Legal (legal counsel) → Counterparty (notification of breakdown where
applicable).
Legal (legal counsel) → Matter Management System (negotiation positions,
revised offers, and final matter status updates).
Matter Management System → Legal (legal counsel) (matter record and
exposure assessment data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Negotiation Position Paper" — written by User task "Prepare
opening negotiation position and authority limits"; read by User task
"Review proposed settlement position against authority limits".
Data Object "Settlement Offer" — written by User task "Revise settlement
offer within authority limits"; read by Send task "Send revised offer to
Counterparty".
Data Object "Mediation Brief" — written by User task "Prepare mediation
brief and supporting materials"; read by Send task "Submit mediation brief
to Mediator".
Data Object "Authorised Settlement Mandate" — written by User task
"Confirm authorised settlement mandate in writing"; read by User task
"Review latest position or mediation recommendation".
Data Object "Settlement Agreement Draft" — written by User task "Draft
settlement agreement terms"; read by the end event leading to Settle or
Obtain Judgment.
"Retrieve matter record and exposure assessment"; written by Service task
"Record final negotiated position in matter record" and Service task
"Update matter record with breakdown status".

V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate takes the confirmed strategy from Develop
Strategy and pursues resolution first through bilateral negotiation with
the Counterparty, escalating to formal mediation if talks stall. Executive
Management authorises each revised settlement position within the
delegation-of-authority policy. The subprocess concludes either with a
signed settlement mandate handed to Settle or Obtain Judgment, or with a
confirmed breakdown that triggers Litigate or Defend.
```

### V20.09 — Settle or Obtain Judgment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text

1. Pools & Lanes

manage the settlement or judgment process.
  Lane "Legal — General Counsel"
  Lane "Finance — Finance Business Partner"
Pool "Counterparty" — the claimant, litigant, or opposing party to the

against the resolved matter.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Counterparty" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.
Pool "Finance / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Counterparty
2. Organisation
3. Insurer
4. Matter Management System
5. Finance / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal — General Counsel lane:
  Message start event "Settlement position or judgment outcome received
    from Litigate or Defend"
  Exclusive gateway "Resolution path?"
  - branch "Judgment obtained": Intermediate message catch event
      "Judgment received from court"
    User task "Review and record judgment terms"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Resolution path"
  - branch "Settlement to be negotiated":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Settlement Agreed" (standard loop)
      containing, in order: User task "Prepare or revise settlement
      offer", Send task "Send settlement offer to counterparty",
      Intermediate message catch event "Counterparty responds to offer",
      Exclusive gateway "Counterparty accepts?",
      - branch "Rejected — revise": loops (continue subprocess)
      - branch "Accepted": User task "Draft and execute settlement
          agreement"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Resolution path"
  User task "Confirm authority limits and obtain settlement approval"
  User task "Record resolution outcome in matter record"
  Send task "Notify insurer of resolution outcome"
  End event "Matter resolved — ready for Close Matter & Capture Lessons"

Finance — Finance Business Partner lane:
  User task "Review financial exposure and existing provision"
  User task "Post final provision adjustment or accrual"
  User task "Confirm payment or receipt of settlement funds"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Settlement Agreed", labelled "Settlement deadline exceeded", leading to

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal — General Counsel lane with the
message start event, passes immediately to the "Resolution path?" gateway
whose "Judgment obtained" branch routes through review of judgment terms
and whose "Settlement to be negotiated" branch enters the loop subprocess;
both branches rejoin at the "Resolution path" merge gateway. Flow
continues to "Confirm authority limits and obtain settlement approval",
then to "Record resolution outcome in matter record", with a parallel
sequence into the Finance — Finance Business Partner lane where the

Message flows:
Counterparty → Organisation — Legal — General Counsel (counterparty

  (matter record and exposure data retrieved for review).
Organisation — Finance — Finance Business Partner → Finance / ERP System
  (provision adjustment and accrual posting).
Finance / ERP System → Organisation — Finance — Finance Business Partner

7. Data objects

Data Object "Settlement Offer" — written by User task "Prepare or revise
  settlement offer"; read by Send task "Send settlement offer to

Data Object "Settlement Agreement" — written by User task "Draft and

Data Object "Judgment Terms" — written by User task "Review and record

Data Object "Authority Approval" — written by User task "Confirm
  authority limits and obtain settlement approval"; read by User task

This subprocess secures resolution of the matter either through an
executed settlement agreement or by recording a court judgment, ensures
financial provisions are adjusted and funds are confirmed in the Finance /

closed.
```

```text
6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs top to bottom within Legal lane from the

Message flows:
Matter Management System → Legal (legal counsel) lane (matter record,

Legal (legal counsel) lane → Matter Management System (matter closure

Company Secretariat (company secretary) lane → Board Reporting System

This subprocess closes the matter by reviewing its final outcome,
capturing and approving a lessons-learned register entry, lifting
any residual legal hold obligations, and marking the matter closed
in the Matter Management System. Company Secretariat then discharges
any board or committee reporting duty and archives the matter file.
Because this is the final subprocess in the V20 value chain, it
produces no handoff to a successor; the matter is fully resolved and
the record is complete.
```

## V21 — Application to Decision

**Teams and roles involved.**
Application to Decision usually involves Intake or Contact Centre, Assessment/Underwriting, Credit or Eligibility Analysis, Verification, Risk, Fraud, Compliance, and Quality Assurance, with an Appeals or Review function for disputed outcomes. Key roles include intake officer, assessor, underwriter, credit analyst, verification officer, fraud analyst, delegated approver, quality reviewer, and appeals officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Applicant. The process is initiated when the applicant submits an application for credit, insurance cover, a grant, a licence, a benefit, admission or membership. Other external parties include credit bureaux and identity verification services, employers and referees, brokers or agents acting for the applicant, and regulators setting eligibility rules.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive the application, check completeness and request missing information, verify identity, gather supporting evidence and third-party data, assess eligibility against criteria, score and price the risk, refer to a delegated authority where limits are exceeded, decide approve, decline or approve with conditions, notify the applicant with reasons, and handle appeals or reviews.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include the application or origination platform, customer portal and document upload, identity verification and credit bureau interfaces, decision engines and scorecards, fraud detection, case management, document management, correspondence generation, and reporting for decision quality and turnaround.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include eligibility criteria and product rules, delegated authority and approval limits, identity verification and anti-money-laundering requirements, responsible lending or suitability obligations, adverse-action and reasons-for-decision requirements, privacy and data-minimisation rules, fraud referral procedures, quality assurance sampling, and appeal rights and timeframes.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The applicant provides the application, identity documents, supporting evidence, consents and declarations, and responses to requests for more information. The process provides the applicant with acknowledgement and reference, requests for further information, status updates, the decision with reasons and any conditions, and appeal rights. Third parties provide bureau reports, verification results and referee responses.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates application records, verification outcomes, evidence documents, scores and decision rationale, referrals and approvals, correspondence, and appeal records. IT systems provide product and eligibility rules, bureau and verification responses, fraud signals, decision-engine outputs, delegated authority limits, and turnaround, approval-rate and quality reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Assessing Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V21.01** Receive Application | Applicant, Broker | Intake (intake officer) | Application / Origination Platform, Customer Portal |
| **V21.02** Check Completeness | Applicant | Intake (intake officer) | Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.03** Verify Identity | Applicant, Identity Verification Service | Verification (verification officer) | Identity Verification Service, Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.04** Gather Supporting Evidence | Applicant, Credit Bureau | Verification (verification officer) | Credit Bureau Interface, Document Management System |
| **V21.05** Assess Eligibility | — | Assessment (assessor) | Decision Engine, Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.06** Score & Price Risk | — | Assessment (underwriter), Risk (credit analyst) | Decision Engine |
| **V21.07** Refer to Delegated Authority | — | Assessment (delegated approver) | Case Management System |
| **V21.08** Decide Outcome | — | Assessment (underwriter), Compliance (compliance officer) | Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.09** Notify Applicant with Reasons | Applicant | Intake (intake officer) | Correspondence System, Customer Portal |
| **V21.10** Handle Appeal or Review | Applicant | Appeals (appeals officer), Quality Assurance (quality reviewer) | Case Management System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V21):

- **External actors:** Applicant (V21.01–V21.04, V21.09, V21.10); Broker (V21.01); Identity Verification Service (V21.03); Credit Bureau (V21.04).
- **Teams:** Intake (V21.01, V21.02, V21.09); Verification (V21.03, V21.04); Assessment (V21.05–V21.08); Risk (V21.06); Compliance (V21.08); Appeals (V21.10); Quality Assurance (V21.10).
- **IT systems:** Application / Origination Platform (V21.01–V21.03, V21.05, V21.08); Customer Portal (V21.01, V21.09); Identity Verification Service (V21.03); Credit Bureau Interface (V21.04); Document Management System (V21.04); Decision Engine (V21.05, V21.06); Case Management System (V21.07, V21.10); Correspondence System (V21.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V21 — Application to Decision — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Application to Decision value chain, from first receipt of an application
through to appeal or review. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands
read top-to-bottom as service realisation: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) shows
what the assessing organisation offers to external participants;
BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) shows the ten subprocesses that realise those
services; APPLICATIONS (bottom band) shows the IT systems that support the
processes. The Applicant and Broker sit on the far left as demand-side actors;
the Identity Verification Service and Credit Bureau sit on the far right as
external delivery and data-provision actors.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Applicant — far left; initiates the chain and receives decisions and
  notifications throughout.
- Broker — far left, below Applicant; acts on behalf of the applicant at
  intake.
- Identity Verification Service — far right; provides identity verification
  results to the process.
- Credit Bureau — far right, below Identity Verification Service; provides
  bureau reports and credit data.

2. Interfaces

- Applicant Portal Interface — accessed by Applicant and Broker; serves the
  Application Submission Service and the Notification and Decision Service.
- Broker Submission Interface — accessed by Broker; serves the Application
  Submission Service.
- Identity Verification Interface — accessed by Identity Verification Service;
  serves the Identity and Evidence Verification Service.
- Credit Bureau Interface — accessed by Credit Bureau; serves the Identity and
  Evidence Verification Service.
- Appeal Lodgement Interface — accessed by Applicant; serves the Appeal and
  Review Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Application Submission Service — accepts applications and supporting
  documents from the applicant or broker and issues an acknowledgement and
  reference.
- Completeness and Information Request Service — checks applications for
  missing information and requests any outstanding items from the applicant.
- Identity and Evidence Verification Service — verifies applicant identity and
  gathers third-party supporting evidence including bureau and referee data.
- Eligibility and Risk Assessment Service — assesses eligibility against
  product rules and scores and prices the risk of the application.
- Delegated Authority Referral Service — routes cases that exceed assessment
  limits to an appropriately authorised approver.
- Decision and Outcome Service — records the approve, decline, or
  conditional-approval decision with full reasons and conditions.
- Notification and Decision Service — communicates the decision, reasons, and
  any conditions to the applicant.
- Appeal and Review Service — accepts and manages appeals or review requests
  from applicants and returns a reviewed outcome.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V21.01 Receive Application — intake officer receives the application from
  the applicant or broker and creates the application record.
- V21.02 Check Completeness — intake officer checks the application for
  completeness and requests missing information from the applicant.
- V21.03 Verify Identity — verification officer confirms applicant identity
  using the identity verification service.
- V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence — verification officer collects bureau
  reports, employer or referee responses, and other third-party data.
- V21.05 Assess Eligibility — assessor evaluates the application against
  eligibility criteria and product rules.
- V21.06 Score & Price Risk — underwriter and credit analyst score and price
  the risk of the application using scorecards.
- V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority — delegated approver receives and acts
  on referrals where approval limits are exceeded.
- V21.08 Decide Outcome — underwriter and compliance officer record the final
  approve, decline, or conditional decision.
- V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons — intake officer generates and sends
  the decision notice with reasons and appeal rights to the applicant.
- V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review — appeals officer and quality reviewer
  manage the appeal or review and communicate the reviewed outcome.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Application / Origination Platform — core platform for application record
  creation, completeness checking, eligibility assessment, and decision
  recording.
- Customer Portal — self-service channel for application submission, document
  upload, status updates, and receipt of decision notices.
- Identity Verification Service (system) — interface and processing layer for
  real-time identity verification checks.
- Credit Bureau Interface — integration layer for retrieving bureau reports
  and credit data from external bureaux.
- Document Management System — stores and manages identity documents,
  evidence files, and supporting materials.
- Decision Engine — applies product eligibility rules, scorecards, and
  pricing models to produce decision-engine outputs.
- Case Management System — manages referral workflows for delegated authority
  and tracks appeal and review cases.
- Correspondence System — generates and distributes decision letters,
  information-request notices, and appeal-rights communications.

6. Relationships

SERVING
- Application Submission Service SERVES Applicant.
- Application Submission Service SERVES Broker.
- Completeness and Information Request Service SERVES Applicant.
- Identity and Evidence Verification Service SERVES Identity Verification
  Service (actor).
- Identity and Evidence Verification Service SERVES Credit Bureau (actor).
- Notification and Decision Service SERVES Applicant.
- Appeal and Review Service SERVES Applicant.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.01 Receive Application.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.02 Check Completeness.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.03 Verify Identity.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.05 Assess Eligibility.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.08 Decide Outcome.
- Customer Portal SERVES V21.01 Receive Application.
- Customer Portal SERVES V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons.
- Identity Verification Service (system) SERVES V21.03 Verify Identity.
- Credit Bureau Interface SERVES V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence.
- Document Management System SERVES V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence.
- Decision Engine SERVES V21.05 Assess Eligibility.
- Decision Engine SERVES V21.06 Score & Price Risk.
- Case Management System SERVES V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority.
- Case Management System SERVES V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review.
- Correspondence System SERVES V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons.

REALISATION
- V21.01 Receive Application REALISES Application Submission Service.
- V21.02 Check Completeness REALISES Completeness and Information Request
  Service.
- V21.03 Verify Identity REALISES Identity and Evidence Verification Service.
- V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence REALISES Identity and Evidence
  Verification Service.
- V21.05 Assess Eligibility REALISES Eligibility and Risk Assessment Service.
- V21.06 Score & Price Risk REALISES Eligibility and Risk Assessment Service.
- V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority REALISES Delegated Authority Referral
  Service.
- V21.08 Decide Outcome REALISES Decision and Outcome Service.
- V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons REALISES Notification and Decision
  Service.
- V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review REALISES Appeal and Review Service.

ASSIGNMENT
- Applicant Portal Interface ASSIGNED TO Customer Portal.
- Broker Submission Interface ASSIGNED TO Application / Origination Platform.
- Identity Verification Interface ASSIGNED TO Identity Verification Service
  (system).
- Credit Bureau Interface (interface) ASSIGNED TO Credit Bureau Interface
  (system).
- Appeal Lodgement Interface ASSIGNED TO Case Management System.

ACCESS
- Applicant ACCESSES Applicant Portal Interface.
- Broker ACCESSES Applicant Portal Interface.
- Broker ACCESSES Broker Submission Interface.
- Identity Verification Service (actor) ACCESSES Identity Verification
  Interface.
- Credit Bureau (actor) ACCESSES Credit Bureau Interface (interface).
- Applicant ACCESSES Appeal Lodgement Interface.
```

### V21.01 — Receive Application

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.01 Receive Application — first subprocess in the Application to
Decision value chain, capturing the moment an application enters the
assessing organisation from an applicant or broker.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation receiving and recording
the application, with lanes for Intake.
Pool "Applicant" — the individual or entity submitting the application.
Pool "Broker" — an agent acting on behalf of the applicant.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — the core system that creates
and stores the application record.
Pool "Customer Portal" — the self-service channel through which applicants
submit documents and receive acknowledgement.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Broker" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Customer Portal" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Broker
3. Assessing Organisation
4. Customer Portal
5. Application / Origination Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Intake lane:

Message start event "Application received from Applicant or Broker"
Exclusive gateway "Submission channel?"
- branch "Direct applicant submission via portal": User task
  "Retrieve application and uploaded documents from Customer Portal"
- branch "Broker submission": User task
  "Receive application package from Broker"
Exclusive merge gateway "Submission channel"
User task "Log application and assign reference number"
Service task "Create application record in Application /
  Origination Platform"
User task "Perform initial triage and classify application type"
Exclusive gateway "Application legible and minimally complete?"
- branch "Yes — proceed": continues to send task below
- branch "No — unworkable submission": Send task
  "Return submission to Applicant or Broker with explanation"
  then End event "Unworkable submission returned — no further
  processing"
Exclusive merge gateway "Application legible and minimally complete"
Send task "Send acknowledgement and reference number to Applicant"
End event "Application received and logged — ready for Check
  Completeness"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Retrieve application
and uploaded documents from Customer Portal" — label "Portal retrieval
timeout (1 business day)" — flows to Send task "Notify Applicant of
portal retrieval failure" then to End event "Submission failed — notify
and close".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the Intake lane flows from the message start event to the
channel gateway; the "Direct applicant submission" branch leads to the
portal retrieval task and the "Broker submission" branch leads to the
broker receipt task; both branches rejoin at the submission channel merge
gateway before continuing to logging, record creation, triage, the
legibility gateway, and finally the acknowledgement send task and end
event. The "No — unworkable submission" branch ends at its own
terminating end event without rejoining.

Message flows:
Applicant → Assessing Organisation / Intake (application form,
  identity documents, consents and declarations submitted directly)
Broker → Assessing Organisation / Intake (application package
  submitted on behalf of applicant)
Customer Portal → Assessing Organisation / Intake (application data
  and uploaded documents retrieved from portal)
Assessing Organisation / Intake → Application / Origination Platform
  (new application record created with reference number)
Assessing Organisation / Intake → Customer Portal (acknowledgement
  and reference number published to applicant self-service view)
Assessing Organisation / Intake → Applicant (acknowledgement message
  with reference number sent directly)
Assessing Organisation / Intake → Broker (acknowledgement message
  with reference number sent where broker submitted)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Application Form" — written by User task "Retrieve
  application and uploaded documents from Customer Portal"; read by
  User task "Perform initial triage and classify application type".
Data Object "Supporting Documents Package" — written by User task
  "Retrieve application and uploaded documents from Customer Portal"
  and User task "Receive application package from Broker"; read by
  User task "Perform initial triage and classify application type".
Data Object "Acknowledgement Notice" — written by Send task "Send
  acknowledgement and reference number to Applicant"; read by no
  further task within this subprocess.

V21.01 receives the incoming application from the applicant or a broker,
assigns it a reference number, creates the authoritative record in the
Application / Origination Platform, and sends the applicant an
acknowledgement. Unworkable submissions are returned immediately. A
complete, logged application is handed to Check Completeness, which
will determine whether all required fields and documents are present
before substantive assessment begins.
```


### V21.02 — Check Completeness

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.02 Check Completeness — second subprocess in the Application to
Decision value chain, triggered when a submitted application is handed from
Receive Application and resolved when the application is confirmed complete
and ready for Verify Identity.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation reviewing application
completeness, with Intake lane.
Pool "Applicant" — the individual or entity that submitted the application.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — the core system of record for
application data and completeness rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Assessing Organisation
3. Application / Origination Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Intake lane:
  Message start event "Application received from Receive Application"
  Service task "Retrieve application record from platform"
  Service task "Run completeness check against product rules"
  Exclusive gateway "Application complete?"
  - branch "Yes": proceed to End event
  - branch "No": User task "Identify missing or deficient items"
               Send task "Issue request for further information to applicant"
               Intermediate message catch event "Applicant response received"
               Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Application Complete"
                 (standard loop) containing, in order: Service task "Re-run
                 completeness check against product rules", Exclusive gateway
                 "Now complete?", branch "Yes": exit loop, branch "No":
                 User task "Identify remaining missing items", Send task
                 "Issue follow-up request to applicant", Intermediate message
                 catch event "Applicant follow-up response received"
               Exclusive merge gateway "Application complete?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Application complete?"
  User task "Mark application as complete in platform"
  End event "Application confirmed complete — ready for Verify Identity"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Application Complete", labelled "Maximum information request period
elapsed", leading to: User task "Record application as withdrawn or
lapsed", then Terminate end event "Application closed — incomplete
and timed out".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Intake lane carries all flow. After the
first completeness check the exclusive gateway "Application complete?"
branches: the "Yes" branch flows directly to the merge gateway and
onward to "Mark application as complete in platform"; the "No" branch
flows through "Identify missing or deficient items", "Issue request
for further information to applicant", the intermediate catch event,
and into the expanded subprocess loop, then exits to the same merge
gateway. Both branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway
"Application complete?" before the final task and end event. The
timer boundary event on the loop exits to "Record application as
withdrawn or lapsed" and then to the terminate end event, bypassing
the merge gateway.

Message flows:
Application / Origination Platform → Assessing Organisation / Intake
  (application record and product completeness rules)
Assessing Organisation / Intake → Applicant (request for further
  information)
Applicant → Assessing Organisation / Intake (response with missing
  items or documents)
Assessing Organisation / Intake → Application / Origination Platform
  (completeness status update and marked-complete flag)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Application Record" — read by "Retrieve application record
  from platform" / written by "Mark application as complete in platform".
Data Object "Completeness Checklist" — read by "Run completeness check
  against product rules" / written by "Identify missing or deficient
  items".
Data Object "Request for Further Information" — written by "Issue request
  for further information to applicant" / read by Applicant pool.
Data Object "Applicant Response" — written by Applicant pool / read by
  "Re-run completeness check against product rules".

Check Completeness receives the submitted application from Receive
Application and confirms it contains every required field, document and
consent before work proceeds further. The intake officer uses the
origination platform's product rules to identify gaps, contacts the
applicant as many times as needed within a defined time limit, and marks
the record complete once all items are satisfied. A timed-out or
irrecoverably incomplete application is closed at this stage. The
subprocess hands a confirmed-complete application record to Verify
Identity.
```


### V21.03 — Verify Identity

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.03 Verify Identity — third subprocess in the Application to
Decision value chain, triggered after Check Completeness confirms the
application is complete.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation running identity
  verification, with Verification team lane.
Pool "Applicant" — the individual whose identity is being verified.
Pool "Identity Verification Service" — external third-party provider
  of identity checks.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — system of record for
  the application and verification outcomes.
Pool "Identity Verification Service (System)" — IT interface to the
  external identity verification service.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Identity Verification Service" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Identity Verification Service (System)" — black-box,
  System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Identity Verification Service
3. Assessing Organisation
4. Identity Verification Service (System)
5. Application / Origination Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Verification lane:
  Message start event "Complete application received from Check
    Completeness"
  User task "Review application for identity documents required"
  Send task "Request identity documents from applicant"
  Intermediate message catch event "Identity documents received from
    applicant"
  User task "Examine submitted identity documents"
  Service task "Submit identity documents to verification service"
  Intermediate message catch event "Verification result received from
    Identity Verification Service (System)"
  Exclusive gateway "Identity verified?"
  - branch "Verified": User task "Record verification outcome in
      Application / Origination Platform"
    End event "Identity verified — ready for Gather Supporting
      Evidence"
  - branch "Unable to verify — further information needed":
      Send task "Request additional identity documents from applicant"
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Identity Verified or Attempts
        Exhausted" (standard loop) containing, in order:
          Intermediate message catch event "Additional documents
            received",
          User task "Examine additional identity documents",
          Service task "Resubmit documents to verification service",
          Intermediate message catch event "Updated verification
            result received"
        Timer boundary event on subprocess "Maximum re-attempt
          period elapsed" — interrupting — leads to escalation path.
      Exclusive merge gateway "Identity verified?"
      User task "Record verification outcome in Application /
        Origination Platform"
      End event "Identity verified — ready for Gather Supporting
        Evidence"
  - branch "Failed — identity cannot be confirmed":
      User task "Record verification failure in Application /
        Origination Platform"
      User task "Refer case to Fraud team for review"
      End event "Identity verification failed — case referred to
        Fraud"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Identity Verified or Attempts Exhausted", labelled "Maximum
  re-attempt period elapsed"; on trigger, flow passes to User task
  "Record verification failure in Application / Origination Platform"
  and then End event "Identity verification failed — case referred to
  Fraud".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Verification lane at the message
start event and passes through document review, the send task to the
applicant, and the message catch waiting for documents, then through
document examination and submission to the verification system, then
waits for the result. The exclusive gateway "Identity verified?" splits
into three branches: the "Verified" branch records the outcome and ends
successfully; the "Unable to verify" branch sends a further request,
enters the standard-loop subprocess (with its timer boundary), rejoins
at the exclusive merge gateway "Identity verified?", records the
outcome, and ends successfully; the "Failed" branch records failure,
refers to Fraud, and ends with a failure end event. The timer boundary
on the loop subprocess exits to the failure path without rejoining the
merge gateway.

Message flows:
  Assessing Organisation → Applicant (request for identity documents)
  Applicant → Assessing Organisation (identity documents submitted)
  Assessing Organisation → Identity Verification Service
    (identity documents for checking)
  Identity Verification Service → Assessing Organisation
    (verification result)
  Assessing Organisation → Identity Verification Service (System)
    (document submission via system interface)
  Identity Verification Service (System) → Assessing Organisation
    (verification result via system interface)
  Assessing Organisation → Application / Origination Platform
    (verification outcome recorded)
  Application / Origination Platform → Assessing Organisation
    (application data and prior verification record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Identity Documents" — written by User task "Examine
  submitted identity documents"; read by Service task "Submit identity
  documents to verification service".
Data Object "Verification Request" — written by Service task "Submit
  identity documents to verification service"; read by Identity
  Verification Service (System).
Data Object "Verification Result" — written by Identity Verification
  Service (System); read by User task "Record verification outcome in
  Application / Origination Platform".

V21.03 Verify Identity takes the complete application accepted by Check
Completeness and confirms that the applicant is who they claim to be.
The verification officer requests and examines identity documents,
submits them to the external Identity Verification Service, and handles
any re-attempts within the permitted window. A confirmed positive
outcome, with the result recorded on the application record, is handed
to Gather Supporting Evidence; a failed outcome is routed to the Fraud
team for further review.
```


### V21.04 — Gather Supporting Evidence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence — fourth subprocess in the
Application to Decision value chain, sitting between Verify Identity
and Assess Eligibility.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation running the
  evidence-gathering process, with lanes for Verification.
Pool "Applicant" — the individual or entity applying, who supplies
  supporting evidence on request.
Pool "Credit Bureau" — external agency providing bureau reports and
  third-party data.
Pool "Credit Bureau Interface" — IT system connecting the process to
  the credit bureau.
Pool "Document Management System" — IT system for storing and
  retrieving evidence documents.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Credit Bureau" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Credit Bureau Interface" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Credit Bureau
3. Assessing Organisation
4. Credit Bureau Interface
5. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Verification lane:
  Message start event "Verified identity record received from
    Verify Identity"
  User task "Identify required supporting evidence"
  Parallel gateway "Request evidence in parallel"
    - branch "applicant documents": Send task "Request supporting
        documents from applicant"
        Intermediate message catch event "Applicant documents
          received"
    - branch "bureau data": Service task "Submit bureau data request"
        Intermediate message catch event "Bureau report received"
  Parallel merge gateway "All evidence received"
  User task "Review completeness of gathered evidence"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient?"
    - branch "yes": continue to store evidence
    - branch "no": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence
        Sufficient" (standard loop) containing, in order: Send task
        "Request additional information from applicant", Intermediate
        message catch event "Additional information received", User
        task "Re-review completeness of gathered evidence"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient"
  Service task "Store evidence documents in Document Management
    System"
  User task "Compile evidence package for assessment"
  End event "Evidence package complete — ready for Assess Eligibility"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Evidence Sufficient", labelled "Maximum evidence chase
  period elapsed"; on trigger, flow goes to an Error end event
  "Evidence not obtained — case stalled".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Verification lane.
After the start event, the verification officer identifies required
evidence, then the parallel gateway splits into two simultaneous
branches — one requesting applicant documents and awaiting the
applicant's reply, the other submitting a bureau request and
awaiting the bureau report. Both branches rejoin at the parallel
merge gateway. The exclusive gateway then tests sufficiency; the
"no" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and returns to the
merge gateway on each iteration until the condition is met. The "yes"
branch bypasses the loop and both converge at the exclusive merge
gateway before evidence is stored and packaged.

Message flows:
  Send task "Request supporting documents from applicant" →
    Applicant (evidence request letter or portal notification)
  Applicant → Intermediate message catch event "Applicant documents
    received" (supporting documents and declarations)
  Send task "Request additional information from applicant" →
    Applicant (follow-up information request)
  Applicant → Intermediate message catch event "Additional
    information received" (additional documents or responses)
  Service task "Submit bureau data request" → Credit Bureau
    Interface (bureau enquiry)
  Credit Bureau Interface → Credit Bureau (forwarded bureau enquiry)
  Credit Bureau → Credit Bureau Interface (bureau report)
  Credit Bureau Interface → Intermediate message catch event "Bureau
    report received" (bureau report and credit data)
  Service task "Store evidence documents in Document Management
    System" → Document Management System (evidence documents for
    storage)
  Document Management System → Service task "Store evidence documents
    in Document Management System" (confirmed document references)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Evidence Requirements List" — written by User task
  "Identify required supporting evidence"; read by Send task
  "Request supporting documents from applicant" and Service task
  "Submit bureau data request".
Data Object "Applicant Supporting Documents" — written by
  Intermediate message catch event "Applicant documents received";
  read by User task "Review completeness of gathered evidence".
Data Object "Bureau Report" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Bureau report received"; read by User task "Review
  completeness of gathered evidence".
Data Object "Evidence Package" — written by User task "Compile
  evidence package for assessment"; read by the end event flow
  passed to Assess Eligibility.

V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence collects all documentary and
third-party data needed to assess the application, running applicant
document requests and credit bureau enquiries in parallel and chasing
any gaps through a controlled loop capped by a timer. Once the
verification officer judges the evidence package complete, it is
stored in the Document Management System and handed to Assess
Eligibility as a consolidated, retrievable record ready for
eligibility testing.
```


### V21.05 — Assess Eligibility

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.05 Assess Eligibility — fifth subprocess in the Application to
Decision value chain, receiving a verified and evidence-complete application
from Gather Supporting Evidence and handing an eligibility determination to
Score & Price Risk.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation conducting eligibility
assessment, containing the Assessment team.
Pool "Decision Engine" — automated rules and scoring system that applies
product eligibility criteria.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — system of record holding the
application, evidence, and eligibility outcome.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Decision Engine" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Assessing Organisation (white-box, process flow here)
2. Decision Engine
3. Application / Origination Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane:
  Message start event "Verified application with supporting evidence received
    from Gather Supporting Evidence"
  User task "Review verified application and evidence package"
  Service task "Submit application to Decision Engine for eligibility check"
  Intermediate message catch event "Eligibility rules result received from
    Decision Engine"
  User task "Interpret eligibility rules result"
  Exclusive gateway "Meets eligibility criteria?"
    - branch "Yes — fully eligible": proceed to record eligibility outcome
    - branch "No — ineligible": proceed to record ineligible outcome
    - branch "Borderline — further review required":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Eligibility Determined" (standard
        loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Conduct manual eligibility review against product rules",
          User task "Request clarification or additional information from case
            record",
          User task "Re-evaluate eligibility position"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Meets eligibility criteria?"
  User task "Record eligibility determination and rationale"
  Service task "Write eligibility outcome to Application / Origination
    Platform"
  User task "Flag application for Quality Assurance sampling if required"
  End event "Eligibility determined — ready for Score & Price Risk"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Eligibility Determined", labelled "Maximum review period elapsed", leading
to a User task "Escalate unresolved eligibility to senior assessor" and
then to an End event "Escalated — eligibility unresolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work proceeds through the Assessment lane from the message
start event through review, submission to the Decision Engine, result
interpretation, and the "Meets eligibility criteria?" gateway. The "Yes"
and "No" branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Meets eligibility
criteria?" before recording the outcome; the "Borderline" branch enters the
standard-loop subprocess and then also rejoins the same merge gateway.
From the merge gateway the flow continues to record the determination, write
it to the platform, apply QA sampling, and reach the end event.

Message flows:
Application / Origination Platform → Assessment lane, Service task "Submit
  application to Decision Engine for eligibility check" (verified application
  record and supporting evidence).
Assessment lane, Service task "Submit application to Decision Engine for
  eligibility check" → Decision Engine (eligibility check request with
  application data).
Decision Engine → Assessment lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Eligibility rules result received from Decision Engine" (rules-based
  eligibility result and flags).
Assessment lane, Service task "Write eligibility outcome to Application /
  Origination Platform" → Application / Origination Platform (eligibility
  determination, rationale, and QA flag).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Verified Application Package" — read by User task "Review
  verified application and evidence package"; read by Service task "Submit
  application to Decision Engine for eligibility check".
Data Object "Eligibility Rules Result" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Eligibility rules result received from Decision Engine"; read
  by User task "Interpret eligibility rules result".
Data Object "Manual Review Notes" — written by User task "Conduct manual
  eligibility review against product rules"; read by User task "Re-evaluate
  eligibility position".

V21.05 Assess Eligibility takes the verified, evidence-complete application
and runs it through the Decision Engine's product and eligibility rules,
supplemented by manual review where the automated result is borderline. The
assessor records a clear eligibility determination — eligible, ineligible, or
escalated — with full rationale written back to the Application / Origination
Platform. A fully eligible outcome, along with its documented rationale, is
handed to Score & Price Risk to proceed with scoring and pricing.
```


### V21.06 — Score & Price Risk

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.06 Score & Price Risk — the sixth subprocess in the Application
to Decision value chain, running after eligibility has been confirmed and
before any referral to a delegated authority.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation conducting the scoring
  and risk-pricing exercise, subdivided into Assessment and Risk lanes.
Pool "Decision Engine" — the scoring and decision-engine system that
  produces risk scores and pricing outputs.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Decision Engine" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Assessing Organisation
2. Decision Engine

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane (underwriter):
  Message start event "Eligible application received from Assess
    Eligibility"
  User task "Review eligibility outcome and prepare risk submission"
  Service task "Submit application data to Decision Engine for scoring"
  Intermediate message catch event "Score and pricing output received"
  User task "Review scorecard output and pricing indication"
  Exclusive gateway "Score within acceptable band?"
    - branch "Yes — within band": continue to merge gateway
    - branch "No — outside band or requires manual override": route to
      Risk lane for credit analyst review
  Exclusive merge gateway "Score within acceptable band"

Risk lane (credit analyst):
  User task "Conduct manual risk assessment and pricing review"
  User task "Propose adjusted risk price or terms"
  Exclusive gateway "Adjusted pricing accepted by underwriter?"
    - branch "Yes — accepted": continue to merge gateway
    - branch "No — unresolvable — escalate": Intermediate escalation
      throw event "Escalate unresolved pricing dispute"; End event
      "Pricing dispute escalated — case held for senior review" (does
      not rejoin)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Adjusted pricing accepted by underwriter"
  (rejoins Assessment lane after merge gateway "Score within acceptable
  band")

Assessment lane (underwriter, continued after merge):
  User task "Record final risk score and agreed pricing terms"
  Service task "Write score, pricing and risk rationale to Application
    Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Referral to delegated authority required?"
    - branch "Yes — limits exceeded": End event "Risk scored and priced
      — ready for Refer to Delegated Authority"
    - branch "No — within limits": End event "Risk scored and priced
      — ready for Decide Outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit application data to
  Decision Engine for scoring" — label "Decision Engine timeout
  (2 minutes)" — flow continues to User task "Handle scoring service
  timeout and retry or escalate".
Interrupting error boundary event on "Write score, pricing and risk
  rationale to Application Platform" — label "Record write failure" —
  flow continues to User task "Resolve platform write error and
  re-submit".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the flow begins in the Assessment lane, passes through
eligibility review and submission to the Decision Engine, then catches
the score reply. At the "Score within acceptable band" gateway the
within-band branch merges immediately at the named merge gateway, while
the outside-band branch crosses to the Risk lane for manual review and
pricing, then tests acceptance at a second gateway; the accepted branch
re-enters the Assessment lane at the merge gateway; the unresolvable
branch ends independently. After the merge, the Assessment lane records
and writes the final score, then splits at a final gateway into two
independent end events based on whether a referral is needed.

Message flows:
  Assessment lane "Submit application data to Decision Engine for
    scoring" → Decision Engine (application data and scoring request).
  Decision Engine → Assessment lane "Intermediate message catch event
    Score and pricing output received" (risk score, pricing indication
    and scorecard detail).
  Assessment lane "Write score, pricing and risk rationale to
    Application Platform" → Application / Origination Platform (final
    score, agreed pricing terms and risk rationale) — note: the
    Application / Origination Platform is a system referenced in this
    subprocess but does not appear as a separate pool; the message flow
    is represented as a service task interaction within the white-box
    pool targeting the named platform.

7. Data objects

Data Object "Eligibility Outcome" — read by User task "Review
  eligibility outcome and prepare risk submission".
Data Object "Scoring Request Package" — written by User task "Review
  eligibility outcome and prepare risk submission"; read by Service task
  "Submit application data to Decision Engine for scoring".
Data Object "Score and Pricing Output" — written by Decision Engine;
  read by User task "Review scorecard output and pricing indication".
Data Object "Manual Pricing Proposal" — written by User task "Propose
  adjusted risk price or terms"; read by Exclusive gateway "Adjusted
  pricing accepted by underwriter?".
Data Object "Risk Score and Pricing Record" — written by User task
  "Record final risk score and agreed pricing terms"; read by Service
  task "Write score, pricing and risk rationale to Application Platform".

This subprocess receives the confirmed-eligible application from Assess
Eligibility and produces a validated risk score and agreed pricing
position for every case that remains in flow. Where the automated
scorecard output falls within acceptable limits the underwriter confirms
it directly; where it does not, the credit analyst proposes a manual
adjustment that the underwriter must accept. The subprocess ends by
persisting the final score and rationale to the Application Platform and
then handing the scored, priced case forward — either to Refer to
Delegated Authority where approval limits are exceeded, or directly to
Decide Outcome where they are not.
```


### V21.07 — Refer to Delegated Authority

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority — subprocess in which the
Assessment team escalates a case that exceeds standard approval limits to a
delegated approver for review and authorisation, sitting between Score &
Price Risk and Decide Outcome in the Application to Decision value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation running the referral and
delegated-authority review process, containing the Assessment team.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system used to record, route and track
delegated-authority referrals and approvals.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Assessing Organisation
2. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane:
  Message start event "Risk score and pricing received from Score & Price Risk"
  User task "Review case against delegated authority limits"
  Exclusive gateway "Within standard approval limit?"
  - branch "yes — within limit": End event "No referral needed —
    ready for Decide Outcome"
  - branch "no — exceeds limit": User task "Prepare referral pack"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Within standard approval limit?"
  Service task "Lodge referral in Case Management System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Delegated approver decision received"
  Exclusive gateway "Referral decision?"
  - branch "approved": User task "Record approval and authority
    details"
  - branch "approved with conditions": User task "Record conditions
    of approval"
  - branch "declined": User task "Record declination with reasons"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Referral decision?"
  User task "Update case file with delegated authority outcome"
  End event "Delegated authority outcome recorded — ready for
    Decide Outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess
"Repeat Until Decision Received" (see note: the referral wait is
modelled as an intermediate catch event on the main flow rather than
a loop; no loop boundary event applies here).
Interrupting timer boundary event on intermediate message catch event
"Delegated approver decision received" — label "Referral response
overdue" — attached to the catch event's containing task context;
if no response is received within the allowed authority review period,
flow continues to User task "Escalate overdue referral to senior
approver".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Assessment lane. From
the start event, the intake review task leads to the first exclusive
gateway; the "yes" branch ends immediately; the "no" branch continues
to prepare the referral pack, then merges at the exclusive merge
gateway, then proceeds to lodge the referral in the Case Management
System, then waits at the intermediate message catch event, then
reaches the referral-decision gateway whose three branches — approved,
approved with conditions, declined — each run to their respective
record tasks before merging at the second exclusive merge gateway,
continuing to the update task and the end event. The timer boundary
event on the catch event diverts to the escalation task, which then
rejoins the flow before the referral-decision gateway.

Message flows:
Assessing Organisation (Service task "Lodge referral in Case
  Management System") → Case Management System (referral pack and
  case details submitted for routing).
Case Management System → Assessing Organisation (Intermediate message
  catch event "Delegated approver decision received") (delegated
  approver decision and authority record returned).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Referral Pack" — written by "Prepare referral pack";
  read by "Lodge referral in Case Management System".
Data Object "Delegated Authority Decision" — written by "Record
  approval and authority details" / "Record conditions of approval" /
  "Record declination with reasons"; read by "Update case file with
  delegated authority outcome".

This subprocess determines whether a case requires escalation beyond
standard approval limits and, where it does, manages the referral to
a delegated approver through to receipt of their decision. It captures
the approval, conditional approval or declination along with any
authority details and conditions, then hands a fully documented
delegated-authority outcome to Decide Outcome so that the final
determination can be made within the governance framework.
```


### V21.08 — Decide Outcome

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.08 Decide Outcome — the subprocess in which the Assessing
Organisation makes a formal approve, decline, or approve-with-conditions
decision on the application and records it, sitting between referral or
scoring and applicant notification.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation processing the
application, containing Assessment and Compliance lanes.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — the origination and
case-record system that stores the decision and rationale.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Assessing Organisation (white-box)
2. Application / Origination Platform (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane (underwriter):
  Message start event "Scored and priced application received from
    Score and Price Risk"
  User task "Review scoring output and referral outcome"
  Exclusive gateway "Referral required and completed?"
  - branch "Yes — referral decision received": Intermediate message
      catch event "Delegated authority decision received"
  - branch "No — within underwriter authority": (continues directly)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Referral required and completed?"
  Exclusive gateway "What is the decision?"
  - branch "Approve": User task "Record approval and set any
      conditions"
  - branch "Approve with conditions": User task "Record conditional
      approval and document conditions"
  - branch "Decline": User task "Record decline and document reasons"
  Exclusive merge gateway "What is the decision?"
  User task "Compile decision rationale and adverse-action reasons"
  Send task "Submit decision record to platform"

Compliance lane (compliance officer):
  User task "Quality-check decision for regulatory compliance"
  Exclusive gateway "Compliance check passed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues)
  - branch "No — requires correction": User task "Return decision
      for correction"
    Intermediate message catch event "Corrected decision received"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Compliance check passed?"
  End event "Decision confirmed — ready for Notify Applicant
    with Reasons"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Quality-check
decision for regulatory compliance", labelled "Compliance review
overdue (24 hours)", triggers Send task "Escalate compliance delay
to Compliance manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Assessment lane with the message
start event, passes through the referral gateway (merging the
referral-received branch and the within-authority branch at the
merge gateway), then through the three-way decision gateway whose
approve, conditional-approve, and decline branches each complete
their respective record tasks before rejoining at the decision merge
gateway; flow then passes to "Compile decision rationale and
adverse-action reasons" and on to "Submit decision record to
platform", crossing to the Compliance lane for "Quality-check
decision for regulatory compliance"; the compliance gateway branches
to "Return decision for correction" (catching the corrected-decision
message event) or continues directly, both branches rejoining at
the compliance merge gateway before reaching the end event.

Message flows:
Assessment lane "Submit decision record to platform" →
  Application / Origination Platform (decision record, conditions,
  decline reasons, and rationale).
Application / Origination Platform → Assessment lane "Review scoring
  output and referral outcome" (scoring output, referral outcome,
  and application record).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Scoring and Referral Output" — read by "Review scoring
  output and referral outcome".
Data Object "Decision Record" — written by "Record approval and set
  any conditions", "Record conditional approval and document
  conditions", and "Record decline and document reasons"; read by
  "Compile decision rationale and adverse-action reasons".
Data Object "Decision Rationale and Adverse-Action Reasons" —
  written by "Compile decision rationale and adverse-action reasons";
  read by "Quality-check decision for regulatory compliance".

V21.08 Decide Outcome is the point at which the Assessing
Organisation converts scoring, pricing, and any delegated-authority
ruling into a formal decision — approve, approve with conditions, or
decline — backed by documented rationale that meets adverse-action
and responsible-lending obligations. The compliance quality check
ensures the decision satisfies regulatory requirements before it is
sealed in the origination platform. The confirmed decision record,
including all conditions and reasons, is handed to Notify Applicant
with Reasons for communication to the applicant.
```


### V21.09 — Notify Applicant with Reasons

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons — the subprocess that communicates
the outcome of the application decision to the applicant, providing reasons,
any conditions, and appeal rights, completing the decision value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation issuing the decision
  notice and managing outbound correspondence.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Intake lane (intake officer)
Pool "Applicant" — the individual or entity that submitted the application
  and receives the notification.
Pool "Correspondence System" — system that generates and dispatches
  formatted decision correspondence.
Pool "Customer Portal" — digital platform through which the applicant may
  also receive and acknowledge the notification.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Correspondence System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Customer Portal" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Assessing Organisation
3. Correspondence System
4. Customer Portal

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Intake lane:
  Message start event "Decision outcome received from Decide Outcome"
  User task "Review decision record and prepare notification content"
  Exclusive gateway "Decision type?"
  - branch "Approved": User task "Draft approval notice with conditions
    and next steps"
  - branch "Declined": User task "Draft decline notice with reasons and
    adverse-action statement"
  - branch "Approved with conditions": User task "Draft conditional
    approval notice listing conditions and acceptance deadline"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision type"
  User task "Confirm appeal rights and timeframes are included in notice"
  User task "Submit notice to Correspondence System for dispatch"
  Service task "Publish notification to Customer Portal"
  Intermediate message catch event "Applicant acknowledgement received"

  - branch "Yes": User task "Record acknowledgement and close

  - branch "No": User task "Send follow-up reminder via Correspondence

    Intermediate timer catch event "Reminder wait period elapsed"
    Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement received after reminder?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Record late acknowledgement and close
      notification task"
    - branch "No — no response": User task "Flag non-response for
      Intake review and log outcome"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement received after reminder"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement received within deadline"
  User task "Update application record with notification outcome"
  End event "Applicant notified — notification complete; application
    referred to Handle Appeal or Review if contested, or closed"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Submit notice to
  Correspondence System for dispatch" — label "Dispatch timeout (24 hours)"
  — triggers User task "Escalate dispatch failure to Intake supervisor";
  flow from escalation task ends in a local End event.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Intake lane carries all flow, starting from
  the message start event through preparation, the Decision type gateway
  (three branches — Approved, Declined, Approved with conditions — merging
  at the Decision type merge gateway), then confirmation of appeal rights,
  submission to Correspondence System, publication to Customer Portal,
  the acknowledgement catch event, the Acknowledgement within deadline
  gateway (Yes branch to record acknowledgement and close; No branch

Message flows:
  Assessing Organisation (User task "Submit notice to Correspondence
    System for dispatch") → Correspondence System (decision notice with
    reasons, conditions, and appeal rights).
  Correspondence System → Applicant (formatted decision letter or email).
  Assessing Organisation (Service task "Publish notification to Customer
    Portal") → Customer Portal (notification and supporting documents).

  Applicant → Assessing Organisation (acknowledgement or response to

7. Data objects

Data Object "Decision Notice" — written by "Draft approval notice with
```
