```text
V21.09 takes the confirmed decision from Decide Outcome, prepares a
formatted notice carrying reasons, any conditions, adverse-action
statements, and appeal rights, dispatches it through the Correspondence

It hands a closed notification record to V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review,
which is activated if the applicant contests the outcome within the
stated timeframe.
```


### V21.10 — Handle Appeal or Review

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review — final subprocess in the Application
to Decision chain, receiving a disputed outcome and producing a reviewed
decision.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the body that processed the original
  application and now handles the appeal or review internally.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Appeals (appeals officer)
  - Quality Assurance (quality reviewer)
Pool "Applicant" — individual or entity lodging the appeal or review
  request.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system supporting appeal case tracking
  and workflow.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Assessing Organisation
3. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Appeals lane:
  Message start event "Appeal or review request received from Applicant"
  User task "Log and register appeal"
  Service task "Open appeal case in Case Management System"
  User task "Acknowledge receipt and advise appeal rights and timeframes"
  Send task "Send acknowledgement to Applicant"
  User task "Retrieve original application record and decision rationale"
  Service task "Pull case file from Case Management System"
  User task "Review grounds of appeal and supporting submissions"
  Exclusive gateway "Grounds of appeal valid?"
  - branch "Invalid — outside scope or time limit":
      User task "Notify Applicant appeal not accepted"
      Send task "Send rejection of appeal to Applicant"
      End event "Appeal rejected — process ends"
  - branch "Valid — proceed to review":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Review Complete" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Examine evidence and original
        decision", User task "Request additional information from Applicant
        if required", Intermediate message catch event "Applicant response
        or information received", User task "Update appeal case record"
      Exclusive gateway "Further escalation needed?"
  - branch "No — appeals officer can determine":
      User task "Prepare review findings and draft revised decision"
      Exclusive gateway merge "Further escalation needed"
  - branch "Yes — refer to Quality Assurance":
      (continues in Quality Assurance lane)
  Exclusive gateway merge "Further escalation needed"
  User task "Record reviewed decision and rationale"
  Service task "Update appeal outcome in Case Management System"
  User task "Compile adverse-action reasons if decision upheld"
  Send task "Send reviewed decision with reasons to Applicant"
  End event "Reviewed decision issued — appeal process concluded"

Quality Assurance lane:
  User task "Conduct independent quality review of original decision"
  User task "Document quality review findings"
  User task "Return review findings to Appeals officer"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Review Complete" — label "Appeal timeframe deadline reached" — triggers
  User task "Escalate overdue appeal to senior appeals officer" in Appeals
  lane, then rejoins the main flow before the "Further escalation needed?"
  gateway.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Appeals lane with the message start
  event and progresses through logging, acknowledgement, case retrieval,
  and grounds review. The "Grounds of appeal valid?" gateway splits to
  a rejection branch ending in its own end event, or a valid branch
  entering the standard-loop subprocess. On exit from the subprocess, the
  "Further escalation needed?" gateway branches either directly to the
  appeals officer determination path or into the Quality Assurance lane;
  both branches merge at the "Further escalation needed" merge gateway
  before the final recording, update, and send tasks, concluding at the
  end event.

Message flows:
  Applicant → Appeals lane (appeal or review request with grounds and
    supporting submissions)
  Appeals lane → Applicant (acknowledgement of appeal and advised
    timeframes)
  Appeals lane → Applicant (request for additional information during
    review loop)
  Applicant → Appeals lane (response or additional information during
    review loop)
  Appeals lane → Applicant (reviewed decision with reasons)
  Appeals lane → Case Management System (open appeal case request)
  Case Management System → Appeals lane (case file and original decision
    rationale)
  Appeals lane → Case Management System (appeal outcome update)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Appeal Request" — written by User task "Log and register
  appeal"; read by User task "Review grounds of appeal and supporting
  submissions".
Data Object "Applicant Submissions" — read by User task "Examine evidence
  and original decision"; written by User task "Update appeal case record".
Data Object "Quality Review Findings" — written by User task "Document
  quality review findings"; read by User task "Return review findings to
  Appeals officer".
Data Object "Reviewed Decision and Rationale" — written by User task
  "Record reviewed decision and rationale"; read by Send task "Send
  reviewed decision with reasons to Applicant".
Data Object "Adverse-Action Reasons" — written by User task "Compile
  adverse-action reasons if decision upheld"; read by Send task "Send
  reviewed decision with reasons to Applicant".

V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review receives a formal appeal or review request
from an applicant disputing the decision issued in V21.09 and registers it
as a tracked case. The appeals officer validates the grounds, works through
the evidence in a controlled loop with a hard deadline boundary, and calls
on Quality Assurance for independent scrutiny where escalation is needed.
The subprocess concludes by recording the reviewed outcome and rationale in
the Case Management System and dispatching the final decision with
mandatory adverse-action reasons to the applicant, bringing the Application
to Decision chain to a close.
```


## V22 — Claim to Settlement

**Teams and roles involved.**
Claim to Settlement usually involves Claims Intake, Claims Assessment, Investigation, Fraud, Supply Chain or Repair Networks, Finance/Payments, Recoveries, Complaints, and Actuarial or Reserving. Key roles include claims consultant, assessor, loss adjuster, investigator, fraud analyst, repairer or supplier coordinator, payments officer, recoveries officer, complaints officer, and reserving analyst.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Claimant — a policyholder, member, patient or beneficiary. The process is initiated when a loss or event is notified. Other external parties include loss adjusters and assessors, repairers and suppliers, medical or expert providers, third parties and their insurers, reinsurers, legal representatives, and ombudsman or dispute-resolution schemes.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive notification of the claim, register it and set an initial reserve, validate cover and eligibility, triage and assign, assess the loss and quantum, investigate where indicators warrant it, approve or decline the claim, arrange repair, service or payment, pursue recoveries and reinsurance, and close the claim with reserve release.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include the claims management platform, policy administration, customer and claims portals, fraud detection and analytics, supplier and repairer networks, payments and disbursement systems, document and image management, reserving and actuarial systems, complaints management, and reinsurance and recoveries systems.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include policy wordings and cover terms, claims handling standards and service timeframes, reserving policy, delegated authority for settlement amounts, fraud referral criteria, supplier panel and pricing agreements, recoveries and subrogation procedure, complaints and external dispute-resolution obligations, and regulatory claims-handling conduct requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The claimant provides notification, incident details, supporting evidence and quotes, bank details and declarations, and receives acknowledgement, cover decisions, assessment outcomes, settlement or repair arrangements, payment advice and complaint rights. Suppliers and experts provide assessments, quotes, reports and invoices; reinsurers and third-party insurers exchange recovery claims and settlements.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates claim records, reserves, cover decisions, assessments and quantum, supplier work orders, payments, recovery and reinsurance claims, and complaint records. IT systems provide policy and cover data, claims history, fraud scores and rules outcomes, supplier pricing and availability, payment status, and claims ratio, leakage and cycle-time reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Insurer" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V22.01** Receive Notification | Claimant | Claims Intake (claims consultant) | Claims Management Platform, Customer Portal |
| **V22.02** Register Claim & Set Reserve | — | Claims Intake (claims consultant), Actuarial (reserving analyst) | Claims Management Platform, Reserving System |
| **V22.03** Validate Cover & Eligibility | Claimant | Claims Assessment (claims consultant) | Policy Administration System |
| **V22.04** Triage & Assign | — | Claims Assessment (claims consultant) | Claims Management Platform |
| **V22.05** Assess Loss & Quantum | Loss Adjuster, Expert Provider | Claims Assessment (assessor) | Claims Management Platform, Document & Image Management |
| **V22.06** Investigate Where Warranted | Third Party | Investigation (investigator), Fraud (fraud analyst) | Fraud Detection Platform |
| **V22.07** Approve or Decline | — | Claims Assessment (assessor), Claims Management (delegated approver) | Claims Management Platform |
| **V22.08** Arrange Repair, Service or Payment | Claimant, Repairer | Supply Chain (repairer coordinator), Finance (payments officer) | Supplier Network System, Payments System |
| **V22.09** Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance | Third-Party Insurer, Reinsurer | Recoveries (recoveries officer) | Recoveries & Reinsurance System |
| **V22.10** Close Claim & Release Reserve | — | Claims Assessment (claims consultant), Actuarial (reserving analyst) | Claims Management Platform, Reserving System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V22):

- **External actors:** Claimant (V22.01, V22.03, V22.08); Loss Adjuster (V22.05); Expert Provider (V22.05); Third Party (V22.06); Repairer (V22.08); Third-Party Insurer (V22.09); Reinsurer (V22.09).
- **Teams:** Claims Intake (V22.01, V22.02); Actuarial (V22.02, V22.10); Claims Assessment (V22.03–V22.05, V22.07, V22.10); Investigation (V22.06); Fraud (V22.06); Claims Management (V22.07); Supply Chain (V22.08); Finance (V22.08); Recoveries (V22.09).
- **IT systems:** Claims Management Platform (V22.01, V22.02, V22.04, V22.05, V22.07, V22.10); Customer Portal (V22.01); Reserving System (V22.02, V22.10); Policy Administration System (V22.03); Document & Image Management (V22.05); Fraud Detection Platform (V22.06); Supplier Network System (V22.08); Payments System (V22.08); Recoveries & Reinsurance System (V22.09).

```text
  irregularity indicators are present.

  delegated authority.
- Repair, Service and Payment Arrangement Service: arranges repair,
  alternative service or direct payment settlement to the Claimant.
- Recoveries and Reinsurance Pursuit Service: pursues subrogation,
  third-party recoveries and reinsurance recoveries.
- Claim Closure and Reserve Release Service: closes the claim file and
  releases or adjusts the outstanding reserve.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve: finalises the claim file, updates
```

### V22.01 — Receive Notification

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.01 Receive Notification — first subprocess in the Claim to
Settlement value chain, where an incoming loss notification from the Claimant
is captured, acknowledged, and passed to claim registration.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Claimant" — the policyholder, member, patient or beneficiary who
notifies the loss and receives acknowledgement.
Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the process; contains the Claims
Intake team with the claims consultant.
  Lane "Claims Intake (Claims Consultant)" — receives and logs the
  notification, captures incident details, requests any missing information,
  and sends acknowledgement.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — core claims system; records the new
notification and issues a claim reference.
Pool "Customer Portal" — digital channel through which the Claimant may
submit notification and supporting evidence, and through which acknowledgement
is returned.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Claimant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Customer Portal" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Claimant
2. Insurer
3. Customer Portal
4. Claims Management Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) lane:
  Message start event "Loss notification received from Claimant"
  User task "Capture notification channel and incident details"
  Exclusive gateway "Notification complete?"
  - branch "Details sufficient": continue to next task
  - branch "Details missing":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Notification Complete"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
        Send task "Request missing information from Claimant",
        Intermediate message catch event "Claimant responds with
        missing details",
        User task "Review and record additional details"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Notification Complete"
  Service task "Log notification in Claims Management Platform"
  Service task "Generate claim reference via Claims Management Platform"
  User task "Perform initial completeness and routing check"
  Send task "Send acknowledgement to Claimant"
  End event "Notification acknowledged — ready for Register Claim
  and Set Reserve"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Notification Complete" — label "Response deadline exceeded (5 business
days)"; on trigger, flow moves to Send task "Send notification-lapse
advisory to Claimant" and then to End event "Notification lapsed —
no further action".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work moves top to bottom through the single Claims Intake
lane. After "Notification complete?" the "Details sufficient" branch
proceeds directly to "Log notification"; the "Details missing" branch
enters the loop subprocess and rejoins at the Exclusive merge gateway
"Notification Complete" before continuing. The timer boundary event on
the subprocess leads to a terminal send task and a separate end event,
not rejoining the main flow.

Message flows:
Claimant → Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) — loss notification,
  incident details and any supporting evidence submitted at first contact.
Customer Portal → Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) — digitally submitted
  notification form and attachments.
Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Customer Portal — acknowledgement
  and claim reference returned to Claimant via portal.
Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Claims Management Platform — new
  notification record written; claim reference retrieved.
Claims Management Platform → Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) — generated
  claim reference number returned.
Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Claimant — acknowledgement letter or
  message with claim reference and next-steps information.

7. Data objects

Data Object "Loss Notification" — written by User task "Capture
  notification channel and incident details"; read by User task "Perform
  initial completeness and routing check".
Data Object "Claim Reference" — written by Service task "Generate claim
  reference via Claims Management Platform"; read by Send task "Send
  acknowledgement to Claimant".
Data Object "Acknowledgement" — written by Send task "Send acknowledgement
  to Claimant"; read by Claimant (external pool, via message flow).
Data Object "Additional Detail Submission" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Claimant responds with missing details"; read by
  User task "Review and record additional details".

V22.01 Receive Notification captures the first contact from the Claimant,
records the channel and incident particulars, iterates to collect any
missing information within the allowed response window, and generates a
claim reference through the Claims Management Platform. Successful completion
hands a complete, acknowledged notification record to V22.02 Register Claim
and Set Reserve, where the formal claim entry and initial reserve will be
established.
```


### V22.02 — Register Claim & Set Reserve

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve — second subprocess in the
Claim to Settlement value chain, receiving a lodged notification from
Receive Notification and handing a registered claim with initial reserve
to Validate Cover & Eligibility.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the claim registration and
reserving process, containing all active work lanes.
  Lane "Claims Intake (Claims Consultant)" — receives the notification,
  creates the claim record, and captures all incident and claimant details.
  Lane "Actuarial / Reserving (Reserving Analyst)" — calculates and sets
  the initial reserve and records it in the reserving system.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — enterprise claims management system
that stores and updates claim records.
Pool "Reserving System" — actuarial reserving system that holds reserve
entries and reserve history.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Reserving System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

Pool "Insurer" — top (process owner, holds the flow).
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — below Insurer.
Pool "Reserving System" — below Claims Management Platform.

  Notification"
  User task "Review notification and confirm completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Notification details sufficient?"
  - branch "No — details missing": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
    Details Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
    "Identify missing information", Send task "Request missing details
    from claimant record", Intermediate message catch event "Updated
    details received"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Repeat Until Details Complete"
  - branch "Yes — details sufficient": continue to next task
  Exclusive merge gateway "Notification details sufficient?"
  Service task "Create claim record in Claims Management Platform"
  User task "Capture incident details, claimant identity, and loss
  description"
  Service task "Assign unique claim reference number"
  Send task "Send acknowledgement and claim reference to claimant record"
  End event "Claim record created — pass to Actuarial / Reserving"

Actuarial / Reserving (Reserving Analyst) lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Claim record created received from
  Claims Intake"
  User task "Review claim type, peril, and initial loss information"
  User task "Calculate initial reserve estimate"
  Exclusive gateway "Reserve within standard delegated authority?"
  - branch "Yes — within authority": continue to record reserve
  - branch "No — exceeds authority": User task "Escalate reserve
    estimate for senior approval", Intermediate message catch event
    "Senior approval received"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Reserve within standard delegated authority?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reserve within standard delegated authority?"
  Service task "Record initial reserve in Reserving System"
  Service task "Update claim record with reserve in Claims Management
  Platform"
  User task "Document reserving basis and assumptions"
  End event "Reserve set and recorded — ready for Validate Cover &
  Eligibility"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Details Complete" — label "Notification chase period expired (5 days)"
— on expiry: End event "Notification incomplete — claim held pending
further contact".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Within the Claims Intake lane, flow runs from the
message start event through the completeness check gateway; the "No"
branch enters the loop subprocess and rejoins the exclusive merge
gateway before continuing to claim creation tasks; the "Yes" branch
bypasses the loop and joins at the same merge. Flow continues through
claim creation, detail capture, reference assignment, and acknowledgement
to the lane end event. In the Actuarial / Reserving lane, flow runs from
the intermediate message catch event through review and calculation, then
to the authority gateway; the "No — exceeds authority" branch escalates
and awaits approval before rejoining the merge gateway; the "Yes" branch
joins directly. Flow continues through reserve recording, claim record
update, and documentation to the final end event.

Message flows:
Claims Management Platform → Claims Intake (Claims Consultant)
  (claim record confirmation and claim reference number)
Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Claims Management Platform
  (new claim record with incident details and claim reference)
Actuarial / Reserving (Reserving Analyst) → Reserving System
  (initial reserve entry with reserving basis)
Reserving System → Actuarial / Reserving (Reserving Analyst)
  (reserve booking confirmation)
Actuarial / Reserving (Reserving Analyst) → Claims Management Platform
  (reserve amount update against claim record)
Claims Management Platform → Actuarial / Reserving (Reserving Analyst)
  (updated claim record confirmation)

Management Platform"; read by "Capture incident details, claimant
identity, and loss description"; read by "Review claim type, peril, and
initial loss information".
Data Object "Claim Reference Number" — written by "Assign unique claim
reference number"; read by "Send acknowledgement and claim reference to
claimant record".
Data Object "Initial Reserve Estimate" — written by "Calculate initial
reserve estimate"; read by "Record initial reserve in Reserving System".
Data Object "Reserving Basis and Assumptions" — written by "Document
reserving basis and assumptions".
claim record with reserve in Claims Management Platform".
reserve in Reserving System".

V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve takes the lodged notification
produced by Receive Notification and transforms it into a formal claim
record complete with a unique reference and a financially approved
initial reserve. Claims Intake captures and validates the incident
details, while the Actuarial / Reserving team calculates and books the
reserve against both the Claims Management Platform and the Reserving
System. The output — a registered claim with a confirmed reserve — is
handed to Validate Cover & Eligibility so that policy terms and
claimant eligibility can be assessed against the recorded event.
```

```text
    - branch "No — policy not found or lapsed": End event "Cover invalid —
        claim declined at eligibility; process ends"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Policy found and active"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Policy found and active"
  User task "Check incident date against policy period"
  Exclusive gateway "Incident within policy period?"
    - branch "No — outside period": End event "Cover invalid —
        incident outside policy period; process ends"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Incident within policy period"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Incident within policy period"

    - branch "No — excluded peril": End event "Cover invalid —
        peril excluded; process ends"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Peril covered"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Peril covered"
  User task "Verify claimant eligibility and insured status"
  Exclusive gateway "Additional evidence required from claimant?"
    - branch "Yes": Send task "Request supporting evidence or declaration"
        Intermediate message catch event "Evidence or declaration received"
        Exclusive merge gateway "Additional evidence required"
    - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Additional evidence required"

        End event "Cover declined — claimant notified; process ends"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Cover confirmed"

  User task "Record cover decision on claim record"

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request supporting evidence or

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all tasks and gateways flow top to bottom within the Claims
Assessment lane. The "Policy found and active?" gateway branches to an
immediate end for the negative branch and merges back to the main flow for
the positive branch. The "Incident within policy period?" and "Peril
covered?" gateways follow the same pattern. The "Additional evidence
required from claimant?" gateway sends a message to the Claimant pool on
the "Yes" branch, waits at an intermediate message catch event for the
reply, then merges with the "No" branch before continuing to the exclusions
check. The "Cover confirmed?" gateway routes negative cases to declination
tasks and a terminal end event; the positive branch merges and continues to
the record task and final end event.

V22.03 validates that the registered claim falls within an active policy,
that the incident occurred within the policy period, that the peril is
covered, and that no exclusion or condition voids cover. Where additional
evidence is needed, the claimant is contacted and given a five-day window
before a default declination is issued. A confirmed cover decision — or a
documented declination — is recorded on the claim and handed to Triage &
Assign as the basis for workload routing and priority setting.
```

```text
& Eligibility and routes it to the right handler at the right
```

```text
    End event "Decision with dispute flag noted — ready for Arrange
      Repair, Service or Payment or external dispute resolution"
  - branch "No — no flag": Exclusive merge gateway "Complaint or dispute
      flag raised?"
  End event "Decision confirmed — ready for Arrange Repair, Service or
    Payment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Conduct authority review and
  confirm or override recommendation" — label "Authority review deadline
  exceeded" — triggers an escalation task "Escalate to senior claims
  management" in the Claims Management lane, ending in a terminate end
  event "Escalation raised — approval stalled".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Claims Assessment lane, flow moves from the
start event through review and the first gateway; the within-authority
branch leads directly to the merge; the exceeds-authority branch passes
through preparation of the referral and then waits for the return from
Claims Management before rejoining the merge. Flow then continues through
cover-terms application, the approve/decline gateway and its merge, the
platform update service task, the decision communication draft, and the
dispute-flag gateway, whose no-flag branch merges and proceeds to the
standard end event while the flag branch reaches its own end event.

Message flows:
  Claims Assessment lane (assessor) → Claims Management Platform
    (Service task "Record decision recommendation in Claims Management
    Platform") — decision recommendation and quantum data.
  Claims Assessment lane (assessor) → Claims Management Platform
    (Service task "Update claim decision status in Claims Management
    Platform") — confirmed approve or decline decision and rationale.
  Claims Management Platform → Claims Assessment lane — updated claim
    record and decision status confirmation.
  Claims Assessment lane (Claims Management lane, delegated approver) →
    Claims Management Platform — authority review outcome and approver
    sign-off record.

7. Data objects

Data Object "Assessment Findings and Quantum" — read by "Review
  assessment findings and quantum".
Data Object "Referral Package" — written by "Prepare referral package
  for delegated approver"; read by "Receive referral and review delegated
  authority limits".
Data Object "Decision Rationale" — written by "Document approval
  rationale and settlement quantum" and "Document decline rationale and
  policy basis"; read by "Update claim decision status in Claims Management
  Platform" and "Draft decision communication to claimant".
Data Object "Decision Communication" — written by "Draft decision
  communication to claimant"; read by "Record dispute flag and note
  complaints rights on decision communication".

V22.07 Approve or Decline takes the assessed loss and quantum from V22.05
and applies delegated authority rules to reach a binding approve or decline
decision, escalating to senior Claims Management when quantum exceeds the
assessor's authority. It records the rationale and cover basis for the
decision, flags any dispute indicators, and hands a confirmed decision
record to V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment so that settlement,
repair, or formal decline can proceed.
```


### V22.08 — Arrange Repair, Service or Payment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment — the subprocess that
converts an approved claim decision into fulfilled repair, service, or
cash settlement within the Claim to Settlement value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the insurance organisation arranging fulfilment of the
  approved claim.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Supply Chain (repairer coordinator)
  - Finance (payments officer)
Pool "Claimant" — the policyholder or beneficiary receiving the repair
  outcome, service, or payment.
Pool "Repairer" — the panel repairer or supplier completing the repair or
  delivering the service.
Pool "Supplier Network System" — IT system managing supplier and repairer
  panel, work orders, and pricing.
Pool "Payments System" — IT system processing and disbursing claim payments.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claimant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Repairer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier Network System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Payments System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Claimant
2. Insurer
3. Repairer
4. Supplier Network System
5. Payments System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Supply Chain lane:
  Message start event "Approved claim decision received from Approve or
    Decline"
  Exclusive gateway "Fulfilment type?"
  - branch "Repair or service required":
      Service task "Check repairer availability and pricing in panel"
      Send task "Issue work order to repairer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Repair completion confirmation
        received from repairer"
      User task "Review repair completion and quality"
      Exclusive gateway "Repair accepted?"
      - branch "Yes — accepted":
          User task "Authorise repairer invoice"
      - branch "No — rework required":
          Send task "Notify repairer of rework requirement"
          Intermediate message catch event "Rework completion confirmation
            received from repairer"
          User task "Authorise repairer invoice"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Repair accepted"
      User task "Notify claimant of repair completion"
      End event "Repair fulfilment complete — ready for Close Claim and
        Release Reserve"
  - branch "Cash settlement or direct payment":
      User task "Confirm bank details and settlement amount with claimant"
      Intermediate message catch event "Bank details and declaration
        received from claimant"
      User task "Prepare payment instruction"
      (continues in Finance lane)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment type"

Finance lane:
  (receives payment instruction from Supply Chain lane)
  Service task "Submit payment instruction to Payments System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Payment confirmation received from
    Payments System"
  User task "Issue payment advice to claimant"
  End event "Payment fulfilment complete — ready for Close Claim and
    Release Reserve"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Issue work order to repairer" —
  label "Repairer acceptance deadline exceeded" — triggers Send task
  "Reassign work order to alternative repairer" in Supply Chain lane,
  rejoining before Intermediate message catch event "Repair completion
  confirmation received from repairer".
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit payment instruction to
  Payments System" — label "Payment processing timeout" — triggers User
  task "Escalate payment failure to Finance team" in Finance lane, ending
  at an Error end event "Payment processing failed".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within Supply Chain lane, flow runs from the message start
event into the Fulfilment type gateway; the repair branch proceeds through
panel check, work order, confirmation, review, the Repair accepted gateway
(rework branch loops to rework confirmation then rejoins), invoice
authorisation, claimant notification, and ends; the payment branch runs
through bank detail confirmation, declaration catch event, and payment
instruction preparation before passing to Finance lane; Finance lane
receives the payment instruction, submits to the Payments System, catches
confirmation, issues advice, and ends. All diverging gateways are matched
by their named merge gateways.

Message flows:
  Insurer (Send task "Issue work order to repairer") → Repairer (work
    order instruction)
  Repairer → Insurer Supply Chain lane (repair completion confirmation)
  Insurer (Send task "Notify repairer of rework requirement") → Repairer
    (rework instruction)
  Repairer → Insurer Supply Chain lane (rework completion confirmation)
  Insurer (User task "Notify claimant of repair completion") → Claimant
    (repair completion notice)
  Insurer (User task "Confirm bank details and settlement amount with
    claimant") → Claimant (settlement confirmation request)
  Claimant → Insurer Supply Chain lane (bank details and declaration)
  Insurer (Service task "Submit payment instruction to Payments System")
    → Payments System (payment instruction)
  Payments System → Insurer Finance lane (payment confirmation)
  Insurer (User task "Issue payment advice to claimant") → Claimant
    (payment advice)
  Insurer (Service task "Check repairer availability and pricing in
    panel") → Supplier Network System (availability and pricing query)
  Supplier Network System → Insurer Supply Chain lane (pricing and
    panel data)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Claim Decision" — read by Supply Chain lane
  (Message start event "Approved claim decision received from Approve or
  Decline").
Data Object "Work Order" — written by User task "Issue work order to
  repairer"; read by User task "Review repair completion and quality".
Data Object "Repairer Invoice" — read by User task "Authorise repairer
  invoice".
Data Object "Payment Instruction" — written by User task "Prepare payment
  instruction"; read by Service task "Submit payment instruction to
  Payments System".
Data Object "Payment Advice" — written by User task "Issue payment advice
  to claimant".
Data Object "Bank Details and Declaration" — read by User task "Prepare
  payment instruction"; written by Intermediate message catch event "Bank
  details and declaration received from claimant".

V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment takes an approved claim
decision and fulfils it either by commissioning a panel repairer to
complete work and confirming quality, or by processing a direct cash
settlement through the payments system and advising the claimant.
It coordinates Supply Chain and Finance teams with the Supplier Network
and Payments systems, and hands a fully fulfilled claim record to
V22.10 Close Claim and Release Reserve.
```


### V22.09 — Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance — the subprocess within the
Claim to Settlement value chain in which the Recoveries team identifies and
pursues subrogation and contribution claims against third-party insurers, and
lodges reinsurance recoveries, following an approved claim decision.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the recoveries and reinsurance
process, containing the Recoveries lane.
Pool "Third-Party Insurer" — external insurer against whom a recovery or
contribution claim is pursued.
Pool "Reinsurer" — external reinsurer to whom reinsurance recovery claims
are submitted.
Pool "Recoveries & Reinsurance System" — IT system managing recovery and
reinsurance claim records and correspondence.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Third-Party Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Reinsurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Recoveries & Reinsurance System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Third-Party Insurer
2. Insurer (white-box)
3. Reinsurer
4. Recoveries & Reinsurance System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Recoveries lane:
  Message start event "Approved claim decision received from Approve
    or Decline"
  User task "Review claim for recovery and reinsurance potential"
  Exclusive gateway "Recovery or reinsurance potential identified?"
  - branch "No recovery or reinsurance applicable":
      End event "No recovery pursued — ready for Close Claim &
        Release Reserve"
  - branch "Recovery potential identified":
      Exclusive gateway "Recovery type?"
      - branch "Third-party / subrogation recovery":
          User task "Prepare subrogation or contribution claim"
          Send task "Lodge recovery claim with third-party insurer"
          Intermediate message catch event "Response received from
            third-party insurer"
          Exclusive gateway "Third-party recovery agreed?"
          - branch "Agreed":
              User task "Record agreed recovery amount"
          - branch "Disputed":
              Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Recovery Resolved"
                (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
                "Escalate or negotiate recovery position", Send task
                "Send updated recovery correspondence to third-party
                insurer", Intermediate message catch event "Updated
                response received from third-party insurer", Exclusive
                gateway "Recovery resolved?"
              Exclusive merge gateway "Recovery resolved"
              User task "Record final recovery outcome"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Third-party recovery agreed"
          Service task "Update recovery record in Recoveries &
            Reinsurance System"
      - branch "Reinsurance recovery":
          User task "Prepare reinsurance recovery claim and bordereaux"
          Send task "Submit reinsurance recovery claim to reinsurer"
          Intermediate message catch event "Reinsurance recovery
            response received"
          Exclusive gateway "Reinsurance recovery accepted?"
          - branch "Accepted":
              User task "Record reinsurance recovery amount"
          - branch "Queried or rejected":
              Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Reinsurance Recovery
                Resolved" (standard loop) containing, in order: User
                task "Respond to reinsurer query or dispute", Send task
                "Send supplementary information to reinsurer",
                Intermediate message catch event "Updated reinsurance
                response received", Exclusive gateway "Reinsurance
                recovery resolved?"
              Exclusive merge gateway "Reinsurance recovery resolved"
              User task "Record final reinsurance recovery outcome"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Reinsurance recovery accepted"
          Service task "Update reinsurance record in Recoveries &
            Reinsurance System"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Recovery type"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Recovery or reinsurance potential identified"
  User task "Reconcile total recoveries against claim payments"
  Service task "Post recovery receipts to Recoveries & Reinsurance
    System"
  End event "Recoveries and reinsurance concluded — ready for Close
    Claim & Release Reserve"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Recovery Resolved" — label "Third-party negotiation deadline exceeded"
— flow to End event "Recovery time-limit escalation — refer to legal
or management".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Reinsurance Recovery Resolved" — label "Reinsurance response deadline
exceeded" — flow to End event "Reinsurance recovery escalation —
refer to senior recoveries officer".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Recoveries lane carries all flow. After the
opening gateway, the "No recovery" branch ends immediately; the
"Recovery potential identified" branch enters the "Recovery type"
gateway whose two branches — "Third-party / subrogation recovery" and
"Reinsurance recovery" — execute their respective loops and system
updates before rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway "Recovery type",
then continuing to reconciliation and the closing system task before
the end event. All loop branches rejoin their named merge gateways
before continuing.

Message flows:
Send task "Lodge recovery claim with third-party insurer" →
  Third-Party Insurer (subrogation or contribution claim)
Third-Party Insurer → Intermediate message catch event "Response
  received from third-party insurer" (recovery response)
Send task "Send updated recovery correspondence to third-party
  insurer" → Third-Party Insurer (updated recovery position)
Third-Party Insurer → Intermediate message catch event "Updated
  response received from third-party insurer" (updated response)
Send task "Submit reinsurance recovery claim to reinsurer" →
  Reinsurer (reinsurance recovery claim and bordereaux)
Reinsurer → Intermediate message catch event "Reinsurance recovery
  response received" (reinsurance recovery acceptance or query)
Send task "Send supplementary information to reinsurer" →
  Reinsurer (supplementary evidence or query response)
Reinsurer → Intermediate message catch event "Updated reinsurance
  response received" (updated reinsurance decision)
Service task "Update recovery record in Recoveries & Reinsurance
  System" → Recoveries & Reinsurance System (third-party recovery
  record update)
Service task "Update reinsurance record in Recoveries & Reinsurance
  System" → Recoveries & Reinsurance System (reinsurance recovery
  record update)
Service task "Post recovery receipts to Recoveries & Reinsurance
  System" → Recoveries & Reinsurance System (reconciled recovery
  receipts)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Claim Decision" — read by User task "Review
  claim for recovery and reinsurance potential".
Data Object "Subrogation or Contribution Claim" — written by User task
  "Prepare subrogation or contribution claim"; read by Send task "Lodge
  recovery claim with third-party insurer".
Data Object "Reinsurance Recovery Claim and Bordereaux" — written by
  User task "Prepare reinsurance recovery claim and bordereaux"; read
  by Send task "Submit reinsurance recovery claim to reinsurer".
Data Object "Third-Party Recovery Response" — read by Exclusive
  gateway "Third-party recovery agreed?".
Data Object "Reinsurance Recovery Response" — read by Exclusive
  gateway "Reinsurance recovery accepted?".

V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance identifies, prepares, and negotiates
all third-party subrogation and reinsurance recovery claims that arise from
an approved settlement, cycling through structured negotiation loops until
each recovery is resolved within its deadline or escalated. On completion, the
reconciled recovery amounts are posted to the Recoveries & Reinsurance System
and the subprocess hands a fully reconciled recoveries position to V22.10
Close Claim & Release Reserve.
```

### V22.10 — Close Claim & Release Reserve

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve — final subprocess of the
Claim to Settlement value chain, closing the claim record and releasing
the reserve once settlement obligations are met.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the close-claim process, with
lanes for Claims Assessment and Actuarial.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — enterprise claims management system.
Pool "Reserving System" — system holding claim reserves and actuarial
data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Reserving System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Insurer (white-box)
2. Claims Management Platform
3. Reserving System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Assessment lane (claims consultant):
  Message start event "Settlement confirmed — ready for Close Claim and
    Release Reserve"
  User task "Review claim for closure readiness"
  Exclusive gateway "All obligations met?"
    - branch "No — outstanding items": Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Until
        Closure Ready" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
        "Identify outstanding obligation", User task "Action outstanding
        item", Intermediate message catch event "Confirmation of
        resolution received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Resolve Until Closure Ready"
    - branch "Yes": continue to next task
  User task "Confirm settlement and recovery positions are finalised"
  User task "Prepare closure documentation and summary"
  Service task "Update claim status to Closed in Claims Management
    Platform"
  Send task "Send closure notification and payment advice to claimant"

Actuarial lane (reserving analyst):
  Intermediate message catch event "Claim closed notification received"
  User task "Review reserve adequacy against final settlement amount"
  Exclusive gateway "Reserve adjustment required?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Calculate reserve release or adjustment"
      Service task "Submit reserve release to Reserving System"
      Intermediate message catch event "Reserve release confirmed"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Reserve adjustment required"
    - branch "No": continue to merge
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reserve adjustment required"
  User task "Record final incurred loss and close reserve"
  Service task "Trigger claims ratio and leakage reporting"
  End event "Claim closed and reserve released — claim lifecycle
    complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Until
Closure Ready", label "Resolution overdue — 10 business days", leading
to User task "Escalate unresolved closure item to team leader" followed
by End event "Closure escalated — awaiting resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Claims Assessment lane with the
message start event, progresses through the readiness check gateway
whose "No" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and rejoins at
the merge gateway, and whose "Yes" branch bypasses it; both branches
converge before confirmation, documentation and status tasks, then the
send task completes the Claims Assessment lane and a message triggers
the Actuarial lane; the Actuarial lane runs through the reserve review,
the adjustment gateway whose "Yes" branch covers calculation, system
submission, and confirmation before rejoining at the merge gateway and
the "No" branch bypasses it; both branches meet at the merge before the
final incurred loss task, reporting task and end event.

Message flows:
Claims Management Platform → Insurer Claims Assessment lane (claim
  record, settlement and recovery position data)
Insurer Claims Assessment lane → Claims Management Platform (claim
  status closed update)
Insurer Claims Assessment lane → Claimant (implied external recipient
  of closure notification and payment advice — carried as send task
  output; no external pool modelled for this subprocess per matrix)
Claims Management Platform → Insurer Actuarial lane (claim closed
  notification)
Insurer Actuarial lane → Reserving System (reserve release instruction)
Reserving System → Insurer Actuarial lane (reserve release confirmation)
Insurer Actuarial lane → Claims Management Platform (final incurred
  loss and reporting trigger)
Claims Management Platform → Insurer Actuarial lane (claims ratio and
  leakage report data)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Closure Readiness Checklist" — written by "Review claim
  for closure readiness"; read by "Confirm settlement and recovery
  positions are finalised".
Data Object "Closure Documentation and Summary" — written by "Prepare
  closure documentation and summary"; read by "Update claim status to
  Closed in Claims Management Platform".
Data Object "Reserve Release Instruction" — written by "Calculate
  reserve release or adjustment"; read by "Submit reserve release to
  Reserving System".
Data Object "Final Incurred Loss Record" — written by "Record final
  incurred loss and close reserve"; read by "Trigger claims ratio and
  leakage reporting".

V22.10 closes out the claim lifecycle by confirming all settlement and
recovery obligations are met, updating the claim status to closed in the
Claims Management Platform, and releasing or adjusting the reserve in the
Reserving System. It produces a final incurred loss record and triggers
claims ratio and leakage reporting, giving Actuarial and management a
complete view of the claim. With the reserve released and the record
closed, the value chain is fully complete.
```


## V23 — Meter to Cash

**Teams and roles involved.**
Meter to Cash usually involves Metering and Field Operations, Meter Data Management, Billing, Revenue Assurance, Customer Service, Credit and Collections, and Finance. Key roles include meter reader or field technician, meter data analyst, billing officer, revenue assurance analyst, customer service agent, credit officer, collections officer, and hardship or concessions officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Consumer or Account Holder whose consumption is measured. The process is initiated on a billing cycle, or by a meter event such as a new connection, an exchange or a suspected fault. Other external parties include metering service providers, network or distribution operators, payment providers, regulators setting tariffs and hardship obligations, and debt collection agencies.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: acquire meter readings, validate and estimate missing or implausible data, apply tariffs and rate the consumption, generate and issue the bill, handle billing enquiries and disputes, receive and allocate payments, manage arrears and hardship arrangements, pursue collections, manage disconnection and reconnection, and perform revenue assurance and leakage analysis.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include meter data management and head-end systems for smart meters, field workforce management, the billing engine and rating tables, customer information and CRM, payment and direct-debit processing, collections and dispute management, general ledger, and revenue assurance analytics.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include metering and reading standards, validation/estimation/editing rules for missing data, tariff and pricing approval, billing accuracy and timeliness obligations, dispute and adjustment authority, hardship and payment-plan policy, disconnection rules and protected-customer exclusions, and regulatory reporting requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The consumer provides meter access, self-reads where applicable, account and contact changes, payments, disputes and hardship applications. The process provides bills and statements, consumption and tariff information, estimated-read notices, reminders and arrears notices, payment plans, and disconnection or reconnection notifications. Network operators and metering providers exchange readings, service orders and outage data.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates meter reads and estimates, rated consumption, invoices and adjustments, payments and allocations, arrears and payment plans, service orders, and general-ledger postings. IT systems provide meter registers and interval data, tariff and calendar rules, account and contact data, payment confirmations, ageing and collections status, and unbilled-revenue and leakage reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Utility" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V23.01** Acquire Meter Readings | Consumer, Metering Service Provider | Metering & Field Operations (field technician) | Meter Data Management System |
| **V23.02** Validate & Estimate Data | — | Meter Data Management (meter data analyst) | Meter Data Management System |
| **V23.03** Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption | — | Billing (billing officer) | Billing Engine |
| **V23.04** Generate & Issue Bill | Consumer | Billing (billing officer) | Billing Engine, Customer Information System |
| **V23.05** Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes | Consumer | Customer Service (customer service agent) | Customer Information System, Dispute Management System |
| **V23.06** Receive & Allocate Payment | Consumer, Payment Provider | Finance (finance officer) | Payment Processing System, General Ledger |
| **V23.07** Manage Arrears & Hardship | Consumer | Credit & Collections (hardship officer) | Collections System |
| **V23.08** Pursue Collections | Consumer, Debt Collection Agency | Credit & Collections (collections officer) | Collections System |
| **V23.09** Manage Disconnection & Reconnection | Consumer, Network Operator | Metering & Field Operations (field technician), Credit & Collections (credit officer) | Field Workforce Management, Customer Information System |
| **V23.10** Perform Revenue Assurance | Regulator | Revenue Assurance (revenue assurance analyst) | Revenue Assurance Analytics |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V23):

- **External actors:** Consumer (V23.01, V23.04–V23.09); Metering Service Provider (V23.01); Payment Provider (V23.06); Debt Collection Agency (V23.08); Network Operator (V23.09); Regulator (V23.10).
- **Teams:** Metering & Field Operations (V23.01, V23.09); Meter Data Management (V23.02); Billing (V23.03, V23.04); Customer Service (V23.05); Finance (V23.06); Credit & Collections (V23.07–V23.09); Revenue Assurance (V23.10).
- **IT systems:** Meter Data Management System (V23.01, V23.02); Billing Engine (V23.03, V23.04); Customer Information System (V23.04, V23.05, V23.09); Dispute Management System (V23.05); Payment Processing System (V23.06); General Ledger (V23.06); Collections System (V23.07, V23.08); Field Workforce Management (V23.09); Revenue Assurance Analytics (V23.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V23 — Meter to Cash — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Meter to Cash value chain, from initial meter reading through to
revenue assurance. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands, read
top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) shows what the chain delivers
to its participants; BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) shows the ten
subprocesses in chain order; APPLICATIONS (bottom band) shows the IT
systems that support them. The Consumer sits on the far left as the
primary demand-side actor; delivery and settlement actors — Metering
Service Provider, Payment Provider, Debt Collection Agency, Network
Operator, and Regulator — sit on the far right. The diagram reads
top-to-bottom as service realisation in ArchiMate terms: Business Service
→ Business Process → Application Component.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Consumer: demand-side actor, placed on the far left; participates in
  reading acquisition, bill receipt, enquiries, payments, arrears,
  collections, and disconnection.
- Metering Service Provider: delivery-side actor, far right; participates
  in meter reading acquisition.
- Payment Provider: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in
  payment receipt and allocation.
- Debt Collection Agency: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in
  collections pursuit.
- Network Operator: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in
  disconnection and reconnection.
- Regulator: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in revenue
  assurance and regulatory reporting.

2. Interfaces

- Meter Access Interface: used by Consumer and Metering Service Provider;
  serves the Meter Reading Acquisition Service.
- Billing & Statement Interface: used by Consumer; serves the Bill
  Generation & Issue Service and the Enquiry & Dispute Service.
- Payment Interface: used by Consumer and Payment Provider; serves the
  Payment Receipt & Allocation Service.
- Collections Interface: used by Debt Collection Agency; serves the
  Collections Pursuit Service.
- Field Order Interface: used by Network Operator; serves the
  Disconnection & Reconnection Service.
- Regulatory Reporting Interface: used by Regulator; serves the Revenue
  Assurance Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Meter Reading Acquisition Service: provides validated interval and
  register reads from meters to initiate billing.
- Data Validation & Estimation Service: provides complete, plausible
  consumption data by correcting or estimating missing reads.
- Tariff Rating Service: provides rated consumption figures by applying
  approved tariffs and pricing rules to metered usage.
- Bill Generation & Issue Service: provides accurate, timely bills and
  statements to the consumer.
- Enquiry & Dispute Service: provides resolution of billing questions,
  disputes and adjustments for the consumer.
- Payment Receipt & Allocation Service: provides receipt, matching and
  allocation of payments against account balances.
- Arrears & Hardship Service: provides payment plans and hardship
  arrangements for consumers in financial difficulty.
- Collections Pursuit Service: provides structured debt recovery action
  for overdue accounts.
- Disconnection & Reconnection Service: provides managed interruption and
  restoration of supply in line with policy rules.
- Revenue Assurance Service: provides leakage detection, unbilled-revenue
  identification and regulatory reporting.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings: collects meter data from smart head-end
  systems, metering service providers and field technicians.
- V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data: applies validation, estimation and
  editing rules to identify and correct implausible or missing reads.
- V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption: rates validated consumption
  against tariff and calendar rules to produce chargeable amounts.
- V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill: assembles rated charges, produces
  invoices and delivers bills to consumers by preferred channel.
- V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes: receives, investigates and
  resolves consumer queries, disputes and billing adjustments.
- V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment: processes incoming payments via all
  channels, matches them to accounts and posts to the ledger.
- V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship: identifies overdue accounts, offers
  payment plans and applies hardship concessions as required.
- V23.08 Pursue Collections: escalates unresolved arrears through
  internal and external collection action.
- V23.09 Manage Disconnection & Reconnection: issues field service orders
  for supply interruption and restoration per policy and exclusions.
- V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance: analyses unbilled usage, detects
  leakage, and produces regulatory and management reports.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Meter Data Management System: manages meter registers, interval data,
  head-end connectivity and estimation outputs.
- Billing Engine: holds rating tables, tariff rules and produces invoices
  and billing adjustments.
- Customer Information System: holds account, contact and service-point
  data; used across billing, disputes and field operations.
- Dispute Management System: records, tracks and resolves billing
  enquiries and formal disputes.
- Payment Processing System: processes payments, direct debits and
  payment-channel confirmations.
- General Ledger: receives and stores financial postings for payments,
  adjustments and write-offs.
- Collections System: manages arrears staging, payment plans, hardship
  arrangements and collection workflows.
- Field Workforce Management: schedules and dispatches field technicians
  for service orders including disconnection and reconnection.
- Revenue Assurance Analytics: analyses meter and billing data to
  identify unbilled revenue, leakage and regulatory exposures.

6. Relationships

SERVING (Application Component SERVES Business Process):
- Meter Data Management System serves V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings.
- Meter Data Management System serves V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data.
- Billing Engine serves V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption.
- Billing Engine serves V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill.
- Customer Information System serves V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill.
- Customer Information System serves V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries &
  Disputes.
- Customer Information System serves V23.09 Manage Disconnection &
  Reconnection.
- Dispute Management System serves V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries &
  Disputes.
- Payment Processing System serves V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment.
- General Ledger serves V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment.
- Collections System serves V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship.
- Collections System serves V23.08 Pursue Collections.
- Field Workforce Management serves V23.09 Manage Disconnection &
  Reconnection.
- Revenue Assurance Analytics serves V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance.

REALISATION (Business Process REALISES Business Service):
- V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings realises Meter Reading Acquisition
  Service.
- V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data realises Data Validation & Estimation
  Service.
- V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption realises Tariff Rating Service.
- V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill realises Bill Generation & Issue Service.
- V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes realises Enquiry & Dispute
  Service.
- V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment realises Payment Receipt &
  Allocation Service.
- V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship realises Arrears & Hardship Service.
- V23.08 Pursue Collections realises Collections Pursuit Service.
- V23.09 Manage Disconnection & Reconnection realises Disconnection &
  Reconnection Service.
- V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance realises Revenue Assurance Service.

ASSIGNMENT (Business Interface ASSIGNED TO Business Actor):
- Meter Access Interface assigned to Consumer.
- Meter Access Interface assigned to Metering Service Provider.
- Billing & Statement Interface assigned to Consumer.
- Payment Interface assigned to Consumer.
- Payment Interface assigned to Payment Provider.
- Collections Interface assigned to Debt Collection Agency.
- Field Order Interface assigned to Network Operator.
- Regulatory Reporting Interface assigned to Regulator.

ACCESS (Business Actor ACCESSES Business Service via Interface):
- Consumer accesses Meter Reading Acquisition Service via Meter Access
  Interface.
- Metering Service Provider accesses Meter Reading Acquisition Service
  via Meter Access Interface.
- Consumer accesses Bill Generation & Issue Service via Billing &
  Statement Interface.
- Consumer accesses Enquiry & Dispute Service via Billing & Statement
  Interface.
- Consumer accesses Payment Receipt & Allocation Service via Payment
  Interface.
- Payment Provider accesses Payment Receipt & Allocation Service via
  Payment Interface.
- Debt Collection Agency accesses Collections Pursuit Service via
  Collections Interface.
- Network Operator accesses Disconnection & Reconnection Service via
  Field Order Interface.
- Regulator accesses Revenue Assurance Service via Regulatory Reporting
  Interface.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V23 - Meter to Cash

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right. Place the chevrons in the order
listed below, one chevron per stage, with no branching or return arrows at
this level. Use the stage names exactly as given.

V23.01. Acquire Meter Readings

V23.03. Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption

V23.07. Manage Arrears & Hardship
V23.08. Pursue Collections
V23.09. Manage Disconnection & Reconnection
V23.10. Perform Revenue Assurance

This chain converts raw meter consumption data into recognised revenue for a
utility. It is triggered either by a scheduled billing cycle or by a meter
event such as a new connection, a meter exchange, or a suspected fault. The
main external participant is the Consumer or Account Holder, whose consumption
is measured at V23.01 and who receives a bill at V23.04, makes payment at
V23.06, and may enter hardship arrangements, face collections, or experience
disconnection and reconnection through V23.07 to V23.09. The chain closes with
V23.10, where Revenue Assurance confirms that all billable consumption has been
captured, leakage is identified, and regulatory reporting obligations are met.
```

### V23.01 — Acquire Meter Readings

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings — first subprocess of the Meter to
Cash value chain, triggered by a billing cycle or meter event and delivering
validated raw reads to Validate & Estimate Data.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the meter-to-cash process, with
lanes for Metering & Field Operations.
Pool "Consumer" — the account holder whose meter is being read.
Pool "Metering Service Provider" — external party that may supply reads
or carry out field visits on behalf of the utility.
Pool "Meter Data Management System" — head-end and meter data management
platform that collects, stores and returns meter register and interval data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Metering Service Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Meter Data Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility
3. Metering Service Provider
4. Meter Data Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Metering & Field Operations lane:
  Timer start event "Billing cycle or meter event triggers read acquisition"
  Exclusive gateway "Read source?"
  - branch "Smart meter — automated collection":
      Service task "Request interval data from head-end system"
      Intermediate message catch event "Interval data received from
        Meter Data Management System"
      User task "Review automated read completeness"
  - branch "Manual read — field visit required":
      User task "Schedule field technician visit"
      Send task "Dispatch read instruction to Metering Service Provider"
      Intermediate message catch event "Read result received from
        Metering Service Provider"
      User task "Record manual meter read"
  - branch "Consumer self-read":
      Send task "Send self-read request to Consumer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Self-read submitted by Consumer"
      User task "Record consumer self-read"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Read source"
  Exclusive gateway "Read obtained?"
  - branch "Yes — read received":
      Service task "Submit reads to Meter Data Management System"
      Intermediate message catch event "Submission acknowledgement
        received from Meter Data Management System"
      User task "Confirm read lodged in register"
  - branch "No — read not received":
      User task "Flag missing read and raise substitution request"
      End event "Missing read flagged — ready for Validate & Estimate Data"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Read obtained"
  End event "Reads acquired and lodged — ready for Validate & Estimate Data"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Schedule field technician visit"
  labelled "Visit overdue" — triggers User task "Escalate unscheduled
  visit to supervisor".
Interrupting timer boundary event on expanded subprocess implicit in
  "Send self-read request to Consumer" wait — labelled "Self-read
  deadline elapsed" — triggers User task "Flag missing consumer
  self-read and raise substitution request", leading to End event
  "Missing read flagged — ready for Validate & Estimate Data".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The single lane flows from the timer start event to the
Read source gateway; the three branches (smart meter, manual, consumer
self-read) each perform their respective tasks and message catches before
rejoining at the Exclusive merge gateway "Read source"; flow continues to
the Read obtained gateway, whose "Yes" branch submits to MDMS and
confirms lodgement before reaching the main end event, and whose "No"
branch flags the missing read and reaches its own end event.

Message flows:
Meter Data Management System → Utility / Metering & Field Operations
  (interval data returned in response to head-end request).
Utility / Metering & Field Operations → Meter Data Management System
  (read submission payload).
Meter Data Management System → Utility / Metering & Field Operations
  (submission acknowledgement).
Utility / Metering & Field Operations → Metering Service Provider
  (field read instruction / dispatch order).
Metering Service Provider → Utility / Metering & Field Operations
  (manual read result).
Utility / Metering & Field Operations → Consumer
  (self-read request).
Consumer → Utility / Metering & Field Operations
  (self-read submission).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Read Instruction" — written by "Schedule field technician
  visit"; read by "Dispatch read instruction to Metering Service Provider".
Data Object "Interval Data File" — written by Meter Data Management
  System (returned on request); read by "Review automated read
  completeness".
Data Object "Manual Read Result" — written by "Record manual meter read";
  read by "Submit reads to Meter Data Management System".
Data Object "Consumer Self-Read Submission" — written by "Record consumer
  self-read"; read by "Submit reads to Meter Data Management System".
Data Object "Missing Read Notification" — written by "Flag missing read
  and raise substitution request"; read by the downstream Validate &
  Estimate Data subprocess.

This subprocess acquires raw consumption data from all available read
sources — smart meter head-end collection, third-party field visits, and
consumer self-reads — and lodges the results in the Meter Data Management
System register. Where a read cannot be obtained, a missing-read flag is
raised. Either outcome is passed to Validate & Estimate Data, which will
confirm the reads are plausible or substitute estimated values before
rating can begin.
```


### V23.02 — Validate & Estimate Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data — second subprocess in the
Meter to Cash value chain, transforming raw meter reads into
validated or estimated consumption data ready for rating.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the validation and
estimation process, with lanes for Meter Data Management.
Pool "Meter Data Management System" — the head-end and MDM
system that stores meter registers, interval data, and
validation rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Meter Data Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Utility (white-box, single lane)
2. Meter Data Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Meter Data Management lane:
  Message start event "Raw meter reads received from Acquire
    Meter Readings"
  Service task "Retrieve interval and register data from MDM
    System"
  Service task "Run validation rules against reads"
  Exclusive gateway "Reads pass validation?"
  - branch "Yes — all reads valid":
      Service task "Mark reads as validated in MDM System"
      Intermediate message catch event "Validation confirmation
        received from MDM System"
  - branch "No — reads missing or implausible":
      Exclusive gateway "Is a prior actual read available for
        estimation?"
      - branch "Yes — prior read available":
          User task "Apply estimation algorithm to derive
            substituted read"
          Service task "Record estimated read and flag in MDM
            System"
          Intermediate message catch event "Estimated read
            confirmation received from MDM System"
      - branch "No — prior read unavailable":
          User task "Escalate missing data to field technician
            for re-read or manual entry"
          Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Read Obtained"
            (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
            "Review re-read or manual entry received", Service
            task "Re-run validation rules against new read"
          Service task "Record accepted read in MDM System"
          Intermediate message catch event "Accepted read
            confirmation received from MDM System"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Estimation or re-read resolved"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reads pass validation"
  User task "Review and approve estimated or substituted reads"
  Exclusive gateway "Approved?"
  - branch "Yes — approved":
      Service task "Finalise and lock validated consumption
        dataset in MDM System"
  - branch "No — rejected, requires correction":
      User task "Amend estimated or substituted read values"
      Sequence flow returns into "Finalise and lock validated
        consumption dataset in MDM System" after amendment
        — model this as a simple loop-back to the finalise task
        via the merge below
  Exclusive merge gateway "Approval outcome resolved"
  Service task "Publish validated consumption dataset to Billing
    Engine"
  End event "Validated consumption data confirmed — ready for
    Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess
"Repeat Until Read Obtained" — label "Re-read deadline 5
business days exceeded" — on trigger, flow exits to User task
"Log data gap and apply regulatory default estimate" then
rejoins at the Exclusive merge gateway "Estimation or re-read
resolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow proceeds through the Meter Data Management
lane in the order above. The "Reads pass validation?" gateway
splits to the validated branch and the missing/implausible
branch; both rejoin at "Reads pass validation" merge. The
"Is a prior read available?" gateway splits into the estimation
branch and the escalation/re-read branch; both rejoin at
"Estimation or re-read resolved" merge. The "Approved?"
gateway splits to the finalise branch and the amend branch;
the amend branch feeds back to merge at "Approval outcome
resolved" before the finalise task.

Message flows:
Utility "Retrieve interval and register data from MDM System"
  → Meter Data Management System (request for interval and
  register data).
Meter Data Management System → Utility "Run validation rules
  against reads" (interval data and validation rule set
  returned).
Utility "Mark reads as validated in MDM System" → Meter Data
  Management System (validated read status update).
Meter Data Management System → Utility (validation
  confirmation).
Utility "Record estimated read and flag in MDM System" → Meter
  Data Management System (estimated read and substitution flag).
Meter Data Management System → Utility (estimated read
  confirmation).
Utility "Record accepted read in MDM System" → Meter Data
  Management System (accepted re-read or manual-entry value).
Meter Data Management System → Utility (accepted read
  confirmation).
Utility "Finalise and lock validated consumption dataset in MDM
  System" → Meter Data Management System (lock and finalise
  instruction).
Utility "Publish validated consumption dataset to Billing
  Engine" → Meter Data Management System (publication
  instruction to forward dataset).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Raw Meter Read File" — read by "Run validation
  rules against reads"; written by "Retrieve interval and
  register data from MDM System".
Data Object "Validation Rule Set" — read by "Run validation
  rules against reads"; written by "Retrieve interval and
  register data from MDM System".
Data Object "Estimated Read Record" — written by "Apply
  estimation algorithm to derive substituted read"; read by
  "Record estimated read and flag in MDM System".
Data Object "Re-read or Manual Entry" — written by "Review
  re-read or manual entry received"; read by "Re-run validation
  rules against new read".
Data Object "Validated Consumption Dataset" — written by
  "Finalise and lock validated consumption dataset in MDM
  System"; read by "Publish validated consumption dataset to
  Billing Engine".

This subprocess takes raw meter reads produced by Acquire Meter
Readings and subjects them to formal validation rules, resolving
missing or implausible data through estimation or field
re-reads, and obtaining analyst approval before locking the
result. It hands a clean, approved, and locked validated
consumption dataset to Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption, giving
that subprocess reliable input for accurate billing.
```


### V23.03 — Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption — third subprocess in the
Meter to Cash value chain, receiving validated consumption data from Validate
& Estimate Data and passing rated consumption to Generate & Issue Bill.

1. Pools & Lanes
```
