```text
Pool "Utility" — the energy or water utility running the rating process,
  containing the Billing team.
Pool "Billing Engine" — the rating and tariff system that applies prices and
  calculates charges.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Billing Engine" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Utility (white-box, single lane)
2. Billing Engine (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Billing lane:
  Message start event "Validated consumption data received from Validate &
    Estimate Data"
  Service task "Retrieve tariff and rate tables from Billing Engine"
  Service task "Identify applicable tariff for account"
  Exclusive gateway "Tariff type?"
  - branch "Time-of-use tariff":
      Service task "Apply time-of-use rate bands to interval data"
  - branch "Flat or block tariff":
      Service task "Apply flat or block rate to consumption volume"
  - branch "Demand or capacity tariff":
      Service task "Calculate peak demand charge from interval data"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Tariff type"
  Service task "Apply standing charges and applicable levies"
  Exclusive gateway "Concession or discount applicable?"
  - branch "Yes":
      Service task "Apply concession or discount to rated amount"
  - branch "No":
      (continue to merge)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Concession or discount applicable"
  Service task "Calculate GST or applicable tax on rated charges"
  User task "Review rated consumption and charges for accuracy"
  Exclusive gateway "Charges acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes":
      (continue to merge)
  - branch "No":
      User task "Correct tariff selection or consumption input"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected data confirmed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Charges acceptable"
  Service task "Write rated consumption record to Billing Engine"
  End event "Rated consumption confirmed — ready for Generate & Issue Bill"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Review rated consumption and charges
  for accuracy" — label "Review overdue (end of rating window)" — triggers
  escalation to a billing supervisor; flow ends at an escalation End event
  "Rating review escalated — billing cycle delayed".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all flow within the Billing lane from the message start event
  through tariff retrieval, the three-branch tariff-type gateway merging back
  at "Tariff type", then standing charges, the two-branch concession gateway
  merging at "Concession or discount applicable", tax calculation, the review
  user task, the two-branch acceptability gateway (the "No" branch passing
  through the correction task and an intermediate message catch event before
  rejoining) merging at "Charges acceptable", the write service task, and
  finally the end event.

Message flows:
  Billing Engine → Billing lane (tariff and rate tables returned to "Retrieve
    tariff and rate tables from Billing Engine")
  Billing lane → Billing Engine ("Apply time-of-use rate bands to interval
    data" sends interval data for rating)
  Billing lane → Billing Engine ("Apply flat or block rate to consumption
    volume" sends volume data for rating)
  Billing lane → Billing Engine ("Calculate peak demand charge from interval
    data" sends demand data for rating)
  Billing lane → Billing Engine ("Write rated consumption record to Billing
    Engine" posts finalised rated record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Consumption Data" — read by "Identify applicable
  tariff for account".
Data Object "Tariff and Rate Tables" — read by "Apply time-of-use rate bands
  to interval data", "Apply flat or block rate to consumption volume",
  "Calculate peak demand charge from interval data".
Data Object "Rated Consumption Record" — written by "Calculate GST or
  applicable tax on rated charges"; read by "Review rated consumption and
  charges for accuracy"; written by "Write rated consumption record to
  Billing Engine".
Data Object "Concession or Discount Schedule" — read by "Apply concession or
  discount to rated amount".

This subprocess receives validated and estimated consumption data, selects the
correct tariff for each account, calculates energy or commodity charges across
all applicable rate structures, and applies standing charges, levies, taxes,
and any eligible concessions. The finalised rated consumption record is
committed to the Billing Engine and handed to Generate & Issue Bill, which
uses it to produce the customer invoice.
```


### V23.04 — Generate & Issue Bill

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill — fourth subprocess in the Meter to
Cash value chain, receiving rated consumption from Apply Tariffs & Rate
Consumption and delivering a bill to the Consumer.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the billing process, containing
  the Billing and related lanes.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Billing (billing officer)
Pool "Consumer" — the account holder who receives and acknowledges the bill.
Pool "Billing Engine" — IT system that generates and formats invoices.
Pool "Customer Information System" — IT system holding account, contact,
  and delivery-preference data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Billing Engine" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Customer Information System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility (white-box)
3. Billing Engine
4. Customer Information System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Billing lane:
  Message start event "Rated consumption received from Apply Tariffs &
    Rate Consumption"
  Service task "Retrieve account and contact details"
  Service task "Assemble bill data"
  Service task "Generate invoice in Billing Engine"
  Service task "Retrieve delivery preferences from Customer Information
    System"
  Exclusive gateway "Delivery channel?"
    - branch "Electronic (email or portal)":
        Send task "Issue bill electronically to Consumer"
    - branch "Post":
        User task "Prepare printed bill for dispatch"
        Send task "Dispatch printed bill to Consumer"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery channel"
  Service task "Record bill issuance in Customer Information System"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Bill acknowledgement window expires
    (14 days)"
  Exclusive gateway "Bill acknowledged or opened?"
    - branch "Yes — acknowledged":
        Intermediate message catch event "Acknowledgement received from
          Consumer"
    - branch "No — no acknowledgement":
        Send task "Send bill delivery follow-up to Consumer"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Bill acknowledged or opened"
  Service task "Update bill status to Issued in Billing Engine"
  End event "Bill issued and confirmed — ready for Handle Billing
    Enquiries & Disputes or Receive & Allocate Payment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Prepare printed bill for dispatch",
  label "Print or dispatch delay (24 hours)", triggers Send task "Escalate
  dispatch delay to billing officer".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The single Billing lane carries the flow from the message
  start event through account retrieval, bill assembly, invoice generation,
  and preference retrieval to the Delivery channel gateway. The Electronic
  branch leads directly to the electronic send task; the Post branch passes
  through the print preparation task then the postal send task. Both branches
  rejoin at the Delivery channel merge gateway, continuing to bill issuance
  recording, the 14-day timer catch event, and the acknowledgement gateway.
  The Yes branch catches the Consumer acknowledgement message; the No branch
  sends a follow-up. Both branches rejoin at the Bill acknowledged merge
  gateway, continuing to the Billing Engine status update and the end event.

Message flows:
  Billing Engine → Utility / Billing lane (generated invoice data) during
    "Generate invoice in Billing Engine".
  Customer Information System → Utility / Billing lane (account, contact,
    and delivery preference data) during "Retrieve account and contact
    details" and "Retrieve delivery preferences from Customer Information
    System".
  Utility / Billing lane → Consumer (bill or invoice) via "Issue bill
    electronically to Consumer" and "Dispatch printed bill to Consumer".
  Utility / Billing lane → Consumer (delivery follow-up notification) via
    "Send bill delivery follow-up to Consumer".
  Consumer → Utility / Billing lane (acknowledgement or read receipt) via
    "Acknowledgement received from Consumer".
  Utility / Billing lane → Customer Information System (bill issuance
    status update) during "Record bill issuance in Customer Information
    System".
  Utility / Billing lane → Billing Engine (issued status) during "Update
    bill status to Issued in Billing Engine".

7. Data objects

Data Object "Rated Consumption Record" — read by "Assemble bill data".
Data Object "Account and Contact Details" — read by "Retrieve account and
  contact details", read by "Retrieve delivery preferences from Customer
  Information System".
Data Object "Invoice" — written by "Generate invoice in Billing Engine",
  read by "Issue bill electronically to Consumer", read by "Prepare printed
  bill for dispatch".
Data Object "Delivery Preferences" — read by "Retrieve delivery preferences
  from Customer Information System", read by "Assemble bill data".

This subprocess takes rated consumption produced by Apply Tariffs & Rate
Consumption, assembles a complete invoice using account and contact data from
the Customer Information System, generates the formatted bill in the Billing
Engine, and delivers it to the Consumer via the preferred channel. On
confirmation that the bill has been issued, the subprocess hands off to both
Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes (should the Consumer query the bill) and
Receive & Allocate Payment (should the Consumer proceed to settle the amount
due).
```


### V23.05 — Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes — the Customer Service
subprocess that receives, investigates and resolves consumer billing enquiries
and disputes before returning a confirmed outcome to the billing and payment
flow.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Consumer" — the account holder raising an enquiry or dispute.
Pool "Utility" — the organisation handling the enquiry and dispute; contains
  all internal lanes.
  Lane "Customer Service" — customer service agent who receives, assesses
    and communicates on enquiries and disputes.
  Lane "Billing" — billing officer who investigates billing accuracy and
    applies adjustments.
Pool "Customer Information System" — IT system holding account, contact and
  billing data.
Pool "Dispute Management System" — IT system used to log, track and close
  disputes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer Information System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Dispute Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Customer Service, Billing)
3. Customer Information System
4. Dispute Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Customer Service lane:
  Message start event "Billing enquiry or dispute received from Consumer"
  User task "Capture enquiry details and verify account"
  Service task "Retrieve account and billing data from Customer
    Information System"
  Exclusive gateway "Enquiry type?"
  - branch "Simple enquiry — information only":
      User task "Provide billing explanation to Consumer"
      Send task "Send enquiry response to Consumer"
      End event "Enquiry resolved — no further action"
  - branch "Dispute raised — requires investigation":
      Service task "Log dispute in Dispute Management System"
      User task "Acknowledge dispute and set expectations with Consumer"
      Send task "Send dispute acknowledgement to Consumer"
      (continues in Billing lane below)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Enquiry type"
  Intermediate message catch event "Investigation outcome received from
    Billing"
  Exclusive gateway "Dispute upheld?"
  - branch "Yes — adjustment warranted":
      User task "Notify Consumer of outcome and adjustment"
      Send task "Send adjustment confirmation to Consumer"
      Service task "Update dispute record as upheld in Dispute
        Management System"
      End event "Dispute upheld and adjustment confirmed — ready for
        Receive and Allocate Payment"
  - branch "No — original bill stands":
      User task "Notify Consumer of outcome — bill confirmed"
      Send task "Send outcome letter to Consumer"
      Service task "Update dispute record as not upheld in Dispute
        Management System"
      Exclusive gateway "Consumer accepts outcome?"
      - branch "Accepts":
          End event "Dispute closed — bill stands — ready for Receive
            and Allocate Payment"
      - branch "Escalates":
          User task "Escalate dispute and advise Consumer of escalation
            path"
          End event "Dispute escalated — referred for external review"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Consumer accepts outcome"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Dispute upheld"

Billing lane:
  User task "Review bill and consumption data for accuracy"
  Service task "Retrieve tariff and rated consumption from Customer
    Information System"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Investigation Complete" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Assess billing components
    against account record", User task "Request supplementary data or
    clarification if required", Intermediate message catch event
    "Supplementary data received"
  Exclusive gateway "Adjustment required?"
  - branch "Yes":
      User task "Raise billing adjustment"
      Service task "Record adjustment in Customer Information System"
  - branch "No":
      (no adjustment task; proceed directly to merge)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Adjustment required"
  Send task "Send investigation outcome to Customer Service"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Investigation Complete", labelled "Investigation deadline elapsed",
  leading to: User task "Escalate overdue investigation" in Billing lane,
  then Send task "Send investigation outcome to Customer Service".
Non-interrupting escalation boundary event on User task "Review bill and
  consumption data for accuracy", labelled "Regulatory response time at
  risk", leading to: User task "Flag impending breach to Customer Service
  team leader".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Customer Service lane the flow moves from the
start event through account verification and data retrieval to the
"Enquiry type?" gateway; the simple-enquiry branch ends at its own End
event; the dispute branch continues through logging and acknowledgement
before crossing to the Billing lane; after the Billing lane completes its
investigation and sends the outcome, the Customer Service lane resumes at
the intermediate message catch event, passes through the "Dispute upheld?"
gateway whose two branches each lead through their respective tasks, the
"No" branch reaching the nested "Consumer accepts outcome?" gateway, both
of whose branches end at their own End events; the "Yes" branch ends at
its End event; all gateway branches are matched by their named merge
gateways as described above.

Message flows:
Consumer → Customer Service ("Billing enquiry or dispute received";
  enquiry or dispute details)
Customer Service → Consumer ("Send dispute acknowledgement"; acknowledgement
  letter)
Customer Service → Consumer ("Send enquiry response"; billing explanation)
Customer Service → Consumer ("Send outcome letter"; dispute outcome —
  bill stands)
Customer Service → Consumer ("Send adjustment confirmation"; adjustment
  confirmation)
Customer Service → Customer Information System ("Retrieve account and
  billing data"; account and billing data request)
Customer Information System → Customer Service (account and billing data
  returned)
Customer Service → Dispute Management System ("Log dispute"; new dispute
  record)
Customer Service → Dispute Management System ("Update dispute record as
  upheld"; upheld status update)
Customer Service → Dispute Management System ("Update dispute record as
  not upheld"; not-upheld status update)
Billing → Customer Information System ("Retrieve tariff and rated
  consumption"; data request)
Customer Information System → Billing (tariff and rated consumption data)
Billing → Customer Information System ("Record adjustment"; adjustment
  posting)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Billing Enquiry Record" — written by User task "Capture
  enquiry details and verify account"; read by User task "Review bill and
  consumption data for accuracy".
Data Object "Dispute Case" — written by Service task "Log dispute in
  Dispute Management System"; read by Service task "Update dispute record
  as upheld in Dispute Management System" and Service task "Update dispute
  record as not upheld in Dispute Management System".
Data Object "Account and Billing Data" — written by Service task "Retrieve
  account and billing data from Customer Information System"; read by User
  task "Provide billing explanation to Consumer" and User task "Review
  bill and consumption data for accuracy".
Data Object "Tariff and Rated Consumption Data" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve tariff and rated consumption from Customer Information System";
  read by User task "Assess billing components against account record".
Data Object "Billing Adjustment" — written by User task "Raise billing
  adjustment"; read by Service task "Record adjustment in Customer
  Information System".
Data Object "Dispute Outcome Notice" — written by Send task "Send
  investigation outcome to Customer Service"; read by User task "Notify
  Consumer of outcome and adjustment" and User task "Notify Consumer of
  outcome — bill confirmed".

This subprocess receives a consumer billing enquiry or dispute and either
resolves it immediately through a billing explanation or routes it through
a structured investigation in the Billing lane, applying adjustments where
warranted and recording all outcomes in the Dispute Management System. A
confirmed upheld adjustment or a closed standing bill is then handed to
Receive and Allocate Payment so the corrected or original balance can be
settled; an escalated outcome exits to an external review path.
```


### V23.06 — Receive & Allocate Payment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment — sixth subprocess in the
Meter to Cash value chain, handling incoming consumer payments and
posting them to accounts and the general ledger.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation receiving and allocating payments,
  containing the Finance team.
Pool "Consumer" — the account holder making a payment.
Pool "Payment Provider" — the external party processing payment
  transactions and returning confirmations.
Pool "Payment Processing System" — IT system handling payment
  authorisation and confirmation.
Pool "General Ledger" — IT system recording financial postings.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Processing System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "General Ledger" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Payment Provider
3. Utility
4. Payment Processing System
5. General Ledger

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Finance lane:

Message start event "Payment received from Consumer or Payment
  Provider"
User task "Identify payment channel and account"
Exclusive gateway "Payment channel?"
  - branch "Direct debit": Service task "Retrieve direct-debit
    instruction from Payment Processing System"
    Intermediate message catch event "Direct-debit confirmation
      received"
  - branch "Online or card payment": Service task "Request payment
      authorisation from Payment Processing System"
    Intermediate message catch event "Authorisation confirmation
      received"
  - branch "Cash or cheque": User task "Record manual payment
      details"
Exclusive merge gateway "Payment channel"
User task "Match payment to outstanding invoice or account"
Exclusive gateway "Payment matched?"
  - branch "Matched": Service task "Post payment to account in
      Payment Processing System"
  - branch "Unmatched": User task "Investigate unmatched payment"
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Payment Matched"
      (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Request
      remittance advice from Consumer", Intermediate message catch
      event "Remittance advice received", User task "Re-attempt
      account match"
    Service task "Post payment to suspense or matched account in
      Payment Processing System"
Exclusive merge gateway "Payment matched"
Service task "Trigger general-ledger posting in General Ledger"
Intermediate message catch event "General-ledger posting
  confirmation received"
User task "Reconcile daily payment run"
Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation balanced?"
  - branch "Balanced": End event "Payment allocated and posted —
      ready for Manage Arrears and Hardship"
  - branch "Discrepancy found": User task "Escalate reconciliation
      discrepancy to Finance supervisor"
    End event "Reconciliation discrepancy escalated — pending
      resolution"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Payment Matched", label "48-hour remittance deadline
  elapsed"; on trigger, flow continues to Service task "Post payment
  to suspense or matched account in Payment Processing System",
  bypassing further match attempts.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work moves top to bottom within the Finance lane.
After the Payment channel gateway, the direct-debit, online/card,
and cash/cheque branches each complete and rejoin at the Payment
channel merge gateway before continuing to the matching step. After
the Payment matched gateway, the matched and unmatched branches
rejoin at the Payment matched merge gateway. The reconciliation
gateway splits to two separate End events; neither branch loops
back.

Message flows:
Consumer → Utility Finance lane (payment instruction or remittance
  advice).
Payment Provider → Utility Finance lane (direct-debit file or
  card-payment settlement notification).
Utility Finance lane → Payment Processing System (direct-debit
  retrieval request; payment authorisation request; post-payment
  instruction).
Payment Processing System → Utility Finance lane (direct-debit
  confirmation; authorisation confirmation; posting acknowledgement).
Utility Finance lane → General Ledger (general-ledger posting
  instruction).
General Ledger → Utility Finance lane (posting confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Payment Instruction" — written by User task "Identify
  payment channel and account"; read by Service task "Match payment
  to outstanding invoice or account".
Data Object "Remittance Advice" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Remittance advice received"; read by User task
  "Re-attempt account match".
Data Object "Payment Authorisation Record" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Authorisation confirmation received"; read by
  Service task "Post payment to account in Payment Processing
  System".

This subprocess captures every inbound payment regardless of channel,
matches it to the correct account, posts the allocation to the
customer ledger via the Payment Processing System, and journals the
entry in the General Ledger. A balanced daily reconciliation
confirms the close of the payment run. Where payment cannot be
matched, the account is held in suspense pending remittance advice
from the Consumer, with a 48-hour timeout to prevent indefinite
suspension. The confirmed allocation is then available to the Manage
Arrears and Hardship subprocess to assess whether an outstanding
balance remains.
```


### V23.07 — Manage Arrears & Hardship

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship — subprocess within the Meter to Cash
value chain that identifies overdue accounts, engages consumers in arrears,
assesses hardship eligibility, and establishes payment arrangements to resolve
outstanding balances before escalation to collections.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation managing arrears and hardship arrangements,
  containing the Credit & Collections team.
Pool "Consumer" — the account holder in arrears who responds to contact,
  provides information, and agrees or declines a payment arrangement.
Pool "Collections System" — IT system supporting arrears tracking, payment
  plan creation, and hardship case management.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Collections System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility
3. Collections System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Credit & Collections lane:

Message start event "Overdue account identified — ready from Generate &
  Issue Bill"
Service task "Retrieve arrears account details"
Send task "Issue arrears notice to consumer"
Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to arrears notice"
Exclusive gateway "Response received?"
- branch "No response within deadline":
    Intermediate timer catch event "Response deadline elapsed"
    End event "No response — account escalated to Pursue Collections"
- branch "Response received":
    Exclusive merge gateway "Response received"
    User task "Record consumer contact and stated circumstances"
    Exclusive gateway "Hardship application indicated?"
    - branch "Yes — hardship indicated":
        User task "Assess hardship eligibility against policy"
        Exclusive gateway "Eligible for hardship arrangement?"
        - branch "Not eligible":
            User task "Notify consumer of ineligibility and options"
            Exclusive gateway "Consumer accepts standard arrangement?"
            - branch "Declines all arrangements":
                End event "Consumer declines — account escalated to
                  Pursue Collections"
            - branch "Accepts standard arrangement":
                Exclusive merge gateway "Consumer accepts standard
                  arrangement"
                User task "Negotiate and agree payment plan terms"
                Service task "Record payment plan in Collections System"
                Send task "Issue payment plan confirmation to consumer"
                Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Plan Completed or
                  Defaulted" (standard loop) containing, in order:
                  Intermediate timer catch event "Instalment due date
                  reached", Service task "Check instalment receipt in
                  Collections System", User task "Record instalment
                  outcome"
                Exclusive gateway "Plan outcome?"
                - branch "Plan completed":
                    Service task "Close arrears case in Collections System"
                    End event "Arrears resolved — balance cleared"
                - branch "Plan defaulted":
                    User task "Attempt re-engagement with consumer"
                    End event "Plan defaulted — account escalated to
                      Pursue Collections"
                Exclusive merge gateway "Plan outcome"
        - branch "Eligible":
            Exclusive merge gateway "Eligible for hardship arrangement"
            User task "Establish hardship payment arrangement"
            Service task "Register hardship case in Collections System"
            Send task "Issue hardship arrangement confirmation to consumer"
            Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Hardship Plan Completed or
              Reviewed" (standard loop) containing, in order:
              Intermediate timer catch event "Hardship review date
              reached", User task "Review hardship case status",
              Service task "Update hardship record in Collections System"
            Exclusive gateway "Hardship plan outcome?"
            - branch "Hardship resolved":
                Service task "Close hardship case in Collections System"
                End event "Arrears resolved — hardship case closed"
            - branch "Circumstances changed — reassess":
                User task "Reassess consumer circumstances"
                Exclusive merge gateway "Hardship plan outcome"
            - branch "Consumer defaults on hardship plan":
                User task "Escalate hardship default for review"
                End event "Hardship default — account escalated to
                  Pursue Collections"
            Exclusive merge gateway "Hardship plan outcome"
    - branch "No — standard arrears only":
        Exclusive merge gateway "Hardship application indicated"
        User task "Negotiate and agree payment plan terms"
        Service task "Record payment plan in Collections System"
        Send task "Issue payment plan confirmation to consumer"
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Plan Completed or Defaulted"
          (standard loop) containing, in order:
          Intermediate timer catch event "Instalment due date reached",
          Service task "Check instalment receipt in Collections System",
          User task "Record instalment outcome"
        Exclusive gateway "Plan outcome?"
        - branch "Plan completed":
            Service task "Close arrears case in Collections System"
            End event "Arrears resolved — balance cleared"
        - branch "Plan defaulted":
            User task "Attempt re-engagement with consumer"
            End event "Plan defaulted — account escalated to
              Pursue Collections"
        Exclusive merge gateway "Plan outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Assess hardship
  eligibility against policy" — label "Assessment overdue (5 business
  days)" — triggers User task "Escalate delayed assessment to team
  leader"; flow continues on the main path.
Interrupting error boundary event on Service task "Record payment plan in
  Collections System" — label "System recording failure" — triggers User
  task "Resolve system error and re-enter plan manually"; flow rejoins
  after plan is recorded.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Credit & Collections lane with the
arrears notice being issued, then waits for consumer response via an
intermediate message catch event. The "No response" branch routes through
a timer catch event directly to an escalation end event. The "Response
received" branch continues to contact recording, then splits on hardship
indication. The hardship-eligible path enters the hardship arrangement
loop before splitting on hardship plan outcome. The hardship-not-eligible
path and the standard-arrears path both enter the payment plan loop before
splitting on plan outcome; completed plans close the case and resolved-end
events are reached, while defaulted plans reach escalation end events.
All diverging gateways are matched by named merge gateways at the points
branches rejoin.

Message flows:
Send task "Issue arrears notice to consumer" → Consumer (arrears notice)
Consumer → Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to arrears
  notice" (consumer response)
Send task "Issue payment plan confirmation to consumer" → Consumer
  (payment plan confirmation)
Send task "Issue hardship arrangement confirmation to consumer" → Consumer
  (hardship arrangement confirmation)
Service task "Retrieve arrears account details" → Collections System
  (arrears account query)
Collections System → Service task "Retrieve arrears account details"
  (arrears account data)
Service task "Record payment plan in Collections System" → Collections
  System (payment plan record)
Service task "Register hardship case in Collections System" → Collections
  System (hardship case registration)
Service task "Check instalment receipt in Collections System" →
  Collections System (instalment receipt query)
Collections System → Service task "Check instalment receipt in Collections
  System" (instalment status)
Service task "Update hardship record in Collections System" → Collections
  System (hardship record update)
Service task "Close arrears case in Collections System" → Collections
  System (case closure instruction)
Service task "Close hardship case in Collections System" → Collections
  System (hardship case closure)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Arrears Notice" — written by Send task "Issue arrears notice
  to consumer"; read by Consumer.
Data Object "Consumer Circumstances Record" — written by User task "Record
  consumer contact and stated circumstances"; read by User task "Assess
  hardship eligibility against policy".
Data Object "Hardship Assessment Outcome" — written by User task "Assess
  hardship eligibility against policy"; read by User task "Establish
  hardship payment arrangement".
Data Object "Payment Plan Agreement" — written by User task "Negotiate and
  agree payment plan terms"; read by Service task "Record payment plan in
  Collections System".
Data Object "Hardship Arrangement Agreement" — written by User task
  "Establish hardship payment arrangement"; read by Service task "Register
  hardship case in Collections System".
Data Object "Instalment Outcome Record" — written by User task "Record
  instalment outcome"; read by Exclusive gateway "Plan outcome?".

This subprocess identifies consumers with overdue balances, contacts them,
assesses hardship eligibility, and establishes either a standard payment
plan or a formal hardship arrangement governed by policy. Instalment
progress is monitored through recurring review loops until the balance is
cleared or the consumer defaults. Accounts that cannot be resolved here —
because the consumer is unresponsive, ineligible, or defaults — are handed
to Pursue Collections with a complete arrears and case history.
```


### V23.08 — Pursue Collections

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.08 Pursue Collections — debt recovery subprocess within the
Meter to Cash value chain, triggered when arrears management has failed to
secure payment or a suitable arrangement.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation pursuing overdue accounts through
collections activity.
  Lane "Credit & Collections (collections officer)" — manages all
  collections activity, agency referral, and account status updates.

Pool "Consumer" — the account holder subject to collections action.
Pool "Debt Collection Agency" — external agency engaged to pursue
  recovery on referred accounts.
Pool "Collections System" — IT system recording collections status,
  agency referrals, and account ageing.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Debt Collection Agency" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Collections System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility
3. Debt Collection Agency
4. Collections System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Credit & Collections (collections officer) lane:

Message start event "Unresolved arrears account received from Manage
  Arrears & Hardship"
User task "Review account and confirm debt balance"
Service task "Retrieve ageing and collections status from Collections
  System"
User task "Select collections strategy"
Exclusive gateway "Strategy selected"
  - branch "Issue final demand notice":
      Send task "Issue final demand notice to Consumer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to final
        demand"
      Exclusive gateway "Response received"
        - branch "Payment received or arrangement agreed":
            User task "Record payment or arrangement in Collections
              System"
            End event "Debt resolved — account returned to normal
              standing"
        - branch "No response or insufficient response":
            (continue to referral path — see below)
      Exclusive merge gateway "Response received"
  - branch "Refer directly to agency":
      (continue to referral path — see below)
Exclusive merge gateway "Strategy selected"
User task "Prepare account referral package"
Send task "Send referral and debt details to Debt Collection Agency"
Intermediate message catch event "Recovery update received from Debt
  Collection Agency"
Exclusive gateway "Recovery outcome"
  - branch "Debt recovered in full or agreed settlement":
      Service task "Post recovery amount to Collections System"
      User task "Close collections case and update account status"
      End event "Debt recovered — account closed in Collections System"
  - branch "Partial recovery — write-off remainder":
      User task "Raise write-off request and obtain approval"
      Service task "Record write-off in Collections System"
      End event "Partial recovery posted — write-off recorded in
        Collections System"
  - branch "Unrecoverable — recommend disconnection":
      User task "Escalate account for disconnection review"
      End event "Unrecoverable debt escalated — ready for Manage
        Disconnection & Reconnection"
Exclusive merge gateway "Recovery outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Issue final demand notice" —
  label "Final demand period expired (14 days)" — if the consumer
  does not respond within the allowed period, flow continues to
  the referral path without waiting for the intermediate catch event.
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Send referral and debt details
  to Debt Collection Agency" — label "Agency acknowledgement timeout
  (5 business days)" — triggers user task "Follow up agency
  acknowledgement" before re-entering the intermediate message catch
  event for recovery updates.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the collections officer lane flows from the start
event through account review and status retrieval, then into the
strategy gateway. The final-demand branch issues the notice, waits
for a consumer response, and tests that response; the payment branch
ends locally while the no-response branch merges back at the strategy
merge gateway and proceeds to the referral path. The direct-agency
branch also merges there. The referral path runs through package
preparation, agency send, and the recovery outcome gateway, whose
three branches each terminate in their own end event without rejoining.

Message flows:
Consumer → Utility, Credit & Collections (Send task "Issue final
  demand notice to Consumer") — consumer response to final demand.
Utility, Credit & Collections (Send task "Issue final demand notice
  to Consumer") → Consumer — final demand notice.
Utility, Credit & Collections (Send task "Send referral and debt
  details to Debt Collection Agency") → Debt Collection Agency —
  account referral package and debt details.
Debt Collection Agency → Utility, Credit & Collections (Intermediate
  message catch event "Recovery update received from Debt Collection
  Agency") — recovery outcome report and amounts collected.
Utility, Credit & Collections (Service task "Retrieve ageing and
  collections status from Collections System") → Collections System —
  status query.
Collections System → Utility, Credit & Collections (Service task
  "Retrieve ageing and collections status from Collections System") —
  ageing and collections status data.
Utility, Credit & Collections (Service task "Post recovery amount to
  Collections System") → Collections System — recovery posting.
Utility, Credit & Collections (Service task "Record write-off in
  Collections System") → Collections System — write-off instruction.
Utility, Credit & Collections (User task "Record payment or
  arrangement in Collections System") → Collections System — payment
  or arrangement record.

7. Data objects

Data Object "Final Demand Notice" — written by "Issue final demand
  notice to Consumer"; read by Consumer.
Data Object "Account Referral Package" — written by "Prepare account
  referral package"; read by "Send referral and debt details to Debt
  Collection Agency".
Data Object "Recovery Update Report" — read by "Intermediate message
  catch event 'Recovery update received from Debt Collection Agency'";
  written by Debt Collection Agency.
Data Object "Write-off Request" — written by "Raise write-off request
  and obtain approval"; read by "Record write-off in Collections
  System".

This subprocess pursues recovery of debts that could not be resolved
through arrears management or hardship arrangements. It issues a final
demand, tests the consumer's response, and where necessary refers the
account to a debt collection agency, then records whatever outcome is
achieved — full recovery, partial recovery with write-off, or
escalation for disconnection. Fully recovered accounts return to
normal standing; unrecoverable ones are handed to Manage
Disconnection & Reconnection for further action.
```


### V23.09 — Manage Disconnection & Reconnection

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.09 Manage Disconnection & Reconnection — subprocess within the
Meter to Cash value chain that executes field disconnection of supply for
unresolved arrears and restores supply on resolution, coordinating credit
decisions, field operations, and network notifications.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation executing disconnection and reconnection
  Lane "Credit & Collections" (credit officer)
  Lane "Metering & Field Operations" (field technician)
Pool "Consumer" — account holder subject to disconnection or reconnection
Pool "Network Operator" — distribution network operator exchanging service
  orders and outage data
Pool "Field Workforce Management" — system managing field job scheduling
  and dispatch
Pool "Customer Information System" — system holding account, contact, and
  service order records

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Network Operator" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Field Workforce Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance
Pool "Customer Information System" — black-box, System = true, single instance

3. Layout

Pool "Consumer" — top
Pool "Network Operator" — second
Pool "Utility" — third (white-box, widest)
Pool "Field Workforce Management" — fourth
Pool "Customer Information System" — bottom

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Credit & Collections lane:
  Message start event "Disconnection authorised — ready from Manage
    Arrears & Hardship"
  User task "Verify disconnection eligibility and protected-customer
    exclusions"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer eligible for disconnection?"
  - branch "Not eligible — protected or exempt": Send task "Issue
    exemption notice to consumer"; End event "Disconnection suppressed
    — case returned to arrears management"
  - branch "Eligible": continue to next step
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer eligible for disconnection"
  User task "Confirm final notice issued and cooling-off period elapsed"
  Send task "Issue disconnection warning to consumer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds within notice
    period"
  Exclusive gateway "Response received within notice period?"
  - branch "Yes — payment or arrangement made": Send task "Cancel
    disconnection order"; End event "Disconnection cancelled — account
    referred to Manage Arrears & Hardship"
  - branch "No — no response": continue to raise field order
  Exclusive merge gateway "Response received within notice period"
  User task "Raise disconnection service order"

Metering & Field Operations lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Disconnection service order received
    from Field Workforce Management"
  User task "Attend site and confirm safe disconnection conditions"
  Exclusive gateway "Safe to disconnect?"
  - branch "No — unsafe or access issue": User task "Record failed
    attempt and reason"; Send task "Notify credit officer of failed
    attempt"; Intermediate message catch event "Rescheduled order
    received from Field Workforce Management"; continue to attend site
    (loop back suppressed — model as):
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Site Accessible or Attempt
      Limit Reached" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
      "Attend site and confirm safe disconnection conditions", Exclusive
      gateway "Safe to disconnect?", User task "Record failed attempt
      and reason", Send task "Notify credit officer of failed attempt"
  - branch "Yes — safe": continue to execute disconnection
  Exclusive merge gateway "Safe to disconnect"
  User task "Execute disconnection and record meter reading at
    disconnection"
  Send task "Submit disconnection completion and meter read to Meter
    Data Management System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Reconnection authorised by Credit
    & Collections"
  User task "Attend site for reconnection"
  User task "Execute reconnection and record meter reading at
    reconnection"
  Send task "Submit reconnection completion and meter read to Meter
    Data Management System"
  End event "Reconnection confirmed — account active, data forwarded to
    Acquire Meter Readings and billing cycle resumed"

Credit & Collections lane (continued after field disconnection):
  Intermediate message catch event "Disconnection completion confirmed"
  User task "Update account status to disconnected in Customer
    Information System"
  User task "Monitor account for payment or hardship application"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconnection condition met?"
  - branch "No — no payment or arrangement": User task "Escalate to
    Pursue Collections"; End event "Account referred to Pursue
    Collections"
  - branch "Yes — payment received or plan agreed": continue to
    authorise reconnection
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reconnection condition met"
  User task "Verify payment or arrangement and confirm reconnection
    authority"
  Send task "Issue reconnection authorisation to field technician"
  Send task "Notify consumer of reconnection scheduled"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Site Accessible or Attempt Limit Reached" — label "Maximum attempt
  period elapsed" — triggers User task "Escalate unresolved access
  issue to credit officer for review" leading to an End event
  "Disconnection unresolved — escalated to credit review".
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Monitor account for
  payment or hardship application" — label "Maximum monitoring period
  elapsed" — triggers User task "Escalate to Pursue Collections"
  leading to End event "Account referred to Pursue Collections".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in Credit & Collections with the message
start event, passing eligibility check (protected-customer branch ends
early; eligible branch continues), through notice issuance and the
notice-period catch event (cancellation branch ends early; no-response
branch continues), to raise service order; flow crosses to Metering &
Field Operations on receipt of the scheduled order, through site
attendance and the safe-to-disconnect gateway (unsafe branch enters the
standard-loop subprocess with its timer boundary; safe branch continues
to execute disconnection), then to completion submission; flow returns
to Credit & Collections for account status update, monitoring, and the
reconnection-condition gateway (no-payment branch ends at collections
referral; payment branch continues to reconnection authorisation); flow
returns to Metering & Field Operations for site attendance and
reconnection execution, ending with the reconnection end event.
Message flows:
  Utility (Credit & Collections) → Consumer (disconnection warning
    notice)
  Consumer → Utility (Credit & Collections) (payment or arrangement
    response within notice period)
  Utility (Credit & Collections) → Field Workforce Management
    (disconnection service order)
  Field Workforce Management → Utility (Metering & Field Operations)
    (scheduled disconnection job)
  Utility (Metering & Field Operations) → Network Operator
    (disconnection completion notification and meter read)
  Network Operator → Utility (Metering & Field Operations) (service
    order acknowledgement and outage confirmation)
  Utility (Metering & Field Operations) → Customer Information System
    (disconnection completion and meter reading at disconnection)
  Utility (Credit & Collections) → Customer Information System
    (account status update to disconnected)
  Utility (Credit & Collections) → Consumer (reconnection scheduled
    notification)
  Utility (Credit & Collections) → Field Workforce Management
    (reconnection service order)
  Field Workforce Management → Utility (Metering & Field Operations)
    (scheduled reconnection job)
  Utility (Metering & Field Operations) → Customer Information System
    (reconnection completion and meter reading at reconnection)
  Utility (Metering & Field Operations) → Network Operator
    (reconnection completion notification)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Disconnection Service Order" — written by User task "Raise
  disconnection service order"; read by User task "Attend site and
  confirm safe disconnection conditions"
Data Object "Protected-Customer Exemption Record" — read by User task
  "Verify disconnection eligibility and protected-customer exclusions"
Data Object "Final Disconnection Notice" — written by Send task "Issue
  disconnection warning to consumer"
Data Object "Meter Reading at Disconnection" — written by User task
  "Execute disconnection and record meter reading at disconnection";
  read by Send task "Submit disconnection completion and meter read to
  Meter Data Management System"
Data Object "Reconnection Authorisation" — written by User task "Verify
  payment or arrangement and confirm reconnection authority"; read by
  Send task "Issue reconnection authorisation to field technician"
Data Object "Meter Reading at Reconnection" — written by User task
  "Execute reconnection and record meter reading at reconnection";
  read by Send task "Submit reconnection completion and meter read to
  Meter Data Management System"

This subprocess governs the full lifecycle from credit-authorised
disconnection through to supply restoration. It enforces eligibility
and protected-customer checks before any field action, coordinates
scheduled site attendance via Field Workforce Management, and exchanges
service order and meter-read data with the Network Operator and
Customer Information System. On reconnection the subprocess hands final
meter reads back to the metering and billing cycle, allowing Acquire
Meter Readings and Generate & Issue Bill to resume normal processing
for the account.
```


### V23.10 — Perform Revenue Assurance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance — final subprocess in the Meter to
Cash value chain, closing the cycle by detecting revenue leakage and reporting
to the regulator.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the revenue assurance process,
  with lanes for Revenue Assurance.
Pool "Regulator" — external regulatory body that receives compliance and
  revenue reports.
Pool "Revenue Assurance Analytics" — IT system supporting leakage
  detection, reconciliation, and reporting.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Revenue Assurance Analytics" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Regulator
2. Utility
3. Revenue Assurance Analytics

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Revenue Assurance lane:
  Timer start event "Scheduled revenue assurance cycle begins"
  User task "Define scope and period for assurance review"
  Service task "Extract unbilled revenue and consumption data from
    Revenue Assurance Analytics"
  User task "Reconcile billed revenue against metered consumption"
  Exclusive gateway "Variance within acceptable tolerance?"
    - branch "Yes — no leakage detected": continue to User task
        "Prepare assurance summary report"
    - branch "No — variance exceeds threshold": User task
        "Investigate revenue leakage and root cause"
      Exclusive gateway "Leakage cause identified?"
        - branch "Yes": User task "Raise adjustment or correction
            action"
          Service task "Record adjustment in Revenue Assurance
            Analytics"
          continue to Exclusive merge gateway
            "Leakage cause identified"
        - branch "No — further review required":
          Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Cause Determined"
            (standard loop) containing, in order:
            User task "Escalate and conduct deeper data analysis",
            User task "Consult source data from upstream
              subprocesses",
            User task "Update leakage investigation findings"
          continue to Exclusive merge gateway
            "Leakage cause identified"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Leakage cause identified"
      continue to User task "Prepare assurance summary report"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Variance within acceptable tolerance"
  User task "Prepare assurance summary report"
  User task "Compile regulatory revenue report"
  Send task "Submit regulatory revenue report to Regulator"
  Intermediate message catch event "Regulatory acknowledgement
    received"
  User task "File completed assurance report and close period"
  End event "Revenue assurance cycle complete — cycle closed and
    findings recorded"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Cause Determined", labelled "Maximum investigation period
  elapsed", leading to User task "Escalate unresolved leakage to
  senior management" and then to an End event "Leakage unresolved —
  escalated for management action".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Revenue Assurance lane runs from the timer
start event through scope definition, data extraction, reconciliation,
and the exclusive gateway on variance tolerance. The "Yes" branch
proceeds directly to report preparation; the "No" branch enters
leakage investigation and the nested "Leakage cause identified"
gateway, whose "Yes" branch raises an adjustment and records it before
rejoining, and whose "No" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess
before rejoining at the merge gateway. Both branches of the outer
gateway rejoin at the exclusive merge "Variance within acceptable
tolerance" before report preparation, regulatory submission, and the
message catch event for acknowledgement, closing at the end event. The
boundary timer on the loop subprocess exits to the escalation task and
its own end event without rejoining the main flow.

Message flows:
Revenue Assurance Analytics → Utility Revenue Assurance lane
  (unbilled revenue, consumption data, leakage and reconciliation
  reporting)
Utility Revenue Assurance lane → Revenue Assurance Analytics
  (adjustment and correction records, confirmed review scope)
Utility Revenue Assurance lane → Regulator (regulatory revenue
  report submission)
Regulator → Utility Revenue Assurance lane (regulatory
  acknowledgement)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Revenue Assurance Review Scope" — written by User task
  "Define scope and period for assurance review"; read by Service task
  "Extract unbilled revenue and consumption data from Revenue Assurance
  Analytics".
Data Object "Unbilled Revenue and Consumption Extract" — written by
  Service task "Extract unbilled revenue and consumption data from
  Revenue Assurance Analytics"; read by User task "Reconcile billed
  revenue against metered consumption".
Data Object "Reconciliation Variance Report" — written by User task
  "Reconcile billed revenue against metered consumption"; read by
  Exclusive gateway "Variance within acceptable tolerance?".
Data Object "Leakage Investigation Findings" — written by User task
  "Investigate revenue leakage and root cause"; read by User task
  "Raise adjustment or correction action".
Data Object "Assurance Summary Report" — written by User task
  "Prepare assurance summary report"; read by User task "Compile
  regulatory revenue report".
Data Object "Regulatory Revenue Report" — written by User task
  "Compile regulatory revenue report"; read by Send task "Submit
  regulatory revenue report to Regulator".

This subprocess closes the Meter to Cash cycle by reconciling all
billed revenue against metered consumption, identifying and correcting
leakage, and producing the regulatory revenue report. Once the
regulator acknowledges receipt and the period is formally filed, the
assurance cycle is complete and the findings are available for the next
cycle's benchmarking and for any audit or regulatory inquiry that
follows.
```


## V24 — Transaction to Return

**Teams and roles involved.**
Transaction to Return usually involves Tax, Finance/Accounting, Accounts Payable and Receivable, Treasury, Payroll, Legal, and external Tax Advisers, with Internal Audit providing assurance. Key roles include tax manager, tax accountant, financial accountant, indirect tax analyst, transfer pricing specialist, payroll manager, treasury analyst, and external tax adviser.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Tax Authority. The process is initiated by a statutory lodgement period ending, a transaction with tax consequences, or an authority query, ruling request or audit. Other external parties include external tax advisers and auditors, customs authorities for trade, and jurisdictions' revenue offices where the organisation operates across borders.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: capture transactions with tax attributes, determine the correct tax treatment, calculate liabilities and credits, reconcile tax accounts to the ledger, prepare the return and supporting workpapers, review and approve, lodge the return, pay or claim the balance, respond to authority queries and audits, and monitor legislative change.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include ERP and the general ledger, tax determination and calculation engines, indirect tax reporting tools, transfer pricing documentation systems, payroll systems, treasury and payment systems, e-filing gateways to revenue authorities, document management for workpapers, and tax provision and reporting tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the tax governance framework and risk appetite, tax determination rules by jurisdiction and product, lodgement calendars and deadlines, review and approval authority for returns, documentation and record-retention requirements, transfer pricing policy, voluntary disclosure procedure, and escalation of uncertain tax positions.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The tax authority provides legislation, rulings, assessments, queries and audit findings, and receives returns, payments, disclosures and supporting documentation. Advisers provide opinions and reviews; the process provides them with data and questions. Customers and suppliers exchange tax invoices and exemption certificates that evidence treatment.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates tax codes and determinations on transactions, calculated liabilities, reconciliations, workpapers, lodged returns, payments, and provisions. IT systems provide transaction detail with tax attributes, ledger balances, rate and rule tables, prior-period comparatives, lodgement confirmations and receipts, and tax position and effective-rate reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V24.01** Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes | Customer, Supplier | Finance / Accounting (financial accountant) | ERP / General Ledger |
| **V24.02** Determine Tax Treatment | — | Tax (indirect tax analyst) | Tax Determination Engine |
| **V24.03** Calculate Liabilities & Credits | — | Tax (tax accountant) | Tax Determination Engine, ERP / General Ledger |
| **V24.04** Reconcile Tax Accounts | — | Finance / Accounting (financial accountant), Tax (tax accountant) | ERP / General Ledger |
| **V24.05** Prepare Return & Workpapers | External Tax Adviser | Tax (tax accountant) | Tax Reporting System, Document Management System |
| **V24.06** Review & Approve | — | Tax (tax manager) | Tax Reporting System |
| **V24.07** Lodge Return | Tax Authority | Tax (tax manager) | E-Filing Gateway |
| **V24.08** Pay or Claim Balance | Tax Authority | Treasury (treasury analyst) | Treasury & Payment System |
| **V24.09** Respond to Queries & Audits | Tax Authority, External Tax Adviser | Tax (tax manager), Legal (legal counsel) | Document Management System |
| **V24.10** Monitor Legislative Change | External Tax Adviser | Tax (tax manager) | Tax Reporting System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V24):

- **External actors:** Customer (V24.01); Supplier (V24.01); External Tax Adviser (V24.05, V24.09, V24.10); Tax Authority (V24.07–V24.09).
- **Teams:** Finance / Accounting (V24.01, V24.04); Tax (V24.02–V24.07, V24.09, V24.10); Treasury (V24.08); Legal (V24.09).
- **IT systems:** ERP / General Ledger (V24.01, V24.03, V24.04); Tax Determination Engine (V24.02, V24.03); Tax Reporting System (V24.05, V24.06, V24.10); Document Management System (V24.05, V24.09); E-Filing Gateway (V24.07); Treasury & Payment System (V24.08).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V24 — Transaction to Return — Service & Application Landscape
(high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Transaction to Return value chain, from the moment a taxable transaction
is captured through lodgement, payment, audit response, and legislative
monitoring. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands, top to bottom:
BUSINESS SERVICES (top) → BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle) → APPLICATIONS
(bottom). The demand-side actors — Customer and Supplier — sit on the far
left; the delivery and settlement actors — Tax Authority, External Tax
Adviser — sit on the far right. The diagram is read top-to-bottom as service
realisation: each application component supports the business processes that,
in turn, realise the business services presented to actors.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Customer — demand-side actor, far left, initiates tax-relevant transactions
  by exchanging invoices and exemption certificates in V24.01.
- Supplier — demand-side actor, far left, exchanges tax invoices in V24.01.
- External Tax Adviser — delivery-side actor, far right, provides opinions and
  review in V24.05, V24.09, and V24.10.
- Tax Authority — settlement-side actor, far right, receives returns, payments,
  and disclosures; issues rulings, assessments, and audit findings in
  V24.07, V24.08, and V24.09.

2. Interfaces

- Transaction Intake Interface — Business Interface accessed by Customer and
  Supplier; serves the Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service (V24.01).
- Adviser Collaboration Interface — Business Interface accessed by External
  Tax Adviser; serves the Return Preparation Service (V24.05), the Audit
  Response Service (V24.09), and the Legislative Monitoring Service (V24.10).
- Lodgement & Payment Interface — Business Interface accessed by Tax
  Authority; serves the Return Lodgement Service (V24.07) and the Balance
  Settlement Service (V24.08).
- Authority Query Interface — Business Interface accessed by Tax Authority;
  serves the Query & Audit Response Service (V24.09).

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service — provides collection and coding
  of transactions with their tax attributes from customers and suppliers.
- Tax Treatment Determination Service — provides the correct tax treatment for
  each transaction by jurisdiction and product.
- Liability & Credit Calculation Service — provides computed tax liabilities
  and recoverable credits across all applicable taxes.
- Tax Account Reconciliation Service — provides reconciled tax accounts
  agreed to the general ledger balances.
- Return Preparation Service — provides completed return workpapers and
  supporting documentation ready for review.
- Return Review & Approval Service — provides authorised sign-off on returns
  against the approved authority matrix.
- Return Lodgement Service — provides timely, compliant lodgement of returns
  to the relevant revenue authority.
- Balance Settlement Service — provides payment of tax liabilities or receipt
  of refund claims from the authority.
- Query & Audit Response Service — provides structured responses to authority
  queries, assessments, and audit findings.
- Legislative Monitoring Service — provides ongoing tracking and assessment
  of legislative changes affecting tax positions.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes — Finance/Accounting and
  Tax teams record and code all transactions with relevant tax attributes.
- V24.02 Determine Tax Treatment — Tax team applies jurisdiction and product
  rules to assign the correct treatment to each transaction.
- V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits — Tax team computes gross
  liabilities and recoverable credits using determination outputs and
  ledger balances.
- V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts — Finance/Accounting and Tax teams reconcile
  calculated tax positions to general ledger balances.
- V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers — Tax team, with External Tax Adviser
  input, assembles the return and supporting workpaper package.
- V24.06 Review & Approve — Tax manager reviews and approves the return
  within the authorised approval authority matrix.
- V24.07 Lodge Return — Tax manager submits the approved return to the Tax
  Authority via the e-filing gateway.
- V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance — Treasury analyst initiates payment of
  assessed liability or processes a refund claim with the Tax Authority.
- V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits — Tax manager and Legal counsel manage
  authority queries and audit findings, supported by External Tax Adviser.
- V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change — Tax manager tracks legislative
  developments with External Tax Adviser and assesses impact on positions.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- ERP / General Ledger — core transactional and accounting system; captures
  transactions with tax attributes and holds ledger balances.
- Tax Determination Engine — applies rate and rule tables to transactions;
  supports treatment determination and liability calculation.
- Tax Reporting System — supports return preparation, review, approval, and
  legislative change monitoring.
- Document Management System — stores workpapers, supporting documentation,
  and audit correspondence.
- E-Filing Gateway — transmits lodged returns electronically to revenue
  authorities and receives lodgement confirmations.
- Treasury & Payment System — initiates tax liability payments and processes
  refund claims with the Tax Authority.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- ERP / General Ledger SERVES V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes
- ERP / General Ledger SERVES V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits
- ERP / General Ledger SERVES V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts
- Tax Determination Engine SERVES V24.02 Determine Tax Treatment
- Tax Determination Engine SERVES V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits
- Tax Reporting System SERVES V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers
- Tax Reporting System SERVES V24.06 Review & Approve
- Tax Reporting System SERVES V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change
- Document Management System SERVES V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers
- Document Management System SERVES V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits
- E-Filing Gateway SERVES V24.07 Lodge Return
- Treasury & Payment System SERVES V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V24.01 REALISES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service
- V24.02 REALISES Tax Treatment Determination Service
- V24.03 REALISES Liability & Credit Calculation Service
- V24.04 REALISES Tax Account Reconciliation Service
- V24.05 REALISES Return Preparation Service
- V24.06 REALISES Return Review & Approval Service
- V24.07 REALISES Return Lodgement Service
- V24.08 REALISES Balance Settlement Service
- V24.09 REALISES Query & Audit Response Service
- V24.10 REALISES Legislative Monitoring Service

ASSIGNMENT (actor assigned to interface):
- Customer ASSIGNED TO Transaction Intake Interface
- Supplier ASSIGNED TO Transaction Intake Interface
- External Tax Adviser ASSIGNED TO Adviser Collaboration Interface
- Tax Authority ASSIGNED TO Lodgement & Payment Interface
- Tax Authority ASSIGNED TO Authority Query Interface

SERVING (interface serves business service):
- Transaction Intake Interface SERVES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture
  Service
- Adviser Collaboration Interface SERVES Return Preparation Service
- Adviser Collaboration Interface SERVES Query & Audit Response Service
- Adviser Collaboration Interface SERVES Legislative Monitoring Service
- Lodgement & Payment Interface SERVES Return Lodgement Service
- Lodgement & Payment Interface SERVES Balance Settlement Service
- Authority Query Interface SERVES Query & Audit Response Service

ACCESS (actor accesses service outcome):
- Tax Authority ACCESSES Return Lodgement Service
- Tax Authority ACCESSES Balance Settlement Service
- Tax Authority ACCESSES Query & Audit Response Service
- External Tax Adviser ACCESSES Return Preparation Service
- External Tax Adviser ACCESSES Query & Audit Response Service
- External Tax Adviser ACCESSES Legislative Monitoring Service
- Customer ACCESSES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service
- Supplier ACCESSES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service
```

```text
Customer — V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes: exchanges
tax invoices and exemption certificates evidencing tax treatment.

Supplier — V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes: exchanges
tax invoices and exemption certificates evidencing tax treatment.

Finance / Accounting — V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax
Attributes: receives transaction data with tax attributes for
recording in the ledger.

Finance / Accounting — V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts: performs ledger
reconciliation, matching tax account balances to the general ledger.

Tax — V24.02 Determine Tax Treatment: applies jurisdiction and product
tax determination rules to classify each transaction.

Tax — V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits: computes tax liabilities
and input-tax credits from classified transactions.

Tax — V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts: reviews reconciled tax balances
and resolves differences.

Tax — V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers: compiles return data and
supporting workpapers for lodgement.

Tax — V24.06 Review & Approve: reviews completed return and workpapers
and provides approval authority sign-off.

Tax — V24.07 Lodge Return: submits approved return via the e-filing
gateway to the revenue authority.

Tax — V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits: manages authority queries,
audit findings, and voluntary disclosures.

Tax — V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change: tracks legislative and
regulatory developments and assesses impact on tax positions.

Treasury — V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance: initiates payment of tax
liabilities or lodges claims for refunds with the tax authority.

Legal — V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits: provides legal counsel
on uncertain tax positions and formal audit responses.

External Tax Adviser — V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers: provides
technical opinions and independent review of return workpapers.

External Tax Adviser — V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits: advises
on audit strategy and assists in preparing authority responses.

External Tax Adviser — V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change: supplies
legislative updates, impact analysis, and advisory opinions.

Tax Authority — V24.07 Lodge Return: receives the lodged return and
issues lodgement confirmation.

Tax Authority — V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance: receives tax payments
and processes refund claims.

Tax Authority — V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits: issues queries,
audit findings, rulings, and assessments; receives disclosures and
supporting documentation.

The boundary contains all ten subprocesses that take a transaction
from initial capture through tax determination, liability calculation,
account reconciliation, return preparation, review, lodgement,
settlement, audit response, and legislative monitoring. It serves the
Tax Authority as the primary regulatory recipient, Customers and
Suppliers as counterparties supplying transaction evidence, and
External Tax Advisers as technical specialists, while the internal
teams of Tax, Finance / Accounting, Treasury, and Legal carry out the
work within the organisation.
```
