**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V24 - Transaction to Return

Draw a single left-to-right sequence of ten chevron shapes, one per
high-level process stage, in the order listed below. Each chevron must
display its stage code and name. No swimlanes, no data flows, and no
system icons appear in this diagram — only the ordered chevron sequence.

V24.01. Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes
V24.02. Determine Tax Treatment
V24.03. Calculate Liabilities & Credits
V24.04. Reconcile Tax Accounts
V24.05. Prepare Return & Workpapers
V24.06. Review & Approve
V24.07. Lodge Return
V24.08. Pay or Claim Balance
V24.09. Respond to Queries & Audits
V24.10. Monitor Legislative Change

This chain converts raw financial transactions into compliant tax
returns and settles the resulting obligations with the Tax Authority.
It is triggered by a statutory lodgement period ending, a transaction
with tax consequences, or a query or audit initiated by the Tax
Authority. Moving left to right, the chain progresses from capturing
taxable transactions through treatment determination, liability
calculation, account reconciliation, return preparation, internal
review, electronic lodgement, and payment or refund claim, closing
with ongoing responses to authority queries and surveillance of
legislative change that feeds back into future cycles.
```
### V24.01 — Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes — first subprocess
of the Transaction to Return value chain, capturing transactional data
with tax attributes from customers and suppliers into the ERP and
general ledger.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity running the tax compliance process,
  containing Finance / Accounting with key role financial accountant.
Pool "Customer" — external party supplying tax invoices and exemption
  certificates for sales-side transactions.
Pool "Supplier" — external party supplying tax invoices and exemption
  certificates for purchase-side transactions.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger" — system recording transactions, tax codes
  and attributes across the organisation.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Supplier
3. Organisation
4. ERP / General Ledger

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Finance / Accounting lane:

  Message start event "Tax invoice or exemption certificate received
    from Customer or Supplier"
  User task "Log and classify incoming tax document"
  User task "Verify tax invoice completeness and validity"
  Exclusive gateway "Document valid?"
  - branch "No — document incomplete or invalid":
      User task "Request corrected document from counterparty"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected document received"
      Sequence flow rejoins at Exclusive merge gateway
        "Document valid check complete"
  - branch "Yes — document valid":
      Sequence flow continues to Exclusive merge gateway
        "Document valid check complete"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Document valid check complete"
  User task "Identify applicable tax attributes (tax type, jurisdiction,
    rate, exemption status)"
  User task "Assign tax codes to transaction line items"
  Exclusive gateway "Tax treatment determinable from existing rules?"
  - branch "No — uncertain or novel tax position":
      User task "Flag transaction for Tax team review"
      End event "Uncertain transaction escalated — ready for
        Determine Tax Treatment"
  - branch "Yes — tax codes assigned":
      Service task "Record transaction with tax attributes in
        ERP / General Ledger"
      User task "Attach supporting tax document to transaction record"
      End event "Transaction with tax attributes captured — ready for
        Determine Tax Treatment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Request corrected
  document from counterparty" — label "Correction overdue (follow-up
  period elapsed)" — triggers User task "Escalate missing document to
  tax manager" which leads to End event "Escalation raised — process
  on hold pending corrected document".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Finance / Accounting lane on receipt
of a tax document, proceeds through validation, with the invalid branch
looping through a corrected-document wait before rejoining the merge
gateway, then continuing through tax attribute identification, code
assignment, and the determinability gateway, whose uncertain branch ends
in escalation and whose confirmed branch ends after recording in the ERP.

Message flows:
Customer → Organisation / Finance / Accounting (tax invoice or exemption
  certificate — sales side)
Supplier → Organisation / Finance / Accounting (tax invoice or exemption
  certificate — purchase side)
Organisation / Finance / Accounting → Customer (request for corrected
  tax document, where applicable)
Organisation / Finance / Accounting → Supplier (request for corrected
  tax document, where applicable)
Organisation / Finance / Accounting → ERP / General Ledger (transaction
  record with tax codes and attributes written via Service task)
ERP / General Ledger → Organisation / Finance / Accounting (confirmation
  of transaction recorded, supporting task "Attach supporting tax
  document to transaction record")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Tax Invoice" — written by "Log and classify incoming tax
  document"; read by "Verify tax invoice completeness and validity";
  read by "Attach supporting tax document to transaction record".
Data Object "Exemption Certificate" — written by "Log and classify
  incoming tax document"; read by "Identify applicable tax attributes
  (tax type, jurisdiction, rate, exemption status)".
Data Object "Transaction Record with Tax Attributes" — written by
  "Assign tax codes to transaction line items"; read by "Record
  transaction with tax attributes in ERP / General Ledger".

This subprocess receives tax invoices and exemption certificates from
customers and suppliers, validates their completeness, assigns the
appropriate tax codes and attributes to each transaction line, and
records the coded transactions in the ERP and general ledger. Confirmed
transactions with full tax attributes, and separately any transactions
flagged as uncertain, are both handed forward to Determine Tax Treatment,
where the Tax team applies jurisdiction-specific rules and resolves any
positions that could not be determined from existing codes alone.
```


### V24.02 — Determine Tax Treatment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.02 Determine Tax Treatment — second subprocess in the
Transaction to Return value chain, receiving tax-attributed transactions
from Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes and handing confirmed tax
treatment to Calculate Liabilities & Credits.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity determining the correct tax treatment
  for each captured transaction, run by the Tax team.
Pool "Tax Determination Engine" — system that holds rate and rule tables
  and applies jurisdiction- and product-specific tax determination rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Determination Engine" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, one lane)
2. Tax Determination Engine (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane (indirect tax analyst):
  Message start event "Tax-attributed transaction data received from
    Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes"
  User task "Review transaction for tax relevance"
  Exclusive gateway "Transaction has tax consequence?"
  - branch "No — non-taxable": End event "Transaction marked
      non-taxable — no further treatment required"
  - branch "Yes — taxable": continues below
  Exclusive merge gateway "Transaction has tax consequence"
  User task "Classify transaction by jurisdiction and product type"
  Service task "Query rate and rule tables in Tax Determination Engine"
  Intermediate message catch event "Determination rules and rates
    returned"
  User task "Assess applicable exemptions and concessions"
  Exclusive gateway "Exemption or concession applicable?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Record exemption basis and supporting
      reference"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Exemption assessed"
  - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Exemption assessed"
  User task "Assign tax codes and treatment to transaction"
  Exclusive gateway "Tax treatment clear and supportable?"
  - branch "Yes — supportable": continues below
  - branch "No — uncertain position":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Position Resolved"
        (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Document
        uncertain tax position", User task "Escalate to tax manager
        for technical review", User task "Revise treatment based on
        review outcome"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Tax treatment clear and supportable"
  User task "Record confirmed tax treatment against transaction"
  Service task "Write confirmed treatment to Tax Determination Engine"
  End event "Tax treatment confirmed — ready for Calculate
    Liabilities & Credits"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Position Resolved", labelled "Lodgement deadline reached", leading to
  End event "Position unresolved at deadline — escalated outside
  subprocess".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The single Tax lane runs from the message start event
through relevance review, the taxable/non-taxable gateway (the
non-taxable branch ends immediately; the taxable branch continues),
to classification, engine query, catch event, exemption assessment
(with its two branches merging before code assignment), to the
supportability gateway (the uncertain branch enters the loop subprocess
before merging back), to final recording and write-back, ending at
the end event.

Message flows:
  Tax lane "Query rate and rule tables in Tax Determination Engine" →
    Tax Determination Engine (jurisdiction and product query)
  Tax Determination Engine → Intermediate message catch event
    "Determination rules and rates returned" (rate and rule tables,
    prior-period comparatives)
  Tax lane "Write confirmed treatment to Tax Determination Engine" →
    Tax Determination Engine (confirmed tax codes and treatment)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Transaction Record" — read by "Review transaction for
  tax relevance"; read by "Classify transaction by jurisdiction and
  product type".
Data Object "Determination Rules and Rates" — read by "Assess
  applicable exemptions and concessions"; written by service task
  "Query rate and rule tables in Tax Determination Engine".
Data Object "Exemption Reference" — written by "Record exemption
  basis and supporting reference"; read by "Assign tax codes and
  treatment to transaction".
Data Object "Uncertain Tax Position Note" — written by "Document
  uncertain tax position"; read by "Escalate to tax manager for
  technical review".
Data Object "Confirmed Tax Treatment" — written by "Record confirmed
  tax treatment against transaction"; read by "Write confirmed
  treatment to Tax Determination Engine".

This subprocess takes each tax-attributed transaction captured in
V24.01 and, by querying the Tax Determination Engine against
jurisdiction and product rules, establishes whether a tax consequence
exists, which exemptions or concessions apply, and what the correct tax
codes are. Uncertain positions are escalated and resolved in a
structured loop before treatment is finalised. The confirmed treatment
record, held on the transaction and written back to the Tax
Determination Engine, is then available to Calculate Liabilities &
Credits to begin computing what is actually owed or recoverable.
```


### V24.03 — Calculate Liabilities & Credits

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits — third subprocess in the
Transaction to Return value chain, receiving coded transactions from Determine
Tax Treatment and producing calculated liabilities and credits ready for
Reconcile Tax Accounts.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the tax calculation process,
  containing the Tax team lane.
Pool "Tax Determination Engine" — tax calculation and rate-rule system.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger" — enterprise resource planning and ledger system.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Determination Engine": black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger": black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation
2. Tax Determination Engine
3. ERP / General Ledger

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane:
  Message start event "Tax-coded transactions received from Determine
    Tax Treatment"
  Service task "Retrieve transaction data and tax codes from ERP"
  Service task "Pull applicable rate and rule tables from Tax
    Determination Engine"
  User task "Review rate and rule tables for completeness and
    currency"
  Exclusive gateway "Rules complete and current?"
    - branch "No — rules require update": User task "Request rule
      table correction from Tax team"; Intermediate message catch
      event "Updated rules received from Tax Determination Engine";
      Exclusive merge gateway "Rules complete and current?"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Rules complete and
      current?"
  Service task "Submit transactions to Tax Determination Engine for
    liability calculation"
  Intermediate message catch event "Calculated liabilities and
    credits returned"
  User task "Review calculated output for reasonableness"
  Exclusive gateway "Output reasonable?"
    - branch "No — variances identified": Expanded Subprocess
      "Repeat Until Variances Resolved" (standard loop) containing,
      in order: User task "Investigate variance", User task
      "Adjust input data or tax codes", Service task "Resubmit
      transactions to Tax Determination Engine", Intermediate
      message catch event "Revised output received", User task
      "Review revised output for reasonableness"; Exclusive merge
      gateway "Output reasonable?"
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Output reasonable?"
  User task "Classify liabilities and credits by tax type and
    jurisdiction"
  User task "Apply prior-period comparative review"
  Exclusive gateway "Material difference from prior period?"
    - branch "Yes — escalation required": User task "Document
      uncertain tax position and escalate to tax manager"; User
      task "Record escalation outcome and rationale"; Exclusive
      merge gateway "Material difference from prior period?"
    - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Material difference
      from prior period?"
  Service task "Post calculated liabilities and credits to ERP /
    General Ledger"
  User task "Record tax provision entries and effective-rate
    calculation"
  End event "Liabilities and credits calculated — ready for
    Reconcile Tax Accounts"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
Until Variances Resolved", labelled "Variance resolution deadline
exceeded", triggering User task "Escalate unresolved variance to
tax manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all elements flow top to bottom within the Tax lane.
The "Rules complete and current?" gateway branches to the correction
loop, which rejoins at the merge gateway before proceeding to
submission. The "Output reasonable?" gateway branches into the
variance-resolution subprocess, which rejoins at the merge gateway
before classification. The "Material difference from prior period?"
gateway branches to the escalation tasks, which rejoin at the merge
gateway before posting to the ledger.

Message flows:
  Tax lane "Retrieve transaction data and tax codes from ERP" →
    ERP / General Ledger (request for transaction detail and tax
    attribute data).
  ERP / General Ledger → Tax lane "Retrieve transaction data and
    tax codes from ERP" (transaction records with tax codes and
    ledger balances).
  Tax lane "Pull applicable rate and rule tables from Tax
    Determination Engine" → Tax Determination Engine (request for
    rate and rule tables).
  Tax Determination Engine → Tax lane "Pull applicable rate and
    rule tables from Tax Determination Engine" (rate and rule
    tables by jurisdiction and tax type).
  Tax Determination Engine → Tax lane "Request rule table
    correction from Tax team" (updated rule tables).
  Tax lane "Submit transactions to Tax Determination Engine for
    liability calculation" → Tax Determination Engine (coded
    transaction batch for calculation).
  Tax Determination Engine → Tax lane "Calculated liabilities and
    credits returned" (calculated liability and credit output).
  Tax lane "Resubmit transactions to Tax Determination Engine" →
    Tax Determination Engine (corrected transaction batch).
  Tax Determination Engine → Tax lane "Revised output received"
    (revised liability and credit output).
  Tax lane "Post calculated liabilities and credits to ERP /
    General Ledger" → ERP / General Ledger (liability and credit
    amounts for posting).
  ERP / General Ledger → Tax lane "Post calculated liabilities and
    credits to ERP / General Ledger" (posting confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Tax-Coded Transaction Batch" — read by "Retrieve
  transaction data and tax codes from ERP"; written by the preceding
  subprocess (Determine Tax Treatment).
Data Object "Rate and Rule Tables" — read by "Review rate and rule
  tables for completeness and currency"; written by "Pull applicable
  rate and rule tables from Tax Determination Engine".
Data Object "Calculated Liability and Credit Output" — written by
  "Calculated liabilities and credits returned"; read by "Review
  calculated output for reasonableness".
Data Object "Variance Investigation Record" — written by
  "Investigate variance"; read by "Adjust input data or tax codes".
Data Object "Uncertain Tax Position Note" — written by "Document
  uncertain tax position and escalate to tax manager"; read by
  "Record escalation outcome and rationale".
Data Object "Tax Provision and Effective-Rate Schedule" — written
  by "Record tax provision entries and effective-rate calculation".

This subprocess takes tax-coded transactions from Determine Tax
Treatment and, using the Tax Determination Engine and ERP rate tables,
produces verified, jurisdiction-classified liability and credit figures
together with a tax provision and effective-rate schedule. Unresolved
variances are escalated before any figures are posted. The confirmed
posted balances are handed to Reconcile Tax Accounts, which will
match them to the general ledger.
```


### V24.04 — Reconcile Tax Accounts

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts — sits in the Transaction to Return
value chain between Calculate Liabilities & Credits and Prepare Return &
Workpapers.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity performing tax account reconciliation.
  Lane "Finance / Accounting" — financial accountant running ledger-side
    reconciliation tasks.
  Lane "Tax" — tax accountant validating tax balances and resolving
    variances.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger" — system providing ledger balances and
  recording reconciliation adjustments.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, with Finance / Accounting lane above Tax lane)
2. ERP / General Ledger

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Finance / Accounting lane:
  Message start event "Calculated liabilities and credits received from
    Calculate Liabilities & Credits"
  Service task "Extract ledger balances for tax accounts"
  Service task "Extract sub-ledger and transaction detail"
  User task "Compile opening and closing tax account balances"
  Intermediate message catch event "Ledger extract confirmed by ERP /
    General Ledger"
  User task "Map ledger balances to tax liability schedule"
  Send task "Forward mapped balances to Tax for validation"

Tax lane:
  User task "Receive mapped balances and tax liability schedule"
  User task "Compare tax liability schedule to calculated liabilities"
  Exclusive gateway "Variances identified?"
    - branch "No variances": proceed to sign-off
    - branch "Variances identified": enter variance resolution subprocess
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Variances Resolved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Investigate source of variance",
    User task "Classify variance as timing, permanent or error",
    User task "Prepare correcting journal or adjustment"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Variances identified?"
  User task "Document reconciliation outcome and adjustments"
  User task "Obtain Tax accountant sign-off on reconciliation"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation approved?"
    - branch "Approved": proceed to notify Finance / Accounting
    - branch "Not approved": return to Finance / Accounting for re-extraction
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation approved?"
  Send task "Notify Finance / Accounting of approved reconciliation"

Finance / Accounting lane (continued):
  User task "Post approved adjustments to ledger"
  Service task "Record finalised reconciliation in ERP / General Ledger"
  End event "Reconciled tax accounts confirmed — ready for Prepare Return
    & Workpapers"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All
  Variances Resolved", labelled "Variance resolution deadline exceeded",
  leading to an escalation End event "Escalate unresolved variances to Tax
  Manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Finance / Accounting lane initiates the process from the
message start event, flowing through extraction and mapping tasks before
handing to Tax lane. In the Tax lane, flow passes through comparison, then
branches at the "Variances identified?" gateway — the variance branch enters
the standard-loop subprocess and rejoins at the merge gateway; the no-
variance branch bypasses the subprocess and also rejoins at the same merge
gateway. Flow continues through documentation and sign-off, then branches
at "Reconciliation approved?" — the approved branch rejoins the merge
gateway and continues to the send task; the not-approved branch returns
to the Finance / Accounting lane for re-extraction, rejoining the main
flow at "Map ledger balances to tax liability schedule". Finance /
Accounting lane then closes with posting and ERP recording before the
end event.

Message flows:
  ERP / General Ledger → Finance / Accounting lane (ledger and sub-ledger
    balance extract)
  Finance / Accounting lane → ERP / General Ledger (approved adjustments
    and finalised reconciliation entries)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Tax Liability Schedule" — written by "Compare tax liability
  schedule to calculated liabilities"; read by "Document reconciliation
  outcome and adjustments".
Data Object "Variance Analysis Report" — written by "Classify variance as
  timing, permanent or error"; read by "Prepare correcting journal or
  adjustment" and "Document reconciliation outcome and adjustments".
Data Object "Correcting Journal" — written by "Prepare correcting journal
  or adjustment"; read by "Post approved adjustments to ledger".

This subprocess reconciles the calculated tax liabilities and credits
against the general ledger balances, investigating and clearing any
variances through a repeating resolution loop before obtaining formal
sign-off and posting approved adjustments. The confirmed, adjusted ledger
positions and variance documentation are handed to Prepare Return &
Workpapers as the authoritative figures on which the return will be based.
```


### V24.05 — Prepare Return & Workpapers

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers — fifth subprocess in the
Transaction to Return value chain, converting reconciled tax account data
into a completed return draft and supporting workpapers ready for review.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity preparing the tax return and workpapers,
  with lanes for Tax.
Pool "External Tax Adviser" — external adviser engaged to review or
  contribute specialist input to the return draft.
Pool "Tax Reporting System" — system used to compile and draft the tax
  return.
Pool "Document Management System" — system used to store and retrieve
  workpapers and supporting documentation.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Tax Adviser" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Reporting System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. External Tax Adviser
2. Organisation
3. Tax Reporting System
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane:

Message start event "Reconciled tax accounts received from Reconcile
  Tax Accounts"
User task "Retrieve reconciled account balances and period data"
Service task "Import transaction and balance data into Tax Reporting
  System"
User task "Map tax codes and categories to return line items"
Service task "Generate return draft from mapped data"
User task "Compile supporting workpapers for each return line"
Exclusive gateway "Is specialist input required from external adviser?"
  - branch "Yes — specialist input required": Send task "Request
    specialist input from External Tax Adviser"
    Intermediate message catch event "Specialist input received from
    External Tax Adviser"
    User task "Incorporate adviser input into return draft and
    workpapers"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Specialist input required"
  - branch "No — no specialist input required": Exclusive merge gateway
    "Specialist input required"
User task "Cross-check return figures against workpapers and ledger
  balances"
Exclusive gateway "Do figures agree?"
  - branch "Yes — figures agree": Exclusive merge gateway "Figures
    agree"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Figures Agree" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Investigate and correct
    discrepancy", User task "Update return draft and workpapers in
    Tax Reporting System", User task "Re-cross-check return figures
    against workpapers and ledger balances"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Figures agree"
User task "Save finalised workpapers to Document Management System"
Service task "Record completed return draft status in Tax Reporting
  System"
User task "Assemble return package for review"
End event "Return draft and workpapers complete — ready for Review
  and Approve"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Request specialist input from
  External Tax Adviser", labelled "Adviser response overdue (lodgement
  calendar deadline approaching)" — triggers Send task "Send reminder
  to External Tax Adviser" and rejoins flow after the intermediate
  message catch event.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow runs entirely within the Tax lane. After the start
event, tasks proceed in order through data import, mapping, draft
generation and workpaper compilation to the first exclusive gateway.
The "Yes" branch sends the adviser request, waits for the reply, and
incorporates it before rejoining at the merge gateway; the "No" branch
skips directly to the merge. After the merge, cross-checking proceeds
to the second exclusive gateway. The "Yes — figures agree" branch
passes straight to the merge gateway; the "No — discrepancy found"
branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and exits to the same merge.
After the merge, finalised workpapers are saved, the draft status is
recorded, the package is assembled, and the end event closes the
subprocess.

Message flows:
Organisation (Send task "Request specialist input from External Tax
  Adviser") → External Tax Adviser (specialist input request).
External Tax Adviser → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Specialist input received from External Tax Adviser") (specialist
  input and commentary).
Organisation (Service task "Import transaction and balance data into
  Tax Reporting System") → Tax Reporting System (period transaction
  and balance data).
Tax Reporting System → Organisation (Service task "Generate return
  draft from mapped data") (generated return draft).
Organisation (User task "Save finalised workpapers to Document
  Management System") → Document Management System (finalised
  workpapers and supporting documents).
Organisation (Service task "Record completed return draft status in
  Tax Reporting System") → Tax Reporting System (return draft
  completion status).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Reconciled Account Balances" — read by "Retrieve
  reconciled account balances and period data".
Data Object "Return Draft" — written by "Generate return draft from
  mapped data"; read by "Cross-check return figures against workpapers
  and ledger balances"; written by "Incorporate adviser input into
  return draft and workpapers"; written by "Update return draft and
  workpapers in Tax Reporting System".
Data Object "Workpapers Package" — written by "Compile supporting
  workpapers for each return line"; read by "Cross-check return figures
  against workpapers and ledger balances"; written by "Update return
  draft and workpapers in Tax Reporting System".
Data Object "Specialist Adviser Input" — read by "Incorporate adviser
  input into return draft and workpapers".

V24.05 transforms reconciled ledger balances into a complete, cross-
checked return draft supported by documented workpapers. It draws in
specialist external adviser input where needed, resolves any figure
discrepancies through a controlled loop, and stores all artefacts in
the Document Management System. The assembled return package is handed
to V24.06 Review & Approve for sign-off before lodgement.
```


### V24.06 — Review & Approve

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.06 Review & Approve — the quality-gate subprocess in which the
tax manager reviews, challenges and formally approves the completed return
and workpapers before lodgement.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity preparing and approving the tax return,
  with lanes for Tax.
Pool "Tax Reporting System" — system supporting review workflow and
  return storage.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Reporting System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation
2. Tax Reporting System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane:

Message start event "Completed return and workpapers received from
  Prepare Return & Workpapers"
Service task "Retrieve return package from Tax Reporting System"
User task "Review return figures and workpapers"
Exclusive gateway "Issues identified?"
  - branch "Yes — issues found": User task "Document review findings
      and required corrections"
    Send task "Return review findings to Tax team for correction"
    Intermediate message catch event "Corrected return package received"
    User task "Re-review corrected return package"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Issues identified?"
  - branch "No — review passed": (continues to approval gateway)
Exclusive merge gateway "Issues identified?"
Exclusive gateway "Uncertain tax position present?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Escalate uncertain tax position to tax
      manager and Legal"
    Intermediate message catch event "Legal opinion received"
    User task "Apply legal opinion and update return position"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Uncertain tax position present?"
  - branch "No": (continues to merge)
Exclusive merge gateway "Uncertain tax position present?"
User task "Record formal approval of return in Tax Reporting System"
User task "Sign off return package"
End event "Return approved — ready for Lodge Return"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess implied by the
  re-review loop — not applicable here as no subprocess is looped.
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Re-review corrected return package"
  labelled "Review deadline exceeded" — triggers User task "Escalate
  overdue review to tax manager"; flow ends at Terminate end event
  "Review escalated — process on hold".
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  'Legal opinion received'" labelled "Legal opinion overdue (5 business
  days)" — triggers User task "Chase legal opinion"; flow rejoins at
  Intermediate message catch event "Legal opinion received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Tax lane with the start event and
  proceeds through retrieval, review and the first gateway. The "Yes"
  branch for issues runs through findings documentation, the send task,
  the catch event and re-review before merging back at the first exclusive
  merge gateway. The "No" branch and the merge gateway output both
  continue to the uncertain-tax-position gateway. The "Yes" branch there
  goes through escalation, the legal-opinion catch event and position
  update before merging at the second merge gateway. Both branches then
  proceed to formal approval recording, sign-off and the end event.

Message flows:
Tax Reporting System → "Retrieve return package from Tax Reporting
  System" (return package including draft return and workpapers)
"Record formal approval of return in Tax Reporting System" → Tax
  Reporting System (approval record and signed-off return package)
"Send task 'Return review findings to Tax team for correction'" →
  Tax Reporting System (review findings log for the Tax team's
  correction workflow)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Return Package" — read by "Review return figures and
  workpapers"; read by "Re-review corrected return package"; written by
  "Apply legal opinion and update return position"; read by "Sign off
  return package".
Data Object "Review Findings" — written by "Document review findings
  and required corrections"; read by "Re-review corrected return package".
Data Object "Legal Opinion" — read by "Apply legal opinion and update
  return position"; written by "Escalate uncertain tax position to tax
  manager and Legal".

V24.06 Review & Approve is the quality and governance gate in the
Transaction to Return chain. The tax manager subjects the completed return
package and workpapers to structured review, resolves any issues or
uncertain tax positions — drawing on legal opinion where needed — and then
formally records approval. The signed-off, approved return package is
handed to Lodge Return, where it will be transmitted to the Tax Authority.
```


### V24.07 — Lodge Return

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.07 Lodge Return — the subprocess in which the tax manager
submits the approved tax return to the Tax Authority via the e-filing
gateway, obtains a lodgement confirmation, and hands the confirmed filing
record to Pay or Claim Balance.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that manage lodgement of the
return.
  Lane "Tax" — tax manager who authorises and oversees lodgement.
Pool "Tax Authority" — the revenue office that receives the return and
issues the lodgement confirmation.
Pool "E-Filing Gateway" — the electronic submission system that routes
the return to the Tax Authority.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Authority" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "E-Filing Gateway" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Tax Authority
2. Organisation (white-box, Lane: Tax)
3. E-Filing Gateway

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane:
  Message start event "Approved return received from Review & Approve"
  User task "Confirm lodgement deadline and jurisdiction requirements"
  User task "Package return and supporting documentation for submission"
  Service task "Submit return via E-Filing Gateway"
  Intermediate message catch event "Lodgement confirmation received"
  Exclusive gateway "Submission accepted?"
    - branch "Yes — confirmation received": proceed to record lodgement
    - branch "No — error or rejection returned":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Submission Accepted"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Review rejection reason and correct return package",
          Service task "Resubmit corrected return via E-Filing Gateway",
          Intermediate message catch event "Resubmission response received"
        Timer boundary event "Lodgement deadline exceeded" mounted on
        this subprocess, interrupting, leading to escalation end event
        "Escalate overdue lodgement — deadline missed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Submission accepted"
  User task "Record lodgement confirmation and filing date"
  User task "Store lodgement confirmation in document repository"
  End event "Return lodged and confirmed — ready for Pay or Claim Balance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "Lodgement deadline exceeded" — mounted
on the Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Submission Accepted"; triggers
an escalation end event labelled "Escalate overdue lodgement — deadline
missed"; does not rejoin the main flow.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the Tax lane runs in the order given above. After the
"Submission accepted?" exclusive gateway, the "Yes" branch proceeds
directly to the exclusive merge gateway "Submission accepted"; the "No"
branch enters the loop subprocess, whose normal exit also rejoins the
same merge gateway. From the merge gateway the flow continues to "Record
lodgement confirmation and filing date", then "Store lodgement
confirmation in document repository", then the end event. The timer
boundary event on the loop subprocess exits to the escalation end event
and does not return.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Submit return via E-Filing Gateway") →
    E-Filing Gateway (return package submitted for routing)
  E-Filing Gateway → Tax Authority (return transmitted to revenue office)
  Tax Authority → E-Filing Gateway (acceptance or rejection response)
  E-Filing Gateway → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
    "Lodgement confirmation received") (lodgement confirmation or error
    detail)
  E-Filing Gateway → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
    "Resubmission response received") (resubmission acceptance or error
    detail)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Tax Return" — read by User task "Package return
and supporting documentation for submission".
Data Object "Lodgement Deadline Schedule" — read by User task "Confirm
lodgement deadline and jurisdiction requirements".
Data Object "Return Submission Package" — written by User task "Package
return and supporting documentation for submission"; read by Service
task "Submit return via E-Filing Gateway".
Data Object "Rejection Notice" — read by User task "Review rejection
reason and correct return package".
Data Object "Lodgement Confirmation" — written by User task "Record
lodgement confirmation and filing date"; read by User task "Store
lodgement confirmation in document repository".

This subprocess takes the reviewed and approved return and formally
lodges it with the Tax Authority through the E-Filing Gateway, handling
any rejection-and-resubmission cycle within a standard-loop subprocess
bounded by the lodgement deadline. On successful acceptance it records
and stores the confirmation receipt, then passes the confirmed filing
record to Pay or Claim Balance so that the resulting liability or refund
can be settled.
```


### V24.08 — Pay or Claim Balance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance — the subprocess in which Treasury
settles the net tax balance with the Tax Authority, either by making a
payment or lodging a refund claim, following the lodged return in V24.07.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity settling its tax balance, with Treasury
  and Tax lanes.
Pool "Tax Authority" — the revenue office receiving payment or processing
  the refund claim.
Pool "Treasury & Payment System" — the payment and banking platform used
  to execute and record transactions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Authority" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Treasury & Payment System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Tax Authority
2. Organisation
3. Treasury & Payment System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Treasury lane:
  Message start event "Lodged return and balance assessment received from
    Lodge Return"
  User task "Review assessed balance and confirm net position"
  Exclusive gateway "Net position?"
  - branch "liability — tax is owed":
      User task "Initiate payment to Tax Authority"
      Service task "Submit payment instruction to Treasury and Payment
        System"
      Intermediate message catch event "Payment confirmation received"
      User task "Record payment and update payment ledger"
      End event "Payment made — ready for Respond to Queries and Audits"
  - branch "credit — refund is due":
      User task "Prepare and lodge refund claim with Tax Authority"
      Send task "Transmit refund claim to Tax Authority"
      Intermediate message catch event "Refund decision received from Tax
        Authority"
      Exclusive gateway "Refund approved?"
      - branch "approved":
          Intermediate message catch event "Refund receipt confirmed"
          User task "Record refund receipt and update payment ledger"
          End event "Refund received — ready for Respond to Queries and
            Audits"
      - branch "rejected or queried":
          User task "Escalate refund dispute to Tax lane"
          End event "Refund disputed — escalated to Respond to Queries
            and Audits"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Refund approved?"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Net position?"

Tax lane:
  User task "Review escalated refund dispute and prepare response"
  Send task "Submit additional documentation to Tax Authority"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Initiate payment to Tax Authority"
  — label "Payment deadline reached" — triggers End event "Payment
  overdue — escalate to Tax Authority".
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Prepare and lodge refund claim with
  Tax Authority" — label "Claim submission deadline reached" — triggers
  End event "Claim filing overdue — escalate".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The flow begins in the Treasury lane, where the balance
is reviewed and the net-position gateway branches either to the liability
path or the credit path. The liability branch runs through payment
initiation, system submission, confirmation catch, and recording, then
ends. The credit branch runs through claim preparation, transmission, a
catch event for the refund decision, the refund-approved gateway, and
then either to receipt recording and end, or to the Tax lane for dispute
handling and end; both branches of the refund gateway merge at "Refund
approved?" before the outer merge at "Net position?". The Tax lane tasks
for dispute handling are reached by sequence flow from the rejected
branch before its end event.

Message flows:
Tax Authority → Organisation / Treasury lane (assessed balance and
  lodgement confirmation — triggers start event).
Organisation / Treasury lane → Tax Authority (payment instruction or
  refund claim submission).
Treasury & Payment System → Organisation / Treasury lane (payment
  confirmation and receipt details).
Organisation / Treasury lane → Treasury & Payment System (payment
  instruction submitted via service task).
Tax Authority → Organisation / Treasury lane (refund decision —
  approved, rejected, or query).
Tax Authority → Organisation / Treasury lane (refund funds receipt
  confirmation).
Organisation / Tax lane → Tax Authority (additional documentation for
  disputed refund).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Assessed Tax Balance" — read by "Review assessed balance
  and confirm net position"; written by "Review assessed balance and
  confirm net position".
Data Object "Payment Instruction" — written by "Initiate payment to Tax
  Authority"; read by "Submit payment instruction to Treasury and Payment
  System".
Data Object "Payment Confirmation" — written by intermediate message
  catch event "Payment confirmation received"; read by "Record payment
  and update payment ledger".
Data Object "Refund Claim" — written by "Prepare and lodge refund claim
  with Tax Authority"; read by "Transmit refund claim to Tax Authority".
Data Object "Refund Decision Notice" — written by intermediate message
  catch event "Refund decision received from Tax Authority"; read by
  exclusive gateway "Refund approved?".
Data Object "Dispute Response Package" — written by "Review escalated
  refund dispute and prepare response"; read by "Submit additional
  documentation to Tax Authority".

V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance takes the net position established by the
lodged return and drives it to financial settlement. Treasury either
executes a payment to the Tax Authority or pursues a refund claim,
recording the outcome in the payment ledger. Any disputed refund is
escalated to the Tax lane for documentation and resubmission. The
subprocess hands a fully settled or formally escalated balance position
to V24.09 Respond to Queries and Audits.
```


### V24.09 — Respond to Queries & Audits

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits — the subprocess in which the
organisation receives, investigates, and formally responds to tax authority
queries and audit requests, supported by Legal and External Tax Advisers,
handing outcomes back to the ongoing compliance cycle.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity managing the query and audit response process,
  with lanes for Tax and Legal.
Pool "Tax Authority" — the external revenue authority issuing queries, audit
  notices, and assessments.
Pool "External Tax Adviser" — outside counsel or tax advisory firm providing
  specialist opinions and review support.
Pool "Document Management System" — the internal system storing workpapers,
  correspondence, and supporting documentation.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Authority" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "External Tax Adviser" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Tax Authority
2. Organisation
3. External Tax Adviser
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane:

Message start event "Query or audit notice received from Tax Authority"
User task "Log and classify query or audit notice"
Service task "Retrieve relevant workpapers and lodged return"
Exclusive gateway "Nature of query?"
- branch "Routine information request": User task "Compile factual response
  and supporting documents"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Nature of query resolved"
- branch "Formal audit or complex query": User task "Convene response team
  and brief Legal and External Tax Adviser"
  Intermediate message catch event "Adviser opinion received"
  User task "Review adviser opinion and consolidate organisation position"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Nature of query resolved"
Exclusive gateway "Position defensible?"
- branch "Yes": User task "Prepare formal written response"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Position assessed"
- branch "No — uncertain tax position": User task "Escalate to tax manager
  and consider voluntary disclosure"
  User task "Prepare voluntary disclosure or amended response"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Position assessed"
Service task "Store response and correspondence in Document Management System"
Send task "Submit response to Tax Authority"
Intermediate message catch event "Authority determination or assessment
  received"
Exclusive gateway "Determination acceptable?"
- branch "Accepted": User task "Record outcome and close query file"
  End event "Query resolved — outcome recorded for Monitor Legislative Change"
- branch "Disputed": User task "Document grounds for objection or appeal"
  End event "Dispute escalated — refer to Legal for objection or appeal"

Legal lane:

User task "Assess legal risk and provide counsel on disputed positions"
User task "Review final response for legal sufficiency prior to submission"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Compile factual response and
  supporting documents" — label "Statutory response deadline reached" — flow
  continues to User task "Escalate to tax manager and consider voluntary
  disclosure" in the Tax lane.
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Prepare formal written
  response" — label "Response deadline reached" — flow continues to Send task
  "Submit response to Tax Authority" immediately, bypassing further review.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Tax lane at the message start event and
moves through logging, classification, and document retrieval before reaching
the "Nature of query?" gateway. The routine branch goes directly to compiling
a response; the formal audit branch routes through the Legal lane for risk
assessment and adviser briefing before rejoining at the merge gateway. After
the merge, the "Position defensible?" gateway splits to either direct response
preparation or escalation and voluntary disclosure, both rejoining at "Position
assessed". The Legal lane task "Review final response for legal sufficiency"
sits between "Position assessed" and the service task writing to the Document
Management System. Flow then passes through submission, the intermediate catch
event awaiting authority determination, the "Determination acceptable?"
gateway, and ends in one of two end events.

Message flows:
Tax Authority → Organisation / Tax lane (query or audit notice — trigger)
Organisation / Tax lane → Tax Authority (formal written response or voluntary
  disclosure — submitted via Send task)
Tax Authority → Organisation / Tax lane (determination or assessment — received
  at intermediate catch event)
External Tax Adviser → Organisation / Tax lane (adviser opinion — received at
  intermediate message catch event "Adviser opinion received")
Organisation / Tax lane → External Tax Adviser (case data, questions, and
  position papers — sent during "Convene response team and brief Legal and
  External Tax Adviser")
Organisation / Tax lane → Document Management System (response package and
  correspondence — written by "Store response and correspondence in Document
  Management System")
Document Management System → Organisation / Tax lane (workpapers and lodged
  return — read by "Retrieve relevant workpapers and lodged return")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Query or Audit Notice" — written by User task "Log and classify
  query or audit notice"; read by Exclusive gateway "Nature of query?".
Data Object "Response Package" — written by User task "Prepare formal written
  response" and User task "Prepare voluntary disclosure or amended response";
  read by Send task "Submit response to Tax Authority".
Data Object "Adviser Opinion" — written by External Tax Adviser pool; read by
  User task "Review adviser opinion and consolidate organisation position".
Data Object "Legal Risk Assessment" — written by User task "Assess legal risk
  and provide counsel on disputed positions"; read by User task "Review final
  response for legal sufficiency prior to submission".
Data Object "Authority Determination" — written by intermediate message catch
  event "Authority determination or assessment received"; read by Exclusive
  gateway "Determination acceptable?".

This subprocess receives a query or audit notice from the Tax Authority and
guides the Tax and Legal teams through classifying the matter, gathering
evidence, obtaining external advice where needed, and submitting a defensible
formal response within statutory deadlines. Accepted determinations are closed
and their outcomes fed into the Monitor Legislative Change subprocess; disputed
assessments are packaged with grounds for objection and referred to Legal for
further action.
```


### V24.10 — Monitor Legislative Change

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change — final subprocess of the
Transaction to Return value chain, closing the compliance cycle by
tracking new tax legislation and updating internal rules and policies.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the entity's internal teams running the
monitoring and update process.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Tax (tax manager)
Pool "External Tax Adviser" — external adviser providing legislative
analysis and opinion.
Pool "Tax Reporting System" — system holding tax rules, rate tables,
and policy documentation.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Tax Adviser" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Reporting System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. External Tax Adviser
2. Organisation
3. Tax Reporting System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Tax lane:
  Message start event "Legislative or regulatory change signal received
    from External Tax Adviser"
  User task "Log and categorise incoming legislative change"
  User task "Assess applicability and materiality to the organisation"
  Exclusive gateway "Material impact identified?"
    - branch "No — not material": End event "Change noted as
        non-material — no further action required"
    - branch "Yes — material": continue to next steps
  Exclusive merge gateway "Material impact identified"
  Send task "Request detailed legislative analysis from External Tax
    Adviser"
  Intermediate message catch event "Legislative analysis received from
    External Tax Adviser"
  User task "Review adviser analysis and identify affected tax
    treatments"
  Exclusive gateway "Policy or rule update required?"
    - branch "No — existing policy adequate": End event "Analysis
        filed — existing policy confirmed adequate"
    - branch "Yes — update required": continue to next steps
  Exclusive merge gateway "Policy or rule update required"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Rules and Policy Updated" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Draft updated tax treatment
    rules and rate table changes", User task "Update tax policy
    documentation and governance records", Service task "Apply updated
    rules and rate tables in Tax Reporting System", User task "Validate
    updated rules against sample transactions"
  User task "Communicate changes to affected teams and stakeholders"
  User task "Record legislative change and update lodgement calendar
    if deadlines affected"
  End event "Legislative change embedded — monitoring cycle complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Rules and Policy Updated" — label "Update overdue: policy deadline
reached" — triggers escalation End event "Escalate overdue update to
tax manager for urgent resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work proceeds within the Tax lane from the message
start event through logging, assessment, and the materiality gateway.
The non-material branch ends immediately. The material branch
continues through the merge gateway to the send task, then waits at
the intermediate message catch event before review and the second
gateway. The non-update branch ends immediately. The update branch
continues through the merge gateway into the loop subprocess, then
to communication and calendar update tasks before the final end event.

Message flows:
External Tax Adviser → Organisation / Tax lane (legislative change
  signal — initial notification of new or amended legislation).
Organisation / Tax lane → External Tax Adviser (request for detailed
  legislative analysis — send task output).
External Tax Adviser → Organisation / Tax lane (legislative analysis
  report — reply to analysis request).
Organisation / Tax lane → Tax Reporting System (updated tax treatment
  rules and rate tables — written during the loop subprocess service
  task).
Tax Reporting System → Organisation / Tax lane (current rate tables
  and rule configurations — read during validation task inside the
  loop subprocess).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Legislative Change Notice" — written by "Log and
  categorise incoming legislative change"; read by "Assess
  applicability and materiality to the organisation".
Data Object "Materiality Assessment Record" — written by "Assess
  applicability and materiality to the organisation"; read by
  "Request detailed legislative analysis from External Tax Adviser".
Data Object "Legislative Analysis Report" — written by (External Tax
  Adviser, via message flow); read by "Review adviser analysis and
  identify affected tax treatments".
Data Object "Updated Tax Treatment Rules" — written by "Draft updated
  tax treatment rules and rate table changes"; read by "Apply updated
  rules and rate tables in Tax Reporting System".

V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change scans incoming legislative and
regulatory signals, assesses their materiality, commissions external
adviser analysis where needed, and then iteratively updates internal
tax treatment rules, rate tables, and policy documentation until the
organisation's compliance framework reflects the new law. By embedding
the changes in the Tax Reporting System and notifying affected teams,
this subprocess ensures that every subsequent cycle of the Transaction
to Return chain — beginning again at V24.01 — operates under current
rules, closing the governance loop for the value chain.
```


## V25 — Data to Insight

**Teams and roles involved.**
Data to Insight usually involves Data Engineering, Data Platform/Operations, Analytics and Business Intelligence, Data Governance and Stewardship, Privacy, and the consuming Business Units. Key roles include data engineer, platform engineer, analytics engineer, data analyst, data scientist, data steward, data owner, privacy officer, and the business sponsor who acts on the result.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Data Providers — third-party data vendors, partners and public data sources — and, where analytics affects them, the Data Subjects whose information is used. The process is initiated by a business question, a scheduled reporting cycle, a new data source becoming available, or a model requiring retraining. Other external parties include cloud and tooling vendors, and regulators where automated decision-making is in scope.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: capture the business question and success measure, identify and assess sources, ingest data, validate quality and profile it, transform and model it, catalogue and document lineage, build the analysis, model or report, review and validate the result, publish and enable access, and monitor usage, accuracy and drift.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include ingestion and pipeline orchestration, data lake and warehouse platforms, transformation tooling, data quality and observability, the data catalogue and lineage store, business intelligence and visualisation, machine-learning platforms and feature stores, access management, and cost and usage monitoring.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include data governance framework and ownership, data classification and handling rules, privacy and consent constraints on secondary use, data quality standards and thresholds, model risk management and validation requirements, access and least-privilege rules, retention and deletion schedules, and change control for pipelines and published reports.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Data providers supply feeds, extracts, schemas and licence terms, and receive usage reporting or payment. Data subjects exercise access, correction and deletion rights, which the process must honour across the platform. Business sponsors provide the question, context and acceptance of results, and receive insights, dashboards and recommendations.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates ingestion jobs, curated datasets, transformation logic, quality rules and results, catalogue entries and lineage, models and their versions, dashboards and reports, and access grants. IT systems provide source schemas and volumes, pipeline run status and failures, quality metrics, model performance and drift signals, and usage, cost and adoption reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V25.01** Capture Business Question | Business Sponsor | Analytics (data analyst) | Business Intelligence Platform |
| **V25.02** Identify & Assess Sources | Data Provider | Data Engineering (data engineer), Data Governance (data steward) | Data Catalogue |
| **V25.03** Ingest Data | Data Provider | Data Engineering (data engineer) | Ingestion & Orchestration Platform, Data Lake |
| **V25.04** Validate Quality & Profile | — | Data Engineering (data engineer), Data Governance (data steward) | Data Quality & Observability Platform |
| **V25.05** Transform & Model Data | — | Analytics Engineering (analytics engineer) | Transformation Tooling, Data Warehouse |
| **V25.06** Catalogue & Document Lineage | — | Data Governance (data steward) | Data Catalogue |
| **V25.07** Build Analysis, Model or Report | — | Analytics (data analyst), Data Science (data scientist) | Business Intelligence Platform, Machine Learning Platform |
| **V25.08** Review & Validate Result | Business Sponsor | Analytics (data analyst), Data Governance (data owner) | Business Intelligence Platform |
| **V25.09** Publish & Enable Access | Data Subject | Data Platform (platform engineer), Privacy (privacy officer) | Business Intelligence Platform, Access Management System |
| **V25.10** Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift | — | Data Platform (platform engineer), Data Science (data scientist) | Data Quality & Observability Platform, Machine Learning Platform |

**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V25 — Data to Insight — Service & Application Landscape
(high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Data to Insight value chain, from the initial business question
through to ongoing monitoring of published insights. The layout uses three
horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES → BUSINESS PROCESSES →
APPLICATIONS. The demand-side actor (Business Sponsor) sits on the far
left; supply-side external participants (Data Provider, Data Subject) sit
on the far right. The view is read top-to-bottom as service → process →
application, expressing ArchiMate service realisation across the chain.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Business Sponsor: demand-side actor, far left; initiates the chain by
  providing the business question and accepts the resulting insights.
- Data Provider: supply-side actor, far right; supplies data feeds,
  extracts, schemas and licence terms to the ingestion steps.
- Data Subject: supply-side actor, far right; exercises access, correction
  and deletion rights affecting published data.

2. Interfaces

- Business Question Interface: accessed by Business Sponsor; serves the
  Question Framing & Scoping service and the Insight Delivery service.
- Data Supply Interface: accessed by Data Provider; serves the Source
  Assessment & Ingestion service.
- Data Rights Interface: accessed by Data Subject; serves the Governed
  Access & Publishing service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Question Framing & Scoping: captures and structures the business
  question, success measure and scope before any data work begins.
- Source Assessment & Ingestion: identifies, assesses, licences and
  ingests data from internal and external providers.
- Data Quality & Validation: profiles ingested data, enforces quality
  standards and thresholds, and gates downstream use.
- Data Transformation & Modelling: transforms raw data into curated,
  analytical models ready for analysis.
- Cataloguing & Lineage: registers datasets, documents lineage and
  maintains the authoritative metadata record.
- Analysis, Modelling & Reporting: builds analyses, statistical or ML
  models, dashboards and reports against curated data.
- Review & Acceptance: validates results against the business question,
  quality standards and model risk requirements.
- Governed Access & Publishing: publishes approved insights and manages
  access under least-privilege and privacy controls.
- Usage, Accuracy & Drift Monitoring: continuously monitors consumption,
  model accuracy and data drift across the platform.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V25.01 Capture Business Question
- V25.02 Identify & Assess Sources
- V25.03 Ingest Data
- V25.04 Validate Quality & Profile
- V25.05 Transform & Model Data
- V25.06 Catalogue & Document Lineage
- V25.07 Build Analysis, Model or Report
- V25.08 Review & Validate Result
- V25.09 Publish & Enable Access
- V25.10 Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Business Intelligence Platform: supports question capture, report and
  dashboard building, result review and published access.
- Data Catalogue: supports source assessment and lineage documentation.
- Ingestion & Orchestration Platform: supports pipeline creation and
  scheduled data ingestion.
- Data Lake: stores raw ingested data at scale.
- Data Quality & Observability Platform: supports quality profiling,
  validation and ongoing drift monitoring.
- Transformation Tooling: supports transformation logic authoring and
  execution.
- Data Warehouse: stores curated, modelled analytical datasets.
- Machine Learning Platform: supports model building, versioning and
  serving; includes feature store capability.
- Access Management System: enforces access grants and least-privilege
  rules at publication.

6. Relationships

SERVING (business service serves business actor or process)
- Question Framing & Scoping serves Business Sponsor.
- Source Assessment & Ingestion serves Data Provider.
- Governed Access & Publishing serves Data Subject.
- Governed Access & Publishing serves Business Sponsor.
- Usage, Accuracy & Drift Monitoring serves Business Sponsor.

REALISATION (business process realises business service)
- V25.01 Capture Business Question realises Question Framing & Scoping.
- V25.02 Identify & Assess Sources realises Source Assessment &
  Ingestion.
- V25.03 Ingest Data realises Source Assessment & Ingestion.
- V25.04 Validate Quality & Profile realises Data Quality & Validation.
- V25.05 Transform & Model Data realises Data Transformation & Modelling.
- V25.06 Catalogue & Document Lineage realises Cataloguing & Lineage.
- V25.07 Build Analysis, Model or Report realises Analysis, Modelling &
  Reporting.
- V25.08 Review & Validate Result realises Review & Acceptance.
- V25.09 Publish & Enable Access realises Governed Access & Publishing.
- V25.10 Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift realises Usage, Accuracy &
  Drift Monitoring.

ASSIGNMENT (application component assigned to business process)
- Business Intelligence Platform assigned to V25.01 Capture Business
  Question.
- Data Catalogue assigned to V25.02 Identify & Assess Sources.
- Ingestion & Orchestration Platform assigned to V25.03 Ingest Data.
- Data Lake assigned to V25.03 Ingest Data.
- Data Quality & Observability Platform assigned to V25.04 Validate
  Quality & Profile.
- Transformation Tooling assigned to V25.05 Transform & Model Data.
- Data Warehouse assigned to V25.05 Transform & Model Data.
- Data Catalogue assigned to V25.06 Catalogue & Document Lineage.
- Business Intelligence Platform assigned to V25.07 Build Analysis,
  Model or Report.
- Machine Learning Platform assigned to V25.07 Build Analysis, Model or
  Report.
- Business Intelligence Platform assigned to V25.08 Review & Validate
  Result.
- Business Intelligence Platform assigned to V25.09 Publish & Enable
  Access.
- Access Management System assigned to V25.09 Publish & Enable Access.
- Data Quality & Observability Platform assigned to V25.10 Monitor
  Usage, Accuracy & Drift.
- Machine Learning Platform assigned to V25.10 Monitor Usage, Accuracy &
  Drift.

ACCESS (actor or process accesses interface)
- Business Sponsor accesses Business Question Interface.
- Data Provider accesses Data Supply Interface.
- Data Subject accesses Data Rights Interface.
- V25.01 Capture Business Question accesses Business Question Interface.
- V25.03 Ingest Data accesses Data Supply Interface.
- V25.09 Publish & Enable Access accesses Data Rights Interface.
```

```text
monitoring of usage, accuracy and drift.
```
