### V25.01 — Capture Business Question

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.01 Capture Business Question — first subprocess of the Data to
Insight value chain, triggered by a business sponsor and producing a
confirmed question and success measure ready for source identification.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that capture, clarify and confirm
the business question and success measure.
  Lane "Analytics" — data analyst who receives the question, facilitates
  scoping and records the confirmed brief.
Lane "Business Sponsor" — external business unit representative who
  initiates the request and accepts the scoped question.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — BI and reporting system used to
  log the question and surface any existing related reports.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Sponsor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Business Sponsor
2. Organisation (Analytics lane)
3. Business Intelligence Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Analytics lane:
  Message start event "Business question received from Business Sponsor"
  User task "Log and register question request"
  Service task "Check for existing reports or analyses"
  Intermediate message catch event "Existing report search result returned"
  Exclusive gateway "Existing asset sufficient?"
  - branch "Yes — existing asset meets need":
      User task "Present existing asset to Business Sponsor"
      Intermediate message catch event "Business Sponsor response received"
      Exclusive gateway "Sponsor accepts existing asset?"
      - branch "Yes — accepted": End event "Existing asset confirmed —
        no further analysis required"
      - branch "No — new analysis needed": continue to Exclusive merge
        gateway "Existing asset sufficient"
  - branch "No — new analysis needed": continue to Exclusive merge
    gateway "Existing asset sufficient"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Existing asset sufficient"
  User task "Facilitate question scoping session"
  User task "Document business question and context"
  User task "Define success measures and acceptance criteria"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Brief Confirmed" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Share drafted brief with Business
    Sponsor", Intermediate message catch event "Sponsor feedback received",
    User task "Revise brief based on feedback"
  User task "Record confirmed brief in Business Intelligence Platform"
  User task "Classify data sensitivity and flag privacy considerations"
  End event "Confirmed brief ready — ready for Identify and Assess Sources"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event, interrupting, attached to Expanded Subprocess
"Repeat Until Brief Confirmed", label "Brief not confirmed within
10 business days" — leads to End event "Brief escalated — timed out
without sponsor sign-off".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Analytics lane at the message start
event, passes through question logging and the existing-asset check, then
through the exclusive gateway "Existing asset sufficient?". The "Yes"
branch passes through presentation and a sponsor-response catch event into
a nested gateway; its "Yes — accepted" branch ends at its own end event
and does not rejoin; its "No" branch rejoins the merge. The "No" branch
from the outer gateway also rejoins the merge. From the merge, flow
continues through scoping, documentation, success-measure definition, the
loop subprocess, brief recording, and privacy classification, ending at
the process end event.

Message flows:
Business Sponsor → Organisation / Analytics (business question submission
  and trigger)
Organisation / Analytics → Business Sponsor (drafted brief for review)
Business Sponsor → Organisation / Analytics (feedback and sign-off on
  brief)
Organisation / Analytics → Business Intelligence Platform (confirmed brief
  logged and registered)
Business Intelligence Platform → Organisation / Analytics (existing report
  or analysis search results)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Business Question Request" — written by User task "Log and
  register question request"; read by User task "Facilitate question
  scoping session".
Data Object "Scoped Brief" — written by User task "Document business
  question and context"; read by User task "Share drafted brief with
  Business Sponsor" and User task "Record confirmed brief in Business
  Intelligence Platform".
Data Object "Success Measures and Acceptance Criteria" — written by User
  task "Define success measures and acceptance criteria"; read by User task
  "Record confirmed brief in Business Intelligence Platform".
Data Object "Privacy and Sensitivity Flag" — written by User task
  "Classify data sensitivity and flag privacy considerations".

This subprocess captures, scopes and confirms the business question and
its success measures before any data work begins. It ensures a sponsor-
approved brief exists, screens for existing assets that may already
answer the need, and attaches an initial privacy and sensitivity flag.
The confirmed brief and acceptance criteria are handed to Identify and
Assess Sources, giving that subprocess a clear statement of what data
will be needed and how the result will be judged.
```


### V25.02 — Identify & Assess Sources

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.02 Identify & Assess Sources — second subprocess of the Data to
Insight value chain, receiving a captured business question and determining
which data sources are fit for use before ingestion begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out source identification
and assessment.
  Lane "Data Engineering" — data engineer identifying candidate sources
  and assessing technical fitness.
  Lane "Data Governance" — data steward assessing compliance, licensing
  and classification suitability.
Pool "Data Provider" — external third-party data vendors, partners and
public data sources supplying metadata, schemas and licence terms.
Pool "Data Catalogue" — the data catalogue system recording source
assessments and approved source entries.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Catalogue" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Provider
2. Organisation
3. Data Catalogue

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Captured business question received from
  Capture Business Question"
  User task "Identify candidate data sources"
  User task "Request source metadata and schema from providers"
  Intermediate message catch event "Source metadata and schema received"
  User task "Assess technical fitness of each source"
  Exclusive gateway "Sources technically adequate?"
  - branch "yes": continue to data governance assessment
  - branch "no — no viable source": End event "No adequate source found
    — process terminated"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sources technically adequate"
  User task "Compile source assessment summary"

Data Governance lane:
  User task "Review data classification and handling requirements"
  User task "Assess licensing, consent and privacy constraints"
  Exclusive gateway "Source approved for use?"
  - branch "approved": continue to catalogue registration
  - branch "not approved — compliance issue": User task "Document
    rejection reason and notify data engineer"; End event "Source
    rejected on compliance grounds — process terminated"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Source approved for use"
  User task "Record approved source in data catalogue"
  Send task "Confirm source approval to Data Engineering"
  Intermediate message catch event "Catalogue entry confirmed"
  End event "Approved sources catalogued — ready for Ingest Data"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request source metadata and schema
from providers" — label "Provider response overdue (5 business days)"
— flow continues to User task "Escalate non-response to data engineer
lead" then rejoins before "Assess technical fitness of each source".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Data Engineering lane with the start
event and candidate identification, moves to requesting and receiving
metadata, then technical assessment with a gateway branching to
termination on no viable source or continuing to compile the summary.
Flow then crosses to the Data Governance lane for classification review,
licensing and privacy assessment, with a gateway branching to a
rejection end event on non-approval or continuing to catalogue
registration and confirmation, before the final end event.

Message flows:
Data Engineering → Data Provider (request for source metadata, schema
and licence terms).
Data Provider → Data Engineering (source metadata, schema and licence
terms supplied).
Data Governance → Data Catalogue (approved source entry written).
Data Catalogue → Data Governance (catalogue entry confirmation returned).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Business Question and Success Measures" — read by "Identify
candidate data sources".
Data Object "Candidate Source List" — written by "Identify candidate
data sources"; read by "Assess technical fitness of each source".
Data Object "Source Metadata and Schema" — written by message receipt
from Data Provider; read by "Assess technical fitness of each source".
Data Object "Technical Assessment Report" — written by "Assess technical
fitness of each source"; read by "Compile source assessment summary".
Data Object "Source Assessment Summary" — written by "Compile source
assessment summary"; read by "Review data classification and handling
requirements".
Data Object "Licence and Privacy Constraint Record" — written by "Assess
licensing, consent and privacy constraints"; read by "Record approved
source in data catalogue".
source in data catalogue".

This subprocess takes the captured business question and works through
technical and governance lenses to determine which data sources are
suitable for use. Data Engineering identifies candidates, requests
schemas and assesses technical fitness, while Data Governance checks
classification, licensing and privacy constraints. The result — a set
of approved, catalogued sources — is handed to Ingest Data so that
pipeline work can begin on a governed, compliant foundation.
```


### V25.03 — Ingest Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.03 Ingest Data — third subprocess of the Data to Insight value
chain, taking assessed and approved sources and loading them into the data
lake via managed ingestion pipelines.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that configure, run and
  monitor ingestion pipelines.
  Lane "Data Engineering" — data engineers who build ingestion jobs,
    trigger runs, handle failures and confirm successful loads.
Pool "Data Provider" — external third-party vendors, partners and
  public data sources that supply feeds, extracts and schemas.
Pool "Ingestion & Orchestration Platform" — the pipeline orchestration
  system that schedules and executes ingestion jobs.
Pool "Data Lake" — the storage platform that receives and holds
  ingested raw datasets.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Ingestion & Orchestration Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Data Lake" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Provider
2. Organisation
3. Ingestion & Orchestration Platform
4. Data Lake

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Approved source list received from Identify
    and Assess Sources"
  User task "Review source specifications and access credentials"
  User task "Configure or update ingestion job"
  Service task "Register ingestion job in orchestration platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Job registration confirmed"
  User task "Trigger ingestion run"
  Intermediate message catch event "Pipeline run status received"
  Exclusive gateway "Run successful?"
    - branch "Yes": proceed to next step
    - branch "No": proceed to failure handling
  Expanded Subprocess "Retry Until Ingestion Succeeds" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Diagnose pipeline failure",
    User task "Resolve configuration or connectivity issue",
    Service task "Retrigger ingestion job",
    Intermediate message catch event "Retry run status received"
    Timer boundary event "48-hour retry limit" on the subprocess,
      interrupting, leading to End event "Ingestion failed —
      escalated to Data Engineering lead"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Run successful"
  Service task "Validate raw file receipt in data lake"
  Intermediate message catch event "Data lake load confirmation
    received"
  Exclusive gateway "Load confirmed?"
    - branch "Yes": proceed to completion
    - branch "No, load error": User task "Raise load error and notify
        platform team", then End event "Load error escalated —
        awaiting platform resolution"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Load confirmed"
  User task "Record ingestion run metadata and dataset location"
  End event "Raw dataset loaded — ready for Validate Quality and
    Profile"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "48-hour retry limit" on Expanded
  Subprocess "Retry Until Ingestion Succeeds" — triggers End event
  "Ingestion failed — escalated to Data Engineering lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work moves top to bottom through the Data Engineering
  lane. After "Run successful?" the "Yes" branch and the resolved
  retry path both rejoin at exclusive merge gateway "Run successful"
  before proceeding to load validation. The "Load confirmed?" gateway
  sends the "No, load error" branch to its own terminal End event,
  while the "Yes" branch rejoins at exclusive merge gateway "Load
  confirmed" and continues to metadata recording and the final End
  event.

Message flows:
  Data Provider → Organisation / Data Engineering (source feed,
    extract or schema supplied for ingestion)
  Organisation / Data Engineering → Ingestion & Orchestration
    Platform (ingestion job registration request)
  Ingestion & Orchestration Platform → Organisation / Data Engineering
    (job registration confirmed)
  Organisation / Data Engineering → Ingestion & Orchestration
    Platform (ingestion run trigger)
  Ingestion & Orchestration Platform → Organisation / Data Engineering
    (pipeline run status — success or failure)
  Ingestion & Orchestration Platform → Data Lake (raw data written
    during pipeline execution)
  Data Lake → Organisation / Data Engineering (load confirmation
    and dataset location)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Source List" — read by User task "Review source
  specifications and access credentials".
Data Object "Source Access Credentials" — read by User task
  "Configure or update ingestion job".
Data Object "Ingestion Job Configuration" — written by User task
  "Configure or update ingestion job"; read by Service task "Register
  ingestion job in orchestration platform".
Data Object "Pipeline Run Log" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Pipeline run status received"; read by User task
  "Diagnose pipeline failure" and Service task "Validate raw file
  receipt in data lake".
Data Object "Ingestion Run Metadata" — written by User task "Record
  ingestion run metadata and dataset location".

This subprocess takes the approved and prioritised source list from
Identify and Assess Sources, builds or updates the necessary ingestion
pipelines, executes the data load, and confirms that raw files are
correctly seated in the data lake with run metadata recorded. A
successfully loaded raw dataset, together with its location reference
and pipeline log, is handed to Validate Quality and Profile, where
content and structure will be assessed before any further processing
begins.
```


### V25.04 — Validate Quality & Profile

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.04 Validate Quality & Profile — quality-gates and profiling step
sitting between ingestion and transformation in the Data to Insight chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that validate and profile ingested
  data, applying quality standards and escalating failures.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Data Engineering (data engineer)
  - Data Governance (data steward)

Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — IT system that executes
  quality checks, profiles datasets, and surfaces metrics and alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, contains all lanes)
2. Data Quality & Observability Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Ingested dataset received from Ingest Data"
  Service task "Trigger quality and profiling run"
  Intermediate message catch event "Quality run results received"
  User task "Review profiling summary and quality scores"
  Exclusive gateway "Quality thresholds met?"
  - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Quality thresholds met"
  - branch "No": User task "Classify and log quality failures"
      Exclusive gateway "Failures blocking?"
      - branch "Recoverable — remediate": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
          Quality Thresholds Met" (standard loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Apply remediation to ingested dataset",
          Service task "Re-trigger quality and profiling run",
          Intermediate message catch event "Re-run results received",
          User task "Review updated quality scores"
          Timer boundary event on subprocess labelled "48-hour remediation
          limit"; on expiry: escalation flow to Data Governance lane
      - branch "Blocking — cannot remediate": End event "Dataset rejected —
          ingestion halted"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Failures blocking"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quality thresholds met"
  User task "Annotate dataset with quality status and profile metadata"
  End event "Dataset validated and profiled — ready for Transform and
      Model Data"

Data Governance lane:
  User task "Review quality failure report"
  Exclusive gateway "Escalation action required?"
  - branch "Approve remediation": Sequence flow rejoining remediation
      subprocess in Data Engineering lane
  - branch "Reject dataset": Send task "Notify Data Engineering of
      rejection decision"
      End event "Quality exception closed — dataset quarantined"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Escalation action required"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Quality Thresholds Met", labelled "48-hour remediation limit"; on
  expiry the flow leaves the subprocess and enters the Data Governance
  lane at User task "Review quality failure report".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Data Engineering lane at the message
start event, proceeds through triggering the run, receiving results,
reviewing scores, and reaching the "Quality thresholds met?" gateway.
The "Yes" branch merges immediately; the "No" branch passes through
"Classify and log quality failures" and the "Failures blocking?" gateway,
whose "Recoverable" branch enters the remediation subprocess and whose
"Blocking" branch ends in the rejection end event. The timer boundary
escalation exits the subprocess and flows into the Data Governance lane;
the Governance gateway's "Approve remediation" branch returns to the
Data Engineering lane to continue the subprocess; the "Reject dataset"
branch ends in a separate end event. All surviving paths rejoin at
"Quality thresholds met" and continue to annotation and the final end
event.

Message flows:
Data Engineering lane (Service task "Trigger quality and profiling run")
  → Data Quality & Observability Platform (quality and profiling job
  submission).
Data Quality & Observability Platform → Data Engineering lane
  (Intermediate message catch event "Quality run results received")
  (quality scores, profile statistics, threshold breach alerts).
Data Engineering lane (Service task "Re-trigger quality and profiling
  run") → Data Quality & Observability Platform (re-run request for
  remediated dataset).
Data Quality & Observability Platform → Data Engineering lane
  (Intermediate message catch event "Re-run results received")
  (updated quality scores and profile).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Ingested Dataset" — read by User task "Review profiling
  summary and quality scores"; read by User task "Apply remediation to
  ingested dataset".
Data Object "Quality Run Results" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Quality run results received"; read by User task "Review
  profiling summary and quality scores".
Data Object "Quality Failure Report" — written by User task "Classify
  and log quality failures"; read by User task "Review quality failure
  report".
Data Object "Remediated Dataset" — written by User task "Apply
  remediation to ingested dataset"; read by Service task "Re-trigger
  quality and profiling run".
Data Object "Quality Profile Annotation" — written by User task
  "Annotate dataset with quality status and profile metadata".

V25.04 Validate Quality & Profile receives the ingested dataset from
V25.03 and subjects it to automated quality checks and statistical
profiling via the Data Quality & Observability Platform, with human
review by Data Engineering and, where failures are escalating, Data
Governance. Datasets that clear thresholds, or are remediated to pass
them, are annotated with their quality status and profile metadata and
handed to V25.05 Transform & Model Data; datasets that cannot be
remediated are quarantined and the ingestion is halted.
```


### V25.05 — Transform & Model Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.05 Transform & Model Data — sits within the Data to Insight
value chain, receiving validated and profiled data from Validate Quality &
Profile and handing a curated, modelled dataset to Catalogue & Document
Lineage.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out transformation
and modelling work.
  Lane "Analytics Engineering" — analytics engineer who designs,
  builds, and tests transformation logic and data models.
Pool "Transformation Tooling" — the transformation execution and
  orchestration tool that runs SQL or code-based transformation jobs.
Pool "Data Warehouse" — the target platform where curated, modelled
  datasets are written and stored.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Transformation Tooling" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Data Warehouse" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, contains all lanes)
2. Transformation Tooling
3. Data Warehouse

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Analytics Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Validated profiled dataset received from
    Validate Quality & Profile"
  User task "Review profiled dataset and define transformation scope"
  User task "Design or update transformation logic and data model"
  Service task "Trigger transformation job in Transformation Tooling"
  Intermediate message catch event "Transformation job result received"
  Exclusive gateway "Transformation job succeeded?"
    - branch "No — job failed": User task "Diagnose and fix
        transformation errors"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Transformation job succeeded?"
      (loop back handled as subprocess below)
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Transformation job
        succeeded?"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Transformation Passes" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Diagnose and fix
    transformation errors", Service task "Trigger transformation job
    in Transformation Tooling", Intermediate message catch event
    "Transformation job result received"
  User task "Review transformed output and validate model structure"
  Exclusive gateway "Model structure acceptable?"
    - branch "No — rework required": User task "Revise model
        definition and rebuild"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Model structure acceptable?"
      (loop handled as subprocess below)
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Model structure
        acceptable?"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Model Accepted" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Revise model definition and
    rebuild", Service task "Trigger transformation job in
    Transformation Tooling", Intermediate message catch event
    "Transformation job result received", User task "Review
    transformed output and validate model structure"
  User task "Apply data classification and handling rules to output"
  User task "Document transformation logic and model version"
  Service task "Write curated dataset to Data Warehouse"
  Intermediate message catch event "Dataset write confirmed"
  End event "Curated modelled dataset ready — proceed to Catalogue
    & Document Lineage"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Transformation Passes" — label "Max retry period elapsed" —
  flows to End event "Transformation failed — escalate to Data
  Engineering".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Model Accepted" — label "Modelling review deadline exceeded"
  — flows to End event "Model review timed out — escalate to Data
  Engineering".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Analytics Engineering lane and
proceeds top to bottom. The "Transformation job succeeded?" gateway
branches to the "Repeat Until Transformation Passes" subprocess on
failure and continues directly past the merge on success. The "Model
structure acceptable?" gateway branches to the "Repeat Until Model
Accepted" subprocess on failure and continues directly past the merge
on success. Both subprocesses carry timer boundary escalations that
exit to their respective error End events without rejoining the main
flow. After both gateways are satisfied, the flow continues through
classification, documentation, warehouse write, and confirmation
before reaching the End event.

Message flows:
  Analytics Engineering (Service task "Trigger transformation job in
    Transformation Tooling") → Transformation Tooling (transformation
    job execution request).
  Transformation Tooling → Analytics Engineering (Intermediate message
    catch event "Transformation job result received") (job completion
    status and run log).
  Analytics Engineering (Service task "Write curated dataset to Data
    Warehouse") → Data Warehouse (curated modelled dataset).
  Data Warehouse → Analytics Engineering (Intermediate message catch
    event "Dataset write confirmed") (write confirmation and table
    metadata).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Profiled Dataset" — read by "Review profiled
  dataset and define transformation scope".
Data Object "Transformation Scope Definition" — written by "Review
  profiled dataset and define transformation scope"; read by "Design
  or update transformation logic and data model".
Data Object "Transformation Logic and Model Definition" — written by
  "Design or update transformation logic and data model"; read by
  "Trigger transformation job in Transformation Tooling"; read by
  "Document transformation logic and model version".
Data Object "Transformation Job Run Log" — read by "Review
  transformed output and validate model structure".
Data Object "Model Version Record" — written by "Document
  transformation logic and model version".

V25.05 takes the validated, profiled dataset produced by V25.04 and
applies analytics-engineering-designed transformation logic to produce
a clean, structured, version-tracked data model written to the Data
Warehouse. The subprocess ensures transformation jobs succeed within
retry and deadline limits, that model structure is reviewed and
accepted, and that classification and handling rules are applied before
the curated dataset is confirmed in storage. The verified curated
dataset and its model version record are then handed to V25.06
Catalogue & Document Lineage for formal cataloguing and lineage
capture.
```


### V25.06 — Catalogue & Document Lineage

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.06 Catalogue & Document Lineage — registers curated datasets,
transformation logic and lineage records in the data catalogue following
Transform & Model Data, making assets discoverable for downstream analysis.

1. Pools & Lanes

lineage.

  registration, applies classifications, reviews lineage completeness and

Pool "Data Catalogue" — the catalogue and lineage store system that receives
and persists all entries.

Pool "Data Catalogue" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box)
2. Data Catalogue (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Governance (data steward) lane:
  Message start event "Transformed dataset and model artefacts received
    from Transform & Model Data"
  User task "Register dataset asset in catalogue"
  Service task "Submit asset registration to Data Catalogue"
  Intermediate message catch event "Asset record confirmed by Data Catalogue"
  User task "Apply data classification and handling tags"
  Service task "Submit classification tags to Data Catalogue"
  Intermediate message catch event "Tags persisted by Data Catalogue"
  User task "Document transformation logic and pipeline steps"
  User task "Map source-to-target lineage"

  Intermediate message catch event "Lineage graph confirmed by Data Catalogue"
  User task "Review catalogue entry and lineage completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Entry complete and lineage verified?"
    - branch "No — gaps found":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Entry Complete" (standard loop)
          containing, in order: User task "Identify and resolve catalogue

          Intermediate message catch event "Corrections confirmed by

        Exclusive merge gateway "Repeat Until Entry Complete"
    - branch "Yes — entry approved":
        continue to next element
  Exclusive merge gateway "Entry complete and lineage verified?"

  End event "Catalogue entry published — ready for Build Analysis,

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all steps run within the Data Governance lane in the order
listed above. The exclusive gateway "Entry complete and lineage verified?"
branches to the "Repeat Until Entry Complete" loop subprocess on the "No"
branch, which rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway "Entry complete and
lineage verified?", and continues straight through on the "Yes" branch,

and publication.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Submit asset registration to Data Catalogue")
    → Data Catalogue (asset registration payload)
  Data Catalogue → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event "Asset
    record confirmed by Data Catalogue") (registration confirmation)
  Organisation (Service task "Submit classification tags to Data Catalogue")
    → Data Catalogue (classification and handling tags)
  Data Catalogue → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event "Tags
    persisted by Data Catalogue") (tag persistence confirmation)
  Organisation (Service task "Submit lineage graph to Data Catalogue")
    → Data Catalogue (lineage graph)
  Data Catalogue → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event "Lineage
    graph confirmed by Data Catalogue") (lineage confirmation)
  Organisation (Service task "Submit corrections to Data Catalogue")

  Data Catalogue → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event

7. Data objects

V25.06 Catalogue & Document Lineage takes the curated datasets and model
artefacts produced by Transform & Model Data and registers them as
```

### V25.07 — Build Analysis, Model or Report

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.07 Build Analysis, Model or Report — the subprocess in which
Analytics and Data Science teams construct the deliverable artefact (dashboard,
statistical analysis, or trained model) that answers the business question,
sitting between Transform & Model Data and Review & Validate Result in the
Data to Insight value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams building the analysis, model or report.
  Lane "Analytics" — data analyst who scopes and builds BI reports and analyses.
  Lane "Data Science" — data scientist who trains, evaluates and packages models.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — BI and visualisation system.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — ML experimentation, training and model
  registry system.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Organisation" — top (holds the process flow).
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — below Organisation.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — below Business Intelligence Platform.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Analytics lane:
  Message start event "Transformed data and models received from Transform &
    Model Data"
  User task "Review business question, success measures and deliverable type"
  Exclusive gateway "Deliverable type?"
  - branch "Analysis or report":
      User task "Design report structure and define visualisation requirements"
      Service task "Query curated dataset in BI Platform"
      User task "Build report or dashboard in BI Platform"
      User task "Annotate findings and draft narrative"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Deliverable type"
  - branch "Trained model":
      (flow passes to Data Science lane — see below)
      Exclusive merge gateway "Deliverable type"
  User task "Conduct internal analyst review of artefact"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Artefact Meets Quality Bar" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Identify gaps or errors in artefact",
    User task "Revise artefact and rerun queries or visuals"
  End event "Artefact ready — ready for Review & Validate Result"

Data Science lane:
  (Receives flow from "Deliverable type?" gateway branch "Trained model")
  User task "Define modelling approach, features and evaluation criteria"
  Service task "Register experiment and configure training run in ML Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Training run complete"
  User task "Evaluate model performance against success measures"
  Exclusive gateway "Performance acceptable?"
  - branch "No":
      User task "Adjust hyperparameters, features or training data"
      (returns to Expanded Subprocess — see note below)
  - branch "Yes":
      User task "Package and register model version in ML Platform"
      (flow returns to Analytics lane at Exclusive merge gateway
        "Deliverable type")
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Model Performance Acceptable" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Adjust hyperparameters, features or
    training data", Service task "Rerun training experiment in ML Platform",
    Intermediate message catch event "Retraining run complete",
    User task "Re-evaluate model performance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Artefact
  Meets Quality Bar" — label "Review deadline exceeded" — triggers End event
  "Artefact iteration timed out — escalate to Analytics lead".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Model
  Performance Acceptable" — label "Training iteration deadline exceeded" —
  triggers End event "Model training timed out — escalate to Data Science lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Analytics lane, passes through the deliverable
  type gateway splitting into an analytics/report branch (remaining in Analytics)
  and a model branch (crossing to Data Science); the Data Science branch runs
  through experiment registration, evaluation and the model performance gateway,
  looping inside the standard-loop subprocess until performance is acceptable,
  then rejoins Analytics at the merge gateway; both branches converge at
  "Exclusive merge gateway Deliverable type" before the internal review and the
  quality-bar loop subprocess, ending at the artefact-ready end event.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Analytics lane, "Query curated dataset in BI Platform") →
    Business Intelligence Platform (query request).
  Business Intelligence Platform → Organisation (Analytics lane,
    "Build report or dashboard in BI Platform") (query results and dataset).
  Organisation (Data Science lane, "Register experiment and configure training
    run in ML Platform") → Machine Learning Platform (experiment configuration
    and training job).
  Machine Learning Platform → Organisation (Data Science lane, Intermediate
    message catch event "Training run complete") (training run completion
    notification and metrics).
  Machine Learning Platform → Organisation (Data Science lane, Intermediate
    message catch event "Retraining run complete") (retraining completion
    notification and updated metrics).
  Organisation (Data Science lane, "Package and register model version in ML
    Platform") → Machine Learning Platform (model artefact and version metadata).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Business Question and Success Measures" — read by "Review business

Data Object "Report or Dashboard Specification" — written by "Design report
  structure and define visualisation requirements"; read by "Build report or
  dashboard in BI Platform".
Data Object "Query Results" — written by "Query curated dataset in BI Platform";
  read by "Build report or dashboard in BI Platform".
Data Object "Completed Report or Dashboard" — written by "Build report or
  dashboard in BI Platform"; read by "Annotate findings and draft narrative".
Data Object "Modelling Approach and Feature Specification" — written by "Define
  modelling approach, features and evaluation criteria"; read by "Register
  experiment and configure training run in ML Platform".
Data Object "Model Evaluation Results" — written by "Evaluate model performance
  against success measures"; read by "Package and register model version in ML

This subprocess produces the primary deliverable — a validated draft report,
dashboard or registered model version — that directly answers the business
question framed in Capture Business Question. It hands a completed, internally
reviewed artefact to Review & Validate Result, where the business sponsor and
data governance owner assess fitness for purpose before publication.
```

### V25.08 — Review & Validate Result

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.08 Review & Validate Result — the subprocess in which the completed
analysis, model or report is reviewed against acceptance criteria, validated by
governance, and either approved for publishing or returned for rework, forming
the final quality gate before access is enabled.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out the review and validation
  workflow, with lanes for Analytics and Data Governance.
Pool "Business Sponsor" — the external stakeholder who reviews the result and
  gives or withholds business sign-off.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — the BI and visualisation system used to
  view, annotate and record the review outcome.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Sponsor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Business Sponsor
2. Organisation (lanes top to bottom: Analytics, Data Governance)
3. Business Intelligence Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Analytics lane:
  Message start event "Analysis, model or report ready — received from Build
    Analysis, Model or Report"
  User task "Prepare result for review"
  Service task "Publish draft result to Business Intelligence Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Business Sponsor review response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Business sponsor satisfied?"
  - branch "No — rework required":
      User task "Log sponsor feedback and determine rework scope"
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Sponsor Satisfied" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Revise analysis or report",
        Service task "Re-publish revised result to Business Intelligence
          Platform", Intermediate message catch event "Business Sponsor
          review response received"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Business sponsor satisfied?"
  - branch "Yes — proceed to governance check":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Business sponsor satisfied?"
  User task "Compile review record and pass to Data Governance"

Data Governance lane:
  User task "Assess result against data quality standards and governance
    policy"
  Exclusive gateway "Governance check passed?"
  - branch "No — issue found":
      User task "Raise governance finding and request remediation"
      Intermediate message catch event "Remediation confirmed by Analytics"
      (rejoins at Exclusive merge gateway "Governance check passed?")
  - branch "Yes — approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Governance check passed?"
  User task "Record governance approval in Business Intelligence Platform"
  End event "Result validated and approved — ready for Publish and Enable
    Access"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Sponsor
  Satisfied" — label "Review cycle limit reached" — triggers an escalation
  end event "Review stalled — escalate to data owner" that does not rejoin
  the main flow.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the flow starts in the Analytics lane, moves through draft
  publication and sponsor review, with the rework loop repeating until
  the sponsor is satisfied, then continues to Data Governance for the policy
  and quality check, looping back if a finding is raised and awaiting
  remediation confirmation before governance approval is recorded and the
  end event fires.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Analytics) → Business Sponsor (draft result shared for review).
  Business Sponsor → Organisation (Analytics) (review response — satisfied or
    rework requested).
  Organisation (Analytics) → Business Intelligence Platform (draft result
    published for viewing).
  Organisation (Analytics) → Business Intelligence Platform (revised result
    re-published after each rework cycle).
  Organisation (Data Governance) → Business Intelligence Platform (governance
    approval recorded).
  Business Intelligence Platform → Organisation (Analytics) (platform
    confirmation of publication).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Draft Result Package" — written by "Prepare result for review";
  read by "Publish draft result to Business Intelligence Platform".
Data Object "Sponsor Review Response" — written by "Log sponsor feedback and
  determine rework scope"; read by "Compile review record and pass to Data
    Governance".
Data Object "Review Record" — written by "Compile review record and pass to
  Data Governance"; read by "Assess result against data quality standards and
  governance policy".
Data Object "Governance Finding" — written by "Raise governance finding and
  request remediation"; read by "Remediation confirmed by Analytics".

This subprocess acts as the final quality gate before any analysis, model or
report reaches end users. It ensures the business sponsor is satisfied with the
result and that the output meets data quality standards and governance policy.
An approved and documented result, with a complete review record, is then handed
to Publish and Enable Access so that audiences and permissions can be configured
and the insight made available.
```


### V25.09 — Publish & Enable Access

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.09 Publish & Enable Access — the subprocess that makes a

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Data Subject" — black-box, single instance.

Top to bottom:
1. Data Subject
2. Organisation (Data Platform lane above Privacy lane)
3. Business Intelligence Platform
4. Access Management System

Data Platform lane:
  Message start event "Validated result received from Review & Validate
  Result"
  User task "Define publication scope and classification"
  User task "Configure asset metadata and access tiers"
  Service task "Deploy asset to Business Intelligence Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Deployment confirmation received"
  User task "Draft access provisioning request"
  Send task "Submit access request for privacy review"

Privacy lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Access request received for review"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Access Request Cleared"
  (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review access request against privacy and consent
    constraints",
    User task "Apply least-privilege and data-classification rules",
    Exclusive gateway "Access request approved?"
  - branch "approved": exit subprocess
  - branch "not approved — revision required": cycle within subprocess

  Exclusive merge gateway "Access request approved"
  Send task "Return clearance decision to Data Platform"

Data Platform lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Clearance decision received"
  Exclusive gateway "Clearance granted?"
  - branch "granted": Service task "Provision access in Access
    Management System"
    Intermediate message catch event "Access grant confirmed"
    User task "Notify requestors and record provisioning"
    Exclusive gateway "Rights request pending from Data Subject?"
    - branch "yes": User task "Honour Data Subject access, correction
      or deletion request"
      Service task "Apply data-subject rights action across platform"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Rights request pending from Data
      Subject"
    - branch "no": Exclusive merge gateway "Rights request pending from
      Data Subject"
    End event "Asset published and access enabled — ready for Monitor
    Usage, Accuracy & Drift"
  - branch "not granted — request revised": User task "Revise
    access provisioning request"
    Send task "Resubmit revised access request for privacy review"
    (flow returns to Privacy lane Intermediate message catch event
    "Access request received for review" via sequence flow back
    through the clearance loop)

    Note: the "not granted" branch loops back to the Privacy lane
    using a sequence flow; this is the one exception to loop-as-
    subprocess because it is an inter-lane resubmission, not a
    within-lane repetition, and the loop condition is already
    carried by the expanded subprocess in the Privacy lane.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Access Request Cleared", labelled "Privacy review deadline exceeded
(5 business days)" — flows to End event "Access provisioning
escalated — review deadline breached".

Interrupting error boundary event on Service task "Deploy asset to
Business Intelligence Platform", labelled "Deployment failure" —
flows to User task "Investigate and remediate deployment failure",
then to End event "Deployment failed — remediation required".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Data Platform lane, moves to the
Privacy lane when the access request is submitted, returns to Data
Platform on clearance, then continues to provisioning and the Data
Subject rights check. The "Clearance granted?" gateway branches to
provisioning (granted) or loops back to Privacy review (not
granted). The "Rights request pending?" gateway branches to the
rights-honouring tasks (yes) or bypasses them (no), both arms
merging at the exclusive merge gateway before the end event.

Message flows:
Organisation (Service task "Deploy asset to Business Intelligence
Platform") → Business Intelligence Platform (deployment instruction).
Business Intelligence Platform → Organisation (Data Platform lane,
Intermediate message catch event "Deployment confirmation received")
(deployment confirmation).
Organisation (Service task "Provision access in Access Management
System") → Access Management System (access grant request).
Access Management System → Organisation (Data Platform lane,
Intermediate message catch event "Access grant confirmed")
(provisioning confirmation).
Data Subject → Organisation (Data Platform lane, Exclusive gateway
"Rights request pending from Data Subject?") (access, correction or
deletion request).
Organisation (Service task "Apply data-subject rights action across
platform") → Data Subject (acknowledgement and rights fulfilment
outcome).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Publication Scope and Classification Record" — written by
User task "Define publication scope and classification"; read by User
task "Configure asset metadata and access tiers".

Data Object "Access Provisioning Request" — written by User task
"Draft access provisioning request"; read by User task "Review access
request against privacy and consent constraints".

Data Object "Clearance Decision" — written by Send task "Return
clearance decision to Data Platform"; read by User task "Notify
requestors and record provisioning".

Data Object "Data Subject Rights Request" — read by User task "Honour
Data Subject access, correction or deletion request"; written by
Service task "Apply data-subject rights action across platform".

requestors and record provisioning".

and record provisioning".

V25.09 Publish & Enable Access takes the reviewed and validated result
from V25.08 and makes it reachable by the right people under the right
conditions. The Data Platform lane deploys the asset, the Privacy lane
clears every access grant against consent and classification rules,
and the Access Management System enforces least-privilege provisioning.
Data Subject rights requests are honoured before the subprocess closes.
The end state — a published, access-controlled asset recorded in the
access register and catalogue — hands the platform directly to V25.10
Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift.
```


### V25.10 — Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.10 Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift — the final subprocess of
the Data to Insight value chain, sustaining published outputs by
tracking consumption, model accuracy and data drift, and triggering
remediation when thresholds are breached.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams running the monitoring
  process, with lanes for Data Platform and Data Science.
Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — the system that
  collects quality metrics, drift signals and pipeline health data.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — the system that tracks model
  performance, version history and drift alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — black-box,
  System = true, single instance.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Quality & Observability Platform
2. Organisation
3. Machine Learning Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Platform lane:
  Timer start event "Monitoring cycle triggered — outputs published
    by Publish & Enable Access"
  Service task "Collect pipeline and usage metrics"
  Service task "Retrieve data quality and drift signals"
  Intermediate message catch event "Quality and drift report
    received"
  Exclusive gateway "Data quality or drift threshold breached?"
  - branch "No breach": Intermediate timer catch event
      "Next monitoring cycle due"
    - rejoin at Exclusive merge gateway
      "Data quality or drift threshold breached?"
  - branch "Breach detected": User task "Raise data quality or
      drift incident"
    Service task "Notify affected consumers"
    Exclusive gateway "Breach resolvable by platform team?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Apply pipeline or configuration fix"
      Service task "Verify fix and re-run quality checks"
      Intermediate message catch event "Fix confirmed by
        Data Quality & Observability Platform"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Breach resolvable by platform team?"
    - branch "No — escalate to Data Science": Send task
        "Escalate drift incident to Data Science"
      Intermediate message catch event "Data Science remediation
        complete"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Breach resolvable by platform team?"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Data quality or drift threshold
      breached?"
  End event "Monitoring cycle complete — platform health sustained"

Data Science lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Drift incident escalated from
    Data Platform"
  Service task "Retrieve model performance and drift metrics"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Model Accuracy Acceptable"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Analyse model degradation and root cause",
    User task "Retrain or recalibrate model",
    Service task "Register updated model version in platform",
    Service task "Run validation against accuracy thresholds"
  User task "Document remediation actions and updated thresholds"
  Send task "Confirm remediation complete to Data Platform"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess
  "Repeat Until Model Accuracy Acceptable" — labelled "Retraining
  deadline exceeded" — triggers an error End event "Model
  remediation failed — escalate to Data Governance".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Data Platform lane with the
timer start event, proceeds through metric collection and drift
retrieval, then reaches the first exclusive gateway; the "No
breach" branch waits at a timer and rejoins the same merge
gateway to restart the cycle; the "Breach detected" branch raises
the incident, notifies consumers, and reaches the second gateway,
whose "Yes" branch applies a fix, verifies it and rejoins the
merge, while the "No" branch sends an escalation message to the
Data Science lane, where the loop subprocess runs until accuracy
is acceptable, after which confirmation returns to the Data
Platform lane and the branches rejoin before the cycle-complete
end event.
Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Collect pipeline and usage metrics")
    → Data Quality & Observability Platform (request for metrics).
  Data Quality & Observability Platform → Organisation
    (Intermediate message catch event "Quality and drift report
    received") (quality metrics and drift report).
  Organisation (Service task "Verify fix and re-run quality
    checks") → Data Quality & Observability Platform (re-check
    request).
  Data Quality & Observability Platform → Organisation
    (Intermediate message catch event "Fix confirmed by Data
    Quality & Observability Platform") (verification result).
  Organisation (Data Science lane, Service task "Retrieve model
    performance and drift metrics") → Machine Learning Platform
    (performance metrics request).
  Machine Learning Platform → Organisation (Data Science lane,
    Service task "Retrieve model performance and drift metrics")
    (model performance and drift data).
  Organisation (Data Science lane, Service task "Register updated
    model version in platform") → Machine Learning Platform
    (updated model version registration).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Drift Incident Record" — written by "Raise data
  quality or drift incident" / read by "Notify affected
  consumers" and "Analyse model degradation and root cause".
Data Object "Remediation Report" — written by "Document
  remediation actions and updated thresholds" / read by
  "Confirm remediation complete to Data Platform".

Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift closes the Data to Insight value
chain by operating a continuous, cycle-based watch over every
published output. The Data Platform lane collects quality and
drift signals on each cycle and resolves pipeline-level breaches
directly, while the Data Science lane takes over when model
degradation requires retraining, registering corrected versions
back into the Machine Learning Platform. The subprocess sustains
the accuracy and trustworthiness of all insights delivered by the
chain and feeds updated thresholds and incident records back into
the governance and catalogue layers that underpin the next
analytical cycle.
```


## V26 — Concept to Commissioning

**Teams and roles involved.**
Concept to Commissioning usually involves Capital Planning, Project Management, Engineering and Design, Procurement, Construction or Delivery, Health and Safety, Quality, Commissioning, Operations and Maintenance, and Finance for capitalisation. Key roles include project sponsor, project manager, design engineer, cost estimator, procurement lead, construction manager, safety officer, quality inspector, commissioning engineer, operations representative, and asset accountant.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Contractors and Consultants delivering the work, and the Regulator or Authority granting approvals and permits. The process is initiated by a capital proposal arising from growth, replacement, compliance or risk. Other external parties include equipment vendors, certifiers and testing authorities, landowners and community stakeholders, and financiers where the project is externally funded.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: develop the concept and business case, obtain funding approval, perform detailed design, obtain permits and approvals, procure contractors and long-lead equipment, mobilise and construct or install, manage variations and progress claims, inspect and test, commission and hand over to operations, and capitalise the asset and close the project.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include capital portfolio and project management, cost estimating and scheduling, engineering design and document control, procurement and contract management, site and safety management, quality and inspection test plans, commissioning and handover systems, enterprise asset management for the resulting asset register, and the fixed-asset ledger.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include capital approval thresholds and stage gates, business case and benefits standards, design standards and review requirements, permit and environmental approval obligations, procurement and contracting policy, safety-in-design and site safety rules, variation and change control authority, inspection and test plan requirements, handover and acceptance criteria, and capitalisation versus expense rules.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Contractors and consultants provide tenders, designs, schedules, progress claims, variations, test results and as-built documentation, and receive scopes, drawings, instructions, approvals and payments. Regulators receive applications, impact assessments and compliance evidence, and provide permits, conditions and inspection outcomes. Community stakeholders provide submissions and receive consultation and notification.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates business cases, approvals and stage gates, designs and drawings, contracts and purchase orders, schedules and progress, variations and claims, inspection and test records, commissioning evidence, asset records and capitalisation entries. IT systems provide budget and forecast positions, cost actuals against estimate, schedule status, document versions and approvals, permit status, and portfolio and benefits reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Project Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V26.01** Develop Concept & Business Case | — | Capital Planning (project sponsor), Engineering (cost estimator) | Capital Portfolio Management System |
| **V26.02** Obtain Funding Approval | Financier | Capital Planning (project sponsor), Finance (asset accountant) | Capital Portfolio Management System |
| **V26.03** Perform Detailed Design | Consultant | Engineering (design engineer) | Engineering Design & Document Control |
| **V26.04** Obtain Permits & Approvals | Regulator, Community Stakeholder | Project Management (project manager), Health & Safety (safety officer) | Document Management System |
| **V26.05** Procure Contractors & Equipment | Contractor, Equipment Vendor | Procurement (procurement lead) | Procurement & Contract Management |
| **V26.06** Mobilise & Construct | Contractor | Construction (construction manager), Health & Safety (safety officer) | Site & Safety Management System |
| **V26.07** Manage Variations & Claims | Contractor | Project Management (project manager), Finance (cost controller) | Procurement & Contract Management, Cost & Schedule System |
| **V26.08** Inspect & Test | Certifier | Quality (quality inspector) | Quality & Inspection Test Plan System |
| **V26.09** Commission & Hand Over | Contractor | Commissioning (commissioning engineer), Operations (operations representative) | Commissioning & Handover System, Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) |
| **V26.10** Capitalise Asset & Close Project | — | Finance (asset accountant), Project Management (project manager) | Fixed Asset Ledger, Capital Portfolio Management System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V26):

- **External actors:** Financier (V26.02); Consultant (V26.03); Regulator (V26.04); Community Stakeholder (V26.04); Contractor (V26.05–V26.07, V26.09); Equipment Vendor (V26.05); Certifier (V26.08).
- **Teams:** Capital Planning (V26.01, V26.02); Engineering (V26.01, V26.03); Finance (V26.02, V26.07, V26.10); Project Management (V26.04, V26.07, V26.10); Health & Safety (V26.04, V26.06); Procurement (V26.05); Construction (V26.06); Quality (V26.08); Commissioning (V26.09); Operations (V26.09).
- **IT systems:** Capital Portfolio Management System (V26.01, V26.02, V26.10); Engineering Design & Document Control (V26.03); Document Management System (V26.04); Procurement & Contract Management (V26.05, V26.07); Site & Safety Management System (V26.06); Cost & Schedule System (V26.07); Quality & Inspection Test Plan System (V26.08); Commissioning & Handover System (V26.09); Enterprise Asset Management / EAM (V26.09); Fixed Asset Ledger (V26.10).

```text
4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- Commissioning & Handover System — manages commissioning checklists,
```

```text
procurement, construction, variation management, inspection, commissioning,
and final capitalisation. It serves seven categories of external actor —
Financier, Consultant, Regulator, Community Stakeholder, Contractor,
Equipment Vendor, and Certifier — and ten internal teams spanning Capital
Planning, Engineering, Finance, Project Management, Health & Safety,
Procurement, Construction, Quality, Commissioning, and Operations.
```
