**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V26 - Concept to Commissioning

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each represented as a chevron, in the order listed below. The chevrons
flow from left to right with no branching. Use exactly the stage names
and codes given.

V26.01. Develop Concept & Business Case
V26.02. Obtain Funding Approval
V26.03. Perform Detailed Design
V26.04. Obtain Permits & Approvals
V26.05. Procure Contractors & Equipment
V26.06. Mobilise & Construct
V26.07. Manage Variations & Claims
V26.08. Inspect & Test
V26.09. Commission & Hand Over
V26.10. Capitalise Asset & Close Project

This chain transforms a capital proposal — arising from growth, asset
replacement, compliance obligation or risk — into an operational asset
recorded on the fixed-asset ledger. It begins when a project sponsor
advances an initial concept and business case through internal stage
gates and ends when the commissioned asset is handed to Operations and
formally capitalised by Finance. Contractors and Consultants are the
primary external participants, delivering design, construction and
testing work across the middle stages of the chain, while the Regulator
grants the permits and approvals without which construction cannot
proceed.
```
### V26.01 — Develop Concept & Business Case

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.01 Develop Concept & Business Case — first subprocess of the
Concept to Commissioning value chain, in which the organisation develops
an initial concept, builds the business case, and prepares it for funding
approval.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal teams developing the concept
and business case, with lanes for Capital Planning and Engineering.
Pool "Capital Portfolio Management System" — the IT system recording the
business case, stage gates and portfolio position.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Capital Portfolio Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Project Organisation (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. Capital Portfolio Management System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Capital Planning lane (project sponsor):
  None start event "Capital proposal initiated — growth, replacement,
    compliance or risk trigger"
  User task "Register capital proposal and assign project sponsor"
  User task "Define project scope and objectives"
  User task "Engage Engineering for concept options and cost estimate"
  Intermediate message catch event "Concept options and order-of-magnitude
    estimate received from Engineering"
  User task "Screen and select preferred concept option"
  User task "Develop business case document"
  User task "Conduct business case review and quality check"
  Exclusive gateway "Business case acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes — proceed": continue to Service task "Submit business case
    to Capital Portfolio Management System"
  - branch "No — rework required": Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until
    Business Case Acceptable" (standard loop) containing, in order: User
    task "Record review findings and required revisions", User task "Revise
    business case sections"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Business case acceptable"
  Service task "Submit business case to Capital Portfolio Management System"
  User task "Obtain stage-gate sign-off from project sponsor"
  End event "Approved business case ready for Obtain Funding Approval"

Engineering lane (cost estimator):
  User task "Develop concept options and assess technical feasibility"
  User task "Prepare order-of-magnitude cost estimate and schedule"
  Send task "Deliver concept options and estimate to Capital Planning"
  User task "Support business case with engineering inputs and assumptions"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until
Business Case Acceptable" — label "Revision deadline exceeded" — triggers
End event "Business case escalated — sponsor intervention required".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Capital Planning lane with the none
start event, proceeds through proposal registration, scope definition and
the request to Engineering, then pauses at the intermediate message catch
event until Engineering returns options and the estimate; flow continues
through concept selection, business case development and review, then
diverges at the "Business case acceptable?" gateway — the No branch enters
the revision subprocess and rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway, while
the Yes branch bypasses it and meets at the same merge; flow then continues
through submission to the system, stage-gate sign-off, and the end event.
In the Engineering lane, work proceeds from developing options and the
estimate through to the send task that triggers the intermediate catch
event in Capital Planning, and continues with supporting inputs while the
business case is drafted.

Message flows:
Engineering lane (Send task "Deliver concept options and estimate to
Capital Planning") → Capital Planning lane (Intermediate message catch
event "Concept options and order-of-magnitude estimate received from
Engineering") (concept options and order-of-magnitude cost estimate).
Capital Planning lane (Service task "Submit business case to Capital
Portfolio Management System") → Capital Portfolio Management System
(business case record and portfolio entry).
Capital Portfolio Management System → Capital Planning lane (User task
"Obtain stage-gate sign-off from project sponsor") (portfolio position,
budget availability and stage-gate status).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Capital Proposal" — written by User task "Register capital
proposal and assign project sponsor"; read by User task "Define project
scope and objectives".
Data Object "Concept Options and Cost Estimate" — written by User task
"Prepare order-of-magnitude cost estimate and schedule"; read by User task
"Screen and select preferred concept option".
Data Object "Business Case Document" — written by User task "Develop
business case document"; read by User task "Conduct business case review
and quality check"; read by Service task "Submit business case to Capital
Portfolio Management System".
Service task "Submit business case to Capital Portfolio Management System";
read by User task "Obtain stage-gate sign-off from project sponsor".

This subprocess captures the capital proposal, develops feasible concept
options with order-of-magnitude cost and schedule, builds and internally
reviews the business case, and records it in the Capital Portfolio
Management System with a sponsor stage-gate sign-off. The approved
business case is then handed to Obtain Funding Approval, which secures
executive or financier authorisation before detailed design may begin.
```


### V26.02 — Obtain Funding Approval

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.02 Obtain Funding Approval — the subprocess that secures
formal capital funding commitment before detailed design begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal teams that prepare, submit
and manage the funding approval process.
  Lane "Capital Planning (project sponsor)"
  Lane "Finance (asset accountant)"
Pool "Financier" — external funder that reviews and commits capital
where the project is externally funded.
Pool "Capital Portfolio Management System" — IT system recording
business cases, approvals and stage gates.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Financier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Capital Portfolio Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Financier
2. Project Organisation
3. Capital Portfolio Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Capital Planning (project sponsor) lane:
  Message start event "Approved business case received from Develop
    Concept and Business Case"
  User task "Review business case for funding submission"
  User task "Confirm funding strategy and source"
  Exclusive gateway "External funding required?"
    - branch "Yes": Send task "Submit funding application to Financier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Financier decision received"
      Exclusive gateway "External funding approved?"
        - branch "No — resubmit": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
          Financier Approves" (standard loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Revise funding application",
          Send task "Resubmit revised application to Financier",
          Intermediate message catch event "Revised decision received"
          Timer boundary event on subprocess labelled "30 days without
          decision" — interrupting — escalate to project sponsor end event
        - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "External funding
          approved"
          Continue to Exclusive merge gateway "Funding strategy resolved"
    - branch "No — internal only": Exclusive merge gateway "Funding
      strategy resolved"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Funding strategy resolved"
  User task "Prepare internal capital approval submission"
  Send task "Submit to capital approval authority"
  Intermediate message catch event "Internal approval decision received"
  Exclusive gateway "Capital approval granted?"
    - branch "No — rejected": End event "Funding rejected — project
      halted" (terminates this subprocess instance)
    - branch "Yes": Exclusive merge gateway "Capital approval granted"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Capital approval granted"
  User task "Record approved funding and stage gate in system"
  Service task "Update approval status in Capital Portfolio Management
    System"

Finance (asset accountant) lane:
  User task "Validate cost estimate against capital thresholds"
  User task "Confirm capitalisation treatment and funding code"
  User task "Issue approved budget and cost code to project"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Financier Approves" — timer type — labelled "30 days without decision"
— leads to End event "Financier non-response — escalation required"
(does not rejoin main flow).

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in Capital Planning with the message start
event and moves through business case review and funding strategy
confirmation. The external-funding gateway splits to the Financier
submission branch or the internal-only branch, both rejoining at
"Funding strategy resolved". Finance lane tasks run in parallel support
— validate cost estimate, confirm capitalisation treatment, and issue
budget code — sequenced after the start event and feeding into the
capital approval submission. After the capital approval gateway, the
approved branch reaches "Record approved funding and stage gate" and
the service task, ending the subprocess. The rejected branch terminates
at its own End event and does not rejoin.

Message flows:
Send task "Submit funding application to Financier" → Financier
  (funding application package)
Financier → Intermediate message catch event "Financier decision
  received" (approval or rejection decision)
Send task "Resubmit revised application to Financier" → Financier
  (revised funding application)
Financier → Intermediate message catch event "Revised decision
  received" (revised approval or rejection)
Send task "Submit to capital approval authority" → Capital Portfolio
  Management System (internal capital approval submission)
Capital Portfolio Management System → Intermediate message catch event
  "Internal approval decision received" (approval decision and
  stage-gate record)
Service task "Update approval status in Capital Portfolio Management
  System" → Capital Portfolio Management System (approved funding
  status and stage-gate confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Business Case" — read by User task "Review business case
  for funding submission".
Data Object "Funding Application" — written by Send task "Submit
  funding application to Financier"; read by Send task "Resubmit
  revised application to Financier".
Data Object "Cost Estimate" — read by User task "Validate cost
  estimate against capital thresholds".
Data Object "Capital Approval Submission" — written by User task
  "Prepare internal capital approval submission"; read by Send task
  "Submit to capital approval authority".
Data Object "Approved Budget and Cost Code" — written by User task
  "Issue approved budget and cost code to project".

This subprocess confirms that sufficient capital authority and funding
commitment exist before the project proceeds to detailed design. It
tests whether external finance is needed, manages the funder interaction
loop until a decision is reached, and obtains internal stage-gate
approval against threshold policy. On completion it hands an approved
funding status, a registered stage gate, and an active budget code to
Perform Detailed Design.
```


### V26.03 — Perform Detailed Design

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.03 Perform Detailed Design — third subprocess in the Concept
to Commissioning value chain, converting the approved business case into
fully detailed, reviewed and issued-for-construction design documents.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal organisation managing the
  project; white-box pool containing Engineering team.
Pool "Consultant" — external design consultant delivering detailed
  design work.
Pool "Engineering Design & Document Control" — IT system managing
  design documents, versions and approvals.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consultant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Engineering Design & Document Control" — black-box, System =
  true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consultant
2. Project Organisation
3. Engineering Design & Document Control

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Engineering lane:

  Message start event "Approved business case and funding approval
    received from Obtain Funding Approval"
  User task "Define design scope and deliverables register"
  User task "Issue design brief and scope to Consultant"
  Intermediate message catch event "Consultant design deliverables
    received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Design Review Complete" (standard
    loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review design deliverables against standards and scope",
    User task "Record review comments and markup",
    Exclusive gateway "Design accepted?",
    - branch "No — comments issued": Send task "Issue review comments
      to Consultant",
    - Intermediate message catch event "Revised design deliverables
      received from Consultant",
    - branch "Yes — design accepted": continue to merge
    Exclusive merge gateway "Design accepted?"
  User task "Approve design documents for issue"
  Service task "Register approved documents in Engineering Design &
    Document Control"
  User task "Confirm design is complete and issue for construction"
  End event "Detailed design complete — ready for Obtain Permits &
    Approvals"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Design Review Complete" — label "Review cycle deadline exceeded" —
  flow continues to: Escalation end event "Escalate design delay to
  project sponsor".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow runs in the Engineering lane from the message
start event through scope definition, issuing the design brief, waiting
for deliverables, then entering the review loop. Inside the loop the
exclusive gateway branches: the "No" branch triggers sending review
comments and catching the revised deliverables before rejoining the
merge gateway; the "Yes" branch exits the loop to document approval.
Flow then proceeds to registration in the system, issuance for
construction, and the end event.

Message flows:
Project Organisation (User task "Issue design brief and scope to
  Consultant") → Consultant (design brief and scope)
Consultant → Project Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Consultant design deliverables received") (design deliverables
  submitted for review)
Project Organisation (Send task "Issue review comments to Consultant")
  → Consultant (review comments and markup)
Consultant → Project Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Revised design deliverables received from Consultant") (revised
  design deliverables)
Project Organisation (Service task "Register approved documents in
  Engineering Design & Document Control") → Engineering Design &
  Document Control (approved design documents for registration)
Engineering Design & Document Control → Project Organisation (User
  task "Approve design documents for issue") (document version and
  approval status confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Design Brief" — written by "Define design scope and
  deliverables register"; read by "Issue design brief and scope to
  Consultant".
Data Object "Deliverables Register" — written by "Define design scope
  and deliverables register"; read by "Review design deliverables
  against standards and scope".
Data Object "Design Deliverables Package" — read by "Review design
  deliverables against standards and scope"; written by "Record review
  comments and markup".
Data Object "Review Comments" — written by "Record review comments and
  markup"; read by "Issue review comments to Consultant".

This subprocess takes the approved business case from Obtain Funding
Approval and produces a fully reviewed, approved and registered set of
design documents ready for regulatory submission and construction.
Engineering engages the Consultant under an iterative review cycle,
ensuring all deliverables meet design standards before documents are
formally issued for construction. The resulting approved design package
is the primary input to Obtain Permits & Approvals.
```


### V26.04 — Obtain Permits & Approvals

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.04 Obtain Permits & Approvals — fourth subprocess in the
Concept to Commissioning value chain, converting completed detailed design
into the permits and regulatory approvals needed to begin construction.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal teams managing permit and approval
  activities, with lanes for Project Management and Health & Safety.
Pool "Regulator" — the authority that receives applications and issues
  permits, conditions and inspection outcomes.
Pool "Community Stakeholder" — external parties who submit on the project
  and receive consultation and notification.
Pool "Document Management System" — the IT system used to manage permit
  applications, impact assessments and compliance evidence.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Community Stakeholder" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Regulator
2. Community Stakeholder
3. Project Organisation
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Project Management lane (project manager):

  Message start event "Approved detailed design received from Perform
    Detailed Design"
  User task "Identify required permits and approval pathways"
  User task "Prepare permit applications and supporting documentation"
  Service task "Upload applications and impact assessments to Document
    Management System"
  Send task "Submit permit applications to Regulator"
  Send task "Issue community consultation and notification"
  Intermediate message catch event "Community submissions received"
  User task "Collate and review community submissions"
  User task "Prepare response to community submissions"
  Send task "Send submission response to Community Stakeholder"
  Intermediate message catch event "Regulator assessment queries received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Regulator Queries Resolved" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Review regulator query",
    User task "Prepare and compile additional information or evidence",
    Service task "Upload additional information to Document Management
    System", Send task "Send additional information to Regulator"
  Intermediate message catch event "Permit decision received from Regulator"
  Exclusive gateway "Permit granted?"
  - branch "Yes — permit granted": continue to Health & Safety lane
  - branch "No — permit refused": End event "Permit refused — project
      halted or redesign required"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Permit granted"

Health & Safety lane (safety officer):

  User task "Review permit conditions and environmental obligations"
  User task "Incorporate permit conditions into safety-in-design register"
  Service task "Record permit conditions and compliance evidence in
    Document Management System"
  User task "Confirm all required permits and approvals obtained"
  End event "Permits and approvals confirmed — ready for Procure
    Contractors & Equipment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Regulator Queries Resolved" — label "Regulator response deadline
  exceeded" — triggers End event "Permit process escalated — sponsor
  notified".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Project Management lane, moving from
identification and preparation of applications through upload, submission
to the Regulator and community notification, then through collection and
response to community submissions, then through resolution of regulator
queries in the loop subprocess, then to receipt of the permit decision
gateway; the "Yes" branch passes to the Health & Safety lane where permit
conditions are reviewed, recorded and confirmed before the process ends;
the "No" branch ends immediately in a permit-refused end event without
rejoining.

Message flows:
Project Management → Regulator (permit applications and supporting
  documentation including impact assessments)
Project Management → Community Stakeholder (consultation notification)
Community Stakeholder → Project Management (community submissions)
Project Management → Community Stakeholder (response to submissions)
Project Management → Regulator (additional information in response to
  assessment queries)
Regulator → Project Management (assessment queries)
Regulator → Project Management (permit decision with conditions)
Project Management → Document Management System (permit applications,
  impact assessments, additional evidence uploaded)
Health & Safety → Document Management System (permit conditions and
  compliance evidence recorded)
Document Management System → Project Management (document versions and
  permit status returned)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Permit Application Package" — written by User task "Prepare
  permit applications and supporting documentation"; read by Service task
  "Upload applications and impact assessments to Document Management
  System" and Send task "Submit permit applications to Regulator".
Data Object "Community Submissions Register" — written by User task
  "Collate and review community submissions"; read by User task "Prepare
  response to community submissions".
Data Object "Regulator Query Log" — written by User task "Review regulator
  query"; read by User task "Prepare and compile additional information or
  evidence".
Data Object "Permit Decision Notice" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Permit decision received from Regulator"; read by Exclusive
  gateway "Permit granted?" and User task "Review permit conditions and
  environmental obligations".
Data Object "Safety-in-Design Register" — written by User task
  "Incorporate permit conditions into safety-in-design register"; read by
  User task "Confirm all required permits and approvals obtained".

This subprocess transforms the approved detailed design into a full set of
regulatory permits and approvals by managing applications, community
consultation, and iterative responses to regulator queries. Permit
conditions are captured in the safety-in-design register so they flow
directly into site safety planning. The confirmed permit package is handed
to Procure Contractors & Equipment, enabling tendering and contract award
to proceed on a legally cleared basis.
```


### V26.05 — Procure Contractors & Equipment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.05 Procure Contractors & Equipment — the procurement subprocess

  tender to Equipment Vendor market".
Data Object "Contractor Tender Submissions" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Contractor tenders received"; read by User task
  "Evaluate contractor tenders".
Data Object "Equipment Vendor Tender Submissions" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Equipment Vendor tenders received"; read by User task
  "Evaluate equipment vendor tenders".
Data Object "Tender Evaluation Report — Contractor" — written by User task
  "Evaluate contractor tenders"; read by Exclusive gateway "Contractor
  tender acceptable?".
Data Object "Tender Evaluation Report — Equipment Vendor" — written by
  User task "Evaluate equipment vendor tenders"; read by Exclusive gateway
  "Equipment vendor tender acceptable?".

This subprocess takes the approved design and scope from Perform Detailed
Design and converts it into binding contractor contracts and equipment
purchase orders. It runs the contractor and equipment vendor procurement
streams concurrently, evaluating tenders, negotiating terms, and recording
all awards in the Procurement & Contract Management system. On completion
it hands a fully contracted and equipped project base to Mobilise &
Construct.
```


### V26.06 — Mobilise & Construct

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.06 Mobilise & Construct — execution subprocess in the Concept to
Commissioning value chain, covering site mobilisation, construction delivery,

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal teams managing and overseeing

  - Health & Safety (safety officer)

Pool "Contractor" — the principal construction contractor performing site

Pool "Site & Safety Management System" — the platform recording safety
  events, site access, inductions, and progress.

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Site & Safety Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Project Organisation (Construction lane, then Health & Safety lane)
3. Site & Safety Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Construction lane:
  Message start event "Contractor awarded and contracts executed — received
    from Procure Contractors & Equipment"
  User task "Issue site access and mobilisation instructions"
  User task "Confirm construction programme and resource plan"
  Send task "Issue approved drawings and scope documents to Contractor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Contractor mobilisation confirmation
    received"
  User task "Conduct pre-construction meeting and site establishment review"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Construction Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Review Contractor progress report and schedule update",
    User task "Conduct site progress meeting",
    User task "Assess works against programme milestones",
    User task "Record progress and cost actuals in system",
    User task "Issue site instructions and resolve construction queries"
  User task "Confirm practical completion and punch-list items"
  User task "Issue notice of practical completion"
  User task "Review and approve site demobilisation plan"
  End event "Practical completion confirmed — ready for Inspect & Test"

Health & Safety lane:
  User task "Verify Contractor safety management plan and site induction
    records"
  Exclusive gateway "Safety plan accepted?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Register site personnel and issue site access
      approval"
  - branch "No": User task "Return safety plan to Contractor for revision"
      Send task "Notify Contractor of safety plan deficiencies"
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised safety plan received"
      (loops back into gateway via Exclusive merge gateway "Safety plan
        accepted merge")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Safety plan accepted merge"
  User task "Log inductions and access approvals in Site & Safety
    Management System"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Construction Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Conduct site safety inspection",
    User task "Record safety observations and near-miss events",
    Service task "Submit safety records to Site & Safety Management System",
    Exclusive gateway "Safety issue identified?"
      - branch "Yes": User task "Issue stop-work or corrective action notice
          to Contractor",
          Intermediate message catch event "Contractor corrective action
            response received",
          Exclusive merge gateway "Safety issue resolved merge"
      - branch "No": Exclusive merge gateway "Safety issue resolved merge",
    User task "Confirm corrective actions closed or no action required"
  User task "Complete final site safety close-out report"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Construction Complete" (Construction lane) — label "Programme milestone
  overrun threshold reached" — triggers User task "Escalate programme delay
  to project sponsor and initiate recovery plan".

Interrupting error boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Construction lane with the message start

  accepted?" branches to approval or revision, with both paths rejoining at

  to induction logging and the concurrent safety-inspection loop. Both lane

  completion is confirmed in the Construction lane, leading to the end event.

Message flows:

  Project Organisation (Health & Safety lane) → Contractor (safety plan

  Contractor → Project Organisation (Health & Safety lane) (revised safety
    plan and corrective action responses)
  Project Organisation (Health & Safety lane) → Site & Safety Management
    System (safety inspection records, induction logs, near-miss events)
  Site & Safety Management System → Project Organisation (Construction lane)
    (progress and cost actuals confirmation)
  Site & Safety Management System → Project Organisation (Health & Safety
    lane) (safety record acknowledgement)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Mobilisation Instructions" — written by User task "Issue site
  access and mobilisation instructions"; read by Contractor.
Data Object "Construction Programme" — written by User task "Confirm
  construction programme and resource plan"; read by User task "Review
  Contractor progress report and schedule update".
Data Object "Approved Drawings and Scope Documents" — read by Send task
  "Issue approved drawings and scope documents to Contractor"; written by
  Engineering Design & Document Control (upstream).
Data Object "Contractor Safety Management Plan" — read by User task "Verify
  Contractor safety management plan and site induction records"; written by
  Contractor.
Data Object "Site Induction Records" — written by User task "Log inductions
  and access approvals in Site & Safety Management System"; read by Service
  task "Submit safety records to Site & Safety Management System".
Data Object "Progress Report" — written by Contractor; read by User task
  "Review Contractor progress report and schedule update".
Data Object "Safety Inspection Record" — written by User task "Record safety

Data Object "Corrective Action Notice" — written by User task "Issue

Data Object "Practical Completion Notice" — written by User task "Issue

Mobilise & Construct takes the awarded contracts from Procure Contractors &
Equipment and manages the full construction phase: mobilising the site,
verifying safety readiness, running concurrent construction-progress and
safety-oversight loops, and closing out the site on practical completion.
It hands a confirmed practical completion notice and a final safety close-out
report to Inspect & Test, giving that subprocess the documented evidence it
needs to begin formal inspection and testing activities.
```

### V26.07 — Manage Variations & Claims

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.07 Manage Variations & Claims — sits within the Concept to
Commissioning value chain, processing contractor-initiated scope changes
and progress claims during construction and delivery.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal teams managing variations
and claims through assessment, approval, and payment authorisation.
  Lane "Project Management" (project manager) — receives and assesses
    variation requests, exercises change control authority, and
    approves or rejects variations.
  Lane "Finance" (cost controller) — reviews cost impact, updates
    cost forecasts, and authorises claim payments.

Pool "Contractor" — external party submitting variation requests and
  progress claims and receiving decisions and payment instructions.

Pool "Procurement & Contract Management" — IT system recording
  contracts, variations, and claim transactions.

Pool "Cost & Schedule System" — IT system maintaining budget
  positions, cost actuals, and schedule status.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement & Contract Management" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Cost & Schedule System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Project Organisation
3. Procurement & Contract Management
4. Cost & Schedule System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Project Management lane:
  Message start event "Variation request or progress claim received
    from Mobilise & Construct"
  User task "Log and classify submission"
  Exclusive gateway "Submission type?"
  - branch "Variation request": User task "Assess scope and cost
      impact of variation"
      Intermediate message catch event "Contractor clarification
        received"
      Exclusive gateway "Variation approved?"
      - branch "Approved": Service task "Record approved variation
          in Procurement & Contract Management"
          Send task "Issue variation order to Contractor"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Variation decision complete"
      - branch "Rejected": Send task "Issue rejection notice to
          Contractor"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Variation decision complete"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Variation decision complete"
      Service task "Update contract value in Procurement &
        Contract Management"
  - branch "Progress claim": User task "Verify claim against
      progress schedule and contract"
      Exclusive gateway "Claim valid?"
      - branch "Disputed": Send task "Issue dispute notice to
          Contractor"
          Intermediate message catch event "Revised claim received
            from Contractor"
          User task "Re-assess revised claim"
          Exclusive merge gateway "Claim assessed"
      - branch "Accepted": Exclusive merge gateway "Claim assessed"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Claim assessed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Submission type resolved"

Finance lane:
  User task "Review cost impact and update forecast"
  Service task "Post forecast and actuals to Cost & Schedule System"
  User task "Authorise payment of claim"
  Service task "Record payment authorisation in Procurement &
    Contract Management"
  End event "Variation or claim resolved — ready for Inspect & Test"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Assess scope and cost
  impact of variation" — label "Assessment period exceeded (5
  business days)" — triggers Send task "Issue holding notice to
  Contractor" and returns to the main flow.

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Verify claim against
  progress schedule and contract" — label "Verification period
  exceeded (10 business days)" — triggers Send task "Issue
  acknowledgement of delay to Contractor" and returns to the main
  flow.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The flow starts in the Project Management lane with
  the message start event, moves to logging and classification, then
  splits at the "Submission type?" gateway. The variation branch
  runs through impact assessment, an intermediate catch event for
  clarification, an approval gateway whose "Approved" branch records
  and issues a variation order and whose "Rejected" branch sends a
  rejection notice, both rejoining at "Variation decision complete",
  then updates the contract value. The progress claim branch runs
  through verification, a validity gateway whose "Disputed" branch
  sends a dispute notice and waits for a revised claim via an
  intermediate catch event before re-assessment, and whose
  "Accepted" branch flows directly to the merge; both rejoin at
  "Claim assessed". Both top-level branches rejoin at "Submission
  type resolved" and flow into the Finance lane for cost review,
  forecast posting, payment authorisation, and payment recording,
  ending at the end event.

Message flows:
  Contractor → Project Management (variation request or progress
    claim submitted)
  Project Management → Contractor (request for clarification on
    variation)
  Contractor → Project Management (clarification response on
    variation)
  Project Management → Contractor (approved variation order)
  Project Management → Contractor (variation rejection notice)
  Project Management → Contractor (dispute notice on claim)
  Contractor → Project Management (revised progress claim)
  Project Management → Contractor (holding notice or delay
    acknowledgement, from boundary event tasks)
  Project Management → Procurement & Contract Management (variation
    and contract value recorded)
  Finance → Procurement & Contract Management (payment authorisation
    recorded)
  Finance → Cost & Schedule System (forecast and cost actuals
    posted)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Variation Request" — written by "Log and classify
  submission"; read by "Assess scope and cost impact of variation".
Data Object "Progress Claim" — written by "Log and classify
  submission"; read by "Verify claim against progress schedule and
  contract".
Data Object "Variation Order" — written by "Record approved
  variation in Procurement & Contract Management"; read by "Issue
  variation order to Contractor".
Data Object "Dispute Notice" — written by "Issue dispute notice to
  Contractor"; read by "Re-assess revised claim".
Data Object "Revised Claim" — written by intermediate catch event
  "Revised claim received from Contractor"; read by "Re-assess
  revised claim".

This subprocess captures every contractor variation request and
progress claim arising during construction, subjects each to
contractual assessment and change-control authority, and ensures
approved scope changes are priced and recorded while valid claims
are authorised for payment. It hands a fully reconciled and
authorised set of contract records and updated cost forecasts to
Inspect & Test, giving that subprocess a reliable baseline of
agreed scope and contract value against which inspection outcomes
and final accounts can be measured.
```


### V26.08 — Inspect & Test

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.08 Inspect & Test — the quality and inspection subprocess that
validates completed works before commissioning begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal teams conducting inspections
  and managing test outcomes.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Quality (quality inspector)
  - Construction (construction manager)

Pool "Certifier" — external certifying body that witnesses hold points
  and issues inspection outcomes.

Pool "Quality & Inspection Test Plan System" — system recording
  inspection, test and non-conformance data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Certifier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Quality & Inspection Test Plan System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Project Organisation (white-box, subdivided into Quality lane above,
   Construction lane below)
2. Certifier
3. Quality & Inspection Test Plan System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Quality lane:
  Message start event "Inspection and test readiness confirmed from
    Mobilise & Construct"
  User task "Review and issue Inspection and Test Plan"
  Service task "Register ITP in Quality & Inspection Test Plan System"
  User task "Schedule inspection hold points and witness points"
  Send task "Notify Certifier of upcoming hold points"
  Intermediate message catch event "Certifier attendance confirmed"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All ITP Items Cleared" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Conduct inspection or test
    activity", Exclusive gateway "Outcome acceptable?",
    - branch "Pass": User task "Record pass result in system",
    - branch "Fail": User task "Raise non-conformance report",
      User task "Initiate corrective action",
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrective action closed",
      User task "Re-inspect failed item",
      Exclusive merge gateway "Outcome acceptable"
  User task "Compile inspection and test records"
  User task "Submit test evidence package to Certifier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Certifier inspection outcome
    received"
  Exclusive gateway "All hold points accepted by Certifier?"
  - branch "Yes — all accepted": continue to close-out
  - branch "No — outstanding items": User task "Record outstanding
      items and assign remedial actions",
      Intermediate message catch event "Remedial actions verified",
      Exclusive merge gateway "All hold points accepted by Certifier"
  Exclusive merge gateway "All hold points accepted by Certifier"
  User task "Obtain signed inspection completion certificate"
  Service task "Close ITP and archive records in system"
  End event "Inspection and test complete — ready for Commission &
    Hand Over"

Construction lane:
  User task "Confirm works ready for inspection"
  User task "Support access and site conditions for inspection"
  User task "Execute remedial or corrective works"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  All ITP Items Cleared", labelled "ITP hold point deadline exceeded",
  leading to User task "Escalate overdue inspection to project manager"
  in Quality lane, then End event "Inspection escalated — process
  suspended pending review".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The flow begins in the Quality lane with the message
  start event and moves through ITP issuance, registration, scheduling
  and hold-point notification. After Certifier attendance is confirmed,
  the loop subprocess cycles through inspect–record–NCR–correct
  activities until all items clear. Post-loop, the Quality lane submits
  evidence, receives the Certifier outcome, and the gateway branches on
  acceptance: the "No" branch triggers remedial assignment and a
  message catch before merging back at "All hold points accepted by
  Certifier"; the "Yes" branch merges at the same point. Both branches
  rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway before proceeding to certificate
  sign-off and ITP archival. The Construction lane runs tasks
  concurrently with Quality lane activities, supporting readiness,
  access, and remedial execution, connected by sequence flows within the
  white-box pool.

Message flows:
  Quality lane "Notify Certifier of upcoming hold points" → Certifier
    (hold point schedule and ITP extract).
  Certifier → Quality lane "Certifier attendance confirmed"
    (attendance confirmation).
  Quality lane "Submit test evidence package to Certifier" → Certifier
    (test records, inspection results, NCR register).
  Certifier → Quality lane "Certifier inspection outcome received"
    (inspection outcome report, hold point sign-offs).
  Quality lane "Register ITP in Quality & Inspection Test Plan System"
    → Quality & Inspection Test Plan System (ITP record created).
  Quality lane "Record pass result in system" → Quality & Inspection
    Test Plan System (pass result written).
  Quality lane "Raise non-conformance report" → Quality & Inspection
    Test Plan System (NCR raised).
  Quality & Inspection Test Plan System → Quality lane "Compile
    inspection and test records" (aggregated test data and NCR status).
  Quality lane "Close ITP and archive records in system" → Quality &
    Inspection Test Plan System (ITP closed and archived).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inspection and Test Plan (ITP)" — written by "Review and
  issue Inspection and Test Plan"; read by "Schedule inspection hold
  points and witness points", "Conduct inspection or test activity".
Data Object "Non-Conformance Report (NCR)" — written by "Raise
  non-conformance report"; read by "Initiate corrective action",
  "Re-inspect failed item".
Data Object "Corrective Action Record" — written by "Initiate
  corrective action"; read by "Re-inspect failed item".
Data Object "Test Evidence Package" — written by "Compile inspection
  and test records"; read by "Submit test evidence package to
  Certifier".
Data Object "Inspection Completion Certificate" — written by "Obtain
  signed inspection completion certificate"; read by "Close ITP and
  archive records in system".

V26.08 Inspect & Test validates that all constructed or installed works
meet the required quality standards by executing the Inspection and Test
Plan, managing non-conformances through corrective action cycles, and
securing formal sign-off from the Certifier at each hold point. The
subprocess produces a signed inspection completion certificate and a
fully archived ITP record, confirming that works are defect-free and
accepted. These outputs hand directly to Commission & Hand Over, giving
the commissioning team verified, certified works ready for functional
testing and operational acceptance.
```


### V26.09 — Commission & Hand Over

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
This subprocess takes the inspected and tested asset and executes all
commissioning test procedures, resolves punch list defects through the
```

### V26.10 — Capitalise Asset & Close Project

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V26.10 Capitalise Asset & Close Project — final subprocess of the
Concept to Commissioning value chain, converting completed project costs into
a registered fixed asset and formally closing the project.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Project Organisation" — the internal team executing capitalisation and
project closure.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Finance (asset accountant)
  - Project Management (project manager)

Pool "Fixed Asset Ledger" — IT system recording the capitalised asset entry.
Pool "Capital Portfolio Management System" — IT system recording project
closure and portfolio status.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Project Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Fixed Asset Ledger" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Capital Portfolio Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Project Organisation (white-box, contains all flow)
2. Fixed Asset Ledger
3. Capital Portfolio Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Project Organisation)

Finance lane:
  Message start event "Handover accepted — ready for Capitalise Asset &
    Close Project"
  User task "Identify capital costs to be capitalised"
  User task "Classify costs against asset components"
  Exclusive gateway "All costs correctly classified?"
    - branch "No — rework required":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Classification Complete"
        (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Review and correct
        cost classification", User task "Recheck classification against
        capitalisation policy"
        Exclusive merge gateway "All costs correctly classified?"
    - branch "Yes":
        Continue to next task
  User task "Create asset record and capitalisation entry"
  Service task "Post capitalisation entry to Fixed Asset Ledger"
  Service task "Record asset in Capital Portfolio Management System"
  User task "Reconcile project costs to capitalised asset value"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation agreed?"
    - branch "Discrepancy identified":
        User task "Investigate and resolve discrepancy"
        Intermediate message catch event "Resolution confirmed"
        Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation agreed?"
    - branch "Agreed":
        Continue to next task
  User task "Expense any non-capital costs to profit and loss"

Project Management lane:
  User task "Compile project close-out report"
  User task "Confirm benefits realisation baseline"
  User task "Obtain project sponsor sign-off on closure"
  Exclusive gateway "Sponsor approves closure?"
    - branch "Not approved — further action required":
        User task "Address outstanding closure items"
        Exclusive merge gateway "Sponsor approves closure?"
    - branch "Approved":
        Continue to next task
  Service task "Update project status to Closed in Capital Portfolio
    Management System"
  User task "Archive project documentation"
  End event "Asset capitalised and project formally closed"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Classification Complete" — label "Classification overdue (5 business days)"
— triggers User task "Escalate classification delay to Finance Manager" in
Finance lane, ending in a terminate end event after escalation.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Finance lane with cost identification and
classification, passing through the classification loop gateway and its merge
before proceeding to asset record creation, ledger posting, portfolio system
recording, and reconciliation. The reconciliation gateway branches to a
discrepancy resolution path that rejoins at the reconciliation merge, then
continues to expensing non-capital costs. Control then passes to the Project
Management lane for close-out reporting, benefits baselining, and sponsor
sign-off. The sponsor approval gateway branches to an outstanding-items
resolution path that rejoins at its merge, then continues to system closure
update, documentation archiving, and the end event.

Message flows:
Capital Portfolio Management System → Finance lane (approved project costs
and budget position for capitalisation reference).
Finance lane (Service task "Post capitalisation entry to Fixed Asset
Ledger") → Fixed Asset Ledger (capitalisation journal entry).
Fixed Asset Ledger → Finance lane (asset register confirmation and asset
identifier).
Finance lane (Service task "Record asset in Capital Portfolio Management
System") → Capital Portfolio Management System (asset record and
capitalised value).
Project Management lane (Service task "Update project status to Closed in
Capital Portfolio Management System") → Capital Portfolio Management System
(project closure status and close-out report reference).
Capital Portfolio Management System → Project Management lane (confirmed
closure record and portfolio update).

capitalisation entry".

entry to Fixed Asset Ledger".

Data Object "Project Close-out Report" — written by User task "Compile

Data Object "Benefits Realisation Baseline" — written by User task "Confirm

V26.10 converts the completed project into a permanent business record by
classifying and posting all capital expenditure to the fixed asset ledger,
reconciling the capitalised value, and expensing any non-capital costs.
Project Management simultaneously produces the close-out report, locks in
the benefits realisation baseline, and secures sponsor sign-off, after which
the project is marked closed in the portfolio system. This subprocess is the
terminal step of the Concept to Commissioning chain and hands a registered,
valued asset to the ongoing operations and finance functions.
```
